From a **quality-engineering perspective**, the profile you pasted is missing a major layer. Building 200+ voice agents is impressive, but production quality requires proving that they are accurate, safe, reliable, fast, observable, and resistant to real-world call conditions.

I would build the Voice AI QA model around these areas:

| Quality area | What must be tested | Example KPI / acceptance criterion |
|---|---|---|
| **1. STT Quality** | Speech recognition accuracy | WER/CER, entity accuracy |
| **2. TTS Quality** | Naturalness, pronunciation, pacing | MOS, pronunciation pass rate |
| **3. Intent Recognition** | Correct caller intention | Intent accuracy > target |
| **4. Entity Extraction** | Name, DOB, phone, date/time, provider | Field-level precision/recall |
| **5. Conversation Quality** | Coherent multi-turn dialogue | Task completion rate |
| **6. LLM Accuracy** | Correct answers | Grounded-answer accuracy |
| **7. Hallucination** | Unsupported responses | Hallucination rate |
| **8. RAG Quality** | Correct clinic information retrieved | Recall@K, Precision@K |
| **9. Appointment Accuracy** | Correct provider/date/time/service | Booking accuracy |
| **10. Transaction Integrity** | No duplicate/incorrect booking | Duplicate transaction rate |
| **11. API Quality** | Correct request/response/error handling | API success/error rate |

| **15. Audio Quality** | Noise, echo, interruptions | Audio-quality score |
| **16. Latency** | Response delay | P50/P95/P99 latency |
| **17. Interruption Handling** | Caller talks over agent | Barge-in success |
| **18. Silence Handling** | Caller doesn't respond | Recovery success |
| **19. Accent Testing** | Different accents/dialects | Accuracy by accent |
| **20. Multilingual** | Language detection/switching | Language task success |
| **21. Noise Robustness** | Car, clinic, street, speakerphone | Task success by noise level |

| **27. Load** | Concurrent calls | Supported concurrent sessions |
| **28. Stress** | Beyond expected capacity | Graceful degradation |
| **29. Reliability** | Long-running production operation | Availability/SLO |

### The critical difference: don't test only the LLM

For a production healthcare voice agent, I would define quality as:

**Voice Quality**

STT → TTS → accent → pronunciation → noise → interruption → silence → latency

**AI Quality**

Intent → entities → prompt → RAG → hallucination → reasoning → tool selection → response

**Functional Quality**

Appointment → cancel → reschedule → provider selection → patient lookup → FAQ → SMS → transfer

**Integration Quality**

Voice platform → n8n → APIs → PMS/EHR → CRM → calendar → SMS/email → database

**Non-functional Quality**

Performance → scalability → reliability → resilience → security → privacy → compliance → cost

**Business Quality**

Call answered → problem resolved → appointment booked → reduced staff workload → patient satisfied.

---

## One scenario should generate dozens of tests

Suppose the caller says:

> "I need to see Dr. Smith sometime next Tuesday afternoon."

A basic developer tests whether it books.

A **QA/FDE/Architect** should test:

Caller exists / doesn't exist → provider exists / unavailable → ambiguous Tuesday → timezone → clinic closed → appointment duration → appointment type → insurance requirement → conflicting appointment → API timeout → duplicate webhook → calendar unavailable → patient changes mind → caller interrupts → caller changes date → background noise → wrong STT transcription → agent misunderstood provider → tool call fails → retry → human escalation.

Then verify the backend:

**Voice transcript → extracted entities → LLM decision → tool call → API request → API response → database → appointment system → confirmation → SMS → audit record.**

That traceability is extremely important.

### Production QA pipeline

I would design the lifecycle as:

**Requirements → Conversation specification → Risk assessment → Test scenarios → Synthetic conversations → Automated evaluation → Integration tests → End-to-end voice tests → Human evaluation → Red-team testing → Load testing → UAT → Canary deployment → Production monitoring → Failed-call analysis → Regression dataset → Continuous evaluation.**

Every production failure should become a **new permanent regression test**.

For 200+ agents, manually testing each agent becomes impractical. You therefore need a **Voice AI Quality Platform** where a golden dataset of perhaps 500–5,000 conversations is automatically replayed whenever the prompt, LLM, voice provider, workflow, API, knowledge base, or clinic configuration changes.

That is where your existing QA/architecture experience could become particularly useful: instead of positioning yourself only as someone who can build a Vapi/Retell/Bolna agent, you can position around **Voice AI Quality Engineering + Agent Evaluation + Production Architecture**. memcite

## But there are bigger problems common to ALL voice agents

The platform is only perhaps **20–30% of the quality problem**. Production failures usually emerge from the complete chain:

**Caller → telecom → audio → VAD → STT/speech model → LLM → RAG → tool → API → clinic system → response → TTS → telecom → caller**

A failure anywhere can appear to the customer as **"the AI doesn't work."**

### 1. Latency is one of the hardest problems

Consider:

**Caller finishes speaking**

→ endpoint detection 300 ms  
→ STT 300 ms  
→ LLM 600 ms  
→ tool 500 ms  
→ TTS 300 ms  
→ network 200 ms

You are already near:

**~2.2 seconds**

That can make conversation feel unnatural.

You therefore need to track:

**TTFT + STT latency + LLM latency + tool latency + TTS latency + end-to-end P50/P95/P99.**

---

### 2. STT errors become business errors

Caller:

> "Book me Tuesday at fifteen thirty."

STT:

> "Book me Tuesday at fifty thirty."

Or:

> "Dr. Sandeep"

becomes:

> "Dr. Sandy."

For healthcare this can propagate:

**STT error → entity error → incorrect tool arguments → incorrect appointment.**

Therefore don't measure only WER.

Measure:

**Critical Entity Error Rate**

for:

**patient name | DOB | phone | provider | date | time | procedure | medication | insurance information**

---

### 3. Barge-in/interruption problems

Caller:

> "I'd like an appointment—"

Agent starts talking.

Caller:

> "Actually Friday."

Agent continues processing Tuesday.

This produces a difficult state problem:

**Audio state ≠ transcript state ≠ LLM state ≠ workflow state.**

You need tests for interruption at virtually every conversation stage.

---

### 4. Tool calling is a major production risk

Suppose the agent calls:

`bookAppointment(patient, provider, date, time)`

Possible failures include:

API timeout → retry → **duplicate appointment**

or:

booking succeeds → response times out → agent assumes failure → retries → **second booking**.

This is why you need:

**idempotency keys + transaction state + retry policies + reconciliation + audit trail.**

---

### 5. Hallucination becomes dangerous in healthcare

Patient:

> "Can I take ibuprofen before my procedure?"

The voice agent shouldn't casually generate medical advice.

Architecture needs:

**Question → risk classifier → approved knowledge/RAG → policy engine → answer OR abstain → human escalation.**

A critical QA metric becomes:

**Unsafe Answer Rate ≈ 0**

rather than merely measuring whether the conversation sounds natural.

---

### 6. Accent + language + code-switching

This is especially important when comparing **Sarvam** against more general STT systems.

Real callers may say:

> "Mujhe kal physiotherapy ka appointment chahiye around 3 PM."

That's:

**Hindi + English + medical term + English time expression.**

Testing should cover:

English → Hindi → Punjabi → Tamil → Telugu → Bengali → code-switching → regional accents → Canadian/US accents.

---

### 7. Background noise

Production calls happen from:

car → street → airport → office → clinic → speakerphone → Bluetooth → poor cellular connection.

Create test datasets with:

**clean / 10 dB / 5 dB / 0 dB SNR**

and compare task completion rather than only transcription accuracy.

---

### 8. Silence and endpoint detection

Another underestimated problem:

Caller:

> "My date of birth is... umm... February... twenty..."

The agent decides the person finished speaking and responds.

Your VAD/endpointing settings directly affect UX.

Too aggressive → interruption.  
Too conservative → awkward silence.

---

### 9. Real-time model versus pipeline trade-off

This is where **Ultravox/Realtime models versus Bolna/LiveKit pipeline architecture** becomes architecturally interesting.

Traditional:

**STT → LLM → TTS**

Advantages:

control + observability + component replacement.

Problems:

latency + orchestration complexity.

Speech-native:

**Audio → realtime model → audio**

Advantages:

natural + potentially lower latency.

Problems:

less deterministic + harder evaluation + harder debugging.

For healthcare, you may therefore use a **hybrid architecture**:

**Realtime voice model for conversation**

but

**deterministic tools/workflow engine for transactions.**

---

## The biggest quality challenge at 200+ agents

Once you reach hundreds of agents, the problem changes.

You cannot have:

**Agent #1 prompt**
**Agent #2 prompt**
...
**Agent #200 prompt**

with developers manually testing every one.

You need a platform:

**Agent Template**
↓
**Brand Configuration**
↓
**Clinic Configuration**
↓
**Knowledge Base**
↓
**Tool Configuration**
↓
**Policy Configuration**
↓
**Generated Agent**
↓
**Automated Test Suite**
↓
**Quality Gate**
↓
**Deployment**
↓
**Production Monitoring**

Then every change triggers something like:

**1,000 synthetic conversations × critical scenarios × languages × noise conditions × failure conditions.**

The release gets blocked when appointment accuracy, safety, latency, hallucination, transfer success, or another critical KPI falls below its threshold.

That is the piece I'd emphasize for you: **Voice AI QA is not conventional software QA.** It combines software testing + LLM evaluation + speech evaluation + telecom testing + integration testing + safety testing + production observability. Given your interest in architect/FDE preparation, building this **Voice Agent Quality Engineering Framework** would be considerably more differentiated than simply demonstrating that you can configure a Bolna/Vapi/Retell agent. memcite

# The architecture I would choose

For the clinic scenario you gave me earlier—dental, physiotherapy, chiropractic, ENT, massage, appointment scheduling, inbound/outbound calls—I would **not** make n8n or the voice platform responsible for critical healthcare transaction integrity.

I'd build:

**Twilio/Telnyx/SIP**  
↓  
### **LiveKit**
↓  
**STT / realtime model**
↓  
**LLM**
↓  
**Deterministic Tool Gateway**
↓  
**Appointment / PMS / EHR / CRM**
↓  
**n8n — secondary automation only**

And use:

**OpenTelemetry + call traces + conversation evaluation + regression testing + human escalation**

around it.

That is slightly more work initially, but much less painful when you reach **50, 100 or 200+ clinic agents**.

### If you tell me "I don't want that engineering headache"

Then I'd change the decision:

**Prototype:** Bolna  
→ **Fast production:** Ultravox  
→ **India multilingual:** Sarvam  
→ **Long-term healthcare platform:** LiveKit

So for your specific question — **"high quality + high trust + less headache"** — there isn't one winner on all three:

**LiveKit = maximum trust/control, somewhat more work.**  
**Ultravox = strongest quality/simplicity balance.**  
**Bolna = easiest implementation.**  
**Sarvam = strongest specialized option for India/multilingual voice.**

→ Voice Agent

→ check doctor
→ check appointment

→ analytics.

For your production-grade/custom architecture.

For Indian multilingual customers.

### The features I would add beyond typical Voice AI platforms

If you are thinking about building your **own layer over Retell/Vapi/Bolna/LiveKit/Ultravox/Sarvam**, the differentiator should not be another call interface.

Build a **Voice Agent Control Plane**:

**Customer/Clinic**
→ Agent template
→ Voice/personality
→ Prompt
→ Knowledge
→ Business rules
→ Tools
→ Phone/SIP
→ Workflow
→ Guardrails
→ QA test suite
→ deployment
→ monitoring
→ analytics
→ optimization.

Then support multiple underlying providers:

**Retell | Vapi | Bolna | LiveKit | Ultravox | Sarvam**

so the customer isn't tightly locked into one.

The particularly valuable product could actually be the **Quality + Governance layer**:

**Agent Quality Score = Speech + Conversation + Task Success + Tool Accuracy + Safety + Latency + Reliability + Customer Experience + Cost**

with every call automatically evaluated and bad calls routed into a regression dataset.

That would move the product from **"we build voice bots"** toward **"enterprise Voice AI platform with QA, governance and multi-provider orchestration."**

## Customer Acquisition → Voice Agent Master Flow

```text
Traffic / Prospect Source
        ↓
Landing Page / Social / QR / Ad
        ↓
Lead Form
        ↓
Consent + Communication Preference
        ↓
Lead Capture API
        ↓
Lead Validation / Deduplication
        ↓

        ↓
Lead Enrichment
        ↓

        ↓
Campaign / Segment
        ↓

        ↓

        ↓
Interested? ────────────── Not Interested
     ↓                           ↓
Qualification                DNC / Nurture
     ↓
Appointment
     ↓
SMS / Email Confirmation
     ↓
CRM Update
     ↓
Human Sales / Clinic Staff
     ↓
Conversion
     ↓
Analytics + Attribution
```

For healthcare, keep **marketing lead data separate from clinical/PHI data** as much as possible.

### 1. Lead acquisition channels

Your acquisition module should accept leads from many sources:

| Source | Capture mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Website | Form | Book consultation |
| Landing page | Campaign form | Free assessment |
| Google Ads | Lead form / landing page | Search campaign |
| Meta | Lead Ads/form | Facebook/Instagram |
| LinkedIn | Lead Gen Forms | Corporate/B2B |
| Instagram | Bio/form link | Consumer campaign |
| TikTok | Lead form | Consumer campaign |
| YouTube | Landing-page CTA | Video campaign |
| QR code | Form URL | Flyer/store/event |
| Email campaign | CTA → form | Existing prospects |
| SMS | Short URL | Existing opted-in contacts |
| Referral | Referral form | Patient/customer referral |
| Event | Registration form | Webinar/open house |
| Chatbot | Conversational form | Website |
| Voice inbound | Voice intake | Caller becomes lead |
| Manual | Staff entry | Walk-in/phone inquiry |
| API | Partner lead | External source |
| CSV | Import | Existing permitted lead base |

Every campaign gets a unique URL, for example:

`/consultation?source=instagram&campaign=summer-physio`

Store the **UTM/source/campaign/ad/creative** with the lead.

Don't collect only email.

For a general service/clinic acquisition form, collect:

**Identity**

Last name

**Contact**

**Intent**

Preferred location  
Preferred appointment time  
Reason for inquiry — keep this non-clinical unless you have the appropriate privacy/compliance design.

**Communication**

Preferred channel:
Email / SMS / Phone

**Consent**

Marketing consent  
SMS consent  
Outbound-call consent where required  
Privacy-policy acknowledgement

**Attribution**

UTM source  
UTM medium  
UTM campaign  
UTM content  
UTM term  
Landing page  
Referrer  
Campaign ID  
Ad ID  
Form ID  
Timestamp

The consent evidence is critical:

```text
consent_type
consent_status
consent_text_version
timestamp
source
form_id
campaign_id
IP/device metadata where appropriate
withdrawal_timestamp
```

For Canada, your design also needs to account for applicable privacy/anti-spam/telemarketing requirements rather than assuming a submitted phone number automatically authorizes every type of marketing call.

---

Form submission should trigger:

```text
      ↓

      ↓
```

# 4. CRM lifecycle

I would standardize the lifecycle across every voice platform:

**New → Validated → Qualified → Call Eligible → Call Scheduled → Calling → Connected → Interested → Appointment Booked → Converted**

with alternative paths:

**No Answer → Retry**

**Busy → Retry**

**Voicemail → Voicemail/SMS workflow**

**Call Later → Scheduled Callback**

**Not Interested → Closed**

**Do Not Call → DNC**

**Wrong Number → Invalid**

**Human Requested → Sales Queue**

**Complaint → Escalation**

This is much more important than which voice provider you select.

---

# 5. Outbound calling plan

When a lead submits a form:

### High-intent lead

For example:

> "I want to book a physiotherapy consultation."

Your workflow can be:

```text
11:02:10 Form submitted
       ↓
11:02:11 Lead validated
       ↓
11:02:12 CRM lead created
       ↓
11:02:13 Consent checked
       ↓
11:02:14 Lead scored = HOT
       ↓
11:02:15 Outbound workflow created
       ↓
Voice Agent Call
       ↓
"Hi John, you recently requested information
about physiotherapy..."
```

But the exact call timing should respect the person's request, consent, local time, calling rules, and your campaign policy—not simply "call everyone immediately."

---

# 6. Voice-agent conversation

The outbound agent needs a deterministic flow.

```text
IDENTIFICATION
↓
DISCLOSURE
↓
VERIFY RIGHT PERSON
↓
REFERENCE THEIR REQUEST
↓
ASK PERMISSION TO CONTINUE
↓
DISCOVER REQUIREMENT
↓
QUALIFY
↓
ANSWER QUESTIONS
↓
HANDLE OBJECTION
↓
CTA
↓
BOOK APPOINTMENT
↓
CONFIRM
↓
SMS/EMAIL
↓
CRM UPDATE
```

For example:

> "Hi Sarah, I'm the virtual assistant for ABC Physiotherapy. You requested information through our website about booking a consultation. Is now a good time to talk?"

That is much better than an unexplained AI cold call.

---

# 7. Lead scoring

Give every lead a score.

| Signal | Example score |
|---|---:|
| Requested appointment | +30 |
| Requested callback | +25 |
| Submitted consultation form | +20 |
| Valid mobile | +10 |
| Valid email | +5 |
| Selected specific service | +10 |
| Selected preferred date | +10 |
| Returning visitor | +5 |
| Opened follow-up | +3 |
| Invalid phone | -50 |
| DNC | **Block** |
| Consent missing where required | **Block campaign** |

Then:

**80–100 → HOT → priority follow-up**

**50–79 → WARM → call/nurture**

**20–49 → NURTURE**

**0–19 → low priority**

But keep **eligibility** separate from **lead score**. A 100-point lead isn't callable if the relevant consent/rules prohibit the call.

---

# 8. One acquisition engine → every voice platform

This is the architecture I recommend.

```text
                  ACQUISITION
                       │
      ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
      ↓                ↓                ↓
     Ads             Website          Social
      │                │                │
      └───────────→ FORM API ←──────────┘
                       │
                Lead Management
                       │
                  Consent Engine
                       │
                  Lead Scoring
                       │
                 Campaign Engine
                       │
              Voice Provider Gateway
                       │
       ┌───────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
       ↓               ↓              ↓          ↓
    Retell           Vapi           Bolna     LiveKit
       ↓               ↓              ↓          ↓
  Ultravox           Sarvam       Other      Custom
       │               │              │          │
       └───────────────┴──────┬───────┴──────────┘
                              ↓
                         Call Result
                              ↓
                            CRM
                              ↓
               Appointment / Sales System
```

This prevents vendor lock-in.

---

## 9. Provider adapter

Create one internal interface such as:

```text
create_agent()
update_agent()

create_call()
cancel_call()

get_call_status()
get_transcript()
get_recording()
get_cost()

transfer_call()

create_campaign()
pause_campaign()

receive_webhook()
```

Then implement:

```text
RetellAdapter
VapiAdapter
BolnaAdapter
LiveKitAdapter
UltravoxAdapter
SarvamAdapter
```

The CRM doesn't care which provider handled the call.

---

# 10. Outbound campaign engine

This should be a substantial module of its own.

It needs:

**Campaign management**

Campaign name  
Target segment  
Agent  
Phone number  
Script/prompt  
Start/end date  
Timezone  
Calling window  
Maximum attempts  
Retry policy  
Voicemail strategy  
SMS strategy  
Human-transfer queue.

**Dialing controls**

Concurrency  
Calls/minute  
Rate limiting  
Provider capacity  
Daily limits  
Contact frequency caps.

**Suppression**

DNC  
Consent withdrawal  
Existing customer exclusions  
Wrong numbers  
Complaint suppression  
Duplicate leads  
Previously converted contacts.

---

# 11. Retry strategy

Don't repeatedly hammer the customer.

An example policy might be:

```text
Attempt 1
↓
No answer
↓
Retry according to campaign policy

Attempt 2
↓
No answer
↓
SMS/email if permitted

Attempt 3
↓
No answer
↓
Move to nurture / human-defined follow-up
```

The actual number/timing of attempts should be configurable by jurisdiction and business policy.

---

# 12. Appointment module

Once interested:

```text
Voice Agent
   ↓
get_locations()
   ↓
get_services()
   ↓
get_providers()
   ↓
get_availability()
   ↓
Customer chooses
   ↓
confirm_details()
   ↓
create_appointment()
   ↓
CRM update
   ↓
SMS
   ↓
Email
```

Important:

**Do not allow the LLM itself to "invent" availability.**

The agent must call the authoritative appointment API.

---

# 13. Automation layer

n8n is useful for:

```text
Form
 → Lead
 → CRM
 → Email
 → SMS
 → Campaign trigger
 → Voice call
 → Call result
 → CRM update
 → Appointment
 → Follow-up
```

But I'd put critical controls—**consent eligibility, DNC, duplicate transaction protection, campaign limits, appointment integrity**—in a proper backend/service rather than relying entirely on a visual workflow.

---

# 14. Dashboard

Your acquisition dashboard should show the whole funnel:

```text
10,000 Visitors
     ↓
1,000 Forms
     ↓
900 Valid Leads
     ↓
750 Call Eligible
     ↓
700 Calls Attempted
     ↓
450 Connected
     ↓
300 Qualified
     ↓
180 Appointments
     ↓
150 Attended
     ↓
110 Customers
```

Then calculate:

**Visitor → Lead %**

**Lead → Call %**

**Connect rate**

**Qualification rate**

**Appointment rate**

**Show rate**

**Conversion rate**

**Revenue/customer**

**CAC**

**Cost/lead**

**Cost/connected call**

**Cost/appointment**

**Cost/acquired customer**

**Revenue/campaign**

**ROAS/ROI**

This gives you a real customer-acquisition system rather than a voice-agent demo.

---

# 15. Add QA to the acquisition funnel

This is particularly important.

For every call capture:

**Did agent identify correctly?**

**Was consent/eligibility valid?**

**Was disclosure made?**

**Did agent understand intent?**

**Were lead details correct?**

**Were unsupported claims made?**

**Was the right service offered?**

**Was the appointment correct?**

**Was CRM updated correctly?**

**Was follow-up sent?**

**Was DNC honored?**

Then calculate:

### Acquisition Voice Quality Score

**Conversation quality + compliance + task success + booking accuracy + integration accuracy + customer experience + technical quality**

---

# 16. What I would build as modules

For your overall Voice AI platform, I would now define these as separate product modules:

**M01 — Landing Page Builder**  
**M02 — Form Builder**  
**M03 — Lead Capture API**  
**M04 — Consent & Preference Management**  
**M05 — Lead Database / CRM**  
**M06 — Deduplication & Validation**  
**M07 — Lead Enrichment**  
**M08 — Lead Scoring**  
**M09 — Segmentation**  
**M10 — Campaign Management**  
**M11 — Outbound Dialer**  
**M12 — Voice Agent Gateway**  
**M13 — Retell/Vapi/Bolna/LiveKit/Ultravox/Sarvam Adapters**  
**M14 — Conversation Engine**  
**M15 — Appointment Engine**  
**M16 — SMS/Email/WhatsApp Follow-up**  
**M17 — Human Handoff**  
**M18 — DNC/Suppression Engine**  
**M19 — QA/Evaluation Engine**  
**M20 — Call Monitoring & Observability**  
**M21 — Attribution**  
**M22 — Funnel Analytics**  
**M23 — Cost/FinOps**  
**M24 — Compliance/Governance**  
**M25 — Admin/Customer Dashboard**

This gives you the foundation for a **multi-tenant Customer Acquisition + Voice AI SaaS**, rather than a collection of individual voice bots.

And importantly, the acquisition module can later support not only healthcare but **real estate, financial services, home services, automotive, education, wellness, legal intake, insurance and other verticals** by changing the form schema, qualification rules, agent template and downstream integrations.

## 🧑 User — msg #26

call script desigin  to speak to customer ,understand the need and explain about the service , talk to him his mother toung , understand customer other needs as well ...align with this service and tracking each ,creating table, liking,dislinke ,time  of call, feedback,etc

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #27

Exactly. This should become a dedicated **Conversation Intelligence + Customer Discovery module**, not just a static sales script. The agent should sell the requested service while continuously learning what the customer wants, prefers, dislikes, can afford, when they want to be contacted, and what adjacent needs exist.

## 1. End-to-end outbound conversation

```text
Lead/Form
   ↓
Customer profile + campaign context
   ↓
Outbound Call
   ↓
Identity + reason for call
   ↓
Ask preferred language
   ↓
Switch to mother tongue/preferred language
   ↓
Permission to continue
   ↓
Understand primary need
   ↓
Deep discovery
   ↓
Understand pain/problem
   ↓
Current solution/provider
   ↓
Expectation
   ↓
Budget sensitivity
   ↓
Timing/urgency
   ↓
Explain ONLY relevant services
   ↓
Capture reaction
   ↓
Understand likes/dislikes
   ↓
Handle questions/objections
   ↓
Discover adjacent needs
   ↓
Cross-sell only where relevant
   ↓
Determine next best action
   ↓
Book / callback / human / nurture
   ↓
Confirm
   ↓
CRM + analytics + follow-up
```

The critical design principle is:

> **Listen → understand → confirm → explain → verify → recommend.**

Don't make the agent give a three-minute sales speech before discovering why the person is interested.

---

# 2. Call opening

For a form-generated lead, the agent already knows the context.

For example:

> "Hi Raj, I'm the virtual assistant calling from ABC Wellness. You recently requested information about our physiotherapy services. Is this a good time for a quick conversation?"

Then:

> "Before we continue, which language would you be most comfortable speaking in—English, Hindi, Punjabi, or another language?"

Store:

```text
preferred_language = Punjabi
detected_language = Punjabi
language_confidence = 0.97
language_switched = true
```

If they say:

> "Hindi chalega."

the agent should naturally continue in Hindi.

If they start mixing languages:

> "Mere shoulder mein problem hai, especially while working from home."

don't force them into pure Hindi.

Support **code-switching** naturally.

---

# 3. Language profile should become persistent customer data

Create:

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| Primary language | Hindi |
| Preferred call language | Hindi |
| Secondary language | English |
| Code switching | Yes |
| Preferred SMS language | English |
| Preferred email language | English |
| Accent/dialect | optional |
| Language confidence | 94% |
| Interpreter/human required | No |

Next call:

> "Would you prefer that we continue in Hindi?"

You don't need to rediscover the preference every time.

---

# 4. Customer discovery script

Instead of asking twenty survey questions, make them conversational.

### Need

> "What made you interested in this service?"

Capture:

`primary_need`

### Problem

> "What is the biggest challenge you're trying to solve?"

Capture:

`pain_point`

### Current situation

> "Are you currently using any similar service?"

Capture:

`current_solution`

### Dissatisfaction

> "Is there anything about the current option that isn't working well for you?"

Capture:

`current_solution_dislike`

### Desired outcome

> "What would make this service really useful for you?"

Capture:

`desired_outcome`

### Priority

> "What's most important to you—quality, convenience, price, timing, location, or something else?"

Capture ranked preferences.

### Timing

> "When are you hoping to get started?"

Capture:

`urgency`

### Price sensitivity

Don't immediately ask:

> "What's your budget?"

A better discovery question is:

> "When choosing a service like this, how important is price compared with quality, convenience and availability?"

That gives you much richer customer psychology.

---

# 5. Build a customer preference matrix automatically

Suppose the customer says:

> "I like the program, but $120 is too expensive. I would prefer an evening online class, maybe three times per week."

The LLM should extract:

| Attribute | Value | Sentiment | Strength |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Service | Program | 👍 | Medium |
| Price | $120 | 👎 | Strong |
| Delivery | Online | 👍 | Strong |
| Time | Evening | 👍 | Strong |
| Frequency | 3× weekly | 👍 | Medium |
| Quality | Important | 👍 | High |

This is extremely valuable.

You're turning **unstructured voice conversations → structured market-research data**.

---

# 6. Likes/dislikes should be first-class entities

Create separate tables.

### `customer_preference`

| Customer | Category | Attribute | Preference | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| C001 | Price | <$80 | Like | +4 |
| C001 | Delivery | Online | Like | +5 |
| C001 | Schedule | Evening | Like | +5 |
| C001 | Schedule | Morning | Dislike | -4 |
| C001 | Commitment | Annual | Dislike | -5 |

Don't store everything in one giant transcript.

The transcript is evidence.

The structured tables are intelligence.

---

# 7. Discover "other needs"

This is where your system can become substantially smarter than a normal voice bot.

Near the end:

> "Besides the service we discussed, is there anything else you're looking for that we might be able to help with?"

Customer:

> "Actually my mother is looking for something gentle because she has difficulty with regular classes."

Extract:

```text
OTHER_NEED

Need: senior-friendly program
For: family member
Interest: high
Urgency: medium
Follow-up required: yes
```

Don't immediately hard-sell.

The system searches the service catalog:

```text
Customer Need
      ↓
Embedding / classification
      ↓
Service Catalog
      ↓
Matching Engine
      ↓
Candidate Services
      ↓
Eligibility/business rules
      ↓
Recommendation
```

If there is a genuine match:

> "We do have a gentler program designed for older adults. Would you like me to give you a quick overview?"

That feels helpful rather than aggressive.

---

# 8. Need → Service matching table

Build a reusable catalog:

| Customer need | Service | Match |
|---|---|---:|
| Stress | Meditation | 92% |
| Flexibility | Yoga | 95% |
| Senior activity | Senior Yoga | 96% |
| Workplace wellness | Corporate Yoga | 93% |
| Children | Kids Yoga | 98% |
| Social/fun activity | Laughter Yoga | 88% |
| Relaxation | Meditation/Breathwork | 94% |
| Online convenience | Online program | 97% |

For another business, replace the catalog.

The **matching engine remains the same**.

---

# 9. Call timing intelligence

You specifically mentioned tracking time. I would go much further.

Store:

```text
call_date
call_start_time
call_end_time
call_duration

customer_timezone

day_of_week

attempt_number

answered
answer_latency

conversation_duration

best_contact_day
best_contact_time

requested_callback_time

customer_busy
customer_rushed

conversion
appointment_booked
```

After enough calls you can discover patterns such as:

**Monday 9 AM**

800 calls → 19% connect → 4% conversion

versus

**Thursday 6 PM**

700 calls → 47% connect → 14% conversion.

Now your AI can learn:

> Thursday evening is substantially more effective for this customer segment.

---

# 10. Customer feedback model

During and after calls capture:

| Dimension | Example |
|---|---|
| Overall interest | High |
| Sentiment | Positive |
| Price reaction | Negative |
| Service reaction | Positive |
| Trust | Medium |
| Convenience | Positive |
| Location | Neutral |
| Timing | Negative |
| Quality perception | High |
| Objection | Price |
| Unanswered question | Weekend availability |
| Competitor mentioned | XYZ |
| Purchase probability | 72% |
| Next action | Callback |
| Preferred callback | Saturday 11 AM |

---

# 11. Objection tracking

Create an `objection` table.

Common categories:

**Price**

"Too expensive."

**Trust**

"I've never heard of your company."

**Timing**

"I don't have time."

**Location**

"Too far."

**Need**

"I don't think I need it."

**Competition**

"I already use another provider."

**Family approval**

"I need to ask my spouse."

**Decision delay**

"I'll think about it."

**Channel**

"Just email me."

**AI**

"I don't want to speak with a bot."

Every objection becomes measurable.

---

# 12. Don't treat a dislike as a rejection

This distinction is extremely important.

Customer:

> "I don't like the price."

doesn't necessarily mean:

**Customer dislikes service.**

Represent it correctly:

```text
service_interest = HIGH
price_sentiment = NEGATIVE
timing_sentiment = POSITIVE
brand_sentiment = POSITIVE
purchase_intent = MEDIUM
```

Then the next-best-action engine could recommend:

**Different package**

rather than:

**Close lead — lost.**

---

# 13. Competitor intelligence

If customer says:

> "XYZ gives me this for $60."

Capture:

```text
competitor = XYZ
competitor_price = 60
competitor_service = ...
competitor_like = price
competitor_dislike = schedule
switching_intent = medium
```

Across 5,000 conversations you could discover:

| Competitor | Mentions | Main reason customers like them | Main complaint |
|---|---:|---|---|
| A | 632 | Price | Support |
| B | 419 | Quality | Cost |
| C | 281 | Location | Availability |

Your Voice AI platform has now become a **continuous market-research engine**.

---

# 14. Conversation-state engine

Don't use one huge prompt.

Build states:

```text
OPEN
 ↓
IDENTIFY
 ↓
LANGUAGE
 ↓
PERMISSION
 ↓
PRIMARY_NEED
 ↓
DISCOVERY
 ↓
PAIN_POINT
 ↓
PREFERENCE
 ↓
SERVICE_EXPLANATION
 ↓
REACTION
 ↓
OBJECTION
 ↓
OTHER_NEEDS
 ↓
SERVICE_MATCHING
 ↓
CTA
 ↓
NEXT_ACTION
 ↓
CONFIRM
 ↓
CLOSE
```

Allow the LLM to converse naturally **inside controlled states**.

That's much safer than giving the model complete freedom.

---

# 15. Customer 360 table

Your final record could look like this:

| Dimension | Customer value |
|---|---|
| Lead | L-10282 |
| Source | Instagram |
| Campaign | Summer-26 |
| Preferred language | Hindi |
| Primary need | Yoga |
| Secondary need | Meditation |
| Other need | Senior yoga for mother |
| Interest | High |
| Preferred delivery | Online |
| Preferred day | Weekend |
| Preferred time | Evening |
| Price sensitivity | High |
| Quality importance | High |
| Main like | Instructor |
| Main dislike | Price |
| Objection | Monthly cost |
| Competitor | ABC Yoga |
| Sentiment | Positive |
| Trust | Medium |
| Intent | 78/100 |
| Call result | Interested |
| Appointment | Trial booked |
| Callback | No |
| DNC | No |

---

# 16. Separate customer, call and feedback tables

Don't put everything in `lead`.

I would use approximately:

```text
CUSTOMER
LEAD
CONSENT
CAMPAIGN
CALL
CALL_ATTEMPT
TRANSCRIPT
CONVERSATION_TURN
LANGUAGE
CUSTOMER_NEED
CUSTOMER_PREFERENCE
LIKE
DISLIKE
FEEDBACK
SENTIMENT
OBJECTION
COMPETITOR_MENTION
SERVICE_INTEREST
SERVICE_MATCH
QUESTION
AGENT_RESPONSE
CALL_OUTCOME
APPOINTMENT
CALLBACK
FOLLOW_UP
DNC
ESCALATION
AGENT_QA
CONVERSION
ATTRIBUTION
```

This gives you a proper analytical model.

---

# 17. Turn-level tracking is even more powerful

For each important exchange:

| Turn | Speaker | Topic | Intent | Sentiment | Need | Like/Dislike |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agent | Opening | Permission | Neutral | — | — |
| 2 | Customer | Language | Preference | Positive | Hindi | Like |
| 5 | Customer | Requirement | Discovery | Neutral | Yoga | — |
| 8 | Customer | Price | Objection | Negative | — | Dislike |
| 12 | Customer | Schedule | Preference | Positive | Evening | Like |
| 16 | Customer | Family | New need | Positive | Senior yoga | — |

You can then reconstruct **why** the customer converted or didn't.

---

# 18. AI-generated post-call intelligence

Immediately after each call:

```text
CALL
 ↓
Transcript
 ↓
Structured Extraction
 ↓
Summary
 ↓
Need Extraction
 ↓
Preference Extraction
 ↓
Like/Dislike
 ↓
Objection
 ↓
Sentiment
 ↓
Competitor Extraction
 ↓
Purchase Intent
 ↓
Next Best Action
 ↓
CRM Update
 ↓
Analytics
```

Example output:

> **Primary need:** Online yoga  
> **Secondary need:** Stress reduction  
> **Additional opportunity:** Senior yoga for mother  
> **Main positive:** Instructor experience  
> **Main objection:** Price  
> **Preferred schedule:** Tue/Thu evenings  
> **Language:** Hindi-English mixed  
> **Purchase intent:** High  
> **Recommended action:** Offer trial class  
> **Follow-up:** Thursday after 6 PM

---

# 19. Then learn across all customers

This is where the architecture becomes powerful.

Imagine **10,000 calls**.

Your dashboard can answer:

**What do customers want most?**

**What do they dislike most?**

**Which service gets most interest?**

**Which requested service don't we currently offer?**

**Which competitor is mentioned most?**

**What price creates resistance?**

**Which languages convert best?**

**Which campaign brings highest-quality leads?**

**What call time works best?**

**Which agent script converts best?**

**Which objection causes the most losses?**

**Which customer needs are increasing?**

**Which new service should the company launch?**

That is much bigger than outbound calling.

You are effectively building:

### **Customer Acquisition + Voice AI + Voice-of-Customer + Market Intelligence + Next-Best-Action**

on top of **Retell / Vapi / Bolna / LiveKit / Ultravox / Sarvam**.

The voice provider should be replaceable. **Your customer intelligence, consent history, service catalog, conversation states, preference model, QA data and market-learning dataset are the strategic assets.**

## 🧑 User — msg #28

what other feature m issing for outbuund call, tracking,monitoring,security,govrancece, AI , repritng,scoring, etc ,resai,expai,govai,riskai,etc

---

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #29

Yes. Quite a lot is still missing if the goal is an **enterprise-grade outbound Voice AI/customer-acquisition platform**. I would expand the architecture beyond calling into roughly **20 control planes**.

## Master feature architecture

| # | Module | Important capabilities | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **LeadAI** | Capture, validate, dedupe, enrich, source attribution | 🔴 |
| 2 | **ConsentAI** | Consent evidence, channel permission, withdrawal, DNC | 🔴 |
| 3 | **SegmentAI** | Customer segmentation, persona, cohorts | 🔴 |
| 4 | **ScoreAI** | Lead score, intent score, propensity, priority | 🔴 |
| 5 | **CallAI** | Inbound/outbound calls, campaigns, retries | 🔴 |
| 6 | **TalkAI** | Dialogue, language, code-switching, personalization | 🔴 |
| 7 | **NeedAI** | Explicit + implicit need discovery | 🔴 |
| 8 | **RecommendAI** | Need → service/product matching | 🔴 |
| 9 | **NextAI** | Next-best-action/offer/channel/time | 🔴 |
| 10 | **QualityAI** | Conversation and technical quality evaluation | 🔴 |
| 11 | **RiskAI** | Operational, AI, customer, security and compliance risk | 🔴 |
| 12 | **ResponsibleAI** | Fairness, transparency, explainability, human oversight | 🔴 |
| 13 | **ExplainAI** | Why lead scored/recommended/routed | 🔴 |
| 14 | **GovernAI** | Policies, models, prompts, approvals, auditability | 🔴 |
| 15 | **SecureAI** | Identity, access, secrets, data/AI security | 🔴 |
| 16 | **ObserveAI** | Logs, metrics, traces, recordings, incidents | 🔴 |
| 17 | **ReportAI** | Operational/business/AI/compliance reporting | 🔴 |
| 18 | **ExperimentAI** | A/B testing of prompts, offers, voices and timing | 🟠 |
| 19 | **CostAI** | Cost/minute, lead, booking, conversion + budgets | 🔴 |
| 20 | **MarketAI** | Voice-of-customer, competitor and unmet-need intelligence | 🟠 |

But underneath these labels there are several capabilities that are easy to miss.

### Outbound campaign controls

You need campaign scheduling, timezone-aware calling, holiday calendars, call windows, concurrency, rate limits, retry rules, contact-frequency caps, number pools, caller-ID management, local presence where appropriate, voicemail handling, answering-machine detection, callback scheduling, campaign pause/kill switch, suppression lists, campaign prioritization and budget limits.

One especially important capability is a **pre-call eligibility engine**:

```text
Lead
 ↓
Valid phone?
 ↓
Consent/authority?
 ↓
DNC?
 ↓
Suppression?
 ↓
Correct jurisdiction?
 ↓
Allowed calling time?
 ↓
Frequency cap?
 ↓
Existing complaint?
 ↓
Already converted?
 ↓
Risk restriction?
 ↓
CALL / DON'T CALL
```

No LLM should be able to bypass this engine.

### Customer intelligence

Beyond likes/dislikes, track explicit needs, inferred needs, unmet needs, emerging needs, urgency, budget sensitivity, quality sensitivity, trust, brand perception, preferred language, preferred channel, preferred call time, decision criteria, decision-maker status, competitor usage, switching reason, churn risk, purchase intent, emotional state, objections and requested products you don't currently offer.

That enables **NeedAI → RecommendAI → NextAI**.

### Much richer scoring

Don't create one mysterious `lead_score = 82`.

Use a scorecard:

| Score | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Lead Score | Overall lead quality |
| Intent Score | Likelihood they genuinely want service |
| Need Score | Strength of identified requirement |
| Fit Score | Match between customer and offering |
| Engagement Score | Interaction level |
| Urgency Score | How soon they need it |
| Trust Score | Confidence in company/service |
| Price Sensitivity | Resistance to price |
| Conversion Score | Probability of conversion |
| Appointment Score | Probability of booking |
| Show Score | Probability of attending |
| Churn Score | Probability of leaving |
| Upsell Score | Additional-service opportunity |
| Competitor Risk | Probability of choosing competitor |
| Complaint Risk | Likelihood of dissatisfaction |
| AI Confidence | Confidence in extracted/inferred information |
| Call Quality | Technical + conversation quality |
| Compliance Risk | Regulatory/contact risk |

And store **reason codes** with every score.

Instead of:

> Conversion = 78%

store:

> Conversion 78% because high service interest + requested callback + acceptable schedule − strong price objection.

That leads directly into **ExplainAI**.

## ExplainAI

You need explanations for more than models.

Explain:

**Why was this customer called?**  
**Why at this time?**  
**Why was this offer recommended?**  
**Why was lead score 82?**  
**Why did AI classify sentiment as negative?**  
**Why did AI transfer to human?**  
**Why was a call blocked?**  
**Why did the campaign select this customer?**

Keep:

```text
decision_id
customer_id
model/version
input_features
decision
confidence
reason_codes
explanation
policy_applied
timestamp
```

This gives you decision provenance.

## ResponsibleAI

For outbound AI, Responsible AI should include fairness, transparency, privacy, explainability, safety, accountability, human oversight and contestability.

A critical requirement:

**language/accent ≠ customer value.**

Monitor whether conversion recommendations or prioritization differ unfairly across appropriate evaluation groups. Be especially careful not to infer sensitive characteristics from speech and then use them for marketing decisions.

Also tell callers when they're interacting with AI where required/appropriate rather than designing the system to impersonate a human.

## GovernAI

Govern much more than models:

**LLM registry**  
**STT/TTS registry**  
**Prompt registry**  
**Agent registry**  
**Tool registry**  
**Knowledge-base registry**  
**Dataset registry**  
**Campaign registry**  
**Policy registry**  
**Risk registry**

Each should have:

`owner → version → status → approval → deployment → change history → rollback`.

For example:

```text
Prompt v17
 ↓
Development
 ↓
Automated QA
 ↓
Safety evaluation
 ↓
Business approval
 ↓
Compliance approval where required
 ↓
Staging
 ↓
Canary
 ↓
Production
 ↓
Continuous monitoring
```

This is particularly important when you have hundreds of agents.

## RiskAI

Create an enterprise AI risk register.

| Risk domain | Example |
|---|---|
| Hallucination | Agent invents service/price |
| Transaction | Incorrect appointment |
| Customer | Excessive calls |
| Reputation | Offensive/inappropriate response |
| Privacy | PII/PHI disclosure |
| Security | Prompt injection |
| Compliance | Calling prohibited contact |
| Fairness | Biased targeting/scoring |
| Model | Model behavior changes |
| Vendor | Voice provider outage |
| Integration | CRM/calendar unavailable |
| Financial | Runaway campaign costs |
| Fraud | Fake leads / abuse |
| Operational | Human transfer unavailable |
| Data | Incorrect/stale customer information |

For each:

**Likelihood × Impact × Detectability → inherent risk → controls → residual risk → owner → review date.**

And introduce automatic **kill switches** for critical thresholds.

## SecureAI

This needs its own architecture.

**IAM/RBAC/ABAC**  
**SSO/MFA**  
**service identities**  
**API authentication**  
**OAuth**  
**secrets vault**  
**encryption**  
**key rotation**  
**network segmentation**  
**PII/PHI masking**  
**recording controls**  
**data minimization**  
**retention/deletion**  
**tenant isolation**  
**prompt-injection defense**  
**tool authorization**  
**API allowlisting**  
**rate limiting**  
**fraud detection**  
**immutable audit trail**

One critical pattern is:

**LLM requests action → Policy Engine → Authorization → Tool Gateway → Business API**

not:

**LLM → database directly.**

## ObserveAI

You need three levels of observability.

**Technical:** CPU/GPU, WebRTC/SIP, packet loss, jitter, STT latency, LLM latency, TTS latency, API latency, P50/P95/P99, error rate, dropped calls.

**AI:** hallucination, confidence, grounding, intent accuracy, entity accuracy, tool-selection accuracy, unsafe response rate, language accuracy.

**Business:** leads, calls, connects, qualified leads, appointments, conversions, revenue, CAC, ROI.

The killer feature is **one distributed Call Trace**:

```text
CALL-98761

Telephony
  ↓ 120ms
VAD
  ↓
STT
  ↓ 280ms
LLM
  ↓ 510ms
Tool decision
  ↓
CRM API
  ↓ 190ms
Calendar API
  ↓ 320ms
TTS
  ↓ 210ms
Customer
```

Click a bad call and see exactly where it failed.

## QualityAI

Create automated conversation evaluation.

Every call gets scores for:

**audio quality + understanding + naturalness + relevance + correctness + grounding + politeness + empathy + interruption handling + tool accuracy + policy compliance + task completion + outcome.**

Then:

`Overall Voice Quality Score = weighted dimensions`

But retain the individual dimensions; one composite number alone can hide critical safety failures.

Create a **Golden Conversation Dataset** and replay it whenever you change:

**LLM / STT / TTS / prompt / tool / workflow / RAG / voice provider / language model.**

## ExperimentAI

This is another missing piece.

Test:

**Prompt A vs B**  
**Male/female/different voice options where appropriate**  
**Opening A vs B**  
**30-sec vs 60-sec discovery**  
**Offer A vs B**  
**Call morning vs evening**  
**English vs preferred-language experience**  
**Immediate vs requested-time callback**

Then measure:

`Connect → Engagement → Qualification → Appointment → Show → Conversion`

Don't optimize simply for "longer calls." A 90-second call producing an appointment can be better than a 10-minute conversation.

## ReportAI

You actually need multiple reporting suites.

**Executive:** leads, conversions, revenue, CAC, ROI, campaign performance.

**Sales:** hot leads, callbacks, objections, pipeline, conversion probability.

**Marketing:** source, campaign, creative, audience, CPL, CAC, attribution.

**Customer intelligence:** likes, dislikes, requested features, unmet needs, preferred times, language, sentiment.

**Voice operations:** calls, connect rate, duration, failures, voicemail, transfers.

**AI quality:** hallucinations, tool accuracy, intent/entity accuracy, confidence, regression.

**Risk/compliance:** blocked calls, consent issues, DNC events, policy violations, complaints, incidents.

**FinOps:** provider cost, STT/TTS/LLM cost, cost/call, cost/lead, cost/appointment, cost/customer.

## MarketAI — a very valuable addition

Aggregate thousands of calls into:

```text
Voice of Customer
      ↓
Need clustering
      ↓
Pain-point clustering
      ↓
Like/dislike analysis
      ↓
Objection analysis
      ↓
Competitor intelligence
      ↓
Price intelligence
      ↓
Unmet-needs detection
      ↓
Trend detection
      ↓
New service opportunities
```

Now management can ask:

> "What are customers asking for that we don't sell?"

and receive an evidence-backed answer from actual conversations.

## A few more modules I would add

Beyond your **ResAI / ExpAI / GovAI / RiskAI** idea, I would add:

**PrivacyAI** — consent, minimization, retention, deletion, PII/PHI.

**ComplianceAI** — jurisdiction/rule engine, DNC, campaign eligibility.

**SafetyAI** — unsafe conversation detection and escalation.

**AuditAI** — immutable decision/call/change trail.

**FraudAI** — fake leads, bot attacks, suspicious calling patterns.

**PolicyAI** — machine-enforceable business/AI policies.

**DriftAI** — conversation/model/data/quality drift.

**IncidentAI** — detection → triage → investigation → remediation → RCA/CAPA.

**HumanAI** — human approval, transfer, review and override.

**TestAI** — synthetic callers, regression, load, chaos and adversarial testing.

**DataAI** — lineage, quality, catalog, ownership and master customer data.

**FinAI** — cost optimization and provider routing.

**RouteAI** — dynamically choose Retell/Vapi/Bolna/LiveKit/Ultravox/Sarvam/STT/TTS/LLM based on language, quality, geography, cost and availability.

That last one is particularly interesting.

Instead of locking the platform to one provider:

```text
                    RouteAI
                       ↓
       ┌───────────────┼──────────────┐
       ↓               ↓              ↓
English/Canada     Hindi/India      Failover
       ↓               ↓              ↓
LiveKit/Retell      Sarvam        Alternative
       ↓               ↓              ↓
   best STT          Sarvam STT      Backup
       ↓
   best LLM
       ↓
   best TTS
```

Then your platform optimizes for **quality + trust + latency + availability + compliance + cost**, not vendor loyalty.

At that point, what you are designing is no longer merely an outbound-call system. It becomes an **AI Customer Acquisition & Conversation Intelligence Platform** with acquisition, Voice AI, CRM, experimentation, QA, Responsible AI, Explainable AI, AI governance, security, risk, observability, FinOps and market intelligence all operating as one control system.

# C. Master edge-case bank

| Edge case | Risk | Required response |
|---|---|---|
| Customer says DNC | Compliance | Immediately suppress |
| Wrong person answers | Privacy | Don't disclose sensitive context |
| Customer is busy | UX | Capture callback time |
| Customer interrupts | Conversation | Barge-in + state repair |
| Silence | UX | Reprompt → graceful close |
| Noise | STT | Denoise/reconfirm |
| Wrong transcription | Transaction | Confirm critical fields |
| Date ambiguity | Booking | Explicit confirmation |
| Duplicate booking | Business | Idempotency |
| Calendar unavailable | Reliability | Callback/human/fallback |
| CRM unavailable | Integration | Queue durable write |
| LLM unavailable | AI | fallback model |
| STT unavailable | Voice | fallback provider |
| TTS unavailable | Voice | fallback voice |
| Telephony failure | Telecom | alternate provider |
| Customer angry | Reputation | de-escalate/transfer |
| Medical/legal question | Safety | abstain/escalate |
| Prompt injection | Security | tool isolation/policy |
| Customer changes language | UX | dynamic language |
| Price objection | Sales | alternative option |
| Competitor mentioned | Intelligence | capture, don't attack |
| Customer requests nonexistent service | Hallucination | state unavailable |
| Multiple people speaking | STT | clarification |
| Bot/fraud caller | Cost | fraud detection |
| Runaway campaign | Financial | budget kill switch |
| Model update degrades results | AI | regression gate/rollback |
| Bad prompt deployed | Quality | version + rollback |
| Provider outage | Reliability | RouteAI failover |
| Transcript contains PII | Privacy | masking/redaction |
| Recording consent withdrawn | Privacy | stop recording/process policy |
| Customer already converted | CX | suppress sales call |

# E. Definition of Done for every module

Do not mark a module complete merely because the API works.

A module is complete only when:

```text
Functional requirements passed
+
Unit tests passed
+
Integration tests passed
+
Security tests passed
+
Performance tests passed
+
Failure cases tested
+
Observability implemented
+
Audit implemented
+
Documentation completed
+
Runbook completed
+
Rollback tested
+
Business UAT passed
+
Production KPI established
```

---

# F. Recommended MVP → Enterprise progression

| Stage | What to build |
|---|---|
| **MVP** | Form → Lead → Consent → Campaign → Voice → Appointment → CRM |
| **V1** | multilingual + NeedAI + ScoreAI + QA + dashboards |
| **V2** | RecommendAI + NextAI + ExplainAI + MarketAI |
| **V3** | RiskAI + ResAI + GovernAI + advanced security |
| **V4** | RouteAI + multiple providers + automated failover |
| **V5** | ExperimentAI + DriftAI + advanced FinAI |
| **Enterprise** | Multi-tenant + 100–1,000+ agents + full control plane |

The most important architectural decision is to keep **customer acquisition, customer intelligence, consent, campaign orchestration, QA, scoring, governance, reporting and data ownership in your platform**, while treating **Retell/Vapi/Bolna/LiveKit/Ultravox/Sarvam as replaceable execution engines**. That design gives you much more control over quality, cost, compliance, vendor lock-in and future product differentiation. memcite

## Phase 0 — Architecture, Requirements, Governance Baseline

This phase creates the foundation for everything else. Do this before choosing Retell, Vapi, Bolna, LiveKit, Sarvam, or Ultravox as the primary provider.

### 0.1 Objectives

The outputs of Phase 0 should be:

| Area | Deliverable |
|---|---|
| Business | Business requirements |
| Customer | Customer journey |
| Calling | Inbound/outbound use cases |
| AI | AI capability requirements |
| Voice | STT/TTS/realtime requirements |
| Integration | API/integration inventory |
| Data | Canonical data model |
| Security | Security architecture |
| Privacy | Privacy/data-classification model |
| Governance | AI governance framework |
| Risk | Initial AI/operational risk register |
| Quality | QA/evaluation strategy |
| NFR | Performance, availability, scalability targets |
| Architecture | Target solution architecture |
| Vendors | Provider evaluation framework |
| Delivery | Backlog, releases and milestones |


# 0.6 Non-functional requirements

These are critical for voice.

### Performance

Example targets:

| Metric | Initial target |
|---|---:|
| Voice response latency P50 | <800 ms |
| Voice response latency P95 | <1.5 sec |
| API latency P95 | <500 ms |
| Booking API P95 | <2 sec |
| Call setup | <5 sec |
| Dashboard query P95 | <3 sec |

Exact values should be benchmarked before production.

### Availability

Start with:

**99.9% platform availability**

Critical call components should have failover strategies.

### Scalability

Design capacity stages:

```text
Stage 1: 10 concurrent calls
Stage 2: 100
Stage 3: 500
Stage 4: 1,000
Stage 5: 10,000+
```

Don't engineer for 10,000 on day one, but don't architect yourself into a dead end.

---

# 0.7 Data classification

Classify everything before implementation.

| Classification | Example |
|---|---|
| Public | Service descriptions |
| Internal | Campaign configuration |
| Confidential | Lead information |
| PII | Name/email/phone |
| Sensitive | Financial/account information |
| PHI | Healthcare information where applicable |
| Restricted | Authentication secrets |

Then establish:

**Where can this data be stored?**

**Who can access it?**

**How long?**

**Can it enter an LLM?**

**Can it appear in logs?**

**Can it be recorded?**

# 0.8 Canonical data architecture

Start with the major domains:

```text
Customer
Lead
Consent
Preference
Need
Campaign
Call
Conversation
Service
Appointment
Feedback
Score
Decision
Risk
Quality
Audit
Cost
```

Every provider must map into this model.

For example, Retell may call something `call_id`, Vapi something slightly different.

Internally:

```text
voice_call_id
provider_call_id
provider
```

This prevents provider-specific schemas from infecting the whole platform.

# 0.14 Quality gates

Before any platform gets selected:

### Speech

STT critical-entity accuracy acceptable.

### Conversation

Customer intent correctly understood.

### Transaction

Appointment fields 100% verified before commitment.

### Safety

No prohibited advice.

### Compliance

DNC/consent policies obeyed.

### Technical

Latency inside acceptable threshold.

### Reliability

Failures gracefully handled.

### Cost

Cost/successful outcome inside target.

# 0.15 Edge cases to design before coding

A good architecture review should answer all of these:

**What if Retell is down?**

**What if Twilio is down?**

**What if LLM times out?**

**What if STT hears the wrong name?**

**What if caller changes language?**

**What if caller interrupts during booking?**

**What if appointment succeeds but API response fails?**

**What if two workers process the same call event?**

**What if customer withdraws consent while campaign queue already contains them?**

**What if CRM is unavailable?**

**What if call recording contains PHI?**

**What if model version changes overnight?**

**What if the prompt suddenly causes conversion to fall 20%?**

Each should have:

```text
Detection
→ fallback
→ recovery
→ logging
→ customer response
→ alert
→ incident
→ regression test
```

## Phase 1 — Customer Acquisition + Smart Form + Attribution + Lead Capture

This phase builds the full front door for outbound Voice AI. The goal is not merely “collect a name and phone number.” It should capture **source, intent, language, service need, consent, preferred contact method, preferred call time, and campaign context**, then create a clean lead ready for scoring and outbound calling.

### 1.1 Target flow

```text
Traffic Source
   ↓
Landing Page
   ↓
Smart Form
   ↓
Validation
   ↓
Consent Capture
   ↓
Bot/Fraud Check
   ↓
Lead API
   ↓
Deduplication
   ↓
Customer Match/Create
   ↓
Lead Create
   ↓
UTM Attribution
   ↓
Preference Capture
   ↓
Campaign Eligibility
   ↓
Lead Score Queue
   ↓
Outbound Call Queue
```

---

## 1.2 Acquisition sources

Support these from the beginning:

| Source | Capture method |
|---|---|
| Website | Embedded form |
| Google Ads | Landing page / lead form |
| Facebook | Meta Lead Ads |
| Instagram | Link/form |
| LinkedIn | Lead Gen Form |
| TikTok | Lead form |
| YouTube | CTA landing page |
| QR code | Campaign-specific URL |
| Email | Tracked CTA |
| SMS | Short URL |
| WhatsApp | Form or conversational intake |
| Referral | Referral code/form |
| Event | Registration form |
| Sales staff | Manual entry |
| Existing CRM | API |
| Partner | API/webhook |
| CSV | Controlled import |

Every source must map to the same canonical lead model.

# 1.3 Landing-page architecture

Recommended:

**Next.js + React**

Create templates rather than separate websites.

Example:

```text
/templates/
    healthcare/
    yoga/
    real-estate/
    home-services/
    education/
```

Then dynamically configure:

```text
tenant
brand
campaign
service
language
location
form
CTA
```

URL example:

```text
https://example.com/physio/free-consultation
?utm_source=instagram
&utm_medium=paid_social
&utm_campaign=calgary_august
&utm_content=video_03
```

---

# 1.4 Smart form design

Do not ask 20 questions on page one.

Use progressive collection.

### Step 1 — Basic identity

```text
First name
Last name
Phone
Email
```

### Step 2 — Need

```text
What service are you interested in?

Physiotherapy
Chiropractic
Massage
ENT
Dental
Yoga
Other
```

### Step 3 — Intent

```text
What would you like to do?

Book appointment
Get more information
Talk to someone
Ask about pricing
Check availability
Request callback
Other
```

### Step 4 — Contact preference

```text
Preferred communication:
Phone
SMS
Email
WhatsApp
```

### Step 5 — Call timing

```text
Call me:
Now
Morning
Afternoon
Evening
Specific date/time
```

### Step 6 — Language

```text
Preferred language:
English
French
Hindi
Punjabi
Tamil
Telugu
Other
```

### Step 7 — Consent

Separate consent checkboxes where legally/operationally appropriate:

```text
I agree to be contacted regarding this request.

I agree to receive marketing communications.

I agree to receive SMS messages.
```

Do not bundle everything into one ambiguous checkbox.

---

# 1.5 Dynamic form logic

The form should adapt.

Example:

Customer chooses:

**Book appointment**

Then show:

```text
Preferred location
Preferred date
Preferred time
Provider preference
```

Customer chooses:

**Pricing**

Then show:

```text
Which service?
Individual/family/corporate?
Preferred frequency?
```

Customer chooses:

**Corporate wellness**

Show:

```text
Company name
Employee count
Location
Program interest
Decision timeline
```

This increases data quality without making every form long.

# 1.7 Attribution schema

Store:

```text
utm_source

gclid
```

Why?

Because later you want to answer:

> Which Instagram creative generated customers that actually booked appointments?

Not simply:

# 1.8 API design

Core endpoint:

```text
POST /api/v1/leads
```

Request:

```json
{
  "first_name": "Raj",
  "email": "raj@example.com",
  "phone": "+14035551234",
  "service_interest": "physiotherapy",
  "intent": "book_appointment",
  "preferred_language": "hindi",
  "preferred_channel": "phone",
  "utm_source": "instagram"
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "lead_id": "L-100012",
  "customer_id": "C-88291",
  "status": "created",
  "call_eligible": true
}
```

Other APIs:

```text
GET  /leads/{id}
PATCH /leads/{id}
POST /leads/{id}/consent
POST /leads/{id}/preferences
POST /leads/{id}/validate
POST /leads/{id}/qualify
```

---

# 1.9 Validation pipeline

Immediately after submission:

```text
Schema validation
   ↓
Required fields
   ↓
Email syntax
   ↓
Phone normalization
   ↓
Phone validity
   ↓
Country detection
   ↓
Consent validation
   ↓
Spam/bot assessment
   ↓
Duplicate detection
   ↓
Customer identity matching
```

---

# 1.10 Phone normalization

Always convert:

```text
4035551234
(403) 555-1234
403-555-1234
+1 403 555 1234
```

to:

```text
+14035551234
```

E.164 internally.

Tools:

`libphonenumber`

or equivalent library.

---

# 1.11 Email validation

Levels:

### L1

Syntax validation.

### L2

Domain exists.

### L3

Disposable-domain detection.

### L4

Optional third-party mailbox validation.

Don't block legitimate leads purely because an external validator is uncertain.

---

# 1.12 Deduplication strategy

Match using multiple attributes.

Example rules:

```text
Exact external customer ID
        ↓
Exact normalized phone
        ↓
Exact normalized email
        ↓
Phone + surname
        ↓
Email + surname
        ↓
Probabilistic identity match
```

Return:

```text
NEW_CUSTOMER
EXISTING_CUSTOMER
POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE
MANUAL_REVIEW
```

---

# 1.13 Critical edge case — shared household phone

Suppose:

```text
Deepa +1...
Praveen +1...
```

same number.

Don't merge solely on phone.

Use:

```text
phone
+ name
+ email
+ relationship/context
```

and maintain multiple contacts when required.

---

# 1.14 Consent record

Store evidence independently from the lead.

Example:

```text
consent_id
customer_id
purpose = CALLBACK
channel = PHONE
status = GRANTED
source = WEB_FORM
text_version = V3
timestamp
ip_metadata
campaign
```

Why independent?

Because consent changes over time.

---

# 1.15 Bot and fraud protection

Protect against:

bot-generated leads  
competitor spam  
fake phone numbers  
automated form attacks  
lead-farming abuse.

Tools:

Cloudflare Turnstile  
reCAPTCHA where appropriate  
rate limiting  
device/IP signals  
honeypot fields.

Don't rely entirely on CAPTCHA.

---

# 1.16 Lead lifecycle

```text
CAPTURED
↓
VALIDATING
↓
VALID
↓
CUSTOMER_MATCHED
↓
CONSENT_VERIFIED
↓
READY_FOR_SCORING
↓
CALL_ELIGIBLE
```

Exception statuses:

```text
INVALID
DUPLICATE
SPAM
CONSENT_MISSING
BLOCKED
MANUAL_REVIEW
```

---

# 1.17 Event generation

Emit events after important actions.

```text
lead.submitted
lead.validated
lead.duplicate_detected
lead.created
customer.matched
consent.recorded
preference.recorded
lead.call_eligible
```

This lets downstream systems subscribe instead of tightly coupling everything.

---

# 1.18 n8n role

Useful workflow:

```text
Form
→ Webhook
→ Validation API
→ CRM
→ Slack notification
→ Email acknowledgement
→ Lead scoring queue
```

But don't put critical identity, consent, DNC and transaction integrity exclusively in n8n.

Those should live in backend services.

Suggested PostgreSQL tables:

```text
customer
```

| L001 | Instagram | paid | physio_aug | reel_04 |
| L002 | Google | search | dental_calgary | ad_17 |

```text
Revenue / campaign
```

Create reusable preference records:

# 1.27 Edge case — user refreshes after Submit

Potential problem:

duplicate submission.

Solution:

Use:

```text
submission_id
idempotency_key
```

Second submission returns existing result.

---

# 1.28 Edge case — double-click submit

Same solution:

idempotent POST.

---

# 1.29 Edge case — CRM unavailable

Do not lose lead.

Architecture:

```text
Form
→ Platform DB SUCCESS
→ Event queue
→ CRM sync async
```

If CRM fails:

```text
RETRY
→ DLQ
→ Alert
```

Lead remains safely stored.

---

# 1.30 Edge case — outbound provider unavailable

Phase 1 should not care.

It emits:

```text
lead.call_eligible
```

Later the campaign/RouteAI components decide provider.

This keeps acquisition vendor-neutral.

---

# 1.31 Edge case — customer requests immediate callback at 2 AM

Don't blindly call.

Store:

```text
requested_callback = immediate
```

then Phase 8 PolicyAI evaluates local policy/calling window.

---

# 1.32 Edge case — customer selects language provider doesn't support

Example:

```text
preferred_language = Punjabi
```

Primary provider doesn't support it well.

Later RouteAI chooses:

```text
Sarvam
or
appropriate multilingual provider
```

instead of losing the lead.

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #38

# Phase 2 — Customer 360 + CRM + MDM + Identity Resolution

Phase 1 gave us a validated lead. Phase 2 answers a harder question:

> **Who exactly is this customer, what do we already know about them, what have they asked for, what do they like/dislike, what conversations have occurred, and what is the authoritative customer record?**

This becomes the data foundation for Voice AI, NeedAI, ScoreAI, RecommendAI, NextAI, RiskAI and ReportAI.

---

## 2.1 Target architecture

```text
Website/Form ──────┐
Instagram/Meta ────┤
Google ────────────┤
LinkedIn ──────────┤
Inbound Call ──────┤
Outbound Call ─────┤
SMS/WhatsApp ──────┤
Email ─────────────┤
CRM ───────────────┤
Appointment ───────┤
Partner API ───────┘
                   ↓
            Identity Gateway
                   ↓
       Normalize + Standardize
                   ↓
             Match Engine
                   ↓
       ┌───────────┴───────────┐
       ↓                       ↓
 Existing Customer          New Customer
       ↓                       ↓
       └───────────┬───────────┘
                   ↓
              Golden Record
                   ↓
             CUSTOMER 360
                   ↓
 ┌─────────────────┼──────────────────┐
 ↓                 ↓                  ↓
Preferences       Needs          Interaction
 ↓                 ↓                  ↓
Likes           Intent              Calls
Dislikes        Services             SMS
Language        Problems             Email
Time            Other Needs          Forms
                   ↓
               AI Features
                   ↓
 NeedAI → ScoreAI → RecommendAI → NextAI
```

---

# 2.2 Don't create one huge Customer table

Separate domains.

Core entities:

```text
CUSTOMER
CONTACT_POINT
ADDRESS
IDENTITY
HOUSEHOLD
ORGANIZATION

LEAD
CONSENT
PREFERENCE
NEED
SERVICE_INTEREST

INTERACTION
CALL
MESSAGE
FORM_SUBMISSION

APPOINTMENT
PURCHASE

FEEDBACK
LIKE
DISLIKE
OBJECTION
COMPETITOR_MENTION

SCORE
DECISION
RISK
QUALITY
AUDIT
```

This will save significant redesign later.

---

# 2.3 Customer master

Example:

```text
customer_id
tenant_id

first_name
middle_name
last_name

display_name

customer_type
customer_status

preferred_language
preferred_channel

created_at
updated_at
source_system
```

Don't unnecessarily put:

phone/email/address/preferences/consent

directly into this table.

Those change independently.

---

# 2.4 Contact-point model

Create:

```text
CONTACT_POINT

contact_point_id
customer_id

type:
 PHONE
 EMAIL
 WHATSAPP
 SMS

value
normalized_value

is_primary
is_verified

verification_method
verified_at

valid_from
valid_to
```

Customer could have:

```text
Home phone
Mobile
Work phone
Personal email
Work email
WhatsApp
```

This becomes important for outbound communication.

---

# 2.5 Customer type

Support:

```text
PROSPECT
LEAD
CUSTOMER
FORMER_CUSTOMER
REFERRAL
FAMILY_MEMBER
CORPORATE_CONTACT
PARTNER
```

A customer can change lifecycle without creating another person record.

---

# 2.6 Household / relationship model

Important for your scenario where someone may ask about a service for their mother.

Don't simply put:

`other_need = senior_yoga`

Instead:

```text
CUSTOMER
   │
   └── RELATIONSHIP
          │
          └── FAMILY MEMBER
```

Example:

```text
C1001 — Raj

relationship:
MOTHER

C1092 — Mrs Kumar
```

Only create/link another identifiable person when appropriate and with proper data handling; otherwise store the need as being "for a family member" without unnecessarily collecting their identity.

---

# 2.7 Organization model

Needed later for corporate sales.

```text
ORGANIZATION

organization_id
name
industry
employee_count
location
website
```

Relationship:

```text
CUSTOMER
   ↓
works_at
   ↓
ORGANIZATION
```

Now the same platform handles:

**B2C + B2B.**

---

# 2.8 Identity resolution

Suppose you receive:

### Existing CRM

```text
Praveen Asthana
403-555-1234
abc@gmail.com
```

New Instagram form:

```text
Praveen
+1 403 555 1234
abc@gmail.com
```

Inbound voice:

> "My name is Praveen."

All should potentially map to:

```text
CUSTOMER_ID = C001
```

---

# 2.9 Identity-resolution pipeline

```text
Incoming Identity
       ↓
Normalize
       ↓
Exact Match
       ↓
Strong Match
       ↓
Fuzzy Match
       ↓
Confidence
       ↓
┌───────────────┬───────────────┐
↓               ↓               ↓
MATCH         REVIEW          CREATE
```

---

# 2.10 Matching hierarchy

### Level 1 — deterministic

Exact external customer ID.

### Level 2

Exact verified phone.

### Level 3

Exact verified email.

### Level 4

Phone + name.

### Level 5

Email + name.

### Level 6

Name + address + other signals.

### Level 7

Probabilistic/fuzzy match.

---

# 2.11 Match confidence

Example:

```text
phone exact       +50
email exact       +40
surname exact     +10
first name fuzzy  +5
address similar   +10
```

Then:

```text
95+    AUTO_MATCH

70–94  REVIEW

<70    CREATE/REVIEW
```

Tune thresholds using actual data.

---

# 2.12 Critical edge case — shared phone

Suppose:

```text
Raj Kumar
+14035550000

Priya Kumar
+14035550000
```

Do NOT merge automatically.

Phone may represent:

family  
business  
clinic  
household.

Solution:

```text
CONTACT_POINT
     ↓
CUSTOMER_CONTACT_RELATION
     ↓
multiple customers
```

---

# 2.13 Critical edge case — recycled phone number

A phone number previously belonged to another person.

Therefore:

```text
valid_from
valid_to
verification_status
```

matter.

Don't assume a phone number represents a permanent identity.

---

# 2.14 Golden Customer Record

MDM creates the authoritative representation.

Example:

```text
CUSTOMER C001

Name:
Raj Kumar

Primary Phone:
+14035551234

Primary Email:
raj@example.com

Preferred Language:
Hindi

Preferred Contact:
Phone

Preferred Call Time:
Evening

Primary Need:
Physiotherapy

Current Intent:
High

Customer Status:
Prospect
```

---

# 2.15 Survivorship rules

Suppose:

CRM says:

`Language = English`

Latest customer conversation says:

> "Please speak to me in Hindi."

Which wins?

Define source authority.

Example:

| Attribute | Preferred source |
|---|---|
| Legal/customer name | verified customer record |
| Phone | verified contact |
| Email | verified contact |
| Language | latest explicit preference |
| Call time | latest explicit preference |
| Consent | consent service |
| Need | latest confirmed conversation/form |
| Appointment | scheduling system |

Never use generic "last update wins" for everything.

```text
confidence
```

```text
Price → < $80

Channel → Phone
```

# 2.18 Need model

```text
CUSTOMER_NEED
```

```text

Physiotherapy
```

# 2.19 Explicit vs inferred needs

This distinction is critical.

Customer explicitly says:

> "I need an evening yoga class."

Store:

```text
explicit = true
confidence = 1.0
```

AI infers:

> likely interested in meditation.

Store:

```text
explicit = false
confidence = 0.63
```

Never make AI inference look like a customer-stated fact.

Identity:

```text
POST /identity/match
POST /identity/merge
POST /identity/unmerge
```

---

# 2.30 Merge capability

You need:

```text
C100
+
C982
↓
C100
```

but preserve:

```text
merge history
source IDs
audit record
old relationships
```

Never physically destroy lineage.

---

# 2.31 Unmerge

Often forgotten.

If AI/operator incorrectly merges two people:

```text
MERGE
↓
discovered error
↓
UNMERGE
```

must be supported.

This is an important MDM feature.

---

# 2.32 Storage strategy

Start:

**PostgreSQL**

Excellent for customer/transactional data.

Optional later:

**OpenSearch**

for transcript/full-text search.

**Object storage**

for recordings and large artifacts.

**Vector DB**

only where semantic retrieval actually provides value.

Don't use vector databases for basic customer master data.

---

# 2.33 Cache

Redis for:

customer-session context  
frequently accessed preferences  
rate limits  
temporary state.

Don't make Redis the system of record.

---

# 2.34 Security

Customer service requires:

RBAC  
tenant isolation  
field-level protection  
encryption  
audit  
data masking.

Example:

Sales user sees:

```text
403-***-1234
```

where full number isn't required.

---

# 2.35 Voice-agent data access

The voice agent should not receive the entire Customer 360 record.

Instead:

```text
Voice Agent
     ↓
Customer Context API
     ↓
Minimum necessary context
```

Example:

```text
first_name
preferred_language
requested_service
preferred_time
last_interaction_summary
```

Not:

every historical record.

This reduces privacy exposure and token usage.

---

# 2.36 Testing — identity

Create test scenarios:

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Exact phone + email | Match |
| Exact phone, different name | Review |
| Exact email | Match |
| Similar name only | No automatic match |
| Shared phone | Multiple candidate |
| Changed email | Match through other identity |
| Recycled number | Review |
| Duplicate CRM record | Merge candidate |
| Unicode name | Correct handling |
| Typo name | Fuzzy candidate |

---

# 2.37 Testing — MDM

Test:

Create  
update  
merge  
unmerge  
survivorship  
source priority  
conflicting values  
historical values.

---

Create synthetic personas.

### Persona A

```text
Raj Kumar
Hindi
+1...
Physiotherapy
Evening
Price sensitive
```

### Persona B

```text
Sarah Williams
English
Massage
Weekend
Quality sensitive
```

```text
Chiropractic

Multiple phone numbers
```

### Persona D

```text
Corporate HR

250 employees
B2B
```

Create 1,000+ synthetic customer records for automated testing.

# 2.39 Performance tests

Test:

100k customers  
1M customers  
10M interactions.

Queries:

Customer lookup by phone  
email  
customer ID  
timeline  
Customer 360.

Targets should be established from actual workload.

# 2.40 Edge case — customer changes preferred language

Old:

`English`

New:

> "Please call me in Punjabi."

Store historical:

```text
English
valid_to = Aug 24

Punjabi
valid_from = Aug 24
```

Next call uses Punjabi.

---

# 2.41 Edge case — contradictory preferences

Call 1:

> Evening preferred.

Call 2:

> Morning is better now.

Use:

latest explicit confirmed preference.

Keep historical data.

---

# 2.42 Edge case — AI wrongly infers preference

AI:

`price_sensitive = true`

Customer never said it.

Mark:

```text
source = AI_INFERENCE
confidence=.58
```

Do not overwrite:

```text
CUSTOMER_CONFIRMED
```

information.

---

# 2.43 Edge case — deletion request

Need workflow:

```text
Customer request
↓
Identity verification
↓
Retention/legal-policy evaluation
↓
Delete/anonymize applicable data
↓
Propagate downstream
↓
Audit completion
```

This needs to include CRM, analytics, recordings and other downstream copies as applicable.

---

# 2.44 Observability

Track:

customer creates/sec  
match rate  
duplicate rate  
manual review rate  
merge rate  
unmerge rate  
CRM sync errors  
data-quality score  
API latency.

---

Show:

### Identity

Name

location.

last touch.

### Needs

primary

### Preferences

language

delivery.

### Engagement

forms  
calls

email.

lead score

### Voice intelligence

sentiment

### Governance

DNC

Before release:

At completion:

**Canonical customer model**

**Customer 360 API**

**Identity-resolution service**

**Matching rules**

**Golden-record logic**
