## 🤖 Assistant — msg #56

# Phase 11 — NeedAI + Voice-of-Customer Intelligence

This phase turns every call, form, SMS, email, and interaction into structured **customer need intelligence**.

The objective is to answer:

> What does the customer actually need, what problem are they trying to solve, what do they value, what do they dislike, what are they not getting today, and what new service opportunities are emerging?

## 11.1 Target architecture

```text
Calls / Forms / SMS / Email / Chat
              ↓
      Conversation Extraction
              ↓
        Need Detection
              ↓
  Explicit vs Inferred Classification
              ↓
       Need Taxonomy Mapping
              ↓
      Pain / Goal / Constraint
              ↓
       Preference Extraction
              ↓
      Like / Dislike Extraction
              ↓
       Objection Extraction
              ↓
      Competitor Intelligence
              ↓
        Unmet Need Detection
              ↓
        Need Clustering
              ↓
       Trend / MarketAI
              ↓
      RecommendAI / NextAI
```

## 11.2 Need types

Do not store everything as `customer_need`.

Separate:

| Need type | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Primary Need | Main reason for inquiry | Physiotherapy |
| Secondary Need | Additional requirement | Evening appointment |
| Functional Need | Task customer wants accomplished | Book appointment |
| Emotional Need | Experience expectation | Wants reassurance/trust |
| Convenience Need | Ease/access | Near home |
| Price Need | Cost-related requirement | Under $80 |
| Language Need | Communication preference | Punjabi |
| Timing Need | Time requirement | Weekend |
| Information Need | Wants explanation | Treatment/service information |
| Support Need | Human help | Speak with receptionist |
| Future Need | Not immediate | Corporate wellness next quarter |
| Unmet Need | No current service match | Home visit |
| Adjacent Need | Related opportunity | Senior program for parent |

## 11.3 Jobs-to-be-Done model

Beyond service names, capture the **job the customer is trying to accomplish**.

Customer says:

> "I work all day, so I need something I can do after work."

Service:

`Yoga`

Actual job:

```text
Maintain wellness
without disrupting work schedule
```

Another:

> "I want somewhere close because I can't drive far."

Actual job:

```text
Access treatment conveniently
```

Store:

```text
job_id
customer_id
job_statement
context
desired_outcome
importance
satisfaction_current
source
confidence
```

This is much more useful for product design than simple service categorization.

## 11.4 Need record

Recommended structure:

```text
CUSTOMER_NEED

need_id
customer_id
interaction_id

need_category
need_subcategory

description

explicit_or_inferred

importance
urgency
confidence

beneficiary
self_or_other

current_solution
desired_outcome

status
confirmed

created_at
updated_at
```

## 11.5 Explicit vs inferred

Customer:

> "I need a Saturday morning appointment."

Store:

```text
need = weekend scheduling
source = CUSTOMER_EXPLICIT
confidence = 1.00
```

AI inference:

> Customer may prefer shorter appointments.

Store:

```text
source = AI_INFERENCE
confidence = 0.58
```

Never mix inferred and explicitly stated needs.

## 11.6 Need confirmation

High-impact inferred needs should be confirmed conversationally.

AI detects:

`possible online preference`

Agent:

> "Would online appointments be helpful for you, or do you prefer in-person?"

Then convert:

```text
AI_INFERENCE
→
CUSTOMER_CONFIRMED
```

This creates better training data as well.

## 11.7 Need hierarchy

For a healthcare/wellness implementation:

```text
Healthcare
 ├── Dental
 │    ├── New appointment
 │    ├── Cleaning
 │    ├── Consultation
 │    └── Follow-up
 │
 ├── Physiotherapy
 │    ├── Consultation
 │    ├── Follow-up
 │    ├── Availability
 │    └── Administrative information
 │
 ├── Chiropractic
 ├── ENT
 └── Massage

Wellness
 ├── Yoga
 ├── Meditation
 ├── Corporate Wellness
 ├── Senior Wellness
 └── Kids Programs

Cross-cutting
 ├── Price
 ├── Timing
 ├── Location
 ├── Language
 ├── Accessibility
 ├── Trust
 └── Human Support
```

Keep clinical diagnosis separate from administrative/service need classification.

## 11.8 Pain-point model

Need and pain are not identical.

Customer may need:

`Physiotherapy appointment`

Pain:

`No evening availability at current provider`

Store:

```text
PAIN_POINT

category
description
severity
frequency
current_solution
satisfaction
source
confidence
```

## 11.9 Pain categories

Common categories:

```text
PRICE
AVAILABILITY
WAIT_TIME
LOCATION
LANGUAGE
CONVENIENCE
QUALITY
TRUST
COMMUNICATION
BOOKING_DIFFICULTY
SUPPORT
TECHNOLOGY
PAYMENT
SERVICE_GAP
```

## 11.10 Customer goals

Capture desired outcome separately.

Example:

```text
Need:
Yoga

Pain:
Can't attend daytime classes

Goal:
Regular exercise after work

Preference:
Online evening class
```

This is much richer than:

`Interested in yoga = true`.

## 11.11 Constraint extraction

Customer decisions are frequently driven by constraints.

Capture:

```text
budget_constraint
time_constraint
location_constraint
transportation_constraint
language_constraint
availability_constraint
family_constraint
work_constraint
technology_constraint
```

Example:

> "I can only come after 6 because of work."

```text
constraint_type = TIME
constraint = after 18:00
strength = HARD
```

## 11.12 Hard vs soft constraints

Important distinction.

Customer:

> "I absolutely cannot come before 6."

```text
constraint_strength = HARD
```

Customer:

> "Evening would be better."

```text
constraint_strength = PREFERENCE
```

RecommendAI must treat these differently.

## 11.13 Likes

Capture likes about:

service, brand, provider, schedule, price, communication, location, voice interaction, previous experience.

Schema:

```text
LIKE

customer_id
interaction_id
object_type
object_id
attribute
reason
strength
confidence
```

Example:

```text
object = clinic
attribute = evening availability
strength = 5
```

## 11.14 Dislikes

Same structure:

```text
DISLIKE
```

Examples:

price, wait time, location, long contracts, pushy calls, AI voice, lack of weekend service.

## 11.15 Likes/dislikes should support chronology

Customer could dislike a feature today and later change opinion.

Maintain:

```text
valid_from
valid_to
```

Don't overwrite customer history.

## 11.16 Objection intelligence

Capture:

```text
objection_type
severity
resolved
resolution_strategy
response
outcome
```

Example:

```text
PRICE
severity = HIGH
resolved = YES
resolution = trial option
outcome = appointment booked
```

Later you can answer:

> Which objection-resolution strategy actually works?

## 11.17 Objection taxonomy

Start with:

```text
PRICE
TRUST
TIMING
LOCATION
QUALITY
CONVENIENCE
CONTRACT
COMPETITOR
NO_NEED
NOT_READY
FAMILY_DECISION
HUMAN_PREFERENCE
AI_RESISTANCE
PAYMENT
OTHER
```

## 11.18 Competitor intelligence

Capture only what the customer actually says.

```text
COMPETITOR_MENTION

competitor_name
service
price_mentioned
customer_like
customer_dislike
switching_reason
switching_intent
confidence
```

Do not use the agent to make unsupported claims about competitors.

## 11.19 Competitor Voice-of-Customer report

Across 10,000 calls:

| Competitor | Mentions | Main Like | Main Dislike | Switching Interest |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| A | 1,180 | Price | Availability | 31% |
| B | 720 | Quality | Price | 24% |
| C | 410 | Location | Customer service | 42% |

This becomes useful market intelligence.

## 11.20 Unmet needs

This is one of the most valuable outputs.

Customer asks:

> "Do you offer home physiotherapy visits?"

Service catalog:

`No`

Create:

```text
UNMET_NEED

need = home physiotherapy
customer_id
location
urgency
willingness_to_pay if explicitly discussed
competitor_available if known
timestamp
```

Aggregate later.

## 11.21 Unmet need scoring

Potential dimensions:

```text
request_frequency
customer_importance
purchase_intent
service_fit_gap
competitor availability
revenue potential
trend growth
```

Example:

```text
Home Visit Demand Score = 87/100
```

This can drive product planning.

## 11.22 Emerging need detection

Track time series:

```text
Senior wellness requests
Jan: 42
Feb: 51
Mar: 68
Apr: 96
```

MarketAI can detect significant growth.

Do not wait for management to manually read transcripts.

## 11.23 Need clustering

Thousands of customers will phrase the same need differently:

> "after office"

> "after work"

> "evening only"

> "later in the day"

All could cluster around:

```text
EVENING_AVAILABILITY
```

Use:

embeddings + clustering + taxonomy mapping.

Possible tools:

sentence embeddings  
HDBSCAN  
K-means where appropriate.

## 11.24 Hybrid classification

Recommended approach:

```text
Rule / taxonomy match
      +
Embedding similarity
      +
LLM extraction
      ↓
Confidence
      ↓
Mapped need
```

Do not rely solely on an LLM label.

## 11.25 Unknown category

Allow:

```text
NEED_UNKNOWN
```

A production taxonomy must allow genuine novelty.

Otherwise models force new requirements into inappropriate old categories.

## 11.26 Taxonomy evolution

Example:

Initially:

```text
Wellness
```

Over time conversations reveal:

```text
Workplace stress
Senior mobility
Posture
Breathwork
```

Govern taxonomy changes:

```text
Proposal
→ Analyst review
→ Product approval
→ version
→ migration/mapping
```

## 11.27 Need taxonomy versioning

Every classification stores:

```text
taxonomy_version
```

This lets you reproduce historical reports.

## 11.28 Need confidence

Example:

Customer:

> "I'd really prefer something after work."

```text
EVENING_AVAILABILITY
confidence=.97
```

Vague statement:

> "My schedule is difficult."

```text
SCHEDULING_CONSTRAINT
confidence=.61
```

Don't pretend all extraction is certain.

## 11.29 Need deduplication

One caller may repeat the same requirement five times.

Do not create five needs.

Use:

```text
semantic similarity
+
same interaction
+
same taxonomy category
```

and update evidence count.

## 11.30 Need persistence

Different needs have different lifetimes.

Example:

`Preferred language`

may persist.

`Needs appointment tomorrow`

expires quickly.

Store:

```text
effective_from
expires_at
```

## 11.31 Beneficiary tracking

Customer may be calling for:

self, mother, child, spouse, employee, organization.

Store:

```text
beneficiary_type
```

without unnecessarily collecting another person's identity.

Example:

```text
need:
Senior wellness

beneficiary:
FAMILY_MEMBER

identity:
NOT COLLECTED
```

This supports privacy minimization.

## 11.32 Service gap analysis

Compare:

```text
Customer Needs
      ↓
Service Catalog
      ↓
MATCH / PARTIAL MATCH / NO MATCH
```

Dashboard:

```text
Matched needs       72%
Partial match       18%
Unmet               10%
```

Then inspect the 10%.

## 11.33 Match-gap reasons

Examples:

```text
SERVICE_NOT_OFFERED
NO_LOCAL_LOCATION
NO_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
NO_EVENING_AVAILABILITY
PRICE_TOO_HIGH
CAPACITY_FULL
DELIVERY_MODE_UNAVAILABLE
```

This converts lost sales into actionable operational data.

## 11.34 Preference intelligence

Aggregate:

```text
Preferred call time
Appointment time
Language
Contact channel
Location
Delivery
Package duration
Price range
```

Example:

| Preference | % |
|---|---:|
| Evening | 41% |
| Weekend | 24% |
| Morning | 18% |
| Afternoon | 17% |

Use this to design service hours and campaigns.

## 11.35 Price intelligence

Capture:

```text
price_asked
price_objection
expected_price
competitor_price
accepted_price
discount_request
```

Avoid asking customers for sensitive financial information unnecessarily.

## 11.36 Price sensitivity curve

Over many interactions:

```text
$50 → objection 8%
$75 → 14%
$100 → 31%
$125 → 52%
```

This can help pricing research, although correlation does not automatically establish optimal price.

## 11.37 Call-time intelligence

Track:

```text
call_hour
weekday
answered
conversation_completed
booking
conversion
DNC
complaint
```

Then analyze:

```text
Best time to reach
Best time to convert
Worst time for complaints
```

by segment.

## 11.38 Language intelligence

Dashboard:

| Language | Calls | Connect | Booking | CSAT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| English | ... | ... | ... | ... |
| Hindi | ... | ... | ... | ... |
| Punjabi | ... | ... | ... | ... |

Use for service quality and resource planning, not sensitive profiling.

## 11.39 Conversation-topic tracking

Each call can contain:

```text
pricing
availability
service
location
insurance/admin
language
competitor
appointment
feedback
```

Store topic sequence.

This can reveal:

> Price conversations frequently occur immediately before drop-off.

## 11.40 Topic-transition analytics

Example:

```text
SERVICE
  ↓
PRICE
  ↓
OBJECTION
  ↓
NOT_INTERESTED
```

versus:

```text
SERVICE
 ↓
AVAILABILITY
 ↓
BOOKING
```

This can improve script design.

## 11.41 Customer question bank

Capture every question customers ask.

Normalize into:

```text
QUESTION

raw_question
normalized_question
topic
answer_available
answer_quality
frequency
```

Then identify:

**top FAQs**

and:

**questions the AI frequently cannot answer.**

## 11.42 Unanswered-question dashboard

Example:

| Question category | Count | Unanswered % |
|---|---:|---:|
| Insurance | 820 | 18% |
| Weekend hours | 630 | 2% |
| Home visits | 440 | 100% |
| Pricing | 1,900 | 1% |

This directly improves knowledge base and services.

## 11.43 Knowledge-gap loop

```text
Unanswered question
      ↓
Knowledge gap
      ↓
Content owner
      ↓
Approved answer
      ↓
Knowledge base
      ↓
Regression test
      ↓
Production
```

This is a powerful continuous-improvement loop.

## 11.44 NeedAI API

Recommended:

```text
POST /needs/extract
POST /needs/confirm

GET /customers/{id}/needs
GET /customers/{id}/unmet-needs

POST /preferences/extract
POST /objections/extract
POST /competitors/extract

GET /market/needs
GET /market/unmet-needs
GET /market/objections
```

## 11.45 Extraction response

Example:

```json
{
  "needs": [
    {
      "type": "SERVICE_NEED",
      "value": "physiotherapy",
      "explicit": true,
      "confidence": 0.99
    },
    {
      "type": "SCHEDULE_NEED",
      "value": "evening",
      "explicit": true,
      "confidence": 0.98
    }
  ]
}
```

## 11.46 Event model

Publish:

```text
need.detected
need.confirmed
need.updated
need.expired

unmet_need.detected

preference.detected
like.detected
dislike.detected

objection.detected
competitor.mentioned

knowledge_gap.detected
```

## 11.47 Post-call pipeline

```text
Call Complete
    ↓
Transcript finalization
    ↓
PII controls
    ↓
Conversation segmentation
    ↓
Need extraction
    ↓
Preference extraction
    ↓
Objection extraction
    ↓
Competitor extraction
    ↓
Question extraction
    ↓
Confidence validation
    ↓
Structured records
    ↓
Customer 360
    ↓
MarketAI
```

## 11.48 Don't process only full transcript

Use both:

**turn-level extraction**

and:

**post-call global extraction**.

Why?

Turn-level detects exactly when preference changed.

Post-call extraction provides overall context.

Compare them for consistency.

## 11.49 Contradiction detection

Turn 4:

> "Evening is best."

Turn 18:

> "Actually weekends are easier."

Final structured state:

```text
preferred_time = weekend
```

Historical evidence preserved.

## 11.50 Sentiment architecture

Avoid one sentiment number.

Capture:

```text
overall_sentiment
service_sentiment
price_sentiment
brand_sentiment
agent_sentiment
competitor_sentiment
```

Example:

```text
service = POSITIVE
price = NEGATIVE
agent = POSITIVE
```

Much more actionable.

## 11.51 Emotion signals

Use carefully.

Possible operational categories:

```text
CALM
CONFUSED
FRUSTRATED
SATISFIED
UNCERTAIN
```

Avoid overclaiming psychological inference from voice.

Treat these as approximate conversational signals, not facts about a person's mental state.

## 11.52 Test dataset

Build manually labeled examples.

At minimum:

```text
500 calls MVP
```

with labels for:

primary need  
secondary need  
preference  
like  
dislike  
objection  
competitor  
unmet need  
question  
outcome.

Later:

2,000+.

## 11.53 Need extraction metrics

Measure:

precision  
recall  
F1.

Example:

```text
Primary Need F1
Secondary Need F1
Preference F1
Objection F1
Competitor extraction F1
```

Don't measure only overall extraction accuracy.

## 11.54 Exact-match vs semantic scoring

For:

phone/date/service ID

use strict structured evaluation.

For:

pain-point summary

semantic/human evaluation can be more appropriate.

## 11.55 Edge case — ambiguous need

Customer:

> "I'm just checking things out."

Don't force:

`Primary need = physiotherapy`.

Use:

```text
need_status = UNCONFIRMED
```

## 11.56 Edge case — contradictory needs

Customer:

> "I want online."

Later:

> "Actually, in-person might be better."

Store latest confirmed preference with historical evidence.

## 11.57 Edge case — sarcasm

Customer:

> "Yeah, that's really cheap."

Could mean the opposite.

Avoid overconfidence.

Use context + lower confidence.

## 11.58 Edge case — hypothetical discussion

> "If my mother ever needed senior yoga, do you offer it?"

Don't automatically create:

`mother currently needs senior yoga`.

Classify:

```text
HYPOTHETICAL_INTEREST
```

## 11.59 Edge case — customer mentions someone else's condition

Do not automatically attach third-party sensitive information to the caller's profile.

Minimize and generalize where possible.

## 11.60 Edge case — agent plants a need

Agent:

> "Do you need meditation too?"

Customer:

> "Maybe."

This is weaker evidence than spontaneous customer demand.

Store source:

```text
AGENT_PROMPTED
```

versus:

```text
CUSTOMER_SPONTANEOUS
```

This distinction is very important for market research.

## 11.61 Demand-quality scoring

For a potential new service:

Customer spontaneously requests it:

strong signal.

Agent asks and customer says maybe:

weak signal.

Therefore calculate:

```text
Demand Strength
```

using:

spontaneity  
explicitness  
urgency  
repetition  
purchase intent.

## 11.62 MarketAI aggregation

Aggregate:

```text
Need Frequency
×
Need Strength
×
Growth
×
Service Gap
×
Conversion Potential
```

to rank opportunities.

## 11.63 Example market opportunity output

```text
Opportunity:
Weekend Senior Wellness

Requests:
312/month

Growth:
+38% over 3 months

Current service coverage:
LOW

Average intent:
HIGH

Top location:
NW

Preferred language:
English/Hindi/Punjabi mix

Primary obstacle:
Weekend capacity

Opportunity score:
88/100
```

This is management-grade information.

## 11.64 Product feedback loop

```text
Voice of Customer
      ↓
Product Gap
      ↓
Business Review
      ↓
New Offering
      ↓
Pilot
      ↓
Campaign
      ↓
Voice Feedback
      ↓
Measure
```

The call center becomes a product-discovery system.

## 11.65 ReportAI dashboards

Create:

### Needs Dashboard

Top needs  
growth  
segment  
location  
language.

### Pain Dashboard

Top pain points  
severity  
trend.

### Preference Dashboard

time  
channel  
language  
location.

### Objection Dashboard

price  
trust

### Competitor Dashboard

mentions

dislikes  
switching reasons.

### Unmet Needs Dashboard

frequency  
trend

## 11.66 QA monitoring

Track:

```text
need_extraction_confidence
unknown_need_rate
manual_correction_rate
taxonomy_mapping_failure
duplicate_need_rate
contradiction_rate
```

A sudden increase in `UNKNOWN_NEED` may indicate customer behavior drift or a broken extractor.

## 11.67 Human validation

Sample conversations regularly.

Example:

```text
5–10% early-stage review
```

then risk-based sampling as quality stabilizes.

Prioritize:

low-confidence extraction  
new need categories  
high-value opportunities  
complaints  
unmet needs.

## 11.68 Model/version governance

Store:

```text
extractor_model
model_version
prompt_version
taxonomy_version
```

for every extracted item.

This provides lineage.

## 11.69 Security/privacy

Before MarketAI aggregation:

minimize/redact unnecessary personal identifiers.

Executives should generally see:

```text
"37 customers requested evening appointments"
```

not unnecessary individual transcript details.

```text
Preferences                   PASS

Dislikes                      PASS
Objections                    PASS

Unknown-category handling     PASS

Test dataset                  PASS
```

### Phase 11 output

One conversation may now produce:

```text
CUSTOMER C10028

PRIMARY NEED
Physiotherapy

JOB TO BE DONE
Get treatment without interfering
with work schedule

PAIN POINT
Current providers lack evening availability

GOAL
Start this week

HARD CONSTRAINT
After 6 PM

PREFERENCE
Nearby location

LIKE

DISLIKE

Price

COMPETITOR
XYZ Physio
```

The next phase is **Phase 12 — RecommendAI + Service/Offer Matching Engine**: converting this structured need profile into explainable service recommendations using catalog rules, eligibility, language, location, schedule, pricing, hard constraints, availability, ranking, alternatives, bundles, cross-sell controls, recommendation confidence, A/B testing, and edge-case handling.

## 🧑 User — msg #57

next

---

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #58

# Phase 12 — RecommendAI + Service / Offer Matching Engine

This phase converts the structured customer profile from NeedAI into **safe, explainable, relevant recommendations**.

The goal is not “the LLM suggests something.” The goal is:

> **Customer need + constraints + preferences + eligibility + availability + price + policy → ranked recommendation → explanation → customer choice.**

## 12.1 Target architecture

```text
Customer 360
    +
NeedAI
    +
Preferences
    +
Segments
    +
Scores
    +
Service Catalog
    +
Pricing
    +
Availability
    +
Policy
       ↓
Candidate Generator
       ↓
Eligibility Filter
       ↓
Constraint Filter
       ↓
Service-Fit Scoring
       ↓
Ranking
       ↓
Explainability
       ↓
Recommendation
       ↓
Customer Reaction
       ↓
Accept / Reject / Alternative
       ↓
NextAI
```

---

## 12.2 Core RecommendAI modules

| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| CatalogAI | Authoritative service catalog |
| Eligibility Engine | Determines whether service can be offered |
| Constraint Engine | Applies hard requirements |
| MatchAI | Need-to-service matching |
| RankAI | Ranks valid alternatives |
| OfferAI | Packages/promotions |
| BundleAI | Related service combinations |
| CrossSellAI | Adjacent need matching |
| AlternativeAI | Best fallback when first option fails |
| ExplainAI | Why recommendation was selected |
| Feedback Loop | Learns from accept/reject outcome |

---

# 12.3 Service Catalog must be authoritative

Create a central catalog.

```text
SERVICE

service_id
tenant_id
name
category
subcategory
description

locations[]
languages[]
delivery_modes[]

duration
base_price
currency

eligibility_rules
contraindications_or_restrictions where applicable

availability_source
booking_type

active_from
active_until

status

approved_content_version
```

The LLM should never invent services outside this catalog.

---

# 12.4 Separate service from offer

Example:

**Service**

Physiotherapy consultation.

**Offer**

First consultation discount.

**Package**

5-session package.

**Promotion**

September campaign.

Model separately:

```text
SERVICE
OFFER
PACKAGE
PROMOTION
```

This avoids pricing confusion.

---

# 12.5 Candidate generation

NeedAI says:

```text
Primary need:
Physiotherapy

Hard constraint:
After 6 PM

Location:
NW

Language:
Hindi preferred
```

Candidate generator might initially return:

```text
Physio Consultation
Sports Physio
General Physio
Virtual Physio
```

Then filters determine what is actually relevant.

---

# 12.6 Hard constraint filtering

Hard constraints must be applied before ranking.

Example:

```text
Customer:
after 18:00 required

Service A:
17:00 only
→ REMOVE

Service B:
18:30 available
→ KEEP
```

Never rank an impossible option highly just because semantic similarity is strong.

---

# 12.7 Hard vs soft preference

Suppose:

```text
Hard:
must be after 6 PM

Soft:
prefers NW location
```

Then:

NW 5 PM → invalid.

Downtown 6:30 PM → valid.

NW 6:30 PM → ideal.

This distinction is critical.

---

# 12.8 Eligibility engine

Check:

```text
service active?
customer eligible?
location supported?
language supported?
delivery supported?
age/service restrictions where relevant?
capacity?
campaign restrictions?
policy restrictions?
```

Output:

```text
ELIGIBLE
INELIGIBLE
REQUIRES_REVIEW
```

---

# 12.9 Service fit score

Example dimensions:

```text
Need Match              30%
Hard Constraint Fit     mandatory
Schedule Fit            15%
Location Fit            10%
Language Fit            10%
Delivery Fit            10%
Price Fit               10%
Availability            10%
Historical Acceptance    5%
```

But hard constraints should usually be filters, not merely weighted penalties.

---

# 12.10 Recommendation ranking

For remaining candidates:

```text
Candidate A = 94
Candidate B = 87
Candidate C = 74
```

Return top 1–3.

Do not overwhelm the customer with ten options.

---

# 12.11 Example recommendation

Customer:

```text
Need:
Physiotherapy

Time:
Evening

Location:
NW

Price:
Moderate concern

Language:
Hindi
```

Output:

```text
1. NW Evening Physio Consultation
   Match = 94

2. Virtual Evening Physio
   Match = 86

3. Downtown Evening Physio
   Match = 79
```

---

# 12.12 Explain recommendation

Agent should be able to say:

> “The NW evening appointment looks like the best fit because you said evening timing and nearby location are most important.”

Internally:

```text
Top reasons:
+ after-6 availability
+ NW location
+ requested service
+ preferred language available
```

This is ExplainAI.

---

# 12.13 Do not expose hidden scoring unnecessarily

Customer does not need:

> “Your fit score is 94.2.”

Translate machine reasoning into useful human explanation.

---

# 12.14 Price matching

Customer says:

> “I want something under $100.”

Pricing API returns:

```text
A = $120
B = $90
C = $75
```

If budget is a hard limit:

remove A.

If budget is only a preference:

A may remain lower-ranked.

---

# 12.15 Price integrity

Always retrieve current pricing from authoritative source.

```text
Recommendation Engine
    ↓
Pricing API
```

Never use an old transcript or cached model memory for current price.

---

# 12.16 Promotion matching

Promotion eligibility:

```text
promotion active?
customer segment eligible?
service eligible?
location eligible?
start/end valid?
usage cap?
customer already used?
```

Only then recommend.

---

# 12.17 Discount authority

If AI can offer discounts:

```text
0–10% → agent allowed
>10% → human approval
```

or whatever business policy defines.

Recommendation cannot override discount policy.

---

# 12.18 Bundle recommendations

Example:

Customer asks about:

Yoga + stress reduction.

Possible bundle:

```text
Yoga
+
Meditation
```

But bundle only if:

need match is real  
customer shows interest  
pricing is valid  
offer policy permits.

Don't force bundles just to increase revenue.

---

# 12.19 Cross-sell engine

Input:

```text
Primary need = Yoga
Additional need = Senior program for mother
```

Potential cross-sell:

```text
Senior Yoga
```

Before explaining:

> “We do have an option that may fit that additional need. Would you like to hear about it?”

Respect rejection.

---

# 12.20 Upsell vs cross-sell

### Upsell

Better/higher-tier version of same need.

Example:

Basic → premium package.

### Cross-sell

Different related service.

Example:

Yoga → meditation.

Track separately.

---

# 12.21 Recommendation context

Recommendations should depend on purpose.

Example:

**Sales call**

recommend service.

**Complaint call**

do not immediately upsell.

**Appointment reminder**

do not inject unrelated offers.

Purpose-aware recommendations are important for customer trust.

---

# 12.22 Recommendation suppression

Suppress recommendations when:

```text
customer angry
complaint active
DNC
human-only
safety escalation
clinical risk
customer already said no
contact pressure excessive
```

Customer experience outranks revenue optimization.

---

# 12.23 Alternative engine

If preferred service unavailable:

```text
Original:
NW Tuesday 6 PM

Unavailable
   ↓
AlternativeAI
```

Possible:

```text
NW Thursday 6 PM
NW Tuesday 7 PM
Virtual Tuesday 6 PM
Downtown Tuesday 6 PM
```

Rank by deviation from customer constraints.

---

# 12.24 Alternative distance score

Measure how far option differs from request.

Example:

```text
Time difference
Location difference
Price difference
Delivery difference
Provider difference
```

Then choose smallest acceptable deviation.

---

# 12.25 Ask before relaxing constraints

If all options fail hard constraint:

Do not silently relax it.

Agent:

> “I don’t see an appointment after 6 PM at that location. Would another location or an earlier time be acceptable?”

Then update constraints if customer agrees.

---

# 12.26 No-match handling

If nothing fits:

```text
NO_MATCH
```

Actions:

human review  
waitlist  
callback  
alternative service  
capture unmet need.

This feeds MarketAI.

---

# 12.27 Unmet-need integration

Example:

Customer needs:

`Home physiotherapy`

Catalog:

no home service.

Create:

```text
UNMET_NEED
```

Do not recommend normal clinic service as though it satisfies the request.

---

# 12.28 Recommendation confidence

Return:

```text
fit_score
confidence
```

Example:

```text
fit = 89
confidence = 97
```

or:

```text
fit = 89
confidence = 54
```

Low confidence may require clarification before recommendation.

---

# 12.29 Clarification engine

Low confidence because:

```text
location unknown
budget unclear
time ambiguous
```

Ask one high-value question.

Example:

> “Is location or evening availability more important to you?”

Then rerank.

---

# 12.30 Avoid excessive questioning

Use **expected information gain** conceptually.

Ask only if answer could materially change recommendation.

If all valid options are identical regardless of one missing field, don't ask it.

---

# 12.31 Service-match explanation record

Store:

```text
recommendation_id
customer_id

service_id
rank
fit_score
confidence

positive_reasons[]
negative_reasons[]

constraints_satisfied[]
constraints_relaxed[]

pricing_version
catalog_version
policy_version

created_at
```

---

# 12.32 Recommendation history

Don't overwrite.

Store:

```text
recommended
accepted
rejected
reason
converted
```

This becomes training data later.

---

# 12.33 Rejection reasons

Capture:

```text
PRICE
TIMING
LOCATION
TRUST
SERVICE_FIT
COMPETITOR
NO_INTEREST
NEEDS_HUMAN
OTHER
```

This helps improve the ranking model.

---

# 12.34 Recommendation learning

Initially:

rules + weighted ranking.

Later train a model using:

```text
customer features
service features
context
recommendation
acceptance
booking
conversion
```

But be careful:

historical recommendations create exposure bias.

Customers cannot accept services they were never shown.

---

# 12.35 Ranking model options

Start:

deterministic weighted scoring.

Later:

logistic regression  
XGBoost  
learning-to-rank.

Potential advanced option:

contextual bandits.

Only after enough data.

---

# 12.36 Don't optimize only CTR/acceptance

A recommendation that gets clicked/accepted but leads to:

cancellation  
complaint  
refund  
poor satisfaction

is not a good recommendation.

Optimize downstream outcomes.

---

# 12.37 Recommendation quality KPI

Measure:

```text
Recommendation Acceptance
Booking Rate
Show Rate
Conversion
Cancellation
Complaint
CSAT
Revenue
Retention
```

And:

```text
Cost / Successful Recommendation
```

---

# 12.38 Recommendation diversity

Don't always show the same highest-margin service.

Apply:

relevance first.

You may use diversity when several genuinely suitable options exist.

---

# 12.39 Margin-aware optimization

Business economics can be considered, but only after:

eligibility  
customer fit  
policy  
quality.

Conceptually:

```text
maximize customer fit
subject to business constraints
```

not:

```text
maximize margin regardless of fit
```

---

# 12.40 Service catalog versioning

Store:

```text
catalog_version
```

because services/pricing change.

Every recommendation must be reproducible.

---

# 12.41 Availability freshness

Availability changes quickly.

Do not recommend:

```text
“Tuesday 6 PM is available”
```

from a cached snapshot several hours old.

Use real-time or appropriately fresh availability API.

---

# 12.42 Reservation/hold strategy

Potential race:

Agent sees one slot.

Two customers try to book simultaneously.

Options:

temporary hold  
optimistic booking  
transactional scheduler API.

Recommendation engine must expect availability to change.

---

# 12.43 Availability edge case

Agent recommends Tuesday 6 PM.

By the time customer says yes, slot gone.

Correct response:

> “That slot was just taken. I can check the closest alternatives.”

Never pretend booking succeeded.

---

# 12.44 Recommendation API

Example:

```text
POST /recommendations
```

Request:

```json
{
  "customer_id": "C10028",
  "need_ids": ["N001"],
  "context": "OUTBOUND_SALES"
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "recommendations": [
    {
      "service_id": "PHYSIO_EVE_NW",
      "rank": 1,
      "fit_score": 94,
      "confidence": 96
    }
  ]
}
```

---

# 12.45 Additional APIs

```text
GET /recommendations/{id}

POST /recommendations/{id}/accept
POST /recommendations/{id}/reject

POST /recommendations/alternatives

GET /services/{id}
GET /services/{id}/availability
GET /services/{id}/price
```

---

# 12.46 Event model

Publish:

```text
recommendation.generated
recommendation.presented
recommendation.accepted
recommendation.rejected

alternative.generated

service.no_match

promotion.presented
promotion.accepted
```

---

# 12.47 Conversation integration

State machine:

```text
NEED CONFIRMED
     ↓
RecommendAI
     ↓
Agent explains recommendation
     ↓
Customer reacts
```

Possible reactions:

```text
ACCEPT
ASK_MORE
PRICE_OBJECTION
TIMING_OBJECTION
REJECT
ALTERNATIVE
HUMAN
```

Route accordingly.

---

# 12.48 Example call

Customer:

> “I want physio after 6 and I don't want to drive too far.”

NeedAI:

```text
physiotherapy
after-6 = HARD
nearby = SOFT/HIGH
```

RecommendAI:

```text
NW 6:30 = 95
Downtown 7:00 = 77
NW 5:00 = INVALID
```

Agent:

> “The best match is the NW clinic at 6:30 PM because it meets your evening requirement and keeps the location nearby.”

---

# 12.49 Testing — service matching

Create:

happy path  
multiple matches  
no match  
hard constraint violation  
soft preference mismatch  
invalid service  
inactive service.

---

# 12.50 Testing — pricing

Test:

current price  
expired price  
promotion active  
promotion expired  
incorrect currency  
price API timeout.

Expected:

never invent/guess.

---

# 12.51 Testing — availability

Test:

available  
slot disappears  
no availability  
provider unavailable  
service full  
location closed.

---

# 12.52 Testing — ranking

Use manually labeled scenarios:

```text
Customer profile
Candidate services
Expected rank order
```

Create 500+ ranking cases as the platform matures.

---

# 12.53 Test example

Customer:

```text
English
Dental
Saturday
NW
Budget flexible
```

Candidates:

A Saturday NW  
B Saturday downtown  
C Monday NW.

Expected:

A > B > C, assuming no other differences.

---

# 12.54 Edge case — conflicting preferences

Customer:

```text
must be cheap
must be premium
```

Clarify what “premium” means.

Do not attempt to mathematically resolve contradictory language without context.

---

# 12.55 Edge case — customer asks “what do you recommend?”

Avoid vague generic answer.

Use structured profile and say:

> “Based on your evening requirement and preferred location, option A appears to fit best.”

---

# 12.56 Edge case — customer requests unavailable service

Say clearly:

> “We don't currently offer that service.”

Then, only if appropriate:

> “I can tell you about the closest alternatives.”

Capture unmet demand.

---

# 12.57 Edge case — service not suitable

If policy/eligibility says no:

Don't let LLM override it.

Return:

```text
INELIGIBLE
```

and follow approved alternative/human path.

---

# 12.58 Edge case — low-confidence inferred need

Do not recommend expensive/additional service based on weak inference.

Require customer confirmation first.

---

# 12.59 Edge case — recommendation fatigue

Don't make five recommendations sequentially after each rejection.

Set:

```text
max_recommendations_per_call
```

After threshold:

offer human help/nurture/close.

---

# 12.60 Edge case — customer says “just tell me the cheapest”

Retrieve valid options.

Rank primarily by price while still enforcing eligibility and hard requirements.

Explain tradeoffs concisely.

---

# 12.61 Edge case — customer says “best quality only”

Rank using approved quality/service criteria, not invented superiority claims.

---

# 12.62 Edge case — customer asks competitor recommendation

Your agent should not pretend to objectively rank competitors unless your product is explicitly built and governed for that.

Provide your own service information and avoid unsupported competitor comparisons.

---

# 12.63 Recommendation fairness

Monitor whether recommendations systematically differ across relevant groups for reasons unrelated to genuine needs/constraints.

Do not use protected traits as optimization shortcuts.

Language can determine communication support, but should not become a proxy for service value.

---

# 12.64 Explainability testing

For every recommendation verify:

reasons correspond to actual inputs.

Bad explanation:

> “Recommended because you prefer evenings.”

when customer never stated that.

This is explanation hallucination.

---

# 12.65 Recommendation drift

Monitor:

acceptance rate  
booking rate  
rejection reasons  
no-match rate.

Example:

```text
NO_MATCH:
5% → 18%
```

Possible cause:

new market need  
catalog issue  
broken availability integration.

---

# 12.66 Shadow testing

New ranking model:

```text
Champion = Rules v5
Challenger = XGBoost v1
```

Run challenger in shadow.

Compare:

rank  
acceptance prediction  
business outcome  
fairness  
latency.

---

# 12.67 A/B testing

Controlled test:

```text
A = one recommendation
B = top three
```

Measure:

conversion  
call duration  
confusion  
complaints.

Or:

```text
A = explain price first
B = explain fit first
```

Again, optimize overall quality, not only conversion.

---

# 12.68 Observability

Track:

```text
recommendations_generated
eligible_candidate_count
no_match_rate
acceptance_rate
rejection_rate
alternative_rate
booking_after_recommendation
recommendation_latency
catalog_errors
pricing_errors
availability_errors
```

---

# 12.69 Recommendation funnel

```text
4,000 Needs Confirmed
      ↓
3,900 Match Found
      ↓
3,500 Recommendation Presented
      ↓
2,200 Accepted
      ↓
1,800 Booking Attempt
      ↓
1,650 Booked
      ↓
1,400 Attended
```

Measure losses at each step.

---

# 12.70 Reporting

Report by:

service  
segment  
language  
campaign  
location  
price tier  
time  
provider.

Questions:

**Which service is recommended most?**

**Which is accepted most?**

**Why do customers reject recommendations?**

**Where is no-match highest?**

**Which services create complaints?**

**Which unmet needs are increasing?**

---

# 12.71 Security

Protect:

pricing APIs  
promotion rules  
customer preference data  
service eligibility.

Require:

RBAC  
tenant isolation  
API authorization  
audit.

Do not allow user-controlled prompts to manipulate catalog query results.

---

# 12.72 Audit record

For every recommendation:

```text
customer
needs
constraints
candidate set
filtered candidates
selected option
ranking score
reasons
catalog version
pricing version
policy version
model version
timestamp
```

This makes decisions reproducible.

---

# 12.73 Definition of Done

Phase 12 is complete when:

```text
Service Catalog               PASS
Offer Catalog                 PASS
Package/Promotion Model       PASS

Candidate Generation          PASS
Eligibility Filtering         PASS
Hard Constraints              PASS
Soft Preferences              PASS

Fit Scoring                   PASS
Ranking                       PASS
Alternatives                  PASS
No-Match Handling             PASS

Pricing Integration           PASS
Promotion Validation          PASS
Availability Integration      PASS

Cross-Sell                    PASS
Upsell                        PASS
Bundle Logic                  PASS

Recommendation Explanation    PASS
Confidence                    PASS

Acceptance Tracking           PASS
Rejection Tracking            PASS
Recommendation History        PASS

Fairness Evaluation           PASS
Drift Monitoring              PASS
Shadow Testing                PASS
A/B Testing                   PASS

Security                      PASS
Audit                         PASS
Monitoring                    PASS
Dashboards                    PASS
UAT                           PASS
```

### Phase 12 output

For our example customer:

```text
CUSTOMER C10028

NEED
Physiotherapy

HARD CONSTRAINT
After 6 PM

SOFT PREFERENCES
NW Calgary
Hindi preferred

PRICE SENSITIVITY
High

CANDIDATES
--------------------------------
NW Physio 6:30 PM       94
Virtual Physio 7 PM     86
Downtown Physio 6 PM    78

RECOMMENDATION
NW Physio 6:30 PM

WHY
✓ Requested physiotherapy
✓ Meets after-6 requirement
✓ Preferred location
✓ Language support available
✓ Within acceptable price profile

CONFIDENCE
96%

ALTERNATIVE
Virtual 7 PM

POLICY
PASS

NEXT
Present recommendation → customer response
```

The next phase is **Phase 13 — NextAI / Next-Best-Action Engine**, which determines whether the system should **book now, offer another option, send information, schedule callback, transfer to human, nurture, request missing data, stop outreach, recover an objection, or take no action** based on the entire customer context and current conversation.

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #61

# Phase 13 — NextAI / Next-Best-Action Engine

This phase decides the **best next action for each customer after every meaningful event**.

The key idea is:

> **Do not just ask “What should the agent say next?” Ask “What action should the business take next?”**

That action may be a call, booking, SMS, email, human transfer, nurture, another offer, follow-up, wait, or stop-contact decision.

## 13.1 Target architecture

```text
Customer 360
   +
NeedAI
   +
SegmentAI
   +
ScoreAI
   +
RecommendAI
   +
Campaign History
   +
Call Outcome
   +
Preferences
   +
Consent / Policy
   +
Appointments
   +
Risk / Complaints
        ↓
    NextAI
        ↓
Candidate Actions
        ↓
Policy Filter
        ↓
Business Rules
        ↓
Action Scoring
        ↓
Action Ranking
        ↓
ExplainAI
        ↓
Execute Best Action
        ↓
Track Outcome
```

## 13.2 Action catalog

Start with a controlled action catalog.

| Action | Example |
|---|---|
| CALL_NOW | High-intent callback |
| SCHEDULE_CALL | Customer prefers later |
| BOOK_APPOINTMENT | Ready to book |
| CHECK_AVAILABILITY | Need date/time |
| OFFER_ALTERNATIVE | Preferred slot unavailable |
| SEND_SMS | Confirmation/follow-up |
| SEND_EMAIL | Detailed information |
| SEND_WHATSAPP | Permitted channel |
| TRANSFER_HUMAN | Complex/high-risk case |
| CREATE_HUMAN_TASK | Sales/clinic follow-up |
| OFFER_TRIAL | Eligible lead |
| OFFER_PACKAGE | Relevant option |
| CROSS_SELL | Confirmed adjacent need |
| NURTURE | Interested but not ready |
| WAIT | Do nothing yet |
| REQUEST_INFORMATION | Missing critical field |
| VERIFY_INFORMATION | Low-confidence data |
| ESCALATE | Complaint/safety issue |
| SUPPRESS | Stop campaign |
| DNC | No future applicable contact |
| CLOSE_LEAD | No viable opportunity |

Do not allow the LLM to invent arbitrary executable action names.

---

# 13.3 Candidate generation

Example customer:

```text
Intent = 92
Service Fit = 90
Urgency = 85
Price Sensitivity = 70
Appointment = none
Preferred time = evening
Consent = valid
```

Candidate actions:

```text
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
CALL_BACK_EVENING
SEND_SERVICE_INFO
OFFER_LOWER_COST_OPTION
```

NextAI then ranks them.

---

# 13.4 Eligibility filtering comes first

Suppose candidate actions are:

```text
CALL
SMS
EMAIL
BOOK
```

But policy says:

```text
CALL = allowed
SMS = blocked
EMAIL = allowed
BOOK = allowed
```

SMS must be removed before scoring.

Therefore:

```text
Candidate Generation
      ↓
PolicyAI
      ↓
Eligible Candidate Set
      ↓
NextAI Ranking
```

Optimization never overrides policy.

---

# 13.5 Rule-based NextAI first

For MVP, use deterministic rules.

Example:

```text
IF
intent > 80
AND
service_fit > 80
AND
availability_known = false

THEN
NEXT_ACTION = CHECK_AVAILABILITY
```

Another:

```text
IF
appointment_selected = true
AND
customer_confirmed = true

THEN
NEXT_ACTION = BOOK_APPOINTMENT
```

Another:

```text
IF
customer_busy = true
AND
callback_time != null

THEN
NEXT_ACTION = SCHEDULE_CALLBACK
```

---

# 13.6 Action priorities

Certain events override normal optimization.

Recommended precedence:

```text
SAFETY / EMERGENCY
        ↓
DNC / PRIVACY
        ↓
COMPLAINT / ESCALATION
        ↓
CUSTOMER EXPLICIT REQUEST
        ↓
EXISTING TRANSACTION
        ↓
HIGH-INTENT ACTION
        ↓
RECOMMENDATION
        ↓
NURTURE / MARKETING
```

If customer asks for a human, don't let an AI conversion model decide another product pitch is more profitable.

---

# 13.7 Customer explicit request

Examples:

> "Call me tomorrow."

Next action:

`SCHEDULE_CALLBACK`

> "Just email it."

Next action:

`SEND_EMAIL`

> "Book that slot."

Next action:

`BOOK_APPOINTMENT`

> "I need a person."

Next action:

`TRANSFER_HUMAN`

Explicit customer instructions should have very high decision weight.

---

# 13.8 Decision state

Create:

```text
NEXT_ACTION_DECISION

decision_id
customer_id
interaction_id

candidate_actions[]

selected_action

score
confidence

reason_codes[]

policy_decision_id

model_version
rule_version

created_at
executed_at
outcome
```

---

# 13.9 Next-action scoring

For non-mandatory actions, conceptually calculate:

```text
Action Utility =
Expected Business Value
× Probability of Success
× Customer Fit
× Confidence
× Channel Fit
− Customer Friction
− Cost
− Risk
```

Never let `Expected Business Value` dominate everything else.

---

# 13.10 Customer-friction score

Important missing feature.

Actions have different friction.

Example:

Repeated outbound call:

high friction.

Requested SMS:

low friction.

Human transfer:

medium/high depending wait.

Track:

```text
CONTACT_PRESSURE
CUSTOMER_EFFORT
INTERRUPTION_COST
```

Then NextAI can choose less intrusive actions.

---

# 13.11 Action example

Customer says:

> "I'm interested, but I'm at work. Call me after six."

Possible actions:

```text
Continue sales conversation     BAD
Send marketing SMS              MAYBE
Schedule evening callback       BEST
```

NextAI:

```text
Selected:
SCHEDULE_CALLBACK

Reason:
customer explicit request
preferred window = after 18:00
intent = high
```

---

# 13.12 No-answer decision tree

```text
Call
 ↓
NO ANSWER
 ↓
Attempt count?
 ↓
Customer preference?
 ↓
Contact pressure?
 ↓
Channel eligibility?
```

Potential actions:

```text
RETRY_LATER
SEND_SMS
SEND_EMAIL
WAIT
CLOSE
```

Don't automatically dial three more times.

---

# 13.13 Busy outcome

Customer explicitly says:

> "Can't talk."

NextAI should determine:

```text
Ask for callback time
```

not:

```text
continue qualification
```

If customer supplies time, schedule exact callback.

---

# 13.14 Voicemail outcome

Candidate actions:

```text
LEAVE_VOICEMAIL
SEND_SMS
SEND_EMAIL
RETRY
```

based on campaign policy and customer permissions.

---

# 13.15 Price objection

Customer:

> "$120 is too much."

Possible NextAI actions:

```text
CHECK_ALTERNATIVE_PACKAGE
OFFER_TRIAL
EXPLAIN_VALUE
HUMAN_REVIEW
NURTURE
```

Not automatically:

```text
DISCOUNT 50%
```

OfferAI + PolicyAI govern valid commercial options.

---

# 13.16 Trust objection

Customer:

> "I've never heard of you."

Possible next action:

```text
PROVIDE_BUSINESS_INFORMATION
SEND_WEBSITE
SEND_EMAIL
HUMAN_CALLBACK
```

rather than pushing booking immediately.

---

# 13.17 Competitor objection

Customer:

> "I'm already with another clinic."

NextAI may choose:

```text
DISCOVER_SWITCHING_REASON
```

if appropriate.

If customer is satisfied and uninterested:

```text
CLOSE/NURTURE
```

Do not harass them.

---

# 13.18 Human-transfer decision

Transfer when:

customer asks  
complex question  
complaint  
low AI confidence  
multiple failed attempts  
high-value B2B opportunity  
restricted healthcare issue  
booking system abnormality.

Store:

```text
transfer_reason
transfer_queue
priority
context_summary
```

---

# 13.19 Smart human handoff

Human should not need to ask everything again.

Provide:

```text
Customer
Need
Language
Conversation summary
Main objection
Service considered
Current state
Actions attempted
Reason for transfer
```

Example:

```text
Raj
Hindi/English
Physio consultation
Wants after 6 PM
Price concern
NW option discussed
Needs human help about insurance
```

---

# 13.20 Human queue selection

Route to:

```text
Sales
Reception
Billing
Service specialist
Complaint team
Clinical staff where appropriate
Technical support
```

based on conversation state.

---

# 13.21 Queue availability

Before offering immediate transfer:

```text
get_queue_status()
```

If wait is excessive:

> "I can arrange a callback instead."

That is better than a failed transfer.

---

# 13.22 Booking action

If customer is ready:

```text
NextAI
 ↓
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
 ↓
PolicyAI
 ↓
Tool Gateway
 ↓
Verify availability again
 ↓
Critical-field confirmation
 ↓
Book
```

NextAI never bypasses transactional validation.

---

# 13.23 Appointment already exists

Customer appears in another campaign.

NextAI detects:

```text
active appointment = true
```

Suppress redundant:

`BOOK_NOW`

and potentially choose:

`CONFIRM_APPOINTMENT`

or `NO_ACTION`.

---

# 13.24 Alternative action

If desired slot unavailable:

```text
OFFER_ALTERNATIVE
```

using RecommendAI.

Do not ask the LLM to improvise random availability.

---

# 13.25 Follow-up information

Customer:

> "Send me the details."

NextAI creates:

```text
SEND_INFORMATION
```

Content engine selects:

service document  
pricing page  
location  
FAQ.

Then channel eligibility is checked.

---

# 13.26 Nurture engine

Not every interested lead should be called again tomorrow.

Possible nurture tracks:

```text
PRICE_RESEARCHER
NOT_READY
FUTURE_NEED
CORPORATE_LONG_CYCLE
SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
```

Actions over time:

email  
content  
callback  
human follow-up.

Respect frequency caps and consent.

---

# 13.27 Wait can be the best action

Important:

```text
NEXT_ACTION = WAIT
```

is valid.

Examples:

customer said "next month."

contact pressure high.

recent follow-up already sent.

waiting for appointment confirmation.

Do not optimize toward constant customer contact.

---

# 13.28 No-action state

Another valid outcome:

```text
NO_ACTION_REQUIRED
```

Example:

appointment booked  
confirmation delivered  
no outstanding request.

This prevents unnecessary workflow churn.

---

# 13.29 Missing-information actions

Suppose:

high intent  
service known  
phone valid  
but location needed for correct recommendation.

NextAI can return:

```text
REQUEST_LOCATION
```

Ask only the missing high-value question.

---

# 13.30 Confidence-aware NextAI

Example:

```text
Recommended action:
BOOK

Confidence:
43%
```

That's dangerous.

Instead use:

```text
REQUEST_CONFIRMATION
```

or:

```text
HUMAN_REVIEW
```

High-impact actions need higher confidence.

---

# 13.31 NextAI with conversation state

Real-time sequence:

```text
Customer turn
 ↓
Intent
 ↓
Need/Preference updates
 ↓
State update
 ↓
Candidate next actions
 ↓
Policy filter
 ↓
Selected action
 ↓
Agent response/tool
```

This can happen every turn.

---

# 13.32 NextAI after call

Post-call NextAI operates at a larger timescale.

Example:

```text
Call completed
 ↓
Post-call extraction
 ↓
Customer 360 update
 ↓
Scores recalculate
 ↓
NextAI
```

Output:

```text
Send confirmation now
Human follow-up tomorrow
Nurture in 30 days
Stop outreach
```

---

# 13.33 Short-term vs long-term actions

Separate:

### Immediate

during call.

### Near-term

minutes/hours/days.

### Lifecycle

weeks/months.

Example:

```text
Immediate:
BOOK

Near-term:
SMS_CONFIRMATION

Long-term:
FOLLOW_UP_AFTER_SERVICE
```

---

# 13.34 Action dependencies

Some actions require prerequisites.

Example:

```text
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
```

requires:

verified customer context  
service  
slot  
confirmation.

`SEND_SMS`

requires:

valid phone  
channel eligibility.

Create action schema:

```text
required_inputs[]
```

---

# 13.35 Action executor

NextAI should not itself implement every action.

Architecture:

```text
NextAI
 ↓
Action Orchestrator
 ↓
Tool Gateway
```

Executors:

```text
CallExecutor
BookingExecutor
SMSExecutor
EmailExecutor
TransferExecutor
CRMTaskExecutor
NurtureExecutor
```

---

# 13.36 Durable workflow

Temporal fits well here.

Example:

```text
Schedule callback
 ↓
Wait 24 hours
 ↓
Recheck consent
 ↓
Recheck customer state
 ↓
Recheck appointment
 ↓
Call
```

If customer already converted during the wait:

cancel callback.

---

# 13.37 Action idempotency

Every action gets:

```text
action_id
idempotency_key
```

A retry cannot:

send three SMS confirmations  
create duplicate appointments  
create duplicate callbacks.

---

# 13.38 Action status

Standardize:

```text
PROPOSED
AUTHORIZED
SCHEDULED
EXECUTING
SUCCEEDED
FAILED
CANCELLED
EXPIRED
```

---

# 13.39 Expiring actions

Example:

```text
OFFER_THIS_SLOT
```

might expire after minutes.

Store:

```text
expires_at
```

Don't execute stale recommendations.

---

# 13.40 Event-triggered cancellation

Suppose:

callback scheduled tomorrow.

Customer books through website tonight.

Event:

```text
appointment.created
```

NextAI workflow should cancel redundant callback where appropriate.

---

# 13.41 Multi-action planning

Sometimes best next action is a small sequence:

```text
BOOK
→ SEND_SMS
→ UPDATE_CRM
```

Represent as an action plan:

```text
ACTION_PLAN
```

with dependencies.

Don't ask LLM to execute a vague chain autonomously.

---

# 13.42 Example action plan

```text
PLAN-9108

1. BOOK_APPOINTMENT
2. UPDATE_CRM
3. SEND_CONFIRMATION_SMS
4. SCHEDULE_REMINDER
```

If Step 1 fails:

Steps 2–4 change accordingly.

---

# 13.43 Saga pattern

For multi-system transactions, consider saga-style compensation.

Example:

Booking created.

CRM update fails.

Do not cancel booking automatically.

Retry CRM asynchronously.

Different actions have different compensation semantics.

---

# 13.44 Scoring each action

Example:

| Action | Success probability | Fit | Friction | Risk | Rank |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Book now | .82 | 95 | Low | Low | 94 |
| Call later | .70 | 80 | Medium | Low | 74 |
| Send email | .43 | 65 | Low | Low | 56 |
| Upsell | .25 | 40 | High | Medium | 22 |

Choose `Book now`.

---

# 13.45 ExplainAI

Store:

```text
Selected:
BOOK_APPOINTMENT

Why:
Customer requested booking
Service fit = high
Slot selected
Customer confirmed
Policy permits booking
```

Operations can inspect decisions.

---

# 13.46 Don't expose manipulative reasoning

Customer-facing explanation should be helpful:

> "Since you've selected the Tuesday evening slot, I can book that for you now."

Not:

> "Our model predicts an 82% likelihood you'll convert."

---

# 13.47 Action feedback

After execution:

```text
action
result
customer_response
business_outcome
```

Example:

```text
Action:
OFFER_TRIAL

Result:
ACCEPTED

Appointment:
BOOKED
```

This becomes future training data.

---

# 13.48 Outcome attribution

Need to know:

> Did NextAI improve results?

Store decision → action → outcome lineage.

```text
decision_id
 ↓
action_id
 ↓
interaction
 ↓
booking
 ↓
conversion
```

---

# 13.49 ML progression

Start:

rules.

Then:

propensity models.

Later potentially:

uplift modeling.

Contextual bandits only after mature controls.

Do not jump directly to reinforcement learning for customer outreach.

---

# 13.50 Why uplift modeling is interesting

Normal model asks:

> Who will buy?

Uplift asks:

> Who is more likely to buy **because we take this action?**

Some high-intent customers would convert without another call.

Calling them unnecessarily adds cost/friction.

This can become a sophisticated NextAI capability later.

---

# 13.51 Treatment options

For uplift analysis:

```text
Call
SMS
Email
Human
No contact
```

Compare incremental effect.

Requires good experimentation and causal design.

---

# 13.52 ExperimentAI integration

Run controlled experiments.

Example:

```text
High-intent, not-ready leads

A:
call next day

B:
send information then call after 3 days
```

Measure:

conversion  
complaint  
cost  
opt-out.

---

# 13.53 Avoid feedback loops

If NextAI always calls customers with high scores, you will have less outcome data for low-scored customers.

This creates selection bias.

Maintain controlled exploration where appropriate.

---

# 13.54 Business constraints

NextAI also considers:

sales capacity  
clinic availability  
campaign budget  
provider concurrency  
human queue capacity.

Don't recommend human transfer if zero staff are available.

---

# 13.55 Capacity-aware NextAI

Example:

Physio availability nearly full.

RecommendAI may rank service highly.

NextAI might:

book remaining slot  
waitlist  
suggest alternative location.

Operational capacity matters.

---

# 13.56 Cost-aware NextAI

Example:

Customer has low probability of answering voice calls but regularly responds to authorized SMS.

NextAI may choose the lower-friction/lower-cost permitted channel.

Optimize:

```text
Cost per successful outcome
```

rather than raw action cost.

---

# 13.57 Risk-aware NextAI

Inputs from RiskAI:

```text
complaint risk
fraud risk
AI uncertainty
transaction risk
safety risk
```

High risk:

human escalation.

Low risk:

automation.

---

# 13.58 Customer-value vs treatment fairness

Do not make access to necessary service depend solely on commercial value scores.

Differentiate:

**sales prioritization**

from:

**service access / safety / support.**

This is particularly important in healthcare contexts.

---

# 13.59 NextAI APIs

Recommended:

```text
POST /next-actions/evaluate

GET /customers/{id}/next-action

GET /decisions/{id}

POST /actions/{id}/execute

POST /actions/{id}/cancel

GET /actions/{id}/status
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "action": "SCHEDULE_CALLBACK",
  "score": 94,
  "confidence": 97,
  "execute_at": "2026-08-25T18:00:00-06:00",
  "reason_codes": [
    "CUSTOMER_REQUESTED_CALLBACK",
    "EVENING_PREFERENCE",
    "HIGH_INTENT"
  ]
}
```

---

# 13.60 Events

Publish:

```text
next_action.generated
next_action.authorized
next_action.executed
next_action.failed
next_action.cancelled

callback.scheduled
human_transfer.requested
nurture.started
lead.closed
```

---

# 13.61 Testing — happy paths

Test:

high intent → booking  
busy → callback  
price objection → alternative  
human requested → transfer  
no answer → retry according to policy  
not ready → nurture.

---

# 13.62 Test conflicts

Examples:

```text
High intent
+
DNC
```

Expected:

`STOP`, not call.

```text
Book intent
+
No available slots
```

Expected:

alternative/waitlist.

```text
Human requested
+
Human queue closed
```

Expected:

callback, not endless hold.

---

# 13.63 Test-data matrix

Build at least 500 decision scenarios.

Dimensions:

intent  
fit  
urgency  
price sensitivity  
policy  
preferences  
appointment status  
complaint state  
channel permissions  
human availability.

Each scenario gets expected action.

---

# 13.64 Edge case — customer asks for two actions

> "Email me the details and call tomorrow."

This can produce:

```text
ACTION_PLAN

1 SEND_EMAIL
2 SCHEDULE_CALLBACK
```

not choose only one.

---

# 13.65 Edge case — contradictory request

> "Don't call me again, but call me tomorrow."

This requires clarification because instructions conflict.

Do not infer.

---

# 13.66 Edge case — stale customer context

NextAI says:

`CALL`

but customer booked five seconds ago.

Execution service revalidates state before action.

This is mandatory.

---

# 13.67 Edge case — customer interacts on another channel

While AI call workflow waits, customer sends SMS:

> "I already booked."

Event cancels redundant next action.

Cross-channel coordination is essential.

---

# 13.68 Edge case — tool execution fails

Selected:

`SEND_EMAIL`

Email provider unavailable.

Options:

retry  
alternative channel if independently authorized  
create human task.

Do not silently mark successful.

---

# 13.69 Edge case — low-confidence language understanding

Instead of choosing an irreversible action:

```text
REQUEST_CLARIFICATION
```

or human transfer.

---

# 13.70 Edge case — customer refuses recommendation

Don't recommend identical offer again 20 seconds later.

Store:

```text
recommendation_rejected
```

and suppress repetitive presentation.

---

# 13.71 Edge case — repeated failed actions

Example:

3 transfer failures.

NextAI should not keep attempting transfer indefinitely.

Switch:

callback/human task.

---

# 13.72 Edge case — sensitive complaint

Immediately prioritize:

```text
ESCALATE
```

over marketing/upsell.

---

# 13.73 Monitoring

Track:

```text
next_actions_generated
actions_executed
action_success_rate
action_failure_rate
human_override_rate
no_action_rate
policy_block_rate
```

Business:

```text
conversion by action
booking by action
cost by action
complaints by action
DNC by action
```

---

# 13.74 Next-action confusion matrix

For manually reviewed decisions:

Compare:

```text
AI recommendation
vs
expert recommendation
```

Example:

| AI | Expert | Count |
|---|---|---:|
| Book | Book | 320 |
| Call | Book | 25 |
| Nurture | Call | 18 |

This exposes systematic problems.

---

# 13.75 Override tracking

Human may change:

```text
AI says CALLBACK
Human says CLOSE
```

Store:

```text
override_reason
```

Frequent overrides become model/rule improvement data.

---

# 13.76 KPI hierarchy

Don't optimize one metric.

Use:

### Customer

CSAT  
complaint rate  
opt-out.

### Business

booking  
conversion  
revenue.

### Operations

call volume  
human workload.

### Financial

cost/outcome.

### Governance

policy violations.

---

# 13.77 Guardrail metrics

An experiment may increase conversion 8% but also:

DNC +40%.

Reject or investigate.

Set guardrails around:

complaints  
DNC  
unsafe actions  
booking errors  
privacy incidents.

---

# 13.78 NextAI dashboard

Example:

```text
Today's Next Actions

Book now                 820
Requested callback       510
Send information         340
Human follow-up          190
Nurture                  680
No action                450
Policy blocked           120
```

Then show success rates.

---

# 13.79 Explainability dashboard

Click customer:

```text
ACTION:
Schedule callback

WHY:
Customer asked for callback
Preferred time: 18:00
Intent: 91
Contactability: 87

NOT SELECTED:
Book now — customer not ready
SMS — channel unavailable
```

Very useful for sales/support.

---

# 13.80 Audit

Store:

decision inputs  
candidates  
filters  
scores  
winner  
model/rule versions  
policy version  
executor result.

Reconstruct every significant automated action.

---

# 13.81 Security

Do not allow NextAI to directly execute arbitrary APIs.

Architecture:

```text
NextAI
 ↓
PolicyAI
 ↓
Action Orchestrator
 ↓
Tool Gateway
```

Use:

RBAC  
service identities  
signed actions  
idempotency  
audit.

---

Phase 13 is complete when:

```text
Action Catalog                   PASS
Candidate Generation            PASS
Policy Filtering                PASS
Action Ranking                  PASS

Priority Rules                  PASS

Booking Action                  PASS
Callback                        PASS
SMS/Email                       PASS
Human Transfer                  PASS
Alternative                     PASS
Nurture                         PASS
Wait / No Action                PASS
Close / Suppress                PASS

Multi-Action Plans              PASS
Dependencies                    PASS
Idempotency                     PASS
Execution Revalidation          PASS

Confidence Handling             PASS
Risk-Aware Decisions            PASS
Capacity Awareness              PASS
Cost Awareness                  PASS

Explainability                  PASS
Outcome Attribution             PASS
Override Tracking               PASS

Golden Decision Dataset         PASS
Regression Testing              PASS
Shadow Mode                     PASS
Experiment Framework            PASS

Security                        PASS
Audit                           PASS
Monitoring                      PASS
Dashboard                       PASS
UAT                             PASS
```

### Phase 13 output

For our running example:

```text
CUSTOMER
C10028

Intent:
94

Service Fit:
94

Need:
Physiotherapy

Constraint:
After 6 PM

NW Physio 6:30 PM

Candidate Actions
--------------------------------
Book now                  71

Call tomorrow             PASS
```
