## 🤖 Assistant — msg #95

# Phase 30 — DataAI + MDM + Customer 360 + Data Quality

This phase creates the **trusted data foundation** for the whole voice-agent platform. If customer, consent, lead, appointment, service, campaign, and interaction data are inconsistent, every downstream AI layer becomes unreliable.

The goal is:

> **One canonical customer/lead view, clear source-of-truth rules, strong identity resolution, measurable data quality, full lineage, and controlled synchronization across CRM, forms, campaigns, voice, booking, messaging, and analytics.**

## 30.1 Target architecture

```text
Forms / Ads / Website / CRM / Call / SMS
Booking / Email / Partner Imports
                 ↓
          Ingestion Gateway
                 ↓
       Schema + Quality Validation
                 ↓
          Identity Resolution
                 ↓
              MDM
                 ↓
          Golden Record
                 ↓
          Customer 360
                 ↓
 ┌───────────────┼────────────────┐
 ↓               ↓                ↓
CampaignAI     NeedAI          NextAI
ScoreAI        PolicyAI        MarketAI
ReportAI       FraudAI         FinAI
```

The important rule is that AI components should not independently invent their own customer representations.

## 30.2 Core data domains

Create canonical models for at least:

| Domain | Examples |
|---|---|
| Customer | person/customer entity |
| Lead | acquisition opportunity |
| Contact Point | phone/email |
| Consent | voice/SMS/email permissions |
| Preference | language/time/channel |
| Address/Location | service geography |
| Campaign | acquisition/outbound program |
| Interaction | call/SMS/email/form |
| Need | customer requirement |
| Appointment | booking |
| Service | clinic/service catalog |
| Provider | therapist/location/provider |
| Offer | pricing/package/promotion |
| Score | intent/conversion/contactability |
| Risk | fraud/security/customer risk |
| Journey | follow-up workflow |

## 30.3 Customer vs lead

Do not treat them as the same thing.

A **Customer** represents a person/entity.

A **Lead** represents an opportunity/context.

One customer can have:

```text
Customer C100
 ├── Lead L101: Physiotherapy
 ├── Lead L102: Massage
 └── Lead L103: Corporate wellness
```

This prevents duplicate customer profiles whenever someone submits another form.

## 30.4 Canonical customer model

Example:

```text
CUSTOMER

customer_id
tenant_id

first_name
last_name

preferred_language
timezone

status

created_at
updated_at
```

Keep this relatively small.

Put phones, emails, addresses and preferences in separate normalized entities.

## 30.5 Contact-point model

```text
CONTACT_POINT

contact_id
customer_id

type:
PHONE / EMAIL

normalized_value
masked_value

verified
verification_method

validity_status

source
first_seen
last_seen

is_primary
```

For phone:

store E.164 normalized value.

For email:

canonical normalized representation.

## 30.6 Phone normalization

Input examples:

```text
4035551234
(403) 555-1234
+1 403 555 1234
```

Canonical:

```text
+14035551234
```

But keep original value separately when useful for audit/source reconstruction.

## 30.7 Email normalization

Handle:

leading/trailing spaces  
case normalization where appropriate  
obvious formatting issues.

Do not aggressively alter local parts in ways that could change valid addresses.

## 30.8 Contact quality

Store:

```text
VALID
INVALID
SUSPECT
UNKNOWN
```

plus:

```text
last_verified_at
```

Do not permanently mark contact invalid after one temporary delivery failure.

## 30.9 Lead model

```text
LEAD

lead_id
customer_id
tenant_id

source
campaign_id

service_interest
lead_status

created_at
first_contact_at
qualified_at
converted_at

intent_score
quality_score
```

## 30.10 Lead status

Standardize:

```text
NEW
VALIDATED
ELIGIBLE
QUEUED
CONTACTED
CONNECTED
QUALIFIED
BOOKED
CONVERTED
NURTURE
CLOSED
DNC
INVALID
```

Avoid each application inventing its own status names.

## 30.11 Lead lifecycle events

Emit:

```text
lead.created
lead.validated
lead.qualified
lead.booked
lead.converted
lead.closed
```

This provides consistent analytics.

## 30.12 Identity resolution

Core problem:

```text
Form A:
Raj Sharma
403-555-1234

CRM:
R. Sharma
+1 403 555 1234

SMS:
raj@example.com
```

Are these the same customer?

Use multi-stage resolution.

## 30.13 Deterministic matching

Highest confidence rules first:

```text
verified_phone exact
verified_email exact
external_customer_id exact
```

These can often provide strong matches.

## 30.14 Probabilistic/fuzzy matching

For unresolved records consider:

name similarity  
phone similarity  
email similarity  
address  
context.

Output:

```text
MATCH
POSSIBLE_MATCH
NO_MATCH
```

Do not automatically merge low-confidence identities.

## 30.15 Match confidence

Example:

```text
verified phone exact     + high
email exact              + high
name fuzzy               + medium
address partial          + medium
```

Then:

```text
identity_confidence = 0.96
```

Threshold:

high → auto-link.

middle → manual/review.

low → new customer.

## 30.16 Identity graph

At scale:

```text
Customer
 ↔ Phone
 ↔ Email
 ↔ Address
 ↔ CRM ID
 ↔ Lead
 ↔ Device where legitimately used
```

This helps fraud detection and customer resolution.

Graph DB is optional; relational implementation works initially.

## 30.17 Golden record

MDM creates:

```text
GOLDEN_CUSTOMER
```

representing best-known current data.

It should not simply copy the newest source blindly.

## 30.18 Survivorship rules

For each attribute define source priority.

Example:

### Preferred language

```text
Customer explicitly confirmed
> CRM verified
> Form
> AI inference
```

### Phone

```text
Customer OTP verified
> CRM verified
> form submission
```

### Appointment

authoritative scheduler always wins.

## 30.19 Attribute-level source of truth

Different systems can own different fields.

| Attribute | Source of truth |
|---|---|
| Appointment | Scheduling system |
| Current price | Pricing service |
| Lead campaign | Campaign platform |
| Phone verification | Identity/contact service |
| DNC | Consent master |
| Preferred language | Customer-confirmed preference |
| Service catalog | Catalog service |

Avoid trying to make CRM authoritative for everything.

## 30.20 Data provenance

Every important value should carry:

```text
value
source
source_record_id
observed_at
confidence
verification_status
```

Example:

```text
preferred_language = Punjabi
source = CALL-821
source_type = CUSTOMER_EXPLICIT
confidence = 1.0
```

## 30.21 Temporal history

Do not overwrite without history.

Customer:

```text
Aug 1: preferred call time = morning
Aug 24: preferred call time = evening
```

Maintain:

```text
valid_from
valid_to
```

This helps audit and personalization.

## 30.22 Bitemporal model for critical data

For advanced requirements consider:

**valid time**

when fact was true.

**system time**

when system learned it.

This is especially useful for consent and governance investigations.

## 30.23 Consent master data

Keep centrally governed:

```text
CONSENT

customer_id
channel
purpose
status

source
captured_at
effective_at
expires_at

evidence
version
```

Channels:

voice  
SMS  
email  
WhatsApp.

Purposes can differ.

## 30.24 DNC master

DNC must be a high-authority dataset.

```text
DNC

customer_id
contact_id
channel
scope
reason
effective_at
source
```

Systems should consume this rather than maintain independent suppression lists only.

## 30.25 Preference master

Track:

```text
language
contact_channel
contact_time
appointment_time
location
delivery_mode
```

with:

source  
confidence  
effective dates.

## 30.26 Explicit vs inferred data

Critical distinction:

```text
CUSTOMER_EXPLICIT
CUSTOMER_CONFIRMED
SYSTEM_VERIFIED
AI_INFERRED
```

Never display AI inference as customer-confirmed fact.

## 30.27 Inferred data TTL

Example:

```text
possible_price_sensitivity
```

may expire after 30 or 90 days.

Do not persist weak inferred characteristics indefinitely.

## 30.28 Customer 360

The operational Customer 360 should consolidate:

```text
Identity
Contact points
Consent/DNC
Preferences
Active leads
Needs
Appointments
Interactions
Campaign history
Scores
Open tasks
Latest outcome
```

But access should remain role-based.

## 30.29 Customer 360 is not one giant table

Bad:

```text
CUSTOMER_ALL_FIELDS
```

with hundreds of columns.

Better:

domain tables + APIs/views.

This improves governance and scalability.

## 30.30 Customer 360 API

Potential:

```text
GET /customers/{id}

GET /customers/{id}/contacts
GET /customers/{id}/preferences
GET /customers/{id}/consents
GET /customers/{id}/leads
GET /customers/{id}/needs
GET /customers/{id}/interactions
GET /customers/{id}/appointments
```

Create purpose-specific views.

## 30.31 Agent-specific customer view

Voice AI receives:

```text
GET /customers/{id}/context?purpose=OUTBOUND_BOOKING
```

Return only:

first name  
preferred language  
service interest  
callback reason  
relevant appointment state.

Not full Customer 360.

## 30.32 Data contract

Each domain publishes schema contract.

Example:

```text
CustomerCreated.v2
```

Fields have:

name  
type  
required/optional  
meaning  
PII classification.

Use schema registry when event scale warrants it.

## 30.33 Schema evolution

Prefer backward-compatible changes.

Safe:

add optional field.

Riskier:

rename/remove field.

Version breaking changes.

## 30.34 Schema validation

At ingestion:

```text
schema valid?
required fields?
types?
enum?
date format?
```

Invalid records go to:

```text
QUARANTINE
```

not directly into production.

## 30.35 Data-quality dimensions

At minimum:

```text
Completeness
Accuracy
Validity
Consistency
Uniqueness
Timeliness
Integrity
```

Add:

lineage/provenance.

## 30.36 Completeness

Example:

Lead requires:

```text
phone OR email
service interest
source
```

Measure:

```text
% leads missing required attributes
```

## 30.37 Accuracy

More difficult.

Check against verified sources.

Example:

appointment date in CRM

vs authoritative scheduler.

Mismatch indicates accuracy problem.

## 30.38 Validity

Examples:

phone format  
email format  
valid service ID  
valid campaign ID.

## 30.39 Consistency

Example:

CRM:

appointment Tuesday 6 PM.

Scheduler:

Thursday 6 PM.

This is consistency failure.

Authoritative source determines correction.

## 30.40 Uniqueness

Track:

duplicate customer  
duplicate lead  
duplicate appointment  
duplicate event.

Use canonical identifiers/idempotency.

## 30.41 Timeliness

Examples:

CRM update delay  
consent propagation delay  
appointment synchronization delay.

For DNC:

timeliness requirement is particularly strict.

## 30.42 Referential integrity

Lead.customer_id must reference valid customer.

Appointment.service_id must reference valid service.

Campaign references valid tenant.

Don't leave orphan data silently.

## 30.43 Data-quality score

For each dataset:

```text
DQ_SCORE

Completeness
Validity
Consistency
Uniqueness
Timeliness
```

But also surface critical errors separately.

A 98% score cannot hide one DNC synchronization failure.

## 30.44 Critical data elements

Define CDEs.

Examples:

```text
customer_id
phone
DNC
consent
appointment date/time
service
price
```

Give them stricter quality controls.

## 30.45 Data-quality rules

Example:

```text
IF appointment.status = BOOKED
THEN appointment_id IS NOT NULL
```

```text
IF consent.status = WITHDRAWN
THEN effective_at IS NOT NULL
```

```text
phone must conform to E.164
```

## 30.46 Rule severity

```text
CRITICAL
HIGH
MEDIUM
LOW
```

Critical:

DNC missing.

Low:

optional marketing tag missing.

## 30.47 Data quarantine

Invalid incoming records:

```text
INGEST
 ↓
VALIDATE
 ↓
QUARANTINE
```

Store:

reason  
source  
record  
timestamp.

Operations can fix/reprocess.

## 30.48 Data-quality repair

Possible:

automatic normalization  
source replay  
manual correction.

Never silently fabricate missing data.

## 30.49 Source-system trust score

Track quality per source:

```text
Website form     96
CRM import       91
Affiliate-A      63
```

This can influence MDM survivorship and FraudAI.

## 30.50 CDC

Use Change Data Capture for systems that support it.

Example:

CRM/database:

```text
change
 ↓
CDC
 ↓
event
 ↓
Customer 360
```

Potential tools:

Debezium  
native cloud CDC.

## 30.51 CDC vs polling

Prefer event/CDC when feasible for:

high-value, high-change data.

Polling can still be reasonable for smaller/simple external systems.

## 30.52 Event ordering

Customer preference updates may arrive out of order.

Use:

event time  
version number.

Avoid stale event overwriting newer preference.

## 30.53 Optimistic locking

For mutable master data:

```text
record_version
```

Update only if expected version matches.

Prevent lost updates.

## 30.54 Conflict resolution

Two sources update same attribute simultaneously.

Use survivorship rules and provenance.

If ambiguity remains:

```text
CONFLICT_REVIEW
```

rather than arbitrary overwrite.

## 30.55 Data reconciliation

Compare:

Customer DB  
CRM  
Booking  
Consent systems.

Scheduled reconciliation detects silent drift.

## 30.56 Appointment reconciliation

Example:

Scheduler:

APT-201 = BOOKED.

CRM:

no appointment.

Action:

enqueue CRM repair.

Do not modify scheduler merely to match CRM.

## 30.57 Contact reconciliation

Phone service says:

invalid.

Customer later successfully verifies.

Latest verified evidence wins.

## 30.58 Data lineage

Track:

```text
source
→ ingestion
→ normalization
→ MDM
→ feature
→ model
→ decision
```

This supports ExplainAI/GovernAI.

## 30.59 OpenLineage/DataHub

At scale consider:

OpenLineage  
DataHub  
OpenMetadata

for technical lineage/catalog.

For MVP, structured metadata tables may suffice.

## 30.60 Data catalog

Register:

datasets  
tables  
fields  
owners  
classification  
quality.

Users should know:

what data means  
where it comes from  
who owns it.

## 30.61 Business glossary

Define:

Lead  
Qualified Lead  
Customer  
Conversion  
DNC  
Appointment.

This avoids reporting disagreement.

## 30.62 Data ownership

Example:

| Domain | Owner |
|---|---|
| Customer | Customer Ops |
| Consent | Compliance |
| Service catalog | Product/Ops |
| Appointment | Clinic operations |
| Campaign | Marketing |
| AI features | AI/Data team |

Technical team is not automatically business-data owner.

## 30.63 Data steward

Each critical domain should have a steward responsible for:

definitions  
quality  
issue resolution.

## 30.64 Master vs transaction data

### Master data

Customer  
Service  
Provider  
Location  
Campaign configuration.

### Transaction data

Calls  
Messages  
Bookings  
Payments  
Interactions.

Treat differently.

## 30.65 Reference data

Examples:

```text
language codes
country codes
service categories
call outcomes
objection taxonomy
```

Version and govern centrally.

## 30.66 Transaction identifiers

Every transaction gets globally unique internal ID.

Example:

```text
call_id
appointment_id
tool_call_id
message_id
```

Never depend solely on provider-specific IDs.

## 30.67 Provider ID mapping

Store:

```text
internal_call_id
provider
provider_call_id
```

This supports provider abstraction.

## 30.68 Data lake/warehouse flow

Operational:

PostgreSQL.

Analytics:

```text
Operational DB
   ↓
CDC/ELT
   ↓
Warehouse/Lakehouse
```

Do not run heavy BI against critical booking DB at scale.

## 30.69 Bronze / Silver / Gold

For a larger lakehouse:

### Bronze

raw events.

### Silver

cleaned/normalized.

### Gold

analytics-ready business models.

Useful if Databricks/Snowflake-like architecture becomes necessary.

## 30.70 Raw data immutability

Where policy permits, retain raw event representation for reconciliation/audit.

Do not allow raw store to become uncontrolled long-term sensitive-data dump.

Retention still applies.

## 30.71 Feature store

For ML models:

```text
FEATURE_STORE
```

Examples:

days_since_last_contact  
previous_answer_rate  
service_fit.

Need:

online/offline consistency.

Feast or managed equivalent later.

## 30.72 Feature lineage

Every feature:

```text
feature_name
source
transformation
version
owner
```

ScoreAI explanation depends on this.

## 30.73 Online/offline skew

Training calculation:

```text
contact_count_30d
```

must match production calculation.

Otherwise model works offline but fails live.

Test feature parity.

## 30.74 Point-in-time joins

Training data must only use information available at prediction time.

Avoid:

future appointment status  
future conversion

as model features.

This is leakage.

## 30.75 Data freshness

Store:

```text
last_updated_at
source_updated_at
```

PolicyAI can require maximum age.

Example:

DNC cache older than threshold:

fail closed/reload.

## 30.76 Cache strategy

Cache:

service metadata  
static configuration.

Avoid stale cache for:

DNC  
consent  
live availability.

Use event-driven invalidation.

## 30.77 Privacy classification

Field-level metadata:

```text
PII
PHI
INTERNAL
PUBLIC
```

Data APIs apply masking/access accordingly.

## 30.78 Data minimization

Customer 360 may know 100 things.

Voice agent may need 5.

Analytics may need zero direct identifiers.

Create purpose-specific projections.

## 30.79 Retention by domain

Example categories:

lead  
call metadata  
recording  
transcript  
customer preferences  
analytics events.

Each gets defined retention rules.

## 30.80 Right-to-delete propagation

Deletion request:

```text
Customer Master
 ↓
CRM
 ↓
Conversation data
 ↓
Analytics
 ↓
Voice providers
```

Track completion.

## 30.81 De-identification for analytics

Analytics tables can replace:

customer ID

with:

pseudonymous analytics ID.

Avoid carrying phone/email into every fact table.

## 30.82 Synthetic test data

Create fake:

customers  
phones  
emails  
consents  
appointments.

Do not copy raw production customer data into dev environments.

## 30.83 Data observability

Monitor:

schema changes  
null rate  
volume  
distribution  
freshness  
duplicates.

Tools later could include:

Great Expectations  
Soda  
Monte Carlo-like commercial tools.

Open-source-first:

Great Expectations/Soda + custom metrics.

## 30.84 Distribution drift

Example:

Normally:

Hindi leads = 25%.

Today:

2%.

Could be:

campaign change

or ingestion problem.

Alert only after context/baseline consideration.

## 30.85 Volume anomaly

Normal:

5,000 leads/day.

Today:

50.

Check source pipeline.

This can look like business decline but be data outage.

## 30.86 Freshness anomaly

CRM CDC stopped 4 hours ago.

Alert:

```text
CRM_DATA_STALE
```

Before staff/AI use outdated records.

## 30.87 Data-quality incident

Lifecycle:

```text
Detect
→ quarantine/contain
→ identify source
→ repair
→ replay
→ reconcile
→ RCA
→ add rule
```

## 30.88 Data issue → AI impact

Example:

Language field mapped incorrectly.

Consequences:

wrong voice route  
poor experience.

DataAI should publish impact to:

RouteAI  
QualityAI  
RiskAI.

## 30.89 Data issue blast radius

GovernAI dependency graph should identify:

which campaigns/models/reports use affected field.

This allows targeted mitigation.

## 30.90 Data contract tests

Before producer changes schema:

run consumer contract tests.

This prevents surprise downstream failures.

## 30.91 Data versioning

Schema:

v1 → v2.

Taxonomy:

v4 → v5.

Reference data:

versioned.

Historical decisions store version used.

## 30.92 Edge case — one phone belongs to family

Do not automatically merge all people sharing it.

Use:

shared contact relationship.

Example:

```text
CONTACT_POINT
phone = X

linked customers:
parent
child
```

where appropriate and minimally necessary.

## 30.93 Edge case — customer changes phone

Keep previous contact history.

Mark:

old inactive  
new primary.

Don't rewrite historical call records.

## 30.94 Edge case — recycled phone number

A phone may later belong to another person.

Identity resolution must use recency/verification.

Do not assume phone = permanent person identity.

## 30.95 Edge case — shared corporate email

Example:

```text
info@company.com
```

May map to organization, not individual.

Support:

PERSON

and:

ORGANIZATION

entities for B2B.

## 30.96 Edge case — typo corrected

Customer initially enters:

```text
raj@gmial.com
```

then corrects it.

Keep audit provenance, but use verified corrected address as current golden value.

## 30.97 Edge case — AI inference conflicts with explicit customer statement

AI:

language likely Hindi.

Customer:

Punjabi.

Customer explicit wins.

## 30.98 Edge case — CRM outdated

CRM says:

morning.

Customer explicitly says:

evening today.

Preference master updates.

CRM receives sync later.

Do not let stale CRM overwrite it.

## 30.99 Edge case — duplicate appointment IDs from providers

Internal appointment ID stays unique.

Provider-specific ID stored in mapping table.

## 30.100 Edge case — source deleted

If partner source disappears, provenance should still identify historical source ID/type.

## 30.101 Edge case — data arrives before customer identity resolved

Store event under temporary identity:

```text
IDENTITY_PENDING
```

Then link after resolution.

Avoid dropping events.

## 30.102 Edge case — merge customers incorrectly

Support controlled:

```text
UNMERGE
```

with audit.

False merges can be extremely harmful.

## 30.103 Merge operation

Before merge:

show candidate records  
evidence  
affected leads/appointments.

High-risk merge may require human review.

## 30.104 Split operation

If records were wrongly merged:

create separate canonical IDs.

Reassign affected records.

Maintain full audit.

## 30.105 MDM review queue

Cases:

possible duplicate  
identity conflict  
shared contact  
source disagreement.

Reviewer can:

merge  
keep separate  
link relationship.

# Phase 31 — CampaignAI + Acquisition Orchestration

This phase turns leads into **controlled, prioritized, policy-aware outbound journeys**.

The goal is:

> **Choose who to contact, why, when, through which channel, with which agent, under what campaign, at what cost, and when to stop.**

## 31.1 Target architecture

```text
Lead Sources
  ↓
Form / CRM / Ads / Partner / Referral
  ↓
DataAI + FraudAI
  ↓
Consent / DNC / PolicyAI
  ↓
Campaign Eligibility
  ↓
Segmentation
  ↓
Lead Priority / ScoreAI
  ↓
Contact Strategy
  ↓
ChannelAI
  ↓
Best-Time / Callback Logic
  ↓
Provider + Agent Route
  ↓
Outbound Job Queue
  ↓
Pre-Dial Revalidation
  ↓
Voice Call / SMS / Email
  ↓
Outcome
  ↓
NextAI / FollowUpAI
  ↓
Campaign Learning
```

---

# 31.2 Campaign objects

Do not create campaigns as simple lists of phone numbers.

Create:

```text
CAMPAIGN

campaign_id
tenant_id

name
purpose
service_id

start_date
end_date

audience_definition
exclusion_definition

channel_strategy
agent_profile

contact_policy
attempt_policy

budget
priority

experiment_id

status

DRAFT
REVIEW
APPROVED
ACTIVE
PAUSED
COMPLETED
CANCELLED
```

---

# 31.3 Campaign types

Support separate campaign types.

| Campaign | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Immediate Lead Callback | Call new form submissions quickly |
| Requested Callback | Customer explicitly requested contact |
| Appointment Conversion | High-intent unbooked lead |
| No-Answer Recovery | Retry unanswered leads |
| Quote Follow-up | Follow up after pricing discussion |
| Nurture | Longer-cycle prospects |
| Reactivation | Previously interested customers |
| Appointment Reminder | Transactional |
| No-Show Recovery | Reschedule missed appointment |
| Corporate Prospecting | B2B |
| Service Launch | New offering |
| Research Campaign | Structured customer feedback |

Different purposes need different contact policies.

---

# 31.4 Lead-source ingestion

Sources may include:

```text
Website form
Landing page
Google Ads
Meta Lead Forms
Instagram
Facebook
LinkedIn
Referral
CRM
CSV import
Partner
Call-in request
WhatsApp
```

Normalize into:

```text
lead.created
```

before campaign logic.

---

# 31.5 Form → campaign flow

Example:

```text
Website Form
   ↓
Lead Created
   ↓
Data Quality
   ↓
Fraud Screen
   ↓
Identity Resolution
   ↓
Consent/Policy
   ↓
Campaign Eligibility
   ↓
ScoreAI
   ↓
Outbound Job
```

Avoid triggering a call directly from the public form without intermediate checks.

---

# 31.6 Campaign eligibility

For each lead evaluate:

```text
correct tenant?
campaign active?
service relevant?
contact valid?
DNC clear?
channel permitted?
calling window valid?
frequency acceptable?
fraud risk acceptable?
lead not already converted?
appointment not already booked?
```

Then:

```text
ELIGIBLE
INELIGIBLE
REVIEW
DEFER
```

---

# 31.7 Exclusion rules

Example:

```text
DNC
Already booked
Already converted
Complaint active
Fraud blocked
No valid phone
Contact frequency exceeded
Explicitly requested future date
Campaign previously completed
```

Exclusion is as important as inclusion.

---

# 31.8 Audience builder

Campaign manager should be able to define:

```text
Service = Physiotherapy
AND
Location = NW
AND
Lead age < 48 hours
AND
Appointment = none
AND
Intent > 60
```

But audience builder must still pass every selected lead through PolicyAI.

---

# 31.9 Segment integration

Use SegmentAI dimensions such as:

```text
HIGH_INTENT
PRICE_RESEARCHER
CALLBACK_REQUESTED
EVENING_PREFERRED
CORPORATE
RETURNING_CUSTOMER
```

Campaigns can target legitimate business segments.

Avoid sensitive-trait targeting.

---

# 31.10 Lead priority

Prioritize with ScoreAI + business rules.

Example:

```text
Requested callback       +50
Specific appointment     +35
High intent              +25
Recent submission        +20
Valid phone              +10
Price objection          -10
Already contacted today  -30
```

Output:

```text
priority_score = 87
```

---

# 31.11 Priority classes

Simplify operationally:

```text
P0 CUSTOMER-REQUESTED
P1 HIGH INTENT
P2 NORMAL LEAD
P3 NURTURE
```

Customer-requested callbacks should usually outrank generic marketing.

---

# 31.12 Lead aging

Lead value often changes with time.

Track:

```text
minutes_since_submission
hours_since_submission
days_since_last_response
```

But do not assume every lead should be contacted instantly.

Respect requested contact time and policy.

---

# 31.13 Speed-to-lead

For applicable inbound leads measure:

```text
form_submit_time
first_attempt_time
```

Metric:

```text
SPEED_TO_LEAD
```

Break down conversion by delay.

Example:

```text
0–5 min
5–30 min
30–120 min
same day
next day
```

This gives your own evidence for optimal response time.

---

# 31.14 Explicit callback time overrides prediction

Customer writes:

> “Please call me after 6.”

Do not call at 2 PM because a model predicts higher conversion.

Store:

```text
customer_requested_window
```

as hard constraint.

---

# 31.15 Best-time-to-call

For customers without explicit preference, calculate from:

```text
previous answer history
time zone
lead source
service
campaign
historical response rates
```

Start rule-based.

Later use predictive models.

---

# 31.16 Best-time model

Potential target:

```text
P(answer | hour, weekday, customer context)
```

Output:

```text
18:00–19:00 = .72
19:00–20:00 = .66
12:00–13:00 = .34
```

Policy and frequency filters still override it.

---

# 31.17 Time zone

Every job must use customer/service timezone.

Store:

```text
customer_timezone
campaign_timezone
```

Do not use server UTC as customer calling time.

---

# 31.18 Contact window engine

Before scheduling:

```text
preferred window
+
business policy
+
campaign policy
+
timezone
```

intersect into:

```text
VALID_CONTACT_WINDOW
```

If no valid intersection:

defer/human review.

---

# 31.19 Contact-pressure engine

Centralize frequency across campaigns.

Example:

Customer:

```text
Call yesterday
SMS today
Email today
```

Campaign B should know that.

Maintain:

```text
CONTACT_LEDGER
```

---

# 31.20 Contact ledger

```text
contact_event_id
customer_id

channel
purpose
campaign_id

timestamp
outcome
```

Use for:

frequency limits  
fatigue scoring  
audit.

---

# 31.21 Contact-pressure score

Possible factors:

```text
calls last 24h
calls last 7d
messages last 24h
unanswered attempts
complaints
recent opt-out behavior
```

Output:

```text
LOW
MEDIUM
HIGH
EXCESSIVE
```

High pressure can result in:

```text
WAIT
```

---

# 31.22 Attempt policy

Each campaign defines:

```text
max_attempts
minimum_gap
maximum_age
voicemail_policy
channel_fallback
```

Example:

```text
attempt 1 → voice
attempt 2 → voice later
attempt 3 → SMS if allowed
```

Do not hardcode one attempt policy globally.

---

# 31.23 No-answer strategy

```text
Call Attempt
   ↓
NO ANSWER
   ↓
Attempt Count
   ↓
Contact Pressure
   ↓
Best Time
   ↓
Channel Eligibility
```

Possible:

```text
retry
SMS
email
wait
close
```

---

# 31.24 Wrong-number outcome

Immediately mark:

```text
phone_status = SUSPECT / WRONG_PERSON
```

depending evidence.

Do not continue campaign attempts on that number until resolved.

---

# 31.25 “Never requested this”

Critical acquisition-quality event.

Actions:

```text
stop current sales flow
capture source
suppress as appropriate
flag lead/source
FraudAI investigation
```

This feeds lead-source reputation.

---

# 31.26 Campaign queue

Create durable outbound jobs:

```text
OUTBOUND_JOB

job_id
campaign_id
customer_id
lead_id

priority
scheduled_for

agent_profile
route_profile

status
```

Statuses:

```text
PENDING
ELIGIBILITY_CHECK
READY
DISPATCHING
STARTED
COMPLETED
DEFERRED
BLOCKED
CANCELLED
```

---

# 31.27 Queue partitioning

Partition by:

tenant  
campaign  
priority

where necessary.

Prevent one huge tenant from starving others.

---

# 31.28 Fair scheduling

At SaaS scale:

```text
Tenant A 100k jobs
Tenant B 500 jobs
```

Don't let A consume all worker capacity.

Use quotas/weighted scheduling.

---

# 31.29 Campaign concurrency

Set:

```text
max_concurrent_calls
calls_per_minute
```

by:

tenant  
campaign  
provider.

Protect:

telephony  
voice providers  
clinic staff.

---

# 31.30 Human-capacity-aware campaigns

Suppose:

campaign can generate 200 transfers/hour.

Clinic has capacity for 10.

CampaignAI should reduce call rate.

Input from HumanOps:

```text
available_human_capacity
```

---

# 31.31 Appointment-capacity-aware campaigns

If Saturday physio is fully booked:

should you continue promoting Saturday appointments aggressively?

CampaignAI can use service capacity.

Possible actions:

pause specific offer  
promote alternative  
waitlist.

---

# 31.32 Budget-aware campaigns

FinAI provides:

```text
campaign_budget_remaining
cost_per_call
cost_per_booking
```

CampaignAI can:

continue  
throttle  
pause.

Policy/customer-requested interactions still follow their own priority rules.

---

# 31.33 Campaign pacing

Avoid spending entire daily budget in first hour.

Possible pacing:

```text
EVEN
ACCELERATED
DEMAND_BASED
```

Use hourly budget allocation.

---

# 31.34 Provider capacity

RouteAI may say:

Provider A best.

But A at concurrency limit.

CampaignAI/RouteAI selects next approved route or throttles.

---

# 31.35 Pre-dial revalidation

This is mandatory.

Immediately before dialing, recheck:

```text
DNC
consent
time window
appointment
customer status
campaign active
fraud status
contact pressure
budget
```

A lead may have changed since it entered queue.

---

# 31.36 Stale outbound job

Example:

Lead queued at 10 AM.

At 2 PM customer books online.

Job scheduled 6 PM.

Pre-dial:

```text
appointment exists
```

Cancel sales call.

---

# 31.37 Policy snapshot vs live state

Keep initial eligibility evidence for audit.

But use **live authoritative state** for execution authorization.

This protects against stale consent/DNC.

---

# 31.38 Dial request

Canonical:

```text
CREATE_CALL

job_id
customer_id
phone_token
campaign_id
agent_id
language
reason
```

Tool/voice gateway then resolves authorized contact data.

Avoid putting raw phone numbers in unnecessary queue payloads.

---

# 31.39 Agent selection

Campaign determines business profile:

```text
PHYSIO_LEAD_AGENT
```

RouteAI then chooses provider/voice/model configuration.

Keep business agent definition separate from infrastructure provider.

---

# 31.40 Language selection

Use:

customer-confirmed preference

then fallback.

If language uncertain:

agent can ask.

Do not infer ethnicity.

---

# 31.41 Script selection

Campaign passes:

```text
campaign_context
reason_for_call
offer
```

ConversationAI selects approved flow.

No arbitrary script pasted directly into voice-provider console.

---

# 31.42 Campaign context

Example:

```text
campaign:
NEW_LEAD_CALLBACK

reason:
Customer submitted physiotherapy form

allowed_offer:
FREE_INITIAL_INFORMATION_SESSION

primary_CTA:
BOOK_CONSULTATION
```

Agent stays within campaign scope while still discovering adjacent needs appropriately.

---

# 31.43 Offer selection

OfferAI validates:

active  
eligible  
budget  
location  
service.

Campaign should never rely on static old offer text.

---

# 31.44 Outbound call outcome

Normalize:

```text
CONNECTED
NO_ANSWER
BUSY
VOICEMAIL
WRONG_NUMBER
FAILED
```

Then conversation disposition:

```text
BOOKED
CALLBACK
QUALIFIED
NURTURE
NOT_INTERESTED
DNC
HUMAN_TRANSFER
```

Keep telephony outcome and business outcome separate.

---

# 31.45 Campaign state update

After every outcome:

```text
campaign_customer_state
```

updates.

Avoid reprocessing the same customer as if nothing happened.

---

# 31.46 Campaign-member model

```text
CAMPAIGN_MEMBER

campaign_id
customer_id
lead_id

eligibility

priority

attempt_count
last_attempt
next_attempt

current_status
final_outcome
```

---

# 31.47 Campaign exit conditions

Examples:

```text
appointment booked
converted
DNC
customer declines
max attempts reached
campaign expired
service unavailable
complaint
```

Every member should eventually exit.

---

# 31.48 Cross-campaign conflicts

Customer enters:

```text
Physio Sales Campaign
```

and:

```text
Appointment Reminder
```

at same time.

Priority:

transactional reminder normally suppresses conflicting sales contact.

Use journey/campaign conflict engine.

---

# 31.49 Campaign hierarchy

Suggested:

```text
Safety/Compliance
      ↓
Transactional
      ↓
Customer-requested
      ↓
Service follow-up
      ↓
Sales
      ↓
Nurture
      ↓
General marketing
```

Lower priority should not interfere with higher.

---

# 31.50 Customer suppression period

After certain events:

complaint  
decline  
recent long conversation.

Set:

```text
cooldown_until
```

Do not immediately place customer into another campaign.

---

# 31.51 Campaign-level kill switch

Operations needs:

```text
PAUSE_CAMPAIGN
```

Instantly stops new jobs.

Active calls handled according to runbook.

---

# 31.52 Source kill switch

If Affiliate A starts sending bad leads:

```text
PAUSE_SOURCE
```

without stopping Google/referral campaigns.

---

# 31.53 Agent kill switch

If specific agent version fails:

Route new campaign calls to previous approved version or pause.

GovernAI controls.

---

# 31.54 Language kill switch

If Punjabi voice quality collapses:

pause Punjabi automated calling.

Possible:

human route  
alternate approved provider.

---

# 31.55 Provider kill switch

If provider outage or quality issue:

RouteAI removes provider.

Campaign continues where fallback capacity permits.

---

# 31.56 Campaign experiment cells

Support:

```text
CONTROL
TREATMENT_A
TREATMENT_B
```

Random assignment where appropriate.

Test:

opening  
callback timing  
SMS before call  
offer.

---

# 31.57 Experiment assignment

Store assignment permanently:

```text
experiment_id
variant
assigned_at
```

Avoid customer switching variants midway.

---

# 31.58 Experiment exclusions

Do not experiment on:

DNC  
critical compliance disclosure  
unsafe clinical pathways.

Some behaviors are not appropriate experimental variables.

---

# 31.59 Experiment metrics

Measure:

connect  
engagement  
booking  
attendance  
customer satisfaction  
DNC  
complaints  
cost.

Not conversion alone.

---

# 31.60 Guardrail metrics

Example:

Variant B booking +7%

but DNC +40%.

Experiment should be rejected/paused.

---

# 31.61 Minimum sample

Avoid declaring winner after 20 calls.

ExperimentAI defines:

minimum sample  
statistical approach  
guardrails.

---

# 31.62 Holdout groups

For some campaigns maintain:

```text
NO_CONTACT_CONTROL
```

where permissible/appropriate.

This helps estimate true incremental effect rather than attribution only.

---

# 31.63 Uplift modeling

Later:

predict who benefits from contact.

Potential treatments:

voice  
SMS  
no contact.

This avoids calling customers who would convert anyway.

Use only after mature experimentation.

---

# 31.64 Campaign optimization objective

Conceptually:

```text
Expected Incremental Contribution
-
Contact Cost
-
Customer Friction
-
Risk
```

subject to:

policy  
capacity  
budget.

---

# 31.65 Campaign-level lead scoring

Some segments may have high customer-level intent but poor service capacity.

Campaign priority considers both:

lead value

and:

business ability to serve.

---

# 31.66 Capacity-aware priority

Example:

Dental has 100 open slots.

Physio has 3.

CampaignAI may allocate more volume to dental rather than create frustrated physio leads.

Do not hide demand; MarketAI still reports shortage.

---

# 31.67 Campaign forecast

Before launch estimate:

eligible leads
expected attempts
connect rate
average minutes
human transfer
appointments
cost

# 31.68 Pre-launch simulation

Example:

10,000 leads
70% eligible
1.6 attempts
55% connect
4 min average

minutes

human transfers  
cost.

Critical:

# 31.88 Campaign test dataset

Create scenarios varying:

consent  
DNC

---

# 31.89 Edge case — customer enters two identical campaigns

Conflict engine should merge/suppress duplication.

One contact, not two calls.

---

# 31.90 Edge case — campaign paused after jobs queued

Pre-dial check:

```text
campaign active? NO
```

Cancel/defer queued jobs.

---

# 31.91 Edge case — DNC added milliseconds before call

Execution-time authoritative check must block call where required.

Avoid relying solely on earlier queue check.

---

# 31.92 Edge case — budget exhausted while queue populated

Stop new discretionary dispatch.

Keep jobs queued/cancel according to campaign policy.

---

# 31.93 Edge case — human queue overloaded mid-campaign

Throttle call creation if campaign generates high transfer demand.

---

# 31.94 Edge case — provider suddenly expensive

FinAI raises anomaly.

RouteAI shifts traffic or CampaignAI throttles if economics unacceptable.

Quality/risk checks first.

---

# 31.95 Edge case — customer requests earlier callback

Update existing scheduled job rather than create another one.

Use dedupe/idempotency.

---

# 31.96 Edge case — callback time missed

Do not silently treat as ordinary retry.

Create:

```text
CALLBACK_SLA_MISSED
```

and recovery workflow.

---

# 31.97 Edge case — user says “not now”

Distinguish:

temporary defer

from:

not interested

from:

DNC.

ConversationAI + NextAI must capture correct disposition.

---

# 31.98 Edge case — voicemail detection wrong

Do not count false voicemail as customer rejection.

Provider/voice QA should monitor detection accuracy.

---

# 31.99 Edge case — campaign ends while conversation active

Let active call finish safely.

Block new calls.

---

# 31.100 Edge case — customer books during active call through another channel

Before final booking:

recheck appointment state.

Avoid duplicate booking.

---

# 31.101 Security

Protect campaign creation/activation.

Require:

RBAC  
approval  
tenant isolation  
audit.

A compromised campaign interface could launch thousands of calls.

---

# 31.102 Campaign budget abuse

Campaign activation should require budget authorization.

Set absolute volume/concurrency caps.

Never trust UI values alone.

---

# 31.103 Audit

Record:

who created campaign  
who approved  
audience definition  
policy version  
agent version  
budget  
changes  
pause/resume.

---

# 31.104 Campaign quality gate

Before scaling:

```text
Critical policy failures = 0
Critical booking errors = 0
Voice quality >= threshold
Complaint/DNC within guardrails
Provider health acceptable
```

# Phase 32 — SegmentAI: Dynamic Customer Segmentation + Lifecycle + Propensity Framework

This phase organizes customers into **operationally useful, explainable, dynamic segments** that CampaignAI, NextAI, RecommendAI, MarketAI, and HumanOps can act on.

The principle is:

> **Segment by current need, behavior, intent, lifecycle, and service context — not by crude stereotypes or permanent personality labels.**

## 32.1 Target architecture

```text
Customer 360
   +
Lead Data
   +
Needs
   +
Preferences
   +
Interactions
   +
Campaign History
   +
Appointments
   +
Scores
        ↓
   SegmentAI
        ↓
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ Lifecycle Segments           │
│ Intent Segments              │
│ Need Segments                │
│ Service Segments             │
│ Timing Segments              │
│ Channel Segments             │
│ Engagement Segments          │
│ Value / Propensity Segments  │
│ Operational Segments         │
└──────────────────────────────┘
        ↓
CampaignAI / NextAI / RecommendAI
```

## 32.2 Segment families

| Family | Examples |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | New lead, qualified, booked, dormant |
| Intent | High, medium, low |
| Need | Physio, dental, massage |
| Timing | Immediate, evening, weekend, future |
| Channel | Voice-preferring, SMS-preferring |
| Engagement | Engaged, no-answer, inactive |
| Objection | Price, trust, timing |
| Service Fit | Strong match, partial match, no match |
| Journey | Callback requested, nurture, reactivation |
| Operational | Human-required, AI-capable |
| Propensity | Likely to book, likely to answer |

A customer may belong to several segments simultaneously.

## 32.3 Do not create one mega-segment

Bad:

```text
HIGH_VALUE_HINDI_EVENING_PRICE_SENSITIVE_PHYSIO_CUSTOMER
```

Better:

```text
Intent = HIGH
Need = PHYSIOTHERAPY
Preferred Contact Window = EVENING
Language Preference = HINDI
Primary Objection = PRICE
```

Composable dimensions are much easier to govern.

## 32.4 Segment record

```text
CUSTOMER_SEGMENT

segment_membership_id
customer_id
segment_id

value

source
confidence

effective_from
effective_until

model_or_rule_version
```

## 32.5 Segment definition

```text
SEGMENT

segment_id
name
category

definition
eligibility_logic

data_inputs[]
owner

version
status
```

## 32.6 Lifecycle model

Recommended core stages:

```text
PROSPECT
   ↓
LEAD
   ↓
VALIDATED
   ↓
CONTACTED
   ↓
CONNECTED
   ↓
QUALIFIED
   ↓
BOOKED
   ↓
ATTENDED
   ↓
CUSTOMER
   ↓
RETURNING
```

Alternative states:

```text
NURTURE
DORMANT
CLOSED
DNC
```

## 32.7 Lifecycle transitions

Store events:

```text
lead.qualified
appointment.booked
appointment.attended
customer.reactivated
```

Then derive segment state.

Don't manually modify lifecycle everywhere.

## 32.8 Intent segments

Example:

```text
VERY_HIGH
HIGH
MEDIUM
LOW
UNKNOWN
```

Based on observable signals.

High-intent examples:

specific service  
specific appointment request  
specific date/time  
explicit callback request.

## 32.9 Intent should decay

Customer had strong intent six months ago.

That should not automatically mean:

```text
HIGH_INTENT forever
```

Use recency.

Conceptually:

```text
Intent =
Current Signals
× Recency Adjustment
```

## 32.10 Intent provenance

Display:

```text
HIGH INTENT

Reasons:
Requested appointment
Selected preferred day
Asked about availability

Last updated:
Today
```

not opaque persona labels.

## 32.11 Need segmentation

Segments:

```text
DENTAL
PHYSIOTHERAPY
CHIROPRACTIC
ENT
MASSAGE
YOGA
CORPORATE_WELLNESS
```

Support:

primary need

and:

secondary needs.

## 32.12 Need-depth segmentation

Example:

```text
SERVICE_EXPLORER
SERVICE_SELECTED
APPOINTMENT_READY
```

Customer may know they need physio but not yet which offering/location.

This matters for conversation flow.

## 32.13 Urgency segment

Possible:

```text
IMMEDIATE
WITHIN_WEEK
WITHIN_MONTH
FUTURE
UNKNOWN
```

Only derive from customer-stated or legitimate operational evidence.

Do not infer clinical urgency unless appropriate workflow supports it.

## 32.14 Timing segments

Examples:

```text
MORNING
AFTERNOON
EVENING
WEEKEND
FLEXIBLE
```

Separate:

contact-time preference

from:

appointment-time preference.

A customer might want:

call after 6 PM

but appointment Saturday morning.

## 32.15 Channel segments

Examples:

```text
VOICE_PREFERRED
SMS_PREFERRED
EMAIL_PREFERRED
WHATSAPP_PREFERRED
HUMAN_PREFERRED
```

Again:

preference does not equal permission.

PolicyAI still determines eligibility.

## 32.16 Language segment

Use explicit/confirmed language preference.

Example:

```text
VOICE_LANGUAGE = HINDI
EMAIL_LANGUAGE = ENGLISH
```

Do not use language as a proxy for ethnicity or economic value.

## 32.17 Engagement segments

Examples:

```text
HIGHLY_ENGAGED
ENGAGED
LOW_ENGAGEMENT
NO_RESPONSE
REACTIVATION
```

Signals:

form activity  
calls answered  
SMS responses  
email engagement  
appointment interaction.

## 32.18 No-response segment

Customer hasn't answered 3 attempts.

This is not the same as:

```text
NOT_INTERESTED
```

Keep separate.

## 32.19 Objection segment

Possible:

```text
PRICE
TRUST
TIMING
LOCATION
QUALITY
CONTRACT
COMPETITOR
```

These can drive script and offer strategy.

## 32.20 Objection resolved state

Store:

```text
PRICE_OBJECTION_ACTIVE
```

and later:

```text
PRICE_OBJECTION_RESOLVED
```

Do not keep stale objections forever.

## 32.21 Service-fit segment

RecommendAI can classify:

```text
STRONG_MATCH
MODERATE_MATCH
WEAK_MATCH
NO_MATCH
```

Useful for campaign prioritization.

## 32.22 Availability-fit segment

Example:

```text
AVAILABLE_NOW
LIMITED_AVAILABILITY
NO_CURRENT_SLOT
WAITLIST
```

This prevents CampaignAI from aggressively calling customers when service cannot currently be delivered.

## 32.23 Customer-state segmentation

Potential operational states:

```text
READY_TO_BOOK
NEEDS_INFORMATION
NEEDS_RECOMMENDATION
NEEDS_CALLBACK
NEEDS_HUMAN
NURTURE
NO_ACTION
```

These are highly actionable.

## 32.24 Dynamic segments

Avoid static nightly-only segmentation for realtime decisions.

Example:

Customer says:

> “Yes, book that.”

Immediately transition:

```text
CONSIDERATION
→ READY_TO_BOOK
```

Event-driven updates are better.

## 32.25 Batch + realtime architecture

Use both:

### Realtime

intent  
current need  
next action.

### Batch

longer-term engagement  
propensity  
reactivation.

```text
Events
   ↓
Realtime Segment Service

Warehouse
   ↓
Batch Segment Jobs
```

## 32.26 Rule-based segmentation first

Example:

```text
IF
appointment_requested = true
AND
appointment_exists = false

THEN
segment = READY_TO_BOOK
```

Another:

```text
IF
last_interaction > 90 days
AND
previous_interest = true

THEN
segment = DORMANT
```

Rules are easier to explain initially.

## 32.27 SQL-style segment definition

Example:

```sql
intent_score >= 80
AND appointment_id IS NULL
AND dnc = false
```

Segment:

```text
HIGH_INTENT_UNBOOKED
```

But PolicyAI still handles contact permission.

## 32.28 Segment overlap

A customer can be:

```text
HIGH_INTENT
EVENING_PREFERENCE
PRICE_OBJECTION
PHYSIO
```

simultaneously.

Do not force mutually exclusive segmentation unless required.

## 32.29 Mutually exclusive segmentation

Some families should be exclusive.

Lifecycle:

```text
LEAD
QUALIFIED
BOOKED
CUSTOMER
```

Only one current lifecycle stage.

Intent family:

usually one current band.

Need family:

can be multi-valued.

Define cardinality explicitly.

## 32.30 Segment precedence

Example lifecycle:

```text
BOOKED
```

should override:

```text
HIGH_INTENT_UNBOOKED
```

Segment rules need precedence/conflict logic.

## 32.31 Segment conflict engine

If two exclusive segments match:

```text
RULE_PRIORITY
```

or:

latest authoritative state.

Do not return inconsistent states.

## 32.32 Segment confidence

Rules based on verified facts:

```text
confidence = HIGH
```

ML/inferred segments:

store probability/confidence.

Example:

```text
PRICE_SENSITIVE
confidence = 0.66
source = MODEL_INFERENCE
```

## 32.33 Segment expiration

Some segments should expire.

Example:

```text
CALLBACK_REQUESTED
```

expires after callback resolution.

```text
EVENING_PREFERENCE
```

may persist longer.

Store TTL per segment type.

## 32.34 Propensity models

Later calculate:

```text
P(answer call)
P(book appointment)
P(attend appointment)
P(reply SMS)
P(require human)
```

Keep them separate.

Do not create one magical customer score.

## 32.35 Booking propensity

Possible features:

recent appointment inquiry  
specific service  
availability lookup  
engagement  
historical interaction.

Avoid inappropriate sensitive variables.

## 32.36 Contactability propensity

Predict:

```text
P(answer | time/channel)
```

using:

previous answers  
time/day  
channel preference.

This feeds CampaignAI.

## 32.37 No-show propensity

Potentially useful operationally for reminder design.

But do not use it to deny appointments.

Use for:

extra reminder/confirmation

not:

lower-quality service.

## 32.38 Human-assist propensity

Predict likelihood the interaction will require a human.

Signals:

complexity  
unsupported question patterns  
previous transfer.

Use to forecast staffing.

## 32.39 Propensity calibration

A 0.8 score should approximately correspond to ~80% observed probability in similar cases.

Track:

Brier score  
calibration plots.

Raw ranking accuracy is not enough.

## 32.40 SegmentAI vs ScoreAI

Keep distinction:

**ScoreAI**

continuous numeric prediction.

**SegmentAI**

business grouping.

Example:

```text
Intent Score = 84
→ HIGH_INTENT segment
```

## 32.41 Persona concept

Avoid fixed psychological personas such as:

```text
The Skeptic
The Cheap Customer
```

Prefer operational personas:

```text
PRICE-CONCERNED RESEARCHER
READY-TO-BOOK EVENING CUSTOMER
CORPORATE EVALUATOR
```

These are evidence-based and temporary.

## 32.42 B2B segmentation

Corporate prospects need different dimensions:

```text
company size
industry
location
decision stage
buyer role
employee wellness need
budget timing
```

Support:

ORGANIZATION

and:

CONTACT

separately.

## 32.43 Corporate lifecycle

Example:

```text
TARGET_ACCOUNT
↓
ENGAGED
↓
DISCOVERY
↓
PROPOSAL
↓
PILOT
↓
CONTRACT
```

Do not use B2C booking lifecycle for corporate sales.

## 32.44 Household/family context

Customer may call for:

self  
child  
parent.

Use:

```text
beneficiary_type
```

rather than creating sensitive household profiling.

## 32.45 Lead-source segments

Examples:

```text
GOOGLE_HIGH_INTENT
INSTAGRAM_RESEARCHER
REFERRAL
CORPORATE_LINKEDIN
```

Useful, but measure actual behavior rather than assuming channel automatically determines intent.

## 32.46 Source × behavior

Better:

```text
source = Instagram
intent = HIGH
```

than:

```text
Instagram = LOW_INTENT
```

This avoids hardcoded stereotypes.

## 32.47 Segment transitions

Store:

```text
SEGMENT_EVENT

customer_id
segment
from_state
to_state
reason
timestamp
```

Then analyze customer journeys.

## 32.48 Segment journey

Example:

```text
NEW_LEAD
→ HIGH_INTENT
→ PRICE_OBJECTION
→ CALLBACK_REQUESTED
→ READY_TO_BOOK
→ BOOKED
```

Very useful for funnel analytics.

## 32.49 Segment transition matrix

Report:

```text
HIGH_INTENT → BOOKED        42%
HIGH_INTENT → NURTURE       28%
HIGH_INTENT → CLOSED        15%
```

This reveals where customers move.

## 32.50 Segment persistence

Store current state for realtime access

plus history for analytics.

```text
customer_segment_current

customer_segment_history
```

## 32.51 Segment API

Potential:

```text
GET /customers/{id}/segments

POST /segments/evaluate

GET /segments/{id}/members

GET /segments/{id}/performance
```

## 32.52 Segment engine response

Example:

```json
{
  "segments": [
    {
      "name": "HIGH_INTENT",
      "confidence": 0.94
    },
    {
      "name": "EVENING_PREFERENCE",
      "confidence": 1.0
    }
  ]
}
```

## 32.53 Campaign integration

CampaignAI asks:

```text
segment membership?
```

Example:

campaign:

```text
HIGH_INTENT
AND
NO_APPOINTMENT
```

But PolicyAI determines whether contact is allowed.

## 32.54 NextAI integration

Segment:

```text
READY_TO_BOOK
```

may increase candidate priority for:

```text
CHECK_AVAILABILITY / BOOK
```

Segment:

```text
INFORMATION_SEEKING
```

may favor:

send details.

## 32.55 RecommendAI integration

Use:

need  
constraints  
segment context

to rank options.

Do not let generic persona outweigh explicit requirements.

## 32.56 HumanOps integration

Segment:

```text
HUMAN_PREFERRED
```

can route more readily to staff.

```text
COMPLEX_CORPORATE
```

may route directly to specialist.

## 32.57 MarketAI integration

Aggregate segment demand:

```text
HIGH_INTENT + WEEKEND
```

to understand actionable opportunity.

## 32.58 FinAI integration

Calculate:

CAC  
cost/booking  
contribution

by segment.

Do not use profitability alone to determine necessary support/service access.

## 32.59 Segment performance

For each segment:

```text
population
connect
booking
attendance
conversion
complaint
DNC
cost
```

This helps assess usefulness.

## 32.60 Segment lift

Suppose:

overall booking = 20%.

HIGH_INTENT booking = 48%.

Then:

```text
lift = 2.4x
```

Useful for evaluating segment quality.

## 32.61 Segment stability

Monitor:

population size  
membership churn.

A segment fluctuating wildly may indicate unstable rules/model.

## 32.62 Segment drift

Example:

```text
HIGH_INTENT
10% → 45%
```

Possible:

campaign change  
model drift  
rule bug.

Monitor.

## 32.63 Segment leakage

Do not define:

```text
HIGH_CONVERSION
```

using future conversion outcome if you're using it to target customers before conversion.

That's target leakage.

Use only information available at segmentation time.

## 32.64 Lookalike modeling

Later, identify leads similar to historically successful customers.

Use legitimate behavioral/service features.

Avoid sensitive or proxy features.

Lookalike output:

```text
similarity_score
```

not:

“this person is the same type.”

## 32.65 Lookalike limitations

Lookalikes can reproduce historical biases.

Require:

feature review  
fairness testing  
incrementality testing.

Do not blindly optimize acquisition based on historic winners.

## 32.66 Fairness tests

Counterfactual examples:

same need  
same timing  
same interactions.

Change only language.

Ensure:

service eligibility  
price  
human access

remain appropriately consistent.

## 32.67 Segment fairness

Monitor whether segment assignment disproportionately changes due to inappropriate proxies.

Example:

`LOW_VALUE`

should not become a proxy for language/neighborhood.

Prefer business-relevant labels.

## 32.68 Segment explainability

Staff view:

```text
SEGMENT
HIGH_INTENT

Why:
Requested appointment
Selected service
Asked for evening availability

Confidence:
94%
```

## 32.69 Segment reason codes

Examples:

```text
SPECIFIC_SERVICE
APPOINTMENT_REQUEST
RECENT_FORM
CALLBACK_REQUEST
NO_RESPONSE_30D
PRICE_OBJECTION
```

## 32.70 Why-not segment

Staff may ask:

> Why isn't this customer READY_TO_BOOK?

Explain:

```text
Missing:
customer has not selected a service/date yet
```

Useful for NextAI.

## 32.71 Segment versioning

Store:

```text
segment_definition_version
```

If HIGH_INTENT threshold changes from 70 to 80:

historical reports remain interpretable.

## 32.72 Segment backfill

When definition changes:

decide whether to:

apply only going forward

or:

recompute history.

Do not silently mix definitions.

## 32.73 Testing rule segments

Given controlled input:

```text
intent = 92
appointment = none
```

Expected:

```text
HIGH_INTENT
UNBOOKED
```

Automate.

## 32.74 ML segment testing

For propensity-based bands:

test:

model performance  
calibration  
stability  
fairness.

## 32.75 Boundary tests

If:

HIGH_INTENT ≥ 80

test:

79.99  
80  
80.01.

Avoid off-by-one/business-rule errors.

## 32.76 Missing-data edge case

If intent inputs unavailable:

```text
UNKNOWN
```

not:

LOW_INTENT.

Unknown and low are different.

## 32.77 Contradictory-data edge case

CRM says:

price concern.

Current call:

> “Price is fine.”

Update current objection segment.

Preserve history.

## 32.78 Multiple-need edge case

Customer:

physio for self  
massage for spouse.

Do not mix into one generic need segment.

Track beneficiary/context.

## 32.79 Customer changes mind

Customer initially:

not ready.

Later:

book now.

Segment transitions immediately.

Do not let stale nightly batch state control conversation.

## 32.80 No-answer edge case

Three unanswered calls do not automatically imply low intent.

Keep:

```text
NO_RESPONSE
```

separate from intent.

## 32.81 High-intent but DNC

Possible state:

```text
HIGH_INTENT
+
DNC
```

Segment remains descriptively true.

PolicyAI still blocks marketing contact.

This separation is important.

## 32.82 High-value but complaint active

CampaignAI should not target merely because value segment is high.

Complaint/suppression state outranks segment economics.

## 32.83 Segment deletion

When underlying customer data is deleted/anonymized:

segment memberships should be appropriately removed/anonymized too.

## 32.84 Sensitive labels

Do not create permanent labels like:

```text
poor
rich
desperate
emotionally vulnerable
```

Use factual business states instead.

## 32.85 Segment dashboard

Show:

population  
growth  
conversion  
cost  
movement.

Example:

| Segment | Customers | Booking | Cost/Booking |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| High Intent | 2,100 | 48% | $11 |
| Information Seeking | 3,500 | 18% | $27 |
| Reactivation | 1,200 | 12% | $42 |

## 32.86 Segment transition dashboard

```text
NEW LEAD
  ↓ 68%
CONNECTED
  ↓ 62%
QUALIFIED
  ↓ 45%
BOOKED
```

Break down by source/service.

## 32.87 Segment overlap dashboard

Example:

```text
HIGH_INTENT
∩
PRICE_OBJECTION
```

Booking = 26%.

HIGH_INTENT without price objection:

52%.

This supports targeted strategy.

## 32.88 Segment cohort reporting

Track customers who entered a segment during same week/month.

Measure future outcomes.

## 32.89 Segment API latency

Realtime segment lookup should be fast.

Do not run a giant warehouse query in the middle of a voice turn.

Maintain current segment store/cache.

## 32.90 Architecture

```text
Events
   ↓
Segment Evaluation Service
   ↓
Current Membership DB / Redis
   ↓
Realtime APIs

Warehouse
   ↓
Batch ML
   ↓
Propensity Scores
   ↓
Segment Service
```

## 32.91 Event triggers

Re-evaluate segments when:

```text
lead.created
call.completed
need.detected
appointment.booked
appointment.cancelled
customer.preference.updated
score.updated
```

Not every event needs full recomputation.

## 32.92 Segment dependency graph

Example:

```text
HIGH_INTENT
depends on:
intent_score
appointment_state
recency
```

If intent-score model changes, GovernAI knows affected segments.

## 32.93 Governance

Each production segment should have:

owner  
business purpose  
definition  
version  
features  
fairness review where appropriate.

Avoid undocumented marketing segments.

## 32.94 Audit

For customer membership:

```text
segment
decision time
inputs
rule/model
reason codes
```

This supports ExplainAI.
