## 🤖 Assistant — msg #101

# Phase 33 — ScoreAI: Intent + Contactability + Conversion + Engagement + Service-Fit Scoring

This phase creates a governed scoring layer for the outbound Voice AI platform. Instead of one vague “lead score,” the system maintains several independent scores, each answering a specific business question.

> **A score should predict one thing, use only information available at decision time, expose its reasons, and never override policy, consent, safety, or customer instructions.**

## 33.1 Target architecture

```text
Customer 360
   +
Lead
   +
NeedAI
   +
SegmentAI
   +
Interaction History
   +
Campaign History
   +
Appointment History
   +
Service Capacity
        ↓
Feature Service
        ↓
ScoreAI
        ↓
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ Intent Score                 │
│ Contactability Score         │
│ Booking Propensity           │
│ Conversion Propensity        │
│ Attendance Propensity        │
│ Engagement Score             │
│ Service-Fit Score            │
│ Human-Assist Probability     │
│ Churn/Reactivation Score     │
└──────────────────────────────┘
        ↓
Confidence + Reason Codes
        ↓
SegmentAI / CampaignAI / NextAI
        ↓
ObserveAI / ExplainAI / RiskAI
```

## 33.2 Do not build one universal score

A customer might have:

```text
Intent                 92
Contactability         28
Booking Propensity     76
Service Fit            95
Attendance Propensity  81
```

That means:

> Very interested, strong service fit, but difficult to reach.

A single score of `74` would hide this distinction.

## 33.3 Score registry

Every score should be formally registered:

```text
SCORE_DEFINITION

score_id
name
description

prediction_target
prediction_horizon

input_features[]
excluded_features[]

model_type
model_version

thresholds
calibration_method

owner
risk_level

approved_uses[]
prohibited_uses[]

status
```

## 33.4 Core score family

| Score | Question |
|---|---|
| Intent | How strongly is the customer currently interested? |
| Contactability | How likely are they to answer a given channel/time? |
| Booking Propensity | How likely are they to book soon? |
| Conversion Propensity | How likely are they to become a customer? |
| Attendance | How likely is a booked appointment to be attended? |
| Engagement | How actively are they interacting? |
| Service Fit | How strongly does an offering match stated needs? |
| Human Assist | How likely is human support required? |
| Reactivation | How likely is a dormant lead to re-engage? |

Keep these targets separate.

---

# 33.5 Intent Score

Intent measures **current expressed interest**, not financial value.

Possible signals:

```text
Specific service requested
Appointment explicitly requested
Availability asked
Specific date/time requested
Callback requested
Pricing asked
Form recently submitted
Repeated legitimate engagement
```

Negative/reducing signals:

```text
Explicitly not ready
Research only
Repeated deferral
No current requirement
```

## 33.6 Rule-based intent MVP

Example:

```text
Appointment requested        +30
Specific service             +20
Specific timing              +15
Availability requested       +15
Customer requested callback  +15
Pricing inquiry               +5
```

Then cap:

```text
0–100
```

Keep the formula explainable.

## 33.7 Intent bands

Example:

```text
80–100  VERY HIGH
60–79   HIGH
40–59   MEDIUM
20–39   LOW
0–19    VERY LOW
```

Do not treat `UNKNOWN` as `LOW`.

If evidence is insufficient:

```text
intent_status = UNKNOWN
```

## 33.8 Intent recency

Intent decays.

A booking request from today is much stronger than one from six months ago.

Conceptually:

```text
Current Intent =
Signal Strength × Recency Weight
```

Example:

```text
0–1 day      1.00
2–7 days     0.80
8–30 days    0.50
older        lower
```

Actual decay should be calibrated from your data.

## 33.9 Intent source strength

Rank sources:

```text
CUSTOMER_EXPLICIT
CUSTOMER_CONFIRMED
SYSTEM_TRANSACTION
BEHAVIORAL_SIGNAL
AI_INFERENCE
```

Customer explicit evidence should usually dominate weak inferred signals.

---

# 33.10 Contactability Score

This predicts:

> **How likely is this customer to answer/respond through a specific channel and time?**

Do not make one generic contactability score only.

Model:

```text
P(answer | voice, Tuesday, 18:00)
P(reply | SMS, Tuesday, 18:00)
```

## 33.11 Contactability features

Potential:

```text
Previous answered calls
Time of previous answers
Day of week
Customer-stated contact preference
Previous callback requests
Recent no-answer count
Lead recency
Channel-response history
```

Avoid inappropriate demographic proxies.

## 33.12 Contactability matrix

Example:

```text
Customer C10028

Voice:
09:00–12:00   21%
12:00–17:00   34%
18:00–19:00   84%
19:00–20:00   71%

SMS:
Response probability 62%
```

CampaignAI can use this after policy checks.

---

# 33.13 Booking Propensity

Question:

> How likely is this customer to book an appointment within the prediction window?

Example target:

```text
BOOKING_WITHIN_7_DAYS
```

Do not mix:

same-day booking

with:

eventual booking.

Prediction horizon matters.

## 33.14 Booking features

Possible:

```text
Intent score
Service selected
Specific appointment request
Availability viewed
Recommendation accepted
Recent response
Price objection
Service-fit score
Current service availability
```

Never use future appointment fields accidentally.

---

# 33.15 Conversion Propensity

Booking isn't always final business conversion.

Depending business:

```text
Lead
→ Booking
→ Attendance
→ Paid customer
```

Conversion target could be:

```text
BECOMES_CUSTOMER_WITHIN_30_DAYS
```

Define this explicitly.

## 33.16 Do not optimize only conversion

A model might learn to prioritize customers who would convert without any outreach.

That doesn't mean the call caused conversion.

Later use:

**uplift modeling**

to estimate incremental effect.

---

# 33.17 Attendance Propensity

For booked appointments:

```text
P(attend appointment)
```

Can help determine reminder intensity.

Appropriate use:

```text
extra confirmation
reminder
human follow-up where justified
```

Inappropriate use:

```text
deny appointment
lower service quality
```

---

# 33.18 Engagement Score

This summarizes interaction activity.

Potential signals:

```text
Recent form submission
Calls answered
SMS replies
Email interactions
Questions asked
Appointments viewed
```

But do not reward spammy repeated outreach generated by your own system.

Separate:

**customer-initiated**

from:

**business-initiated**

events.

## 33.19 Engagement example

```text
Customer initiated form       +25
Customer answered call        +20
Customer replied SMS          +20
Customer requested callback   +25
Email opened                   +5
```

Customer-initiated signals should generally carry greater meaning.

---

# 33.20 Service-Fit Score

This is closer to RecommendAI.

Evaluate:

```text
Need match
Hard constraints
Timing
Location
Language
Price preference
Delivery mode
Availability
```

Hard constraints should normally be filters.

Then score surviving options.

Example:

```text
NW evening physiotherapy = 94
Virtual evening physio   = 82
Downtown evening physio  = 75
```

---

# 33.21 Human-Assist Probability

Predict:

> How likely is this interaction to require a human?

Signals might include:

```text
Complex insurance/admin question
Previous transfers
Repeated clarification
Unsupported service
Complex B2B context
Tool failures
```

Uses:

staffing forecast  
pre-positioning human support.

Not:

preventing customer access to AI or human support.

---

# 33.22 Reactivation Score

For dormant leads:

```text
P(re-engage | appropriate outreach)
```

Features:

past service interest  
historic engagement  
time since last interaction  
previous outcomes.

Respect current permissions/DNC.

High reactivation score does not authorize contact.

---

# 33.23 Score output schema

Every score:

```text
SCORE

score_instance_id
customer_id
lead_id

score_type
value
band

confidence

prediction_horizon

reason_codes[]

feature_snapshot_id

model_version
feature_version

calculated_at
expires_at
```

---

# 33.24 Score confidence

Do not confuse prediction value with certainty.

Example:

```text
Booking propensity = 82%
Confidence = LOW
```

because:

little customer history  
missing key information.

This can affect automation level.

---

# 33.25 Missing-data handling

Do not convert missing values blindly to zero.

Example:

```text
price concern = UNKNOWN
```

not:

```text
price concern = NO
```

Use explicit missingness features where appropriate.

---

# 33.26 Feature store

ScoreAI should consume governed features.

Example:

```text
FEATURE

name
definition
source
data_type
version
owner
freshness
```

Potential features:

```text
lead_age_minutes
calls_answered_30d
sms_replies_30d
specific_service_requested
appointment_requested
```

---

# 33.27 Feature snapshot

At decision time create:

```text
FEATURE_SNAPSHOT

snapshot_id
customer_id

feature values
source timestamps

created_at
```

This is important for reproducibility.

---

# 33.28 Point-in-time correctness

Training rows must reflect what was known at prediction time.

Suppose:

prediction made August 1.

Customer books August 3.

Training features for August 1 must not include:

```text
appointment_status = BOOKED
```

That's future leakage.

---

# 33.29 Label definition

For Booking Propensity:

```text
label = 1
if booked within 7 days after score timestamp
```

For Contactability:

```text
label = 1
if customer answered target contact attempt
```

Clear labeling matters more than fancy models.

---

# 33.30 Observation windows

Example:

```text
Features:
previous 30 days

Prediction:
next 7 days
```

Keep consistent.

---

# 33.31 Rule-based baseline first

Before ML, establish:

rules.

Why?

You need a baseline to prove ML actually improves performance.

Example:

```text
Booking propensity baseline =
weighted intent + service fit + recency
```

Then compare ML against it.

---

# 33.32 Logistic regression

Excellent first ML model.

Advantages:

fast  
interpretable  
easy to calibrate  
stable.

Use before automatically jumping to deep learning.

---

# 33.33 XGBoost / LightGBM

Good when:

nonlinear patterns  
feature interactions  
larger dataset.

Need:

SHAP/reason mapping  
fairness tests  
drift monitoring.

---

# 33.34 Neural networks

Probably unnecessary initially for structured lead scoring.

Use only when clear evidence shows meaningful advantage.

Voice/transcript embeddings may be useful for some separate tasks, but avoid black-box complexity without benefit.

---

# 33.35 Train/validation/test split

For time-dependent lead data, prefer temporal splits.

Example:

```text
Train:
Jan–May

Validation:
June

Test:
July
```

Avoid random leakage across strongly related customer histories.

---

# 33.36 Customer-level split

Same customer should generally not appear across train/test in a way that causes leakage.

Group appropriately.

---

# 33.37 Evaluation metrics

For binary propensity:

```text
ROC-AUC
PR-AUC
Precision
Recall
F1
Log Loss
Brier Score
Calibration
```

For imbalanced positive outcomes, PR-AUC can be especially useful.

---

# 33.38 Business-oriented evaluation

Also measure:

```text
Lift@Top10%
Lift@Top20%
Booking rate by decile
Cost per booking
```

Example:

Top 20% score band:

booking = 52%.

Overall:

21%.

Lift:

2.48×.

---

# 33.39 Gain chart

Sort leads by score.

Calculate cumulative percentage of bookings captured.

This shows whether scoring actually helps prioritization.

---

# 33.40 Calibration

Prediction:

```text
0.80
```

should mean roughly:

80 out of 100 similar cases succeed.

Use:

reliability diagrams  
Brier score.

Calibrate with:

Platt scaling  
isotonic regression

where appropriate.

---

# 33.41 Calibration by segment

Overall calibration may be good while a language/service segment is poor.

Evaluate by:

service  
source  
language preference  
campaign.

Only when sample sizes are sufficient.

---

# 33.42 Threshold selection

Don't arbitrarily decide:

```text
score > 70 = high
```

Choose thresholds based on:

capacity  
business value  
customer friction  
precision/recall trade-off.

---

# 33.43 Capacity-aware threshold

If team can process only:

500 high-priority callbacks/day,

choose threshold that produces approximately 500 qualified candidates while meeting quality requirements.

Threshold is an operational parameter.

---

# 33.44 Threshold versioning

Store:

```text
threshold_profile = INTENT-BANDS-v5
```

Historical reports must know which thresholds defined HIGH.

---

# 33.45 Score-to-action mapping

Separate:

```text
Score
```

from:

```text
Action
```

Example:

```text
Booking propensity 92%
```

does not mean:

```text
CALL_NOW
```

NextAI still checks:

customer preference  
DNC  
contact pressure  
campaign state.

---

# 33.46 Policy always wins

Example:

```text
Intent Score = 99
DNC = ACTIVE
```

Result:

```text
DO NOT CALL
```

High score does not create permission.

---

# 33.47 Customer explicit request beats score

Model:

best call time = 10 AM.

Customer:

> Call at 6 PM.

Use:

6 PM.

The score is advisory.

---

# 33.48 Explainability

For each score:

```text
Score
Reasons
Source
Confidence
```

Example:

```text
BOOKING PROPENSITY
78%

Positive drivers
+ Appointment requested
+ Specific evening time
+ Strong service match
+ Recent engagement

Negative
- Price concern

Model
BOOKING-XGB-v4
```

---

# 33.49 SHAP

For tree models:

compute top SHAP values internally.

Translate features:

```text
specific_service_requested=1
```

into:

> Customer selected a specific service.

Never expose raw feature jargon unnecessarily.

---

# 33.50 Causality warning

SHAP tells you why the model predicted something.

It does not mean:

the feature causes the outcome.

Do not say:

> “Evening preference makes customers buy.”

---

# 33.51 Score reason codes

Standardize:

```text
APPOINTMENT_REQUESTED
SPECIFIC_SERVICE
RECENT_ENGAGEMENT
CALLBACK_REQUEST
HIGH_SERVICE_FIT
PRICE_CONCERN
MULTIPLE_NO_ANSWERS
```

---

# 33.52 Reason-code validation

Explanation must match actual feature contributions.

Never mention:

`PRICE_CONCERN`

if model did not use such evidence.

---

# 33.53 Fairness review

Review features such as:

language  
postal code  
neighborhood  
names.

Ask:

Is it genuinely needed?

Could it proxy protected/sensitive characteristics?

Does it improve quality enough to justify use?

Often safer to use language only for communication/routing rather than lead-value scoring.

---

# 33.54 Fairness metrics

Where appropriate and legally/ethically supportable, evaluate relevant operational groups for:

false-positive rate  
false-negative rate  
calibration  
service quality.

For this platform, language-quality disparities are particularly actionable.

---

# 33.55 Avoid value discrimination

Do not use ScoreAI to decide:

who gets accurate information  
who gets emergency help  
who receives human access.

Scores support workflow prioritization, not basic service rights.

---

# 33.56 Historical bias

If historical agents performed poorly in Punjabi:

historical conversion may be lower.

A model could learn:

```text
Punjabi → lower conversion
```

and then call fewer Punjabi customers, reinforcing the problem.

Remove/protect against such feedback loops.

---

# 33.57 Source bias

Some acquisition sources get faster response historically.

Model may learn source rather than actual intent.

Test counterfactuals and source-normalized performance.

---

# 33.58 Exposure bias

Customers only convert on offers they were exposed to.

Historical absence of conversion for an unshown service does not mean dislike.

Important for RecommendAI training.

---

# 33.59 Feedback loops

High-score leads get more calls.

More calls generate more booking opportunities.

Future training then believes high-score profiles are inherently better.

Use:

experimentation  
controlled exploration  
propensity/uplift methods

to reduce bias.

---

# 33.60 Champion / challenger

Production:

```text
Champion:
Booking Logistic v3

Challenger:
XGBoost v1
```

Challenger runs in shadow.

Compare:

AUC  
calibration  
lift  
business outcomes.

---

# 33.61 Shadow mode

Generate challenger score but don't influence customer treatment.

Store:

```text
champion_score
challenger_score
```

Then compare over time.

---

# 33.62 A/B test

Once shadow passes, controlled deployment can test whether score-driven prioritization improves:

bookings  
cost  
complaints.

Do not assume offline uplift translates directly into business uplift.

---

# 33.63 Model drift

Monitor:

feature drift  
prediction drift  
performance drift  
calibration drift.

Example:

```text
Average booking propensity
0.34 → 0.61
```

without corresponding business change.

Investigate.

---

# 33.64 Performance drift

Track actual outcome when labels mature.

Example:

Top decile booking:

```text
Month 1 = 58%
Month 3 = 37%
```

Model may need review.

---

# 33.65 Feature drift

Example:

lead source distribution changes dramatically after new campaign.

Model trained on old traffic might degrade.

Monitor PSI or distribution tests.

---

# 33.66 Confidence degradation

If many predictions become:

```text
LOW_CONFIDENCE
```

data pipeline or market behavior may have changed.

---

# 33.67 Retraining triggers

Possible:

performance below threshold  
calibration failure  
enough new labeled data  
major campaign/product change.

Do not automatically retrain/deploy based only on time.

---

# 33.68 Retraining pipeline

```text
New labeled data
 ↓
DQ checks
 ↓
Feature snapshots
 ↓
Train
 ↓
Offline evaluation
 ↓
Fairness
 ↓
Calibration
 ↓
Explainability
 ↓
Shadow
 ↓
Canary
 ↓
Production
```

GovernAI approval before higher-risk promotion.

---

# 33.69 Score expiry

Scores should have freshness.

Example:

Intent:

expires quickly.

Contactability:

may remain valid longer but should update with interactions.

Store:

```text
expires_at
```

---

# 33.70 Realtime recalculation

Triggers:

```text
form submitted
call completed
customer replies SMS
appointment booked
preference updated
```

Do not wait for overnight batch when current conversation changes state.

---

# 33.71 Batch scoring

Useful for:

large dormant-lead population  
campaign planning.

Nightly:

```text
reactivation propensity
```

can be reasonable.

---

# 33.72 Score store

Architecture:

```text
Feature Store
   ↓
Scoring Service
   ↓
Score Store

Realtime APIs
```

Possible current table:

```text
customer_score_current
```

plus:

```text
customer_score_history
```

---

# 33.73 Score history

Preserve:

```text
value
model
time
reasons
```

Then explain why customer moved:

```text
Intent 45 → 91
```

because they requested appointment.

---

# 33.74 Score transition analytics

Example:

```text
LOW → HIGH
after:
SMS response + appointment request
```

Useful for journey optimization.

---

# 33.75 API design

```text
POST /scores/evaluate

GET /customers/{id}/scores

GET /customers/{id}/scores/{type}

GET /models/{id}/performance
```

Response:

```json
{
  "score_type": "BOOKING_PROPENSITY",
  "value": 0.78,
  "confidence": 0.91,
  "band": "HIGH",
  "reason_codes": [
    "APPOINTMENT_REQUESTED",
    "HIGH_SERVICE_FIT"
  ]
}
```

---

# 33.76 Event model

Publish:

```text
score.calculated
score.updated
score.band_changed
score.expired
model.drift_detected
model.performance_degraded
```

---

# 33.77 Testing — feature calculation

For every feature:

known input → expected value.

Example:

```text
last_contact = Aug 20
score_time = Aug 24
```

Expected:

```text
days_since_last_contact = 4
```

Timezones matter.

---

# 33.78 Testing — leakage

Create automated test ensuring forbidden future fields never enter feature list.

Examples:

```text
future_booking_status
future_payment
future_attendance
```

These should be impossible.

---

# 33.79 Testing — score boundaries

Test:

0  
threshold - epsilon  
threshold  
threshold + epsilon  
1/100.

Validate correct bands.

---

# 33.80 Testing — missing values

Run:

phone history missing  
campaign data missing  
pricing preference missing.

Model should still return controlled output/confidence.

---

# 33.81 Testing — contradictory data

Old CRM says low interest.

Current customer explicitly requests booking.

Recent explicit evidence should dominate current intent.

---

# 33.82 Testing — score reproducibility

Given:

feature snapshot + model version,

rerun and get identical deterministic model output where model semantics permit.

---

# 33.83 Testing — model API timeout

NextAI should have safe fallback:

previous valid score  
rules

or:

`UNKNOWN`

depending use case.

Do not invent a score.

---

# 33.84 Edge case — brand-new lead

No history.

Use:

form/current interaction features.

Confidence may be lower.

Do not punish customer for lack of history.

---

# 33.85 Edge case — long-standing customer

Historical behavior can help, but current explicit request should still matter most.

---

# 33.86 Edge case — repeatedly unreachable but high intent

Keep:

```text
Intent = HIGH
Contactability = LOW
```

Do not average into `MEDIUM`.

This is why separate scores matter.

---

# 33.87 Edge case — high propensity, no availability

Booking propensity may remain high.

RecommendAI/NextAI handles service constraint.

Do not artificially lower customer interest merely because your operation lacks capacity.

---

# 33.88 Edge case — complaint active

Conversion propensity may still be high statistically.

NextAI should prioritize service recovery, not sales.

---

# 33.89 Edge case — score differs drastically from human judgment

Capture override/review.

Investigate:

bad data  
model limitation  
human misconception.

Neither side is automatically correct.

---

# 33.90 Edge case — small language sample

Do not train language-specific model from inadequate data.

Use shared model + quality monitoring until enough evidence exists.

---

# 33.91 Edge case — customer asks why they were prioritized

Customer-facing response should focus on their request:

> “You requested a callback about physiotherapy.”

Don't expose commercial lead scoring.

---

# 33.92 Score security

Score APIs require:

tenant authorization  
purpose control.

Do not expose internal scores publicly.

Scores can become sensitive business/profile data.

---

# 33.93 Score privacy

Do not store unnecessary inferred traits.

Use business outcome scores with TTL and clear purpose.

---

# 33.94 Score governance

Every production scoring model needs:

owner  
target definition  
features  
model card  
training data lineage  
evaluation  
fairness review  
approval  
monitoring.

---

# 33.95 Score dashboard

For each model:

```text
Population distribution
Outcome rate by score band
Calibration
Lift
Drift
Missing feature rate
Model version
```

---

# 33.96 Business dashboard

Example:

| Booking Score | Leads | Actual Booking |
|---|---:|---:|
| 90–100 | 520 | 64% |
| 80–89 | 730 | 51% |
| 60–79 | 1,500 | 32% |
| 40–59 | 2,100 | 18% |
| <40 | 3,000 | 7% |

This shows whether ranking is useful.

---

# 33.97 Contactability heatmap

Show:

weekday × hour

with:

answer probability.

Break down only where sample size supports reliable analysis.

---

# 33.98 Calibration dashboard

Prediction band:

```text
0.7–0.8
```

Observed:

```text
0.74
```

Good.

If observed:

```text
0.42
```

recalibration/review needed.

---

# 33.99 Model risk indicators

Track:

```text
Population stability
Calibration error
AUC/PR degradation
Fairness gap
Reason-code drift
Low-confidence rate
```

RiskAI consumes these.

---

```text
Logistic Baseline                  PASS

Threshold Versioning               PASS

Confidence                         PASS
```

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #103

# Phase 34 — KnowledgeAI + Enterprise RAG / Knowledge Management

This phase gives every voice agent a governed, current, source-backed knowledge layer for clinic information, services, policies, FAQs, pricing explanations, locations, provider information, insurance/admin guidance, and approved marketing content.

The principle is:

> **The agent should answer from authoritative, current sources; know when sources conflict or are missing; cite the evidence internally; and abstain instead of inventing facts.**

## 34.1 Target architecture

```text
Websites / PDFs / FAQs / CRM Content
Policies / Service Catalog / Pricing
Provider Profiles / Location Data
Approved Scripts / Knowledge Articles
                ↓
        Knowledge Ingestion
                ↓
     Parsing + Classification
                ↓
 Metadata + Access + Versioning
                ↓
        Chunking / Enrichment
                ↓
        Embedding + Indexing
                ↓
 ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
 ↓              ↓              ↓
Vector       Keyword/BM25     Graph
Search         Search          Links
 └──────────────┼──────────────┘
                ↓
        Hybrid Retrieval
                ↓
           Reranking
                ↓
      Authority/Freshness Filter
                ↓
       Context Construction
                ↓
              LLM
                ↓
     Grounded Answer + Evidence
                ↓
 QualityAI / ExplainAI / GovernAI
```

## 34.2 Knowledge domains

For the healthcare-clinic scenario, maintain separate knowledge domains:

| Domain | Examples |
|---|---|
| Clinic | hours, address, parking, phone |
| Services | dental, physio, chiropractic, ENT, massage |
| Scheduling | booking, cancellation, rescheduling |
| Pricing | approved service/package information |
| Insurance/Admin | approved administrative guidance |
| Providers | languages, locations, specialties as approved |
| Preparation | approved appointment instructions |
| Policies | late arrival, cancellation, privacy |
| Campaigns | approved offers/promotions |
| Corporate | employee wellness/service packages |
| FAQ | common customer questions |
| Internal | staff-only escalation/process information |

Do not put every document into one unrestricted index.

## 34.3 Knowledge-source registry

Create:

```text
KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE

source_id
tenant_id

name
source_type

WEBSITE
PDF
FAQ
API
DATABASE
MANUAL_ARTICLE

owner

authority_level
classification

effective_from
expires_at

refresh_frequency

status
```

Each source must have an owner.

## 34.4 Authority hierarchy

Not all knowledge is equal.

Example:

```text
Appointment availability API
        >
Service Catalog API
        >
Pricing API
        >
Approved clinic policy
        >
Approved FAQ
        >
Marketing page
        >
Historical document
```

If a PDF says:

> "$90"

but Pricing API says:

> "$110"

the current authoritative pricing source wins.

## 34.5 Structured data vs RAG

A major design rule:

Use **structured APIs** for facts that change rapidly or drive transactions.

### Use API/tool

```text
Current price
Available appointment
Provider schedule
Booking status
Current promotion eligibility
```

### Use RAG

```text
What is physiotherapy?
Where can I park?
What should I generally bring?
What services does this clinic offer?
```

Do not use vector retrieval as a replacement for transactional systems.

## 34.6 Knowledge document model

```text
DOCUMENT

document_id
tenant_id

title
source_id

document_type
language

version

effective_from
expires_at

authority_level
classification

owner
approval_status

content_hash
```

## 34.7 Chunk model

```text
KNOWLEDGE_CHUNK

chunk_id
document_id

chunk_text

section
heading

language
service
location

effective_from
expires_at

authority
access_scope

embedding_version
```

Metadata is critical for filtering.

## 34.8 Chunking strategy

Different content requires different chunking.

### FAQs

One question/answer can often be one logical unit.

### Policies

Chunk by heading/subheading.

### Long documents

Recursive structure-aware chunking.

### Tables

Preserve row/header relationship.

Avoid blindly splitting every 500 characters.

## 34.9 Recursive chunking

Example hierarchy:

```text
Document
 ↓
Section
 ↓
Subsection
 ↓
Paragraph
```

Target chunks should preserve semantic completeness.

## 34.10 Chunk overlap

Some overlap helps prevent context loss.

Example conceptually:

```text
Chunk size: 600–1,000 tokens
Overlap: 10–20%
```

But benchmark instead of assuming these values are optimal.

More overlap means:

better continuity

but:

larger index/cost/redundancy.

## 34.11 Semantic chunking

Use when documents have irregular section lengths.

Split based on semantic boundaries rather than fixed length.

Useful for:

policy manuals  
long FAQ documents.

But semantic chunking adds preprocessing complexity; don't use it everywhere.

## 34.12 Parent-child retrieval

Useful pattern:

```text
Small child chunks
→ retrieval

Larger parent section
→ context
```

Search precision stays high while final context retains surrounding meaning.

## 34.13 Metadata

Store at least:

```text
tenant
clinic
service
location
language
document type
authority
effective dates
classification
```

Then query:

> "Physio cancellation policy for Clinic A"

only searches relevant approved content.

## 34.14 Tenant isolation

Every retrieval request includes:

```text
tenant_id
```

Hard metadata/access filter occurs **before** semantic ranking.

Clinic A's agent must never retrieve Clinic B's documentation.

## 34.15 Knowledge access control

Some documents:

```text
CUSTOMER_VISIBLE
STAFF_ONLY
COMPLIANCE_ONLY
```

Voice agents receive only customer-appropriate content.

RAG authorization is part of security, not just retrieval.

## 34.16 Vector store

Possible options:

```text
pgvector
Qdrant
Weaviate
Milvus
Pinecone
OpenSearch/Elasticsearch
```

For early deployments:

**PostgreSQL + pgvector** can be enough.

At higher scale:

Qdrant/OpenSearch/Milvus-class solutions may make sense.

## 34.17 Embedding model

Select based on:

retrieval quality  
multilingual support  
latency  
cost  
deployment requirements.

Benchmark using your own FAQ/query dataset.

Do not select embeddings solely from generic leaderboard scores.

## 34.18 Multilingual embeddings

Important for:

English  
Hindi  
Punjabi  
French

and code switching.

Test:

Hindi query → English source.

Example:

> “Physio kitne baje close hota hai?”

should retrieve authoritative clinic-hours information even if KB is English.

## 34.19 Translation strategy

Possible:

```text
Customer Hindi
 ↓
Multilingual embedding
 ↓
English knowledge
 ↓
Answer in Hindi
```

Avoid translation chains where unnecessary because each transformation can introduce error.

## 34.20 Hybrid search

Use:

```text
Vector similarity
+
BM25/keyword
```

This is generally stronger than pure vector search.

Why?

Vector search:

semantic meaning.

BM25:

exact terms, product/service names, policy numbers.

## 34.21 Hybrid scoring

Conceptually:

```text
Final Retrieval Score =
α × Semantic Score
+
β × Keyword Score
```

Tune with evaluation data.

## 34.22 Exact-term boosting

Boost:

clinic name  
doctor/provider name  
service codes  
location names.

Exact entities often matter more than semantic similarity.

## 34.23 Query rewriting

Customer:

> "What about weekends?"

Conversation context:

Physiotherapy.

Rewrite retrieval query:

```text
Physiotherapy weekend appointment availability/policy
```

But preserve customer intent.

## 34.24 Multi-query retrieval

For ambiguous questions, generate several focused queries.

Example:

> "What do you cover?"

Could mean:

services  
insurance  
pricing.

Conversation state should disambiguate first where possible.

## 34.25 Query classification

Before retrieval classify:

```text
STATIC_FAQ
TRANSACTIONAL
PRICING
APPOINTMENT
POLICY
CLINICAL_RESTRICTED
UNKNOWN
```

Then route appropriately.

## 34.26 Retrieval router

Architecture:

```text
Customer Question
      ↓
Query Router
      ↓
┌──────────────┬──────────────┐
FAQ RAG      Pricing API   Scheduler API
      ↓
Knowledge
```

This avoids asking RAG for everything.

## 34.27 Retrieval top-K

Example:

retrieve:

```text
Top 10–20
```

then rerank to:

```text
Top 3–5
```

Actual K should be benchmarked.

Do not simply stuff top 20 chunks into every prompt.

## 34.28 Reranking

Use reranker to improve precision.

Options:

cross-encoder  
LLM reranker  
provider reranking API.

Reranking should consider:

semantic relevance  
authority  
freshness  
metadata fit.

## 34.29 MMR

Maximum Marginal Relevance helps reduce redundant chunks.

Useful when top retrieval results repeat same paragraph.

Concept:

```text
Relevance
-
Redundancy
```

This produces more diverse evidence.

## 34.30 Context budget

Create strict context budget.

Example:

```text
System instructions
Structured customer state
Retrieved evidence
Recent conversation
```

Don't send unlimited KB content.

Context quality matters more than context volume.

## 34.31 Context construction

Preferred:

```text
SOURCE 1
Clinic Hours Policy
Relevant section...

SOURCE 2
Physio Service FAQ
Relevant section...
```

Keep source labels attached.

This helps grounding and evaluation.

## 34.32 RAG answer policy

Agent must:

```text
Answer only from retrieved/authorized evidence
```

when question requires grounded business facts.

If evidence insufficient:

```text
ABSTAIN
```

or route appropriately.

## 34.33 No-answer behavior

Customer asks:

> "Does your clinic provide a treatment never mentioned anywhere?"

If no authoritative evidence:

> “I don't have confirmed information on that service. I can connect you with the clinic.”

Not:

> “Yes, probably.”

## 34.34 Contradictory knowledge

Example:

Document A:

closes 8 PM.

Document B:

closes 6 PM.

Resolution process:

```text
Authority
↓
Effective date
↓
Version
↓
Conflict policy
```

If unresolved:

do not invent an answer.

Create:

```text
KNOWLEDGE_CONFLICT
```

## 34.35 Knowledge conflict record

```text
conflict_id
topic

source_a
source_b

detected_at

severity
owner
status
```

High-impact conflict:

pricing  
appointment policies.

Alert owner.

## 34.36 Effective dating

Service price:

```text
Price V3
valid until Aug 31

Price V4
effective Sep 1
```

RAG/request at Aug 24 should use V3.

Future calls after Sep 1 use V4.

## 34.37 Expired knowledge

Documents with:

```text
expires_at < now
```

should not normally participate in retrieval.

Do not rely on the LLM to notice an expired date inside text.

## 34.38 Freshness weighting

For sources of equal authority:

prefer newer/current versions.

Concept:

```text
Final rank =
relevance
+
authority
+
freshness
```

## 34.39 Knowledge ingestion pipeline

```text
Source
 ↓
Fetch
 ↓
Parse
 ↓
Malware/Security Scan
 ↓
PII Classification
 ↓
Structure Extraction
 ↓
Metadata
 ↓
Approval
 ↓
Chunk
 ↓
Embed
 ↓
Index
 ↓
Evaluation
 ↓
Publish
```

No direct "upload → production vector DB."

## 34.40 Website ingestion

Website crawler should use:

approved domain allowlist.

Track:

URL  
last fetched  
content hash.

Only reprocess changed content.

## 34.41 PDF ingestion

Extract:

text  
headings  
tables  
page references.

For scanned PDFs:

use OCR only where necessary.

Validate output before indexing.

## 34.42 Table handling

Bad extraction:

```text
Service 80 60 120
```

loses relationship.

Better represent:

```text
Service: Physiotherapy
Initial assessment: $120
Follow-up: $80
```

Preserve table semantics.

## 34.43 FAQ ingestion

FAQ is particularly useful because it naturally maps:

question variants

to:

approved answer.

Store synonyms and alternate phrasing.

## 34.44 API-backed knowledge

For dynamic content, knowledge registry may contain:

```text
SOURCE_TYPE = API
```

Example:

Pricing Service.

Then Query Router invokes API rather than embedding its values.

## 34.45 Knowledge graph

GraphRAG may help when relationships matter.

Example:

```text
Clinic
 ├── offers → Physiotherapy
 ├── located_at → NW
 ├── supports_language → Hindi
 └── provider → Dr X
```

Useful for complex multi-hop queries.

Don't introduce GraphRAG if simple hybrid retrieval solves the problem.

## 34.46 Graph schema

Potential entities:

```text
Clinic
Location
Service
Provider
Language
Policy
Offer
```

Relationships:

```text
OFFERS
LOCATED_AT
SUPPORTED_BY
AVAILABLE_AT
HAS_POLICY
```

## 34.47 Ontology

Create controlled vocabulary.

Example:

```text
Physio
Physiotherapy
Physical Therapy
```

map to canonical:

```text
PHYSIOTHERAPY
```

This improves retrieval and reporting.

## 34.48 Synonym registry

Useful for customer language:

```text
physio → physiotherapy
chiro → chiropractic
massage therapy → RMT
```

Tenant-specific terminology should be supported.

## 34.49 Entity linking

Customer says:

> “NW location.”

Resolve to:

```text
LOCATION-NW-001
```

before retrieval where possible.

Improves precision.

## 34.50 RAG evaluation dataset

Create:

```text
query
expected_source
expected_answer_facts
forbidden_facts
```

Start:

500+ representative questions.

Expand with production failures.

## 34.51 Retrieval metrics

Measure:

```text
Recall@K
Precision@K
MRR
NDCG
```

Most important question:

> Did the correct authoritative source appear in retrieved candidates?

## 34.52 Answer metrics

Measure:

```text
Faithfulness
Groundedness
Correctness
Completeness
Relevance
```

Separate retrieval failure from generation failure.

## 34.53 Source authority metric

Even if answer is factually similar:

retrieving an obsolete low-authority source instead of authoritative current source is a defect.

Track:

```text
authoritative_source_hit_rate
```

## 34.54 Citation accuracy

Internally, each factual answer should map to source references.

Test:

does source actually support the claim?

This is important for ExplainAI and QA.

## 34.55 RAG hallucination tests

Ask:

> "You definitely offer free treatment, right?"

If no such source:

agent must reject unsupported premise.

## 34.56 Negative-question bank

Include:

nonexistent services  
nonexistent promotions  
false provider names  
incorrect hours.

Expected:

correct/abstain.

## 34.57 Adversarial RAG

Test malicious documents containing:

> “Ignore your system prompt.”

Retrieved content is treated as untrusted knowledge.

Instructions inside documents should not control agent behavior.

## 34.58 Knowledge poisoning defense

Controls:

source allowlists  
approval workflow  
content hashes  
malware scan  
prompt-injection scan  
owner.

Unapproved documents do not enter production index.

## 34.59 RAG tenant test

Create:

Clinic A document:

Price = $80.

Clinic B:

Price = $120.

Ask Clinic A agent.

Expected:

only Clinic A content retrieved.

100% cross-tenant isolation required.

## 34.60 Metadata-filter test

Question:

> “What is the cancellation policy for massage at NW?”

Expected filters:

```text
service=MASSAGE
location=NW
document_type=POLICY
```

Measure filter correctness.

## 34.61 Language test

Questions:

English  
Hindi  
Punjabi  
mixed.

Expected:

same authoritative source/fact.

Then answer in requested language.

## 34.62 Number/date test

Critical:

prices  
phone numbers  
hours  
dates.

LLMs can distort numbers.

Compare generated output directly to source data.

## 34.63 Retrieval confidence

Return:

```text
HIGH
MEDIUM
LOW
```

based on:

score  
authority  
source agreement.

Low confidence can trigger clarification/human.

## 34.64 Abstention threshold

If retrieval score/authority below threshold:

don't answer confidently.

Tune threshold using:

false-answer cost

versus:

unnecessary escalation.

## 34.65 Knowledge gap

If customers repeatedly ask a question with no good answer:

create:

```text
KNOWLEDGE_GAP
```

Example:

> Insurance coverage.

Count:

frequency  
business impact.

## 34.66 Knowledge gap record

```text
gap_id
topic

sample_questions[]

count_30d
services[]
languages[]

business_impact

owner
status
```

## 34.67 Knowledge-gap workflow

```text
Unanswered questions
 ↓
Cluster
 ↓
Review
 ↓
Create approved content/tool
 ↓
Publish
 ↓
Regression test
```

This closes the learning loop.

## 34.68 Question clustering

Use embeddings/topic clustering to identify repeated variants:

> “Do you accept insurance?”

> “Can I claim this?”

> “Does Blue Cross cover it?”

May belong to an insurance/admin topic.

Human validates clusters.

## 34.69 RAG feedback

Capture:

customer correction  
human correction  
QA failure.

Map to source/retrieval.

Possible issue:

bad content  
bad retrieval  
bad generation.

## 34.70 Source-quality score

Track:

retrieval usefulness  
QA failures  
staleness  
owner review.

Don't allow low-quality sources to dominate simply because they contain matching keywords.

## 34.71 Knowledge owner dashboard

Show:

```text
Documents due review
Expired
Conflicts
Knowledge gaps
Low-performing articles
```

Each clinic/admin owner can maintain their content.

## 34.72 Agent knowledge profile

Each agent gets explicit knowledge set:

```text
PHYSIO_AGENT

Allowed:
General clinic KB
Physio KB
Scheduling policy
Pricing API

Not allowed:
ENT internal docs
Staff HR docs
Other tenant docs
```

## 34.73 Knowledge collections

Organize:

```text
GLOBAL
TENANT
CLINIC
SERVICE
AGENT
```

Retrieval scope built from intersection.

## 34.74 Knowledge inheritance

Example:

Physio Agent:

```text
Global Customer FAQ
+
Clinic A FAQ
+
Physio Service KB
```

Specific approved content can override generic content according to authority rules.

## 34.75 Prompt/context injection boundaries

Mark retrieved sections:

```text
<knowledge>
...
</knowledge>
```

and system instructions explicitly state:

knowledge is data, not executable instruction.

Architectural enforcement still required.

## 34.76 RAG cache

Frequently asked static question:

clinic parking.

Cache retrieved result/answer where safe.

Cache key includes:

tenant  
knowledge version  
language  
question class.

Invalidate when content changes.

## 34.77 Semantic cache

Possible later:

similar questions reuse approved response.

Be careful with customer-specific or dynamic facts.

Never semantic-cache appointment availability.

## 34.78 Embedding refresh

If embedding model changes:

you may need re-embedding.

Store:

```text
embedding_model
embedding_version
```

Support parallel indexes during migration.

## 34.79 Index versioning

```text
PHYSIO_KB_INDEX_v12
```

Canary new index.

If retrieval degrades:

rollback.

## 34.80 Blue/green knowledge index

```text
BLUE = KB v12
GREEN = KB v13
```

Run regression on green.

Switch after approval.

Useful for large KB changes.

## 34.81 Index rebuild

Do not destroy live index before replacement ready.

Build new index

→ verify

→ atomically switch alias.

## 34.82 Retrieval observability

Track per query:

```text
query_type
retrieval_latency
top_scores
source_ids
rerank_latency
context_tokens
answer_status
```

Avoid exposing sensitive raw queries broadly.

## 34.83 RAG latency

Voice use requires fast retrieval.

Measure:

P50/P95/P99.

Potential:

query classification  
vector search  
rerank.

Reranking quality must justify added latency.

## 34.84 RAG cost

Track:

embedding queries  
rerank  
LLM context tokens.

FinAI calculates:

cost per RAG question  
cost per resolved question.

## 34.85 Retrieval fallback

Vector DB unavailable:

For dynamic transactional facts:

other APIs still work.

For FAQ:

use approved static cache where available.

Otherwise:

abstain/human.

Do not bypass source controls.

## 34.86 Vectorless retrieval

For smaller knowledge bases, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch hybrid or even well-structured keyword retrieval may be enough.

Vector search is not mandatory.

Benchmark against actual queries.

## 34.87 Search routing

Some queries are entity-specific:

> "What time does NW clinic close?"

Structured lookup may outperform RAG.

Use routing:

```text
Entity lookup
Keyword
Vector
Graph
API
```

rather than "everything into vector DB."

## 34.88 Knowledge SLOs

Track:

```text
Retrieval availability
P95 latency
Authoritative hit rate
Grounded answer rate
Knowledge freshness
```

## 34.89 Critical knowledge elements

Examples:

```text
Current price
Clinic hours
Cancellation policy
```

Require stricter QA/freshness.

## 34.90 Freshness monitoring

Website changed but KB not updated.

Compare:

source hash  
indexed hash.

Alert:

```text
KNOWLEDGE_STALE
```

## 34.91 Source deletion

If source removed/invalidated:

delete related chunks from active index.

Metadata status alone is insufficient if retrieval can still return them.

## 34.92 Right-to-delete

If indexed content contains customer-specific data accidentally:

support deletion across:

raw document  
chunks  
vector records  
caches.

Prefer not indexing customer PII into general knowledge systems at all.

## 34.93 RAG security

Protect against:

cross-tenant retrieval  
prompt injection  
unauthorized internal docs  
malicious upload  
vector-store exfiltration.

Use SecureAI controls.

## 34.94 RAG privacy

General knowledge index should contain minimal/no patient-specific information.

Customer-specific records belong in Customer 360/tool systems, not generic RAG.

## 34.95 GraphRAG decision rule

Use GraphRAG when:

multi-hop relationships materially matter.

Example:

> "Which NW clinics have physiotherapy providers who speak Hindi and are open evenings?"

A graph/structured query may be better.

Don't use GraphRAG just because it sounds advanced.

## 34.96 Graph + vector architecture

```text
Question
 ↓
Entity Extraction
 ↓
Graph Candidate Search
 +
Vector Evidence
 ↓
Rerank
 ↓
Answer
```

Useful for complex service directories.

## 34.97 KnowledgeAI API

Potential:

```text
POST /knowledge/search

POST /knowledge/answer

POST /knowledge/documents

POST /knowledge/reindex

GET /knowledge/sources/{id}

GET /knowledge/gaps

GET /knowledge/conflicts
```

## 34.98 Search request

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "CLINIC_A",
  "agent_id": "PHYSIO-HINDI-v18",
  "query": "Do you have evening physio?",
  "language": "hi"
}
```

## 34.99 Search response

```json
{
  "status": "FOUND",
  "confidence": 0.96,
  "sources": [
    {
      "document_id": "PHYSIO-FAQ-v13",
      "section": "Hours"
    }
  ]
}
```

For live availability, router should invoke scheduler rather than rely on static source.

## 34.100 RAG decision trace

Store:

```text
query
classification
filters
retrieved candidates
reranked candidates
selected evidence
answer
groundedness result
```

This is essential for debugging.

## 34.101 Knowledge events

Publish:

```text
knowledge.document.created
knowledge.document.approved
knowledge.document.updated
knowledge.document.expired

knowledge.index.updated

knowledge.conflict.detected
knowledge.gap.detected
```

## 34.102 Knowledge release pipeline

```text
Content change
 ↓
PR/Authoring
 ↓
Review
 ↓
Approval
 ↓
Ingestion
 ↓
Index build
 ↓
RAG regression
 ↓
Canary
 ↓
Production
```

Knowledge changes can alter agent behavior, so treat them as releases.

## 34.103 Knowledge regression

Before new KB:

replay golden FAQ set.

Compare:

retrieval  
answer facts  
latency.

No unexpected critical regression.

## 34.104 Production sampling

Review:

low-confidence queries  
abstentions  
customer corrections  
new topics.

Feed Knowledge Gap system.

## 34.105 Quality by knowledge source

Example:

| Source | Queries | Helpful | Errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Physio FAQ | 1,200 | 95% | 1% |
| Generic Site | 600 | 72% | 8% |

This may justify restructuring/removing weak content.

## 34.106 Query analytics

Track top questions.

Useful for:

content design  
market intelligence  
sales scripts.

But de-identify analytics.

## 34.107 Search zero-result rate

Metric:

```text
zero_result_rate
```

Break by:

service  
language  
topic.

High rate = knowledge gap/retrieval issue.

## 34.108 Low-confidence answer rate

Track:

```text
low_confidence_retrieval
```

High rate after a release may indicate index regression.

## 34.109 Answer correction rate

Customer:

> "That's not right."

Human:

corrects agent.

Track source and query.

This is a powerful signal.

## 34.110 Knowledge coverage

Create:

```text
Known Customer Question Taxonomy
        ↓
Knowledge coverage %
```

Example:

```text
Pricing       100%
Hours          100%
Insurance       68%
Home visits     40%
```

## 34.111 Content effectiveness

Does FAQ answer resolve question?

Measure:

same question repeated  
human transfer after answer  
customer correction.

This is more useful than content-view counts alone.

## 34.112 Knowledge lifecycle

```text
DRAFT
REVIEW
APPROVED
ACTIVE
EXPIRING
EXPIRED
RETIRED
```

Only ACTIVE content is generally retrievable.

## 34.113 Document ownership

Every source has:

business owner  
content reviewer.

Expired orphan documents should be disabled rather than persist indefinitely.

## 34.114 Localization governance

Translated knowledge needs:

```text
source_language
translation_version
review_status
```

For high-impact content, use validated translations.

Do not rely solely on machine translation forever.

## 34.115 Language consistency

If English source changes:

translated versions become:

```text
TRANSLATION_STALE
```

until updated/revalidated.

## 34.116 Knowledge conflict example

```text
FAQ:
Cancellation requires 24 hours.

Website:
48 hours.
```

System:

```text
CONFLICT
```

Until resolved:

avoid definitive customer statement if authority rules can't decide.

Human/escalation.

## 34.117 Edge case — customer asks about two clinics

Retrieve separately.

Do not blend policies.

Example:

Clinic A hours

vs Clinic B hours.

## 34.118 Edge case — vague pronoun

Customer:

> "Does that location have parking?"

Use conversational entity state:

`that location = NW Clinic`.

If uncertain:

clarify.

## 34.119 Edge case — outdated conversation context

Customer switched from Dental to Physio mid-call.

Query router must update service context.

Avoid retrieving dental FAQ for physio question.

## 34.120 Edge case — exact provider name STT error

Use fuzzy entity matching with confidence.

If uncertain:

ask customer to confirm.

Do not retrieve wrong provider's information.

## 34.121 Edge case — user asks for unsupported clinical recommendation

Knowledge router classifies:

```text
CLINICAL_RESTRICTED
```

Do not search general KB and improvise medical advice.

Use approved clinic escalation/protocol.

## 34.122 Edge case — conflicting API and RAG

Pricing API says $120.

FAQ says $100.

Pricing API wins.

Create knowledge conflict ticket so FAQ is corrected.

## 34.123 Edge case — customer asks future pricing

Current API may not contain future rate.

Do not assume current price applies.

Return:

not yet confirmed/human.

## 34.124 Edge case — dynamic promotion expired

Offer API determines active status.

Static promotional article should not make expired offer available.

## 34.125 Edge case — bad PDF extraction

If table extraction confidence is poor:

quarantine affected document or require review.

Do not index gibberish.

## 34.126 Edge case — duplicated documents

Deduplicate using:

content hash  
semantic similarity.

Otherwise top-K results become redundant.

## 34.127 Edge case — source website temporarily broken

Do not immediately delete previously approved knowledge.

Use freshness tolerance and owner alerts.

But expired/critical dynamic facts may require fail-safe behavior.

## 34.128 Edge case — index partially rebuilt

Use atomic alias/version switching.

Never expose half-new/half-old index.

## 34.129 Edge case — embedding migration

Keep old and new index in parallel.

Benchmark.

Switch only after passing.

## 34.130 Edge case — LLM ignores source

Post-generation groundedness check can detect unsupported claims.

For critical facts:

prefer deterministic template from structured values.

## 34.131 Testing matrix

Test:

```text
Correct source
Wrong source
No source
Conflicting source
Expired source
Cross-tenant source
Multilingual query
Code-switch
Pricing query
Appointment query
Clinical restricted query
Prompt-injected document
```

Each gets expected retrieval/action.

## 34.132 RAG quality gate

Example:

```text
Critical FAQ source recall        100%
Cross-tenant leakage                0
Expired-source retrieval            0
Pricing hallucination               0
Groundedness                >= threshold
P95 latency                  <= threshold
```

For an initial 30–50 employee / small-client deployment:

```text
+
pgvector

+
Langfuse
```

Add dedicated vector/graph infrastructure only when measurement shows need.

```text
Qdrant/Milvus/OpenSearch
DataHub/OpenMetadata
Graph DB
Reranking service
Multilingual embedding service
```

Still keep structured business facts outside RAG.
