## 🤖 Assistant — msg #109

# Phase 37 — RecommendAI + OfferAI + Service / Slot / Package Recommendation

This phase decides **which approved service, appointment slot, location, package, or offer best fits the customer's stated need and constraints**.

The principle is:

> **Filter impossible or inappropriate options first, then rank only feasible choices by customer fit, availability, quality, policy, and value.**

RecommendAI answers **“which option?”** while NextAI answers **“should we recommend something now?”**

## 37.1 Target architecture

```text
Customer / Conversation
        ↓
NeedAI + Preferences + Constraints
        ↓
Service Catalog / Availability / Pricing / Offers
        ↓
PolicyAI + Eligibility
        ↓
Hard Constraint Filter
        ↓
Candidate Services / Slots / Packages
        ↓
RecommendAI Ranking
        ↓
ExplainAI
        ↓
Top Recommendation + Alternatives
        ↓
ConversationAI / HumanOps
```

## 37.2 Recommendation domains

Support separate recommendation types.

| Recommendation | Example |
|---|---|
| Service | Physio vs massage |
| Location | NW vs downtown |
| Appointment slot | Tuesday 6:30 vs Thursday 7:00 |
| Provider | Approved provider matching constraints |
| Delivery mode | In-person vs virtual |
| Package | Single session vs approved package |
| Offer | Eligible promotion |
| Channel | Voice/SMS/email—usually NextAI |
| Alternative | Closest feasible substitute |

Do not use one model for every recommendation problem.

## 37.3 Recommendation object

```text
RECOMMENDATION

recommendation_id
customer_id
lead_id

recommendation_type

candidate_id
rank
score

hard_constraints_passed

reason_codes[]
tradeoffs[]

confidence

pricing_version
availability_snapshot

model_or_rule_version
created_at
expires_at
```

## 37.4 Hard constraints

Hard constraints must remove candidates before ranking.

Examples:

```text
Service not offered
Location unacceptable
Required language unavailable
Customer said "NW only"
Slot before requested time
Provider unavailable
Offer ineligible
Policy restriction
Capacity exhausted
```

An impossible candidate should not merely receive a lower score.

## 37.5 Soft preferences

Soft preferences influence ranking:

```text
Preferred location
Preferred time
Preferred provider
Shorter travel
Lower price
Sooner appointment
Language preference
Delivery mode
```

Customer can trade these off.

## 37.6 Hard vs soft example

Customer says:

> “I need physiotherapy after 6 PM, preferably NW.”

Interpret:

```text
SERVICE = PHYSIO        HARD
TIME >= 18:00           HARD
LOCATION = NW           SOFT
```

Candidates:

```text
NW 6:30      PASS
NW 7:15      PASS
Downtown 6:45 PASS
NW 5:00      FAIL
```

RecommendAI ranks the first three only.

## 37.7 Constraint provenance

Store:

```text
constraint
value
hard_or_soft
source
confidence
```

Example:

```text
time >= 18:00
HARD
customer explicit
confidence 1.0
```

This makes recommendation behavior explainable.

## 37.8 Service catalog

Create canonical:

```text
SERVICE

service_id
tenant_id
name
category
description

locations[]
delivery_modes[]

eligibility_rules
duration
pricing_reference

active
```

RecommendAI should consume catalog IDs, not free-text service names.

## 37.9 Service-fit ranking

Potential dimensions:

```text
Need match
Customer stated goal
Location fit
Timing fit
Language fit
Delivery-mode fit
Price fit
Current availability
```

Example:

```text
Physio Assessment   96
Virtual Physio      82
Massage Therapy     31
```

Do not recommend unrelated services simply because they are more profitable.

## 37.10 Need matching

NeedAI might produce:

```text
primary_need = PHYSIOTHERAPY
confidence = 0.98
```

RecommendAI retrieves services mapped to that need.

If need confidence low:

NextAI may choose clarification before recommendation.

## 37.11 Recommendation confidence

Example:

```text
Recommendation:
NW Physio Assessment

Score:
94

Confidence:
HIGH
```

Confidence depends on quality/completeness of customer constraints and source data—not just ranking gap.

## 37.12 Candidate generation

Use catalog/query filtering first:

```text
service_type=PHYSIO
tenant=Clinic-A
active=true
```

Then enrich with:

availability  
price  
location  
language.

Avoid sending an entire enterprise service catalog to an LLM.

## 37.13 Slot recommendation

For appointment slots, generate candidate set from authoritative scheduler.

Example:

```text
Tuesday 6:30 NW
Tuesday 7:15 NW
Thursday 6:00 Downtown
Thursday 7:00 NW
```

Then apply constraints and ranking.

## 37.14 Slot score

Conceptually:

```text
Slot Score =
Time Fit
+ Location Fit
+ Customer Preference
+ Provider Fit
+ Convenience
```

Not:

```text
Revenue potential
```

unless there is a legitimate secondary business rule.

## 37.15 Earliest is not always best

Customer wants:

after 6.

Available:

Tuesday 5 PM  
Thursday 6:30 PM.

Do not recommend Tuesday simply because it's earlier.

Constraint satisfaction matters first.

## 37.16 Top-K recommendations

Voice interaction usually needs only:

```text
1–3 options
```

not 15.

Example:

> “I have Tuesday at 6:30 or Thursday at 7 at the NW clinic.”

This reduces cognitive load.

## 37.17 Diversity

If offering multiple options, make them meaningfully different where helpful.

Example:

```text
Option A: preferred NW + later date
Option B: downtown + sooner
```

rather than three nearly identical 6:30/6:45/7:00 slots unless customer wants detailed choices.

## 37.18 Alternative recommendation

When perfect match unavailable:

```text
Best Exact Match      NONE

Alternative 1
Same location, next day

Alternative 2
Same time, different location
```

Explain trade-off explicitly.

## 37.19 Why-not recommendation

Customer asks:

> “Why not Tuesday?”

Answer from actual constraints:

> “The Tuesday options available are before your requested 6 PM time.”

This is much more trustworthy than vague ranking explanations.

## 37.20 Service unavailable

If no feasible candidate:

```text
NO_MATCH
```

Then possible NextAI actions:

```text
WAITLIST
OFFER ALTERNATIVE
CALLBACK
HUMAN
```

Do not force a recommendation.

## 37.21 Recommendation status

Use:

```text
EXACT_MATCH
GOOD_MATCH
PARTIAL_MATCH
NO_MATCH
```

This helps ConversationAI set expectations.

## 37.22 OfferAI

Separate OfferAI from service recommendation.

OfferAI determines:

```text
Which promotion/package is currently valid and eligible?
```

RecommendAI can then rank eligible offers.

## 37.23 Offer model

```text
OFFER

offer_id
tenant_id

name
service_id

effective_from
expires_at

eligibility_rules

price
discount
currency

usage_limit
campaigns[]

status
```

## 37.24 Offer eligibility

Check:

```text
Offer active?
Correct service?
Correct campaign?
Customer eligible?
Usage limit available?
Location eligible?
Date valid?
```

Only then can agent mention it.

## 37.25 Never let LLM invent offers

Bad:

> “I can probably give you 20% off.”

Offer must come from:

```text
OfferAI / Pricing Service
```

with explicit eligibility.

## 37.26 Offer recommendation

Example candidates:

```text
Standard Assessment
New-Customer Offer
3-Session Package
```

After eligibility:

```text
Standard        ALLOWED
New Customer    ALLOWED
3 Session       NOT ELIGIBLE
```

Rank only first two.

## 37.27 Price-fit reasoning

Customer says:

> “I'm looking for something under $100.”

Hard budget constraint if explicit.

Do not recommend $140 package as “best fit” unless clearly presented as outside budget and customer asks for alternatives.

## 37.28 Budget uncertainty

Customer asks:

> “What's the cheapest option?”

Use Pricing API.

Do not infer customer income or affordability.

## 37.29 Package recommendation

Package ranking may consider:

```text
Customer need
Expected usage
Customer preference
Price
Commitment level
Eligibility
```

Avoid pressuring customers into larger packages merely because margin is higher.

## 37.30 Revenue-aware ranking guardrail

If business wants economic optimization:

```text
Customer Fit
must first exceed minimum threshold.
```

Then commercial value may break ties among similarly appropriate options.

Never rank poor-fit option first purely for margin.

## 37.31 Multi-objective ranking

Use lexicographic logic:

```text
1. Eligibility
2. Hard constraints
3. Customer need fit
4. Explicit preference
5. Availability
6. Quality
7. Convenience
8. Cost/value
9. Business economics
```

This keeps recommendations customer-centered.

## 37.32 Weighted scoring baseline

For soft factors:

```text
Score =
0.30 Need Fit
+0.20 Time Fit
+0.15 Location Fit
+0.10 Language Fit
+0.10 Price Fit
+0.10 Availability
+0.05 Other preference
```

Weights are illustrative; calibrate with business/user research.

## 37.33 Rule-based MVP

Start with:

```text
filter hard constraints
↓
score soft preferences
↓
sort
↓
return top K
```

This is often enough for initial deployment.

## 37.34 Learning-to-rank later

With sufficient feedback:

```text
XGBoost ranking
LightGBM LambdaMART
```

could learn ranking patterns.

But only after establishing trustworthy labels and exposure controls.

## 37.35 Recommendation labels

Possible labels:

```text
option presented
option selected
option booked
appointment attended
customer satisfaction
```

Selection is not always quality.

A customer may choose poor option because only one was shown.

## 37.36 Exposure bias

If Option B was never shown, absence of booking is not a negative label.

Log:

```text
candidate set
presented set
selected option
```

This is essential for learning.

## 37.37 Position bias

First option may get selected more frequently simply because it was first.

Experiments should account for this.

## 37.38 Recommendation event

```text
RECOMMENDATION_EVENT

customer
candidate_set[]
presented_set[]
ranking_version

selected_candidate
outcome
```

This creates proper training data.

## 37.39 Service recommendation reason codes

Examples:

```text
PRIMARY_NEED_MATCH
TIME_MATCH
LOCATION_MATCH
LANGUAGE_MATCH
PRICE_MATCH
EARLIEST_FEASIBLE
CUSTOMER_REQUESTED_PROVIDER
```

## 37.40 Negative reason codes

Examples:

```text
OUTSIDE_TIME_WINDOW
LOCATION_MISMATCH
PRICE_ABOVE_PREFERENCE
NO_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
NO_CAPACITY
INELIGIBLE_OFFER
```

Useful for alternative explanations.

## 37.41 Recommendation explanation

Staff/customer-friendly:

```text
Recommended:
NW clinic, Tuesday 6:30 PM

Why:
✓ Physiotherapy
✓ After 6 PM
✓ Preferred NW location
✓ Current slot available
```

## 37.42 Trade-off explanation

Alternative:

```text
Downtown Tuesday 6:00 PM

Trade-off:
Earlier availability
but not preferred location
```

Helpful when exact match unavailable.

## 37.43 Do not expose internal ranking weights

Customer doesn't need:

```text
score = 0.8743
```

Explain actual needs/preferences instead.

## 37.44 Recommendation freshness

Slots/prices can become stale.

Store:

```text
availability_snapshot_time
price_version
expires_at
```

Before transaction:

revalidate.

## 37.45 Booking race condition

Agent recommends Tuesday 6:30.

Another customer books it 10 seconds later.

At booking:

scheduler returns conflict.

NextAI asks RecommendAI for next feasible options.

Never pretend the slot remains available.

## 37.46 Slot reservation

If scheduler supports temporary holds:

use carefully.

```text
HOLD_SLOT
```

must have:

TTL  
customer/session owner  
release.

Prevent capacity abuse.

## 37.47 Offer race condition

Promotion limit:

100 uses.

Customer hears offer while usage 99.

At booking it may be exhausted.

OfferAI must revalidate before commitment.

## 37.48 Location ambiguity

Customer says:

> “Near me.”

Resolve allowed location context before ranking.

Do not infer precise geolocation without permission.

## 37.49 Language support

Customer wants Hindi.

Candidate clinic may have:

AI Hindi support

but no Hindi-speaking human.

Represent separately:

```text
AI_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
HUMAN_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
```

Recommendation should not imply human language support unless true.

## 37.50 Provider recommendation

If recommending a specific clinician/provider:

use only approved attributes:

service eligibility  
availability  
location  
customer-stated preferences.

Avoid ranking clinicians by inappropriate sensitive characteristics.

## 37.51 Provider load balancing

Operational load can be a secondary factor among equally suitable providers.

Do not degrade customer fit simply to balance workload unless necessary.

## 37.52 Capacity-aware recommendation

Candidate:

excellent fit

but zero available capacity.

Mark:

```text
WAITLIST_ONLY
```

instead of recommending as immediately bookable.

## 37.53 Service quality input

If one route/provider/location has operational quality issues:

RiskAI/QualityAI can reduce or remove it.

Example:

booking system at Clinic B degraded.

Do not recommend Clinic B if transaction cannot reliably complete.

## 37.54 Health service guardrail

RecommendAI should recommend clinic services based on the customer's stated administrative/service need.

It should not diagnose:

> “Your symptoms mean you need chiropractic instead of physiotherapy.”

Clinical service-selection decisions need approved clinical protocols/human oversight where appropriate.

## 37.55 Cross-sell recommendation

Only if:

```text
secondary need explicitly identified
```

or relevant approved relationship exists.

Example:

customer asks:

> “Do you also offer massage?”

Then recommending massage information is appropriate.

Do not manufacture unrelated needs.

## 37.56 Upsell guardrail

Upgrades/packages can be suggested only if:

benefit is relevant  
offer is eligible  
customer has not objected to upselling.

Avoid repeated upsell after refusal.

## 37.57 “Cheapest” preference

If customer explicitly prioritizes price:

ranking can emphasize:

```text
price_fit
```

within feasible appropriate services.

Do not secretly hide lower-priced valid options.

## 37.58 “Soonest” preference

If customer says:

> “I just need the earliest option.”

Then time becomes dominant soft/hard constraint.

Recommendation engine should adapt weights.

## 37.59 Preference hierarchy

Example:

```text
Customer:
"NW only, earliest possible after six."

HARD:
NW
after 6

SOFT:
earliest
```

Keep parsed semantics explicit.

## 37.60 Constraint conflict

Customer:

> “NW only, tomorrow at 6.”

No match.

Do not silently relax NW.

Ask:

> “There isn't an NW slot tomorrow at 6. Would you prefer another day at NW or tomorrow at another location?”

NextAI chooses clarification.

## 37.61 Constraint relaxation

Only relax a constraint if:

it is soft

or:

customer explicitly authorizes relaxation.

Track:

```text
constraint_relaxed
approved_by_customer
```

## 37.62 Recommendation plan

Possible:

```text
Exact option
Alternative same location
Alternative same time
```

This makes fallback systematic.

## 37.63 Recommendation diversity

For service packages:

don't return three versions of the same expensive package.

Where appropriate, include:

standard  
lower-commitment  
alternative delivery mode.

But only if valid for need.

## 37.64 Recommendation confidence gap

If top scores:

```text
94
93
92
```

don't pretend top option is dramatically superior.

Present choices.

If:

```text
96
61
44
```

stronger top recommendation is justified.

## 37.65 Tie handling

Tie-break by:

customer explicit preference  
earlier feasible slot  
lower friction  
lower cost to customer  
stable deterministic ID

according to business policy.

## 37.66 Recommendation rejection

Customer says:

> “No, I don't want downtown.”

Update:

```text
location downtown = rejected
```

Do not recommend it again in same context.

## 37.67 Rejection reason

Capture:

```text
PRICE
LOCATION
TIME
PROVIDER
FORMAT
OTHER
```

Feeds MarketAI.

## 37.68 Recommendation learning loop

```text
Recommendation
↓
Customer Response
↓
Selected / Rejected
↓
Booking
↓
Attendance
↓
Feedback
↓
Evaluation
```

Use downstream outcomes, not selection alone.

## 37.69 Recommendation quality metrics

Track:

```text
Top-1 acceptance
Top-3 acceptance
Booking after recommendation
Constraint violation rate
Customer correction rate
Recommendation rejection reason
```

Critical:

```text
hard_constraint_violation = 0
```

## 37.70 Recommendation regret

Later measure:

could a better feasible option have existed?

Useful offline metric.

Example:

customer rejects recommended 7 PM because 6:30 was also available and closer to preference.

## 37.71 Precision@K

For labeled recommendation datasets:

```text
Precision@1
Precision@3
MRR
NDCG
```

Where appropriate.

## 37.72 Constraint satisfaction metric

Separate from ranking quality.

```text
% recommendations satisfying all hard constraints
```

Target for critical constraints:

100%.

## 37.73 Alternative usefulness

Measure:

when top choice rejected,

how often alternative succeeds.

This validates backup strategy.

## 37.74 Recommendation latency

Voice requires fast response.

For slot ranking:

candidate retrieval + scoring should typically be lightweight.

Avoid calling large LLM for simple sorting.

## 37.75 Deterministic scoring

Service/slot recommendation can often be deterministic Python/rules.

Use LLM mainly for:

extracting preferences  
explaining options.

This reduces cost and variability.

## 37.76 Recommendation cache

Static service ranking may be cached.

Live appointment slots should not be cached beyond safe freshness window.

## 37.77 Candidate-set observability

Store:

```text
candidate_count
filtered_count
filter_reasons
top_scores
```

This helps understand why `NO_MATCH` occurs.

## 37.78 NO_MATCH monitoring

High NO_MATCH rate may indicate:

capacity shortage  
catalog issue  
bad preference extraction.

MarketAI should consume it.

## 37.79 Offer acceptance analytics

Track by offer:

presented  
accepted  
booked  
attended  
cancelled  
complaints.

Do not optimize only presentation-to-click/acceptance.

## 37.80 Offer fatigue

Customer repeatedly sees same promotion.

Maintain:

```text
offer_exposure_count
last_exposure
```

Avoid repeated pressure.

## 37.81 Offer conflict

Two promotions applicable.

Rules define:

stackable?  
mutually exclusive?  
higher-priority?

Do not let LLM combine them arbitrarily.

## 37.82 Offer stacking

Store:

```text
stacking_policy
```

Example:

```text
WELCOME10 + CORPORATE = NOT_ALLOWED
```

Tool/OfferAI enforces.

## 37.83 Promotion expiration

Agent must never speak an expired offer.

Offer retrieval filters:

```text
effective_from <= now < expires_at
```

and transaction revalidation.

## 37.84 Experimenting with recommendation ranking

Safe experiments:

ordering of similarly appropriate slots  
number of alternatives  
format of presentation.

Guardrails:

constraint adherence  
complaints  
customer effort.

## 37.85 Pricing experiments

If business legally/ethically supports variable pricing experiments:

GovernAI must approve.

Customer-facing pricing must remain transparent and non-discriminatory.

For most MVP healthcare service scenarios, keep pricing deterministic.

## 37.86 Fairness review

Test whether equivalent needs/preferences produce equivalent service recommendation eligibility.

Do not use:

race  
religion  
ethnicity  
inferred health vulnerability

for commercial ranking.

## 37.87 Language fairness

Same service/time/location request in English vs Hindi should retrieve the same feasible appointment set, subject only to legitimate language-support requirements.

## 37.88 Source bias

Historical customers from one campaign may have chosen Package A more often.

Don't automatically infer Package A is better for future customers from that source.

Use customer constraints first.

## 37.89 Popularity bias

Frequently selected service may dominate ranking.

Do not suppress niche but better-fitting options.

## 37.90 Feedback-loop risk

Recommended options get more exposure, so they collect more acceptance data.

Use controlled exploration in low-risk ranking experiments.

## 37.91 RecommendAI + NextAI

Boundary:

```text
NextAI:
Should we recommend now?

RecommendAI:
What should we recommend?
```

Keep this clean.

## 37.92 RecommendAI + NeedAI

NeedAI supplies:

need  
constraints  
preferences.

RecommendAI maps them to candidates.

## 37.93 RecommendAI + KnowledgeAI

KnowledgeAI provides descriptive information about candidate services.

RecommendAI should not rank based on unstructured unsupported claims.

## 37.94 RecommendAI + PricingAI / OfferAI

Pricing/Offer service supplies:

current price  
eligible offers.

RecommendAI consumes verified values.

## 37.95 RecommendAI + Scheduler

Scheduler supplies:

current availability.

RecommendAI ranks slots but does not create bookings directly.

## 37.96 RecommendAI + PolicyAI

Policy can remove:

ineligible offers  
restricted services  
invalid customer-action combinations.

## 37.97 RecommendAI + RiskAI

Risk can remove/deprioritize candidates with:

operational degradation  
unreliable transaction path.

## 37.98 RecommendAI + FinAI

Internal platform cost may help break ties between equally suitable technical routes.

Customer-facing service recommendation should focus primarily on customer need and legitimate business rules.

## 37.99 RecommendAI + MarketAI

Aggregate rejections and NO_MATCH:

```text
"No weekend slots"
"Too expensive"
"Wrong location"
```

become market intelligence.

## 37.100 RecommendAI API

Potential:

```text
POST /recommendations/services
POST /recommendations/slots
POST /recommendations/offers
POST /recommendations/packages

GET /recommendations/{id}
```

## 37.101 Slot request

```json
{
  "customer_id": "C10028",
  "service_id": "PHYSIO",
  "constraints": {
    "after": "18:00",
    "preferred_location": "NW"
  }
}
```

## 37.102 Response

```json
{
  "status": "EXACT_MATCH",
  "recommendations": [
    {
      "slot": "Tuesday 18:30",
      "location": "NW",
      "score": 0.96
    },
    {
      "slot": "Thursday 19:00",
      "location": "NW",
      "score": 0.91
    }
  ]
}
```

## 37.103 Recommendation events

Publish:

```text
recommendation.created
recommendation.presented
recommendation.selected
recommendation.rejected
recommendation.expired
```

## 37.104 Offer events

```text
offer.eligible
offer.presented
offer.accepted
offer.rejected
offer.expired
```

## 37.105 Golden recommendation dataset

Create scenarios:

```text
Need
Hard constraints
Soft preferences
Candidate set
Expected feasible candidates
Expected top recommendation
Forbidden candidates
```

Example:

```text
Physio
After 6
NW preferred

Expected:
NW 6:30 first

Forbidden:
NW 5 PM
```

## 37.106 Hard-constraint tests

These should be 100%.

Examples:

```text
Customer says "NW only"
→ no downtown recommendation
```

```text
Budget hard cap $100
→ no $130 option presented as valid match
```

## 37.107 Ranking tests

Given three valid candidates:

ensure preference ranking correct.

## 37.108 Offer eligibility tests

Test:

expired offer  
wrong campaign  
existing customer  
usage limit exhausted  
location mismatch.

Expected:

not presented.

## 37.109 Race-condition tests

Candidate available at retrieval

but unavailable at booking.

Expected:

graceful recovery and new recommendations.

## 37.110 Missing-price test

If price unavailable:

do not treat as $0.

Mark:

```text
PRICE_UNKNOWN
```

and avoid claiming affordability.

## 37.111 Missing-availability test

If scheduler unavailable:

do not recommend specific slot as available.

Possible:

general service recommendation + callback.

## 37.112 Contradictory preference test

Old profile:

NW preferred.

Current conversation:

> “Downtown is better now.”

Current explicit preference wins.

## 37.113 Multiple beneficiary edge case

Customer asks:

physio for self  
massage for parent.

Generate separate recommendation contexts.

Do not mix constraints.

## 37.114 Customer rejects all recommendations

Do not continue cycling through endless options.

NextAI can choose:

human  
waitlist  
callback  
close.

## 37.115 Customer asks for something unavailable

Example:

Sunday midnight.

Explain no match and offer closest alternatives.

Do not distort availability.

## 37.116 Customer asks “What do you recommend?”

If service selection has clinical implications, stay within approved administrative recommendation logic.

Example:

> “Based on the service you requested and the times you prefer, this option fits best.”

Not:

> “Based on your symptoms, you should choose treatment X.”

## 37.117 Explainability dashboard

For each recommendation monitor:

```text
Top reason codes
NO_MATCH reasons
Rejection reasons
Constraint violations
Alternative success
```

## 37.118 Recommendation dashboard

Example:

| Type | Presented | Accepted | Booked |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Exact Match | 5,200 | 68% | 55% |
| Good Match | 2,100 | 49% | 36% |
| Partial | 900 | 21% | 12% |

This helps validate matching logic.

## 37.119 Service gap dashboard

```text
NO_MATCH due to:
Weekend availability       34%
Location                   22%
Price                      18%
Language support           10%
```

Feeds MarketAI.

## 37.120 Offer dashboard

Track:

eligibility  
presentation  
acceptance  
booking  
revenue  
complaints.

## 37.121 Recommendation drift

Monitor:

candidate distributions  
score distributions  
acceptance.

Example:

NW suddenly disappears from recommendations.

Could indicate:

capacity issue  
scheduler integration bug.

## 37.122 Rule/model versioning

Every recommendation stores:

```text
candidate_generator_version
filter_version
ranking_version
```

Needed for reproducibility.

## 37.123 Shadow ranking

Candidate ranking v2 runs without affecting presented options.

Compare:

top-K overlap  
predicted quality.

Then controlled experiment.

## 37.124 Canary

New ranking:

5% traffic.

Guardrails:

constraint violations = 0  
complaints  
booking integrity  
customer effort.

## 37.125 Security

Recommendation service should not have unrestricted database access.

Use:

catalog  
scheduler  
pricing  
offer APIs.

Tenant isolation applies throughout.

## 37.126 Privacy

Recommend using:

customer-stated needs/preferences.

Do not use unrelated sensitive customer data to optimize commercial offers.

## 37.127 Governance

Govern:

catalog mapping  
ranking rules/model  
offer policy  
experiments  
reason codes.

Every production version has an owner.

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #111

# Phase 38 — NeedAI: Intent + Need + Pain Point + Objection Extraction

This phase converts every customer interaction into a structured understanding of **what the customer wants, why they want it, what is blocking them, how urgent it is, and what should happen next**.

> **NeedAI should capture evidence-backed customer needs without turning loose AI inference into permanent customer facts.**

## 38.1 Target architecture

```text
Forms / Voice Calls / SMS / Email / Chat / Surveys
                    ↓
             Interaction Parser
                    ↓
                NeedAI
                    ↓
 ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Intent Extraction                  │
 │ Primary / Secondary Need           │
 │ Pain Point                         │
 │ Desired Outcome                    │
 │ Constraint Extraction              │
 │ Objection Detection                │
 │ Urgency                            │
 │ Decision Stage                     │
 │ Likes / Dislikes                   │
 │ Question Extraction                │
 │ Unmet Need                         │
 │ Competitor Mention                 │
 └────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓
        Evidence + Confidence
                    ↓
Customer 360 / SegmentAI / ScoreAI
RecommendAI / NextAI / MarketAI
```

## 38.2 What NeedAI should extract

| Dimension | Example |
|---|---|
| Intent | BOOK_APPOINTMENT |
| Primary need | Physiotherapy |
| Secondary need | Massage information |
| Pain point | No evening availability |
| Desired outcome | Appointment after work |
| Timing constraint | After 6 PM |
| Location constraint | NW preferred |
| Price concern | Moderate |
| Trust concern | Low |
| Urgency | Within 7 days |
| Decision stage | Ready to book |
| Like | Evening availability |
| Dislike | Price |
| Question | “Do you accept insurance?” |
| Competitor | Customer mentioned another clinic |
| Unmet need | Weekend appointment |

---

# 38.3 Canonical Need object

```text
NEED

need_id
customer_id
lead_id
interaction_id

need_type
service_id

primary_or_secondary

status

confidence
source_type

explicit_or_inferred
evidence_ref

first_detected_at
last_confirmed_at

effective_from
expires_at
```

Statuses:

```text
DETECTED
CONFIRMED
ACTIVE
RESOLVED
SUPERSEDED
EXPIRED
```

---

# 38.4 Separate intent from need

These are different.

Customer:

> “I need physiotherapy information.”

Need:

```text
PHYSIOTHERAPY
```

Intent:

```text
INFORMATION_REQUEST
```

Later:

> “Book Tuesday.”

Intent changes:

```text
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
```

Need remains physiotherapy.

---

# 38.5 Intent taxonomy

Recommended top-level intents:

```text
GET_INFORMATION
CHECK_PRICE
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
BOOK
RESCHEDULE
CANCEL

REQUEST_CALLBACK
REQUEST_HUMAN

ASK_INSURANCE
ASK_LOCATION
ASK_PROVIDER
ASK_HOURS

COMPARE_SERVICE
COMPARE_COMPETITOR

COMPLAIN
PROVIDE_FEEDBACK

DNC
NOT_INTERESTED

OTHER
UNKNOWN
```

Avoid hundreds of overlapping intent labels at MVP.

---

# 38.6 Multi-intent support

Customer:

> “How much is physio, and do you have anything Tuesday evening?”

Extract:

```text
INTENT 1
CHECK_PRICE

INTENT 2
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
```

Set one as:

```text
PRIMARY_INTENT
```

based on conversation/task context.

---

# 38.7 Intent evidence

Store:

```text
intent = CHECK_AVAILABILITY
evidence_turn = TURN-18
confidence = 0.97
```

This makes ExplainAI possible.

---

# 38.8 Explicit vs inferred need

Customer:

> “I need physiotherapy.”

```text
EXPLICIT
confidence = HIGH
```

Customer:

> “My back has been bothering me.”

Do **not** automatically conclude:

```text
PHYSIOTHERAPY
```

as a definitive clinical service need.

For healthcare-adjacent flows, that may require approved service-triage rules or human involvement.

---

# 38.9 Primary need

The current main business requirement.

Example:

```text
PRIMARY NEED
Physiotherapy appointment
```

This drives:

ConversationAI  
RecommendAI  
NextAI.

---

# 38.10 Secondary need

Customer may reveal another requirement.

Example:

> “My mother is also looking for massage.”

Store separately:

```text
SECONDARY NEED
Massage

beneficiary = OTHER
```

Do not merge the mother's need into the caller's primary profile.

---

# 38.11 Need hierarchy

Useful structure:

```text
CATEGORY
Healthcare service

SERVICE
Physiotherapy

SUB-NEED
Evening appointment

DELIVERY
In-person

LOCATION
NW
```

This gives MarketAI much cleaner reporting.

---

# 38.12 Need ontology

Normalize synonyms:

```text
physio
physical therapy
physiotherapy
```

→

```text
PHYSIOTHERAPY
```

Similarly:

```text
chiro
chiropractic
```

→ canonical service.

---

# 38.13 Need taxonomy registry

```text
NEED_TYPE

need_type_id
canonical_name
parent_need

synonyms[]
languages[]

owner
version
status
```

Need taxonomy itself should be governed.

---

# 38.14 Pain point extraction

Need tells you what customer wants.

Pain tells you **what problem/friction exists**.

Examples:

```text
NO_EVENING_AVAILABILITY
HIGH_PRICE
LONG_WAIT
DISTANCE
NO_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
DIFFICULT_BOOKING
TRUST_CONCERN
NO_HUMAN_SUPPORT
```

---

# 38.15 Pain object

```text
PAIN_POINT

pain_id
customer_id
interaction_id

category
subcategory

severity
confidence

explicit_or_inferred
evidence_ref

status
```

---

# 38.16 Pain severity

Use:

```text
LOW
MEDIUM
HIGH
CRITICAL
```

Example:

> “Evening would be nicer.”

LOW/MEDIUM preference.

> “I absolutely cannot come before 6.”

HIGH constraint.

Do not treat every mention equally.

---

# 38.17 Need vs pain example

Customer:

> “I want physiotherapy, but I can never find appointments after work.”

```text
NEED
Physiotherapy

PAIN
Availability

CONSTRAINT
After 6 PM
```

All three are distinct.

---

# 38.18 Desired outcome

Extract what success looks like.

Example:

```text
desired_outcome =
book physiotherapy within 7 days
after 6 PM
NW preferred
```

This is very useful for NextAI.

---

# 38.19 Desired outcome object

```text
DESIRED_OUTCOME

outcome_id
customer_id

goal
target_date
constraints[]

confidence
evidence
```

---

# 38.20 Constraint extraction

Constraints can include:

```text
TIME
DATE
LOCATION
PRICE
LANGUAGE
CHANNEL
PROVIDER
DELIVERY_MODE
```

Each needs:

```text
HARD / SOFT
```

classification.

---

# 38.21 Constraint example

Customer:

> “I can only come after 6, but NW would be better.”

Extract:

```text
TIME >= 18:00
HARD

LOCATION = NW
SOFT
```

RecommendAI depends on this distinction.

---

# 38.22 Constraint correction

Customer:

> “Actually, downtown is fine.”

Update:

```text
LOCATION NW
SUPERSEDED

LOCATION downtown acceptable
CONFIRMED
```

Don't preserve old constraint as active.

---

# 38.23 Price concern

Do not create generic:

```text
PRICE_SENSITIVE
```

without evidence.

Capture:

```text
PRICE_OBJECTION
```

when expressed.

Example:

> “$120 is more than I expected.”

Structured:

```text
objection_type = PRICE
strength = MEDIUM
expected_price = UNKNOWN
```

unless customer gives expected price.

---

# 38.24 Price expectation

Customer:

> “I was hoping for around $80.”

Store:

```text
price_expectation
amount = 80
currency = CAD
basis = session
```

This is much richer than a binary price objection.

---

# 38.25 Objection taxonomy

Recommended:

```text
PRICE
TIMING
LOCATION
TRUST
QUALITY
COMMITMENT
COMPETITOR
NOT_READY
NEEDS_APPROVAL
HUMAN_PREFERENCE
AI_PREFERENCE
```

---

# 38.26 Objection object

```text
OBJECTION

objection_id
customer_id
interaction_id

type
strength

status

ACTIVE
RESOLVED
SUPERSEDED

confidence
evidence_ref
```

---

# 38.27 Objection resolution

Customer:

> “That price is okay if evening appointments are available.”

Price objection may transition:

```text
ACTIVE
→ RESOLVED
```

Do not keep using stale price concern in future calls indefinitely.

---

# 38.28 Trust concern

Examples:

> “Is this a real clinic?”

> “How experienced are the therapists?”

Store:

```text
TRUST_CONCERN
```

This can trigger:

KnowledgeAI  
verified credential content  
human support.

---

# 38.29 Timing objection vs timing preference

Differentiate:

> “Evening would be preferable.”

Preference.

> “I cannot come during daytime.”

Constraint.

> “You called at a bad time.”

Contact timing objection.

These should not be collapsed.

---

# 38.30 Decision stage

Operational stages:

```text
AWARENESS
INFORMATION_SEEKING
COMPARING
CONSIDERING
READY_TO_BOOK
DEFERRED
BOOKED
CLOSED
```

This helps NextAI avoid over-selling.

---

# 38.31 Decision-stage evidence

Example:

Customer:

> “I'm just comparing prices.”

Stage:

```text
COMPARING
```

Customer:

> “Book Tuesday.”

Stage:

```text
READY_TO_BOOK
```

Use explicit evidence where possible.

---

# 38.32 Urgency

Capture business urgency:

```text
IMMEDIATE
WITHIN_DAYS
WITHIN_WEEK
WITHIN_MONTH
FUTURE
UNKNOWN
```

Avoid turning health complaints into clinical urgency unless approved triage process exists.

---

# 38.33 Urgency evidence

Customer:

> “I want an appointment this week.”

```text
WITHIN_WEEK
explicit
```

Customer:

> “Sometime later.”

```text
FUTURE
```

---

# 38.34 Like extraction

Customer says:

> “I like that you have evening appointments.”

Store:

```text
LIKE
EVENING_AVAILABILITY
```

---

# 38.35 Dislike extraction

Customer:

> “I don't like the package commitment.”

Store:

```text
DISLIKE
PACKAGE_COMMITMENT
```

MarketAI aggregates these.

---

# 38.36 Preference vs like

Preference:

```text
Prefers NW
```

Like:

```text
Likes weekend availability
```

The latter may not mean it is required.

Keep concepts separate.

---

# 38.37 Question extraction

Every meaningful customer question becomes:

```text
QUESTION

question_id
customer_id
interaction_id

question_type
normalized_question

answered
answer_source

confidence
```

This feeds KnowledgeAI.

---

# 38.38 Question taxonomy

Examples:

```text
PRICE
INSURANCE
AVAILABILITY
LOCATION
PARKING
SERVICE
PROVIDER
HOURS
CANCELLATION
PROMOTION
```

---

# 38.39 Unanswered question

If no grounded answer:

```text
answered = false
```

Then aggregate to:

Knowledge Gap.

Don't hide unresolved questions in transcript.

---

# 38.40 Unmet need

Customer wants something not currently available.

Example:

> “I need Saturday physiotherapy.”

But no Saturday capacity.

```text
UNMET_NEED

service = PHYSIO
need = WEEKEND_SLOT
reason = NO_CAPACITY
```

This feeds MarketAI.

---

# 38.41 Unmet need types

```text
SERVICE_NOT_OFFERED
NO_CAPACITY
NO_TIME_MATCH
NO_LOCATION_MATCH
NO_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
PRICE_MISMATCH
DELIVERY_MODE_GAP
```

---

# 38.42 Competitor mention extraction

Customer:

> “Lifemark has evening appointments.”

Store:

```text
COMPETITOR_MENTION

name = Lifemark
claim = evening availability
source = customer_reported
```

Do not automatically treat claim as verified fact.

---

# 38.43 Competitor sentiment

Possible:

```text
POSITIVE
NEGATIVE
NEUTRAL
```

But store actual reason if available.

Example:

```text
LIKE
Competitor availability

DISLIKE
Competitor wait time
```

---

# 38.44 Decision dependency

Customer:

> “I need to ask my spouse.”

Store:

```text
DECISION_DEPENDENCY
FAMILY_DISCUSSION
```

B2B:

> “I need approval from HR.”

```text
DECISION_DEPENDENCY
HR_APPROVAL
```

Useful for follow-up planning.

---

# 38.45 Buying criteria

Extract explicit selection criteria:

```text
PRICE
TIME
LOCATION
QUALITY
LANGUAGE
CONVENIENCE
TRUST
```

Rank if evidence supports it.

Example:

> “Timing matters more than price.”

```text
priority:
TIME > PRICE
```

RecommendAI can use this.

---

# 38.46 Buying-criteria object

```text
BUYING_CRITERION

criterion
importance

source
confidence
```

Avoid inferring priority from one vague mention.

---

# 38.47 Reason for dislike

Instead of:

```text
DISLIKE = PRICE
```

capture:

```text
current price exceeds expectation
```

when explicitly stated.

Richer evidence improves MarketAI.

---

# 38.48 Sentiment caution

NeedAI may consume sentiment as supporting context, but sentiment should not dominate need extraction.

Customer may sound annoyed yet still want to book.

Treat:

```text
SENTIMENT
```

and:

```text
INTENT
```

separately.

---

# 38.49 Emotion inference caution

Avoid strong labels such as:

```text
ANGRY PERSON
ANXIOUS CUSTOMER
```

Prefer:

```text
customer expressed frustration about wait time
```

Situational, evidence-backed, temporary.

---

# 38.50 Source hierarchy

Need evidence priority:

```text
Customer explicit statement
        >
Customer confirmation
        >
Verified transaction
        >
Form selection
        >
Behavioral inference
        >
LLM inference
```

Use this for conflict resolution.

---

# 38.51 Multi-source needs

Form says:

Massage.

Current call says:

> “Actually I'm looking for physio now.”

Current explicit request supersedes active need for this lead/context.

Keep historical massage lead if still relevant.

---

# 38.52 Context isolation

A person can simultaneously have:

```text
Lead 1:
Physio for self

Lead 2:
Massage for parent
```

NeedAI should attach need to:

customer + lead + beneficiary/context.

Not just customer globally.

---

# 38.53 Longitudinal need history

Example:

```text
June
General physio information

July
Price comparison

August
Ready to book evening physio

August 24
Booked
```

This supports journey analysis.

---

# 38.54 Need history record

Store:

```text
need
status
from
to
source
```

Don't just overwrite the latest.

---

# 38.55 Need confidence

Example:

```text
Primary need = Physiotherapy
confidence = 0.99

Secondary need = Massage
confidence = 0.68
```

Low-confidence secondary inference should not trigger unsolicited marketing.

---

# 38.56 Confirmation policy

Confirm when:

need is transaction-critical  
inference confidence low  
multiple services possible.

Example:

> “Just to confirm, you're asking about physiotherapy, correct?”

Do not confirm obvious facts endlessly.

---

# 38.57 Extraction pipeline

```text
Transcript Turn
      ↓
Language Detection
      ↓
Intent Classification
      ↓
Entity / Slot Extraction
      ↓
Need / Pain / Objection Extraction
      ↓
Normalization
      ↓
Confidence
      ↓
Evidence Mapping
      ↓
State Update
```

---

# 38.58 Structured extraction

Use strict schema output.

Example:

```json
{
  "primary_need": "PHYSIOTHERAPY",
  "intent": "CHECK_AVAILABILITY",
  "constraints": [
    {
      "type": "TIME",
      "value": "AFTER_18_00",
      "strength": "HARD"
    }
  ]
}
```

This is safer than parsing free-form LLM summaries.

---

# 38.59 Pydantic/schema validation

Validate:

enum values  
confidence range  
required evidence references.

Unknown label:

```text
UNKNOWN
```

rather than allowing invented category.

---

# 38.60 Rule + LLM hybrid

Use rules for obvious signals:

```text
"stop calling"
→ DNC
```

Use LLM/classifier for nuanced:

need  
objection  
multi-intent.

Critical outcomes should be reinforced with deterministic checks.

---

# 38.61 Negation handling

Critical.

```text
"I want massage."
```

vs:

```text
"I don't want massage."
```

NeedAI must distinguish.

Build dedicated negation tests.

---

# 38.62 Conditional language

Customer:

> “If you have something after 6, I might book.”

Extract:

```text
need = PHYSIO
time constraint = AFTER_6
intent = CONDITIONAL_INTEREST
```

Not:

```text
BOOK
```

---

# 38.63 Hypothetical statements

Customer:

> “If my mother needed massage, do you offer it?”

Do not automatically create:

```text
active massage need for mother
```

Classify as:

```text
INFORMATION_QUERY / HYPOTHETICAL
```

---

# 38.64 Past need

Customer:

> “I needed physio last year.”

Do not make it active current need.

Temporal extraction matters.

---

# 38.65 Future need

Customer:

> “Maybe in September.”

Store:

```text
future_interest
```

with timing.

Do not trigger immediate high-pressure campaign.

---

# 38.66 Conditional objection

> “Price isn't a problem if insurance covers it.”

Primary blocker may be:

```text
INSURANCE_UNCERTAINTY
```

not price.

NeedAI should preserve conditional relationship.

---

# 38.67 Compound objection

Customer:

> “It's expensive and downtown is too far.”

Extract:

```text
PRICE
LOCATION
```

Both active.

Don't force one primary objection unless reporting requires it.

---

# 38.68 Objection priority

If needed:

```text
primary_objection
secondary_objections[]
```

based on explicit emphasis.

---

# 38.69 Objection strength

Example:

> “A little expensive.”

LOW/MEDIUM.

> “There's no way I can pay that.”

HIGH.

Use careful qualitative strength, not psychological profiling.

---

# 38.70 Question vs objection

Customer:

> “Why is it $120?”

Could be:

PRICE_QUESTION

not necessarily:

PRICE_OBJECTION.

NeedAI should classify tone/content carefully.

ConversationAI can ask/observe follow-up.

---

# 38.71 FAQ vs buying concern

> “Do you have parking?”

Maybe ordinary information.

> “I won't come unless there's parking.”

Now:

```text
parking = HARD CONSTRAINT
```

Context changes meaning.

---

# 38.72 Explicit preference extraction

Customer:

> “Text me the details.”

Store:

```text
preferred_followup_channel = SMS
```

But PolicyAI still decides whether SMS is permitted.

---

# 38.73 Contact preference vs marketing consent

NeedAI extracts preference.

ConsentAI/PolicyAI owns permission.

Never infer:

```text
prefers SMS
```

→

```text
marketing SMS consent = yes
```

---

# 38.74 Customer feedback extraction

At end:

> “The call was useful but too long.”

Store:

```text
LIKE = useful information
DISLIKE = conversation duration
```

This feeds QualityAI.

---

# 38.75 Agent-generated bias

If agent asks:

> “Price is the main concern, right?”

and customer says:

> “Maybe.”

Mark:

```text
AGENT_PROMPTED
```

with lower evidence weight than spontaneous objection.

This prevents scripts from manufacturing market insights.

---

# 38.76 Spontaneous vs prompted

Store:

```text
SPONTANEOUS
PROMPTED
CONFIRMED_AFTER_PROMPT
```

Very important for MarketAI.

---

# 38.77 Form-source bias

A dropdown forces one service selection.

Call reveals broader/more accurate need.

Customer conversation can update but preserve form provenance.

---

# 38.78 Survey extraction

Survey responses are often structured already.

Do not send simple structured choices through LLM unnecessarily.

Use direct mapping.

LLM only for:

free-text feedback.

---

# 38.79 Email extraction

Long email may contain:

multiple questions  
multiple needs  
history.

NeedAI should segment content and preserve evidence references.

---

# 38.80 Call summary is not NeedAI

Summary:

> Customer asked about physio and price.

NeedAI structured output:

```text
Primary Need = PHYSIO
Intent = CHECK_PRICE
Objection = NONE
Decision Stage = INFORMATION_SEEKING
```

Structured semantics are far more useful.

---

# 38.81 NeedAI API

Potential:

```text
POST /need/extract

GET /customers/{id}/needs
GET /leads/{id}/needs

GET /interactions/{id}/intent
GET /interactions/{id}/objections
```

---

# 38.82 Extraction request

```json
{
  "interaction_id": "CALL-90182",
  "text": "I need physio after six, preferably NW."
}
```

---

# 38.83 Extraction response

```json
{
  "primary_need": {
    "type": "PHYSIOTHERAPY",
    "confidence": 0.99
  },
  "intent": {
    "type": "CHECK_AVAILABILITY",
    "confidence": 0.91
  },
  "constraints": [
    {
      "type": "TIME",
      "value": "AFTER_18_00",
      "strength": "HARD"
    },
    {
      "type": "LOCATION",
      "value": "NW",
      "strength": "SOFT"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

# 38.84 Need events

Publish:

```text
need.detected
need.confirmed
need.updated
need.resolved

intent.detected

objection.detected
objection.resolved

constraint.updated

question.detected
unmet_need.detected
```

---

# 38.85 NeedAI + ConversationAI

ConversationAI uses extracted:

intent  
need  
missing constraints.

Then chooses next dialogue state.

---

# 38.86 NeedAI + RecommendAI

RecommendAI requires:

primary need  
hard constraints  
soft preferences.

NeedAI supplies these.

---

# 38.87 NeedAI + NextAI

Example:

```text
intent = BOOK
need = PHYSIO
slot = missing
```

NextAI:

```text
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
```

---

# 38.88 NeedAI + ScoreAI

Intent score uses:

explicit booking request  
availability request  
callback request.

NeedAI provides governed signals.

---

# 38.89 NeedAI + SegmentAI

NeedAI outputs can create:

```text
PHYSIO
READY_TO_BOOK
PRICE_OBJECTION
```

segments.

---

# 38.90 NeedAI + MarketAI

Aggregate:

needs  
unmet needs  
objections  
questions  
likes/dislikes.

This is one of MarketAI's richest data sources.

---

# 38.91 NeedAI + KnowledgeAI

Question:

insurance.

KnowledgeAI attempts answer.

If none:

Knowledge gap.

---

# 38.92 NeedAI + HumanOps

Complex/restricted need can trigger:

specialist queue.

Example:

```text
insurance/admin
```

→ clinic admin.

---

# 38.93 NeedAI + DataAI

Need records become part of Customer 360 with:

provenance  
confidence  
history.

DataAI manages survivorship.

---

# 38.94 Golden Need dataset

Build scenario bank with:

```text
utterance
expected intent
expected need
expected constraints
expected objections
expected evidence
```

At least:

500 MVP examples.

Grow to thousands across languages.

---

# 38.95 Test categories

Include:

single intent  
multi-intent  
negation  
conditional  
historical  
future  
sarcasm-light ambiguity  
code switching  
objections  
corrections  
secondary needs.

---

# 38.96 Multilingual test

English:

> “I need physio Tuesday evening.”

Hindi-English:

> “Tuesday evening physio chahiye.”

Punjabi/English equivalents.

Expected canonical output:

same structured semantics.

---

# 38.97 Code-switch test

```text
"Price thoda high hai, but Tuesday evening works."
```

Expected:

```text
PRICE_OBJECTION
TIME_PREFERENCE = TUESDAY EVENING
```

---

# 38.98 Negation test

```text
"I don't need massage."
```

Expected:

no active massage need.

---

# 38.99 Correction test

Turn 1:

> Tuesday.

Turn 2:

> Sorry, Thursday.

Expected:

Thursday active.

Tuesday superseded.

---

# 38.100 Hypothetical test

> “If I needed massage, could I book online?”

Expected:

information request

not active massage lead.

---

# 38.101 Past-tense test

> “I used physio last year.”

Expected:

historical mention.

Not current need.

---

# 38.102 Unmet-need test

> “I need Sunday, but you only have weekdays.”

Expected:

```text
UNMET_NEED = WEEKEND_AVAILABILITY
```

---

# 38.103 Objection-vs-question test

> “How much is it?”

Question.

> “That's too expensive.”

Objection.

Critical distinction.

---

# 38.104 Buying-criteria test

> “Location matters more to me than price.”

Expected:

```text
priority:
LOCATION > PRICE
```

---

# 38.105 Confidence threshold

Low-confidence extraction:

```text
intent confidence = .52
```

ConversationAI may clarify.

Don't write strong profile data silently.

---

# 38.106 Precision vs recall

For critical signals like DNC:

favor extremely high recall with deterministic phrase handling.

For secondary marketing need:

favor higher precision to avoid intrusive follow-up.

Different labels need different thresholds.

---

# 38.107 Evaluation metrics

Intent:

```text
Precision
Recall
F1
Confusion Matrix
```

Need extraction:

```text
Precision/Recall/F1
```

Slots/entities:

```text
Exact Match
Entity F1
Critical Entity Accuracy
```

---

# 38.108 Objection evaluation

Track per class:

price  
trust  
timing.

Macro F1 matters if some objection types are rare.

---

# 38.109 Critical entity error rate

For:

time  
date  
service  
location.

Track separately.

An average extraction F1 can hide dangerous date errors.

---

# 38.110 Evidence-grounding metric

For every extracted need/objection:

Does cited interaction turn actually support it?

Measure:

```text
Evidence Accuracy
```

This improves explainability.

---

# 38.111 Hallucinated-need rate

Critical KPI:

```text
AI creates need customer never expressed
```

Keep extremely low.

Particularly important for cross-sell.

---

# 38.112 Over-extraction

LLM may interpret every statement as business signal.

Example:

> “I'm driving.”

Do not create:

```text
transportation need
```

unless relevant.

Use taxonomy and business scope.

---

# 38.113 Under-extraction

Customer says three needs in one sentence.

System captures only last.

Test compound statements.

---

# 38.114 Taxonomy drift

Customers begin asking:

```text
home visit
```

frequently, but taxonomy lacks category.

NeedAI emits:

```text
OTHER_NEW_NEED
```

MarketAI clusters it.

Human reviews and adds new canonical taxonomy if warranted.

---

# 38.115 Unknown bucket

Always keep:

```text
UNKNOWN / OTHER
```

Don't force every statement into existing category.

---

# 38.116 Taxonomy versioning

Store:

```text
NEED-TAXONOMY-v8
OBJECTION-TAXONOMY-v5
```

Historical analytics must know which version applied.

---

# 38.117 Model versioning

Every extraction logs:

```text
model
prompt
taxonomy
language model/profile
```

Required for reproducibility.

---

# 38.118 Rule/model split

Examples:

```text
DNC phrase
→ deterministic + model confirmation

Need/objection
→ LLM/classifier

Date/time
→ specialized parser + LLM context

Service entity
→ ontology/entity linker
```

A multi-component extractor is better than one giant prompt.

---

# 38.119 Latency

Realtime turn extraction must be fast.

Run in parallel where possible:

intent  
entity extraction.

Avoid multiple sequential LLM calls.

---

# 38.120 Async enrichment

Not everything needs to happen during live call.

Realtime:

intent  
critical slots  
DNC  
primary need.

Post-call async:

detailed likes  
dislikes  
market signals  
secondary themes.

This reduces latency and cost.

---

# 38.121 Two-tier extraction

```text
TIER 1 — REALTIME
intent
need
critical constraints
DNC
booking entities

TIER 2 — POST-CALL
pain taxonomy
likes/dislikes
competitor intelligence
secondary needs
market research signals
```

Strong architecture choice.

---

# 38.122 Cost control

Use small/fast models for:

classification  
entity extraction.

Use larger LLM only for genuinely ambiguous multi-turn analysis.

FinAI measures cost/extraction.

---

# 38.123 Observability

Per extraction log:

```text
interaction
turn
model
latency
tokens
outputs
confidence
evidence refs
```

With appropriate redaction.

---

# 38.124 Drift monitoring

Track:

intent distribution  
need distribution  
unknown rate  
objection rate  
confidence.

Example:

```text
UNKNOWN NEED
2% → 19%
```

Could indicate:

new market trend  
model regression.

---

# 38.125 Correction monitoring

Customer/human changes:

```text
service = massage
```

to:

```text
physio
```

Track correction rate by:

label  
language  
model.

---

# 38.126 Language-quality dashboard

Example:

| Language | Intent F1 | Critical Entity Accuracy | Correction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| English | 96 | 99 | 1.2% |
| Hindi | 94 | 97 | 2.1% |
| Punjabi | 89 | 91 | 6.8% |

This determines rollout quality.

---

# 38.127 Edge case — customer says “whatever is cheapest”

Need known:

physio.

Constraint:

price priority.

Don't infer:

low income.

---

# 38.128 Edge case — customer asks for mother-tongue support

Store:

```text
LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE
```

not ethnicity.

---

# 38.129 Edge case — customer mentions medical symptom

Do not convert symptom into autonomous diagnosis or recommended treatment.

Keep:

```text
customer-stated concern
```

and route according to healthcare policy if relevant.

---

# 38.130 Edge case — customer says “urgent”

Could mean:

business urgency.

Do not equate automatically with medical emergency.

ConversationAI/approved triage handles clarification.

---

# 38.131 Edge case — agent asks leading question

Agent:

> “Price is a concern?”

Customer:

> “Not really.”

Expected:

```text
NO_ACTIVE_PRICE_OBJECTION
```

not price objection.

---

# 38.132 Edge case — competitor statement

> “XYZ is terrible.”

Store:

customer-reported negative competitor sentiment.

Do not propagate as verified market fact.

---

# 38.133 Edge case — service names overlap

Example:

massage therapy vs physiotherapy.

Entity linker uses ontology/context.

Low confidence → clarify.

---

# 38.134 Edge case — multiple locations

> “NW or NE is fine.”

Store:

```text
acceptable_locations = [NW, NE]
```

not arbitrary primary location only.

---

# 38.135 Edge case — “anytime except morning”

Store negative constraint:

```text
EXCLUDE MORNING
```

Constraint engine must support exclusions.

---

# 38.136 Edge case — “not Tuesday”

Date exclusion:

```text
DAY != TUESDAY
```

Don't lose negated scheduling constraints.

---

# 38.137 Edge case — customer wants no sales

Customer:

> “Just answer my question; don't sell me anything.”

Store:

```text
INFORMATION_ONLY
NO_UPSELL_CURRENT_INTERACTION
```

ConversationAI must respect it.

---

# 38.138 Edge case — customer dislikes AI

Store:

```text
HUMAN_PREFERENCE
```

NextAI/HumanOps can route.

Do not treat as general company rejection.

---

# 38.139 Security

NeedAI has no direct transactional tool permissions.

It extracts structured information only.

Actions remain with NextAI/ToolAI.

---

# 38.140 Privacy

Avoid storing:

unnecessary sensitive inferred characteristics.

Persist only business-relevant, governed fields.

Use TTL for weak inferences.

---

# 38.141 Governance

Every NeedAI deployment should document:

taxonomy  
model  
prompt  
confidence thresholds  
critical labels  
prohibited inference classes  
evaluation.

---

```text
None yet

COMPETITOR
None

EVIDENCE
Mapped to conversation turns

NEXTAI
CHECK_AVAILABILITY

RECOMMENDAI
Rank evening physiotherapy slots

MARKETAI
Price objection signal recorded

STATUS
STRUCTURED / EXPLAINABLE
```

The next phase is **Phase 39 — FollowUpAI + Journey Orchestration**, covering callbacks, SMS/email/WhatsApp follow-ups, no-answer recovery, nurture, appointment reminders, post-visit follow-up, conditional journeys, timing, channel coordination, journey state, cancellation when customer converts, SLA, idempotency, Temporal/n8n workflow design, and cross-channel fatigue control.

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #113

# Phase 39 — FollowUpAI + Journey Orchestration

This phase manages everything that happens **after the current interaction**: callbacks, no-answer recovery, SMS/email/WhatsApp follow-up, nurture, reminders, human tasks, and cancellation of obsolete future actions.

> **The core rule: every future action must be conditional on the latest customer state when it is actually executed.**

## 39.1 Target architecture

```text
Call / Form / SMS / Email / Booking Event
                ↓
             NextAI
                ↓
          FollowUpAI
                ↓
      Journey Orchestrator
                ↓
┌───────────────────────────────────┐
│ Callback                          │
│ SMS                               │
│ Email                             │
│ WhatsApp                          │
│ Human Task                        │
│ Reminder                          │
│ Nurture                           │
│ Reactivation                      │
│ Survey / Feedback                 │
└───────────────────────────────────┘
                ↓
        WAIT / TIMER / EVENT
                ↓
        Revalidate Current State
                ↓
            Execute
                ↓
       Observe Outcome
                ↓
      NextAI Re-evaluation
```

## 39.2 Journey types

| Journey | Typical trigger |
|---|---|
| Requested callback | “Call me tomorrow after 6.” |
| No-answer recovery | Customer doesn't answer |
| Information follow-up | “Send me details.” |
| Quote follow-up | Pricing discussed |
| Nurture | Interested but not ready |
| Appointment reminder | Booking exists |
| Confirmation | Booking completed |
| Reschedule recovery | Appointment cancelled |
| No-show recovery | Appointment missed |
| Human follow-up | AI needs staff help |
| Feedback | Interaction completed |
| Reactivation | Dormant lead |
| Complaint recovery | Complaint unresolved |
| Knowledge follow-up | Question could not be answered live |

## 39.3 Journey object

```text
JOURNEY

journey_id
tenant_id
customer_id
lead_id

journey_type
purpose

trigger_event
current_state

priority
status

started_at
next_action_at
expires_at

policy_profile
workflow_version
```

Statuses:

```text
ACTIVE
WAITING
EXECUTING
PAUSED
COMPLETED
CANCELLED
EXPIRED
FAILED
```

## 39.4 Journey step

```text
JOURNEY_STEP

step_id
journey_id

action_type

CALL
SMS
EMAIL
WHATSAPP
HUMAN_TASK
WAIT
CHECK_CONDITION

scheduled_for

status
attempt_count

condition
result
```

## 39.5 Never schedule blind future actions

Bad:

```text
Call tomorrow 6 PM
→ automatically execute tomorrow
```

Better:

```text
Call tomorrow 6 PM
        ↓
Pre-execution check
        ↓
Has customer booked?
DNC changed?
Customer cancelled callback?
Campaign active?
Valid time?
Phone valid?
        ↓
Execute / Cancel / Recalculate
```

This prevents most annoying outbound behavior.

## 39.6 Requested callback

Customer:

> “Call me tomorrow at 6:30.”

Create:

```text
journey_type = REQUESTED_CALLBACK

scheduled_for = tomorrow 18:30
source = CUSTOMER_EXPLICIT
priority = HIGH
```

Customer-selected timing should be preserved exactly where policy permits.

## 39.7 Callback state

```text
REQUESTED
↓
SCHEDULED
↓
READY
↓
DISPATCHED
↓
CONNECTED
↓
COMPLETED
```

Alternative outcomes:

```text
NO_ANSWER
CANCELLED
BLOCKED
FAILED
```

## 39.8 Callback pre-check

Immediately before dispatch:

```text
Customer still wants callback?
DNC clear?
Phone valid?
Current time valid?
No conflicting appointment?
No duplicate call active?
```

Then PolicyAI authorizes.

## 39.9 Missed callback SLA

A customer-requested callback is different from generic marketing.

Track:

```text
requested_for
actual_attempt_at
lateness_seconds
```

KPI:

```text
ON_TIME_CALLBACK_RATE
```

If missed:

create recovery/escalation rather than silently treating it as another campaign attempt.

## 39.10 Callback rescheduling

Customer changes:

> “Actually call Thursday.”

Update existing journey.

Do not create:

Tuesday callback

plus:

Thursday callback.

Use journey idempotency.

## 39.11 Information follow-up

Customer:

> “Send me details.”

NextAI may create:

```text
SEND_SMS_DETAILS
```

or:

```text
SEND_EMAIL_DETAILS
```

based on explicit customer request + channel authorization.

## 39.12 Message composition

Use approved structured template.

```text
Hi {first_name},

Here are the physiotherapy details you requested:
{approved_link}

If you'd like, you can book here:
{booking_link}
```

Do not generate unconstrained marketing text for each message.

## 39.13 Template registry

```text
MESSAGE_TEMPLATE

template_id
channel
purpose
language
version

variables[]
content
approval_status
```

Examples:

```text
PHYSIO_INFO_SMS_EN_v4
PHYSIO_INFO_SMS_HI_v3
APPOINTMENT_REMINDER_v7
```

## 39.14 Dynamic facts

Never hardcode:

price  
appointment  
promotion

inside old message template.

Template references:

```text
Pricing Service
Booking Service
OfferAI
```

at render time.

## 39.15 Channel coordination

Customer may receive:

voice  
SMS  
email.

Maintain a central:

```text
COMMUNICATION_LEDGER
```

so workflows don't operate independently.

Example:

```text
14:00 Voice call
14:02 SMS sent
```

Another journey should see that before sending more messages.

## 39.16 Communication ledger

```text
communication_id
customer_id

channel
purpose
journey_id

sent_at
delivered_at

status
outcome
```

This feeds contact-pressure logic.

## 39.17 Cross-channel fatigue

Calculate:

```text
calls_24h
sms_24h
emails_24h
messages_7d
```

Then PolicyAI/NextAI can decide:

```text
ALLOW
WAIT
SUPPRESS
```

Do not optimize channels independently.

## 39.18 No-answer recovery

Example:

```text
Attempt 1
NO ANSWER
    ↓
FollowUpAI
    ↓
Contactability + Policy
    ↓
Wait until preferred window
    ↓
Attempt 2
```

Not:

```text
Call again immediately
```

## 39.19 No-answer progression

Illustrative:

```text
Attempt 1 → Voice
↓
WAIT
↓
Attempt 2 → Voice at alternate approved time
↓
Optional approved SMS
↓
STOP/NURTURE
```

Actual sequence should come from campaign policy and customer preference.

## 39.20 No-answer is not rejection

Maintain:

```text
NO_RESPONSE
```

separate from:

```text
NOT_INTERESTED
```

This distinction affects future journeys and reporting.

## 39.21 Busy outcome

If customer says:

> “I'm in a meeting.”

This is stronger than generic no-answer.

NeedAI captures:

```text
TEMPORARILY_BUSY
```

FollowUpAI should preferably ask/obey callback time.

## 39.22 Voicemail

If voicemail is detected:

campaign policy determines whether:

leave voicemail  
hang up  
send permitted message.

Never include sensitive healthcare details in voicemail unless explicitly approved.

## 39.23 Voicemail content

Safer general example:

> “This is ABC Clinic returning your request. Please call us back at the clinic number.”

Avoid:

> “We're calling about your physiotherapy condition…”

when privacy considerations make that inappropriate.

## 39.24 Nurture journey

Customer interested but not ready.

```text
INFORMATION
↓
WAIT
↓
Useful follow-up
↓
WAIT
↓
Re-evaluate
```

Nurture should not mean perpetual weekly contact.

## 39.25 Nurture entry criteria

Possible:

```text
interest present
not ready now
future contact appropriate
channel eligible
```

Explicit rejection may instead mean CLOSE.

## 39.26 Nurture exit criteria

```text
BOOKED
CONVERTED
DNC
NOT_INTERESTED
COMPLAINT
EXPIRED
```

Every nurture journey must have termination.

## 39.27 Long-term defer

Customer:

> “Maybe in three months.”

Set:

```text
defer_until
```

Do not send weekly follow-ups during the defer period unless independently requested/allowed.

## 39.28 Reactivation

Dormant customer/lead:

```text
historical interest
+
current eligibility
+
reactivation score
```

can enter approved reactivation campaign.

Always re-check current permissions.

## 39.29 Appointment confirmation journey

After authoritative booking:

```text
BOOKING_SUCCESS
       ↓
Send Confirmation
       ↓
Delivery Tracking
       ↓
If failure
   alternate approved channel/human task
```

## 39.30 Appointment reminder journey

Example:

```text
Appointment
    ↓
T-48h reminder
    ↓
T-24h optional confirmation
    ↓
T-2h reminder if appropriate
```

Exact cadence depends on clinic policy and customer preference.

## 39.31 Reminder payload

Use authoritative scheduler.

```text
appointment_id
date
time
location
service
```

Do not rely on stale cached conversation values.

## 39.32 Appointment changed

If appointment moves:

all old reminder steps must be invalidated.

Journey listens to:

```text
appointment.rescheduled
```

and recomputes reminders.

## 39.33 Appointment cancelled

Cancel all future reminders.

Potentially start:

```text
RESCHEDULE_JOURNEY
```

only if appropriate.

## 39.34 Customer booked externally

Customer books through website after AI interaction.

Event:

```text
appointment.booked
```

FollowUpAI cancels:

sales callback  
lead nurture  
booking reminder requests inconsistent with new state.

This closed-loop cancellation is critical.

## 39.35 No-show journey

If scheduler confirms:

```text
NO_SHOW
```

possible NextAI:

```text
SEND_RESCHEDULE_LINK
CALLBACK
HUMAN_TASK
```

based on policy/customer relationship.

Do not infer reasons for no-show.

## 39.36 Cancellation recovery

Customer cancels appointment.

Possible:

```text
Ask if they want to reschedule
```

or approved asynchronous follow-up.

Respect explicit:

> “Don't contact me about this.”

## 39.37 Post-visit follow-up

Potential:

feedback  
next appointment information  
approved educational content.

Avoid clinical recommendations outside approved workflow.

## 39.38 Feedback journey

Example:

```text
Visit Complete
 ↓
WAIT 2 hours/day
 ↓
Send short feedback request
```

Survey:

```text
Was scheduling easy?
Was communication clear?
```

Avoid excessive survey frequency.

## 39.39 Complaint journey

Complaint detected:

```text
Commercial journey paused
↓
Human task
↓
Resolution
↓
Customer-confirmed closure
```

Do not continue promotional nurture while complaint unresolved.

## 39.40 Human-task journey

Example:

AI cannot answer insurance question.

Create:

```text
HUMAN_TASK
skill = CLINIC_ADMIN
SLA = HIGH
```

FollowUpAI tracks until:

assigned  
completed.

## 39.41 Task escalation

If SLA missed:

```text
agent
→ supervisor
→ operations manager
```

depending severity.

## 39.42 Knowledge-gap follow-up

If customer asked unanswered question:

```text
question captured
↓
human resolves
↓
approved answer available
↓
customer follow-up if requested/appropriate
```

Also feed KnowledgeAI gap backlog.

## 39.43 Conditional journey

Example:

```text
SEND_DETAILS
↓
WAIT 24h
↓
IF BOOKED
    END
ELSE IF CUSTOMER_REPLIED
    NextAI
ELSE
    Evaluate callback
```

This is preferable to fixed linear automation.

## 39.44 Event-driven journey

Do not rely only on timers.

A journey should react to:

```text
customer.replied
appointment.booked
DNC.updated
complaint.created
call.connected
```

Immediately.

## 39.45 Timer + event race

Suppose callback timer fires at 6 PM at same time customer books online.

Need atomic/current-state check before call dispatch.

The event store/current state resolves conflict.

## 39.46 Temporal orchestration

Temporal is a strong fit for durable journeys:

```text
Start workflow
↓
Send SMS
↓
sleep 24h
↓
wait for booking signal
↓
re-evaluate
```

It preserves workflow state across service restarts.

## 39.47 n8n role

n8n can be useful for:

simple integrations  
marketing workflows  
internal automation  
rapid prototyping.

For core production journeys involving:

DNC  
booking  
transaction integrity  
long-running recovery

prefer durable custom/Temporal-style orchestration.

## 39.48 Hybrid orchestration

Recommended:

```text
Temporal
→ core customer journey state

n8n
→ low-risk peripheral workflow
```

Example:

Temporal:

callback/booking.

n8n:

weekly internal report export.

## 39.49 Workflow definition

```text
WORKFLOW_DEFINITION

workflow_id
version

trigger
steps[]

conditions[]
timeouts[]
retry_policies[]

exit_conditions[]
```

## 39.50 Journey context

```text
JOURNEY_CONTEXT

customer_id
lead_id

current_need
current_intent

preferences
consent

appointment_state
campaign_state

completed_actions[]
```

Don't store unbounded raw transcript in workflow state.

## 39.51 Idempotency

Every step needs:

```text
idempotency_key
```

Example:

```text
SMS:
journey_id + step_id
```

Workflow retry must not send duplicate message.

## 39.52 Exactly-once illusion

Assume messages/events can arrive multiple times.

Design:

```text
at-least-once
+
idempotent operations
```

especially for:

SMS  
calls  
CRM updates.

## 39.53 Step retry

Technical failure:

SMS API 500.

Retry with:

backoff + jitter.

Business result:

customer opted out.

Never retry.

Classify error type.

## 39.54 Retry policy

```text
TRANSIENT
→ retry

PERMANENT
→ fail step

POLICY_BLOCK
→ terminate/suppress

UNKNOWN_TRANSACTION
→ reconcile
```

## 39.55 SMS unknown state

Provider timeout after send request.

Do not immediately resend.

Use message ID/provider reconciliation to determine whether delivery was created.

## 39.56 Delivery tracking

Statuses:

```text
QUEUED
SENT
DELIVERED
FAILED
UNDELIVERABLE
```

Record provider reason.

## 39.57 Email tracking

Track:

send  
delivery  
bounce.

Open tracking should only be used when appropriate and governed; don't over-rely on it as strong engagement evidence.

## 39.58 WhatsApp

Where implemented:

use approved templates/consent rules.

Track:

sent  
delivered  
read where appropriately available  
reply.

PolicyAI determines eligibility.

## 39.59 Channel fallback

Example:

SMS fails permanently.

Possible:

email

only if:

allowed  
available  
appropriate.

Do not automatically spray every channel.

## 39.60 Customer preferred channel

Explicit preference:

```text
SMS
```

should generally outrank inferred best channel.

But transaction-critical delivery may have approved fallback rules.

## 39.61 Journey priority

Suggested hierarchy:

```text
P0 Safety / Complaint
P1 Customer-requested callback
P1 Transactional appointment
P2 Human follow-up
P3 Sales follow-up
P4 Nurture
P5 Research/marketing
```

Higher priority can suppress conflicting lower-priority journeys.

## 39.62 Journey conflict

Customer has:

```text
NEW_LEAD_NURTURE
APPOINTMENT_REMINDER
```

The appointment is already booked.

Nurture should exit.

Transactional reminder continues.

## 39.63 Journey arbitration service

Given all active journeys:

```text
Journey A
Journey B
Journey C
```

decide:

continue  
pause  
cancel.

This prevents channel chaos.

## 39.64 Customer journey state

Maintain overall:

```text
CUSTOMER_JOURNEY_STATE

active_journeys[]
next_action
next_scheduled_action
last_contact
contact_pressure
```

Campaigns consume this before adding new journeys.

## 39.65 Duplicate journeys

Same event arrives twice.

Before creating:

```text
REQUESTED_CALLBACK
```

check:

existing active matching journey.

Return existing ID.

## 39.66 Journey expiry

Example:

price quote follow-up relevant for:

14 days.

After:

```text
EXPIRED
```

Do not execute old campaign journey indefinitely.

## 39.67 Content freshness

A delayed message may contain:

offer  
price  
location.

At execution time retrieve fresh values.

Do not freeze dynamic commercial content inside workflow for weeks.

## 39.68 Offer expiration

Journey planned:

send promotion tomorrow.

Promotion expires tonight.

At render:

OfferAI returns:

not active.

NextAI recomputes.

Never send expired offer.

## 39.69 Link management

Use controlled links for:

booking  
forms  
surveys.

Track:

journey  
campaign

without exposing sensitive customer data in URL.

## 39.70 Form follow-up

Customer receives form link.

Track:

```text
form_sent
form_opened if appropriate
form_started
form_completed
```

On completion:

cancel unnecessary reminder.

## 39.71 Form reminder

If incomplete:

one approved reminder may be appropriate.

Don't repeatedly nag.

Use:

attempt limits  
cooldown.

## 39.72 Lead-source handoff

Example:

Instagram lead form.

Journey:

```text
Lead
↓
Verification
↓
SMS confirmation
↓
Requested voice callback
```

depending campaign design and authorization.

## 39.73 Email collection

If customer provides email during voice call:

NeedAI/DataAI capture.

Tool verifies/normalizes.

Consent/preference captured separately.

FollowUpAI uses email only for authorized purpose.

## 39.74 Message personalization

Good:

first name  
requested service  
requested information.

Avoid unnecessary inferred personalization.

Example bad:

> “Because you're price sensitive…”

Keep messages natural and minimal.

## 39.75 Multilingual follow-up

Store:

```text
preferred_written_language
```

separately from voice language.

Customer may speak Hindi but prefer English SMS.

## 39.76 Translation control

Use approved multilingual templates for high-volume/important messages.

Avoid translating transaction-critical dates/times through unconstrained free text when structured formatting can be used.

## 39.77 Timezone

All future scheduling must be timezone-aware.

Store canonical UTC internally where useful plus customer-local timezone.

Display and execute according to local business rules.

## 39.78 Daylight-saving changes

Long-term callbacks/reminders crossing DST require timezone IDs:

```text
America/Edmonton
```

not static:

```text
UTC-6
```

## 39.79 Quiet/contact windows

Journey timer reaching scheduled time does not guarantee execution.

PolicyAI rechecks permitted communication window.

If blocked:

calculate next appropriate time.

## 39.80 Frequency caps

Example:

journey wants SMS.

Global contact ledger shows frequency threshold reached.

Result:

```text
DEFER / SUPPRESS
```

depending policy.

## 39.81 Fatigue score

Possible components:

```text
contacts_24h
contacts_7d
unanswered_attempts
recent_declines
recent_complaint
```

NextAI can choose WAIT.

## 39.82 Customer disengagement signal

Repeated:

no answer  
no reply.

Do not keep increasing message frequency.

Journey eventually exits/nurtures at lower frequency.

## 39.83 Negative-response detection

Customer SMS:

> STOP

Immediately:

```text
journey interruption
→ suppression workflow
```

Do not wait until next scheduled step.

## 39.84 Positive-response detection

Customer:

> Yes, tomorrow works.

Event:

```text
customer.replied
```

NextAI updates/schedules callback.

Do not continue old automated message sequence.

## 39.85 Reply routing

Replies can be:

```text
BOOKING
QUESTION
CALLBACK
DNC
COMPLAINT
OTHER
```

Route to:

ConversationAI/NextAI/HumanOps.

## 39.86 Booking-link conversion

SMS:

booking link.

Customer books.

Need attribution:

```text
journey_id
step_id
message_id
```

Then calculate:

message → booking.

## 39.87 Journey attribution

Track:

first touch  
assisted touch  
last touch.

Do not automatically claim follow-up caused booking.

For causality use holdouts/experiments.

## 39.88 Journey experiments

Safe variables:

timing  
message length  
channel ordering.

Guardrails:

DNC  
complaints  
fatigue  
conversion.

## 39.89 Example experiment

A:

```text
SMS immediately → callback next day
```

B:

```text
callback only
```

Measure:

booking  
customer satisfaction  
cost.

## 39.90 Holdout

For marketing nurture:

maintain no-follow-up control where appropriate.

Compare incremental conversion.

This tells you whether journey helps at all.

## 39.91 Journey effectiveness

Metrics:

```text
journey_started
journey_completed
conversion
booking
reply
unsubscribe
complaint
cost
```

## 39.92 Step effectiveness

For each step:

```text
sent
delivered
response
booking afterward
```

## 39.93 Journey drop-off

Example:

```text
1,000 journeys
 ↓
950 SMS delivered
 ↓
240 replies
 ↓
120 bookings
```

Useful for optimization.

## 39.94 Callback dashboard

Track:

scheduled  
on-time  
connected  
no answer  
booking.

Break down by:

campaign  
agent  
time band  
language.

## 39.95 Messaging dashboard

Track:

SMS/email/WhatsApp:

sent  
delivery  
failure  
reply  
opt-out.

## 39.96 Journey dashboard

Show:

```text
Active
Waiting
Overdue
Failed

```

plus:
