## 39.97 SLA monitoring

Examples:

customer callback overdue  
human task overdue  
booking confirmation unsent.

Create alerts based on severity.

## 39.98 Workflow stuck detection

Detect journey in:

```text
EXECUTING
```

too long.

Possible:

worker failure  
external API wait  
logic bug.

ObserveAI alerts.

## 39.99 Timer drift

Measure scheduled time vs actual execution.

Voice callback timing quality is customer-facing.

## 39.100 Dead-letter queue

Events/workflow tasks that repeatedly fail:

```text
DLQ
```

Need:

owner  
retry policy  
age.

Critical customer tasks must not disappear.

## 39.101 Journey replay

Reconstruct:

```text
trigger
step sequence
events
decisions
outcomes
```

Useful for audit/RCA.

Replay in non-side-effect mode.

## 39.102 Journey versioning

Record:

```text
workflow_version
template_versions
policy_version
```

A customer journey should remain reproducible.

## 39.103 Migration of active journeys

If workflow V5 becomes V6:

decide whether existing journeys:

continue V5

or:

migrate.

Do not silently change state-machine semantics mid-flight without strategy.

## 39.104 Safe migration

Typical:

new journeys use V6.

Existing V5 complete.

Use explicit migration only where necessary.

## 39.105 Kill switch

Support:

```text
PAUSE JOURNEY TYPE
PAUSE CHANNEL
PAUSE CAMPAIGN
```

Example:

SMS provider sends duplicates.

Pause SMS steps without necessarily stopping customer-requested voice callbacks.

## 39.106 Provider failure

SMS provider down.

Possible:

queue  
fallback provider  
alternate channel.

Policy + cost + message criticality determine behavior.

## 39.107 Voice-provider failure before callback

RouteAI selects approved fallback.

If no safe route:

reschedule / human task.

Do not simply mark callback complete.

## 39.108 CRM failure

Journey continues if CRM is noncritical.

Persist canonical event.

Sync later.

## 39.109 Scheduler failure

Appointment reminder data cannot be verified.

Do not send potentially incorrect date/time.

Wait/retry/human escalation depending proximity.

## 39.110 Edge case — customer books between SMS render and send

Perform final state check just before send where relevant.

For promotional/booking-follow-up message:

cancel.

## 39.111 Edge case — customer DNCs while delayed message queued

Policy check at execution prevents send.

Queue entry alone is not authorization.

## 39.112 Edge case — message delivery delayed hours

If content is time-sensitive:

revalidate before retrying.

A reminder after appointment time should not be sent.

## 39.113 Edge case — customer responds from another phone/email

Identity resolution tries to link with appropriate confidence.

Do not expose customer data until identity/context validated.

## 39.114 Edge case — duplicate webhook

Provider delivers same:

```text
message.delivered
```

twice.

Event handler idempotent.

## 39.115 Edge case — out-of-order events

Receive:

DELIVERED

before:

SENT event due network timing.

State model should tolerate event ordering using provider timestamps/versioning.

## 39.116 Edge case — two journeys schedule same callback

Arbitration/deduplication merges into one.

## 39.117 Edge case — customer wants both SMS and call

Represent ordered actions:

```text
SMS now
CALL tomorrow 18:00
```

Both customer-requested.

Still reevaluate before call.

## 39.118 Edge case — customer says “don't text me, call only”

Set:

```text
SMS_SUPPRESSED
VOICE_PREFERENCE
```

Do not let fallback channel ignore this.

## 39.119 Edge case — unsupported written language

Use customer-approved fallback language or human handling.

Do not send poor-quality critical translation.

## 39.120 Edge case — booking cancelled after reminder sent

Upcoming future reminders cancelled.

No way to retract already delivered message; next communication should reflect latest status if needed.

## 39.121 Journey security

Workflow engine should not expose arbitrary tool execution.

Steps reference approved action IDs.

Example:

```text
SEND_TEMPLATE
CREATE_CALLBACK
CREATE_HUMAN_TASK
```

not arbitrary code.

## 39.122 Template injection

User-provided text must never become executable workflow/template instructions.

Escape and validate variables.

## 39.123 Link security

Use:

HTTPS  
short-lived/signed links where appropriate  
no raw PHI/PII in query strings.

## 39.124 Privacy

Message content should follow minimum-necessary principle.

A locked-phone notification may expose SMS text.

Design sensitive healthcare communications accordingly.

## 39.125 Consent separation

Transactional appointment message and marketing nurture are different purposes.

PolicyAI evaluates purpose-specific consent.

Don't reuse transactional permission as marketing permission.

## 39.126 Journey audit

Store:

```text
why journey started
who/what created it
steps executed
policy decision
content/template
provider outcome
why stopped
```

Potential:

```text
POST /journeys
GET /journeys/{id}

POST /journeys/{id}/pause

POST /journeys/{id}/signal

GET /customers/{id}/journeys
```

Example:

```text
POST /journeys/{id}/signal
```

Signal:

```json
{
  "type": "APPOINTMENT_BOOKED",
  "appointment_id": "APT-1028"
```

Workflow immediately reacts.

## 39.130 Test scenario — requested callback

Input:

```text
"Send me details and call tomorrow after 6."
```

Expected:

```text
SMS now
Callback tomorrow after 6
```

If booking occurs before callback:

```text
callback cancelled
```

## 39.131 Test — DNC after scheduling

Journey scheduled.

Customer opts out.

Expected:

all affected future marketing/contact steps cancelled or blocked according to purpose/scope.

## 39.132 Test — appointment booked

Lead nurture active.

Booking arrives.

Expected:

nurture ends.

Appointment confirmation/reminder begins.

## 39.133 Test — duplicate event

Same `appointment.booked` twice.

Expected:

one confirmation journey.

## 39.134 Test — transient messaging failure

First send returns 503.

Retry once/twice according policy.

Expected:

one actual message.

## 39.135 Test — permanent invalid phone

SMS provider:

INVALID_NUMBER.

Expected:

mark contact problem.

No endless retries.

## 39.136 Test — customer reply interrupts timer

Journey waiting 24h.

Customer replies in 2h.

Expected:

timer path superseded and NextAI reevaluates.

## 39.137 Test — expired promotion

Scheduled message references offer.

Offer expired before execution.

Expected:

don't send expired offer.

## 39.138 Test — timezone

Customer timezone:

America/Edmonton.

Callback:

6 PM local.

System executes at correct offset, including DST transitions.

## 39.139 Test — contact fatigue

Another campaign already contacted twice.

Current nurture wants third message.

Expected:

frequency policy determines defer/block.

Create golden scenarios for:

callback  
no-answer  
nurture  
reminder  
cancellation  
no-show

complaint

multi-channel.

Each defines:

trigger

10k  
100k

```text
Customer benefit
+
task completion

-
```

But keep policy as hard constraint.

## 39.145 FollowUpAI + NextAI

NextAI decides:

what should happen.

FollowUpAI executes:

when/how over time.

At every meaningful event, NextAI can revise the plan.

## 39.146 FollowUpAI + CampaignAI

CampaignAI determines:

campaign eligibility/attempt policy.

FollowUpAI manages individual customer workflow.

## 39.147 FollowUpAI + PolicyAI

PolicyAI authorizes every channel/action at execution time.

This is non-negotiable.

skill queue

## 39.149 FollowUpAI + FinAI

cost per journey

## 39.150 FollowUpAI + MarketAI

why customers defer  
what information they request  
what follow-ups work.

Useful for acquisition strategy.

# Phase 40 — ObserveAI: Voice / Agent / Workflow Observability Control Plane

This phase creates the **operational nervous system** for the entire voice-agent platform. It connects calls, dialogue turns, STT/TTS, LLMs, tools, workflows, policies, providers, costs, and customer outcomes into one traceable view.

> **ObserveAI should let you answer: What failed? Where? Why? For which customer/campaign/provider/version? What is the impact? And what should happen automatically next?**

## 40.1 Target architecture

```text
Voice Provider / Telephony
        ↓
Voice Gateway
        ↓
ConversationAI
        ↓
NeedAI / NextAI / RecommendAI
        ↓
KnowledgeAI / ToolAI / PolicyAI
        ↓
FollowUpAI / Temporal
        ↓
CRM / Booking / SMS / Email

Every component
        ↓
OpenTelemetry SDK / Collector
        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Logs                            │
│ Metrics                         │
│ Traces                          │
│ Events                          │
│ AI Evaluations                  │
│ Cost Telemetry                  │
│ Voice Quality                   │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
        ↓
Observability Backend
        ↓
Grafana / dashboards / alerts
        ↓
QualityAI / RiskAI / FinAI
        ↓
Incident / Auto-Mitigation
```

## 40.2 Three observability layers

You need to monitor three distinct things:

| Layer | What you monitor |
|---|---|
| Infrastructure | CPU, RAM, pods, DB, network |
| Application | APIs, queues, retries, errors |
| AI/Voice | STT, TTS, LLM, agent decisions, tools, conversation quality |

Traditional APM alone is not enough for voice agents.

## 40.3 Canonical correlation IDs

Every customer journey needs identifiers such as:

```text
trace_id
tenant_id
customer_id
lead_id
campaign_id
journey_id
call_id
conversation_id
agent_id
agent_version
```

Then one problematic appointment can be traced from:

```text
Form
→ Lead
→ Campaign
→ Call
→ Turn
→ Tool
→ Booking
→ SMS
```

## 40.4 Distributed trace hierarchy

A call trace might look like:

```text
CALL-90182
│
├── call.initialize
├── telephony.connect
├── conversation.turn.001
│   ├── stt
│   ├── needai.extract
│   ├── nextai.evaluate
│   ├── tts
│
├── conversation.turn.002
│   ├── stt
│   ├── knowledge.search
│   ├── rerank
│   ├── llm.generate
│   └── tts
│
├── conversation.turn.003
│   ├── check_availability
│   └── scheduler_api
│
├── conversation.turn.004
│   └── book_appointment
│
└── call.complete
```

This is the level of visibility you want in production.

Standardize tracing using OpenTelemetry where possible.

Instrument:

```text
HTTP
gRPC
database

Temporal

tool execution
vector search

```

Use one trace context across services.

## 40.16 Logging architecture

Use structured JSON logs.

Bad:

```text
"Something failed"
```

Better:

```json
{
  "event": "booking_failed",
  "call_id": "CALL-90182",
  "tool": "BOOK_APPOINTMENT",
  "error_code": "SCHEDULER_TIMEOUT"
}
```

This makes logs queryable.

## 40.17 Log levels

Use consistently:

```text
DEBUG
INFO
WARN
ERROR
CRITICAL
```

Example:

`NO_ANSWER` is generally not an ERROR.

A scheduler timeout may be ERROR.

Confirmed DNC bypass is CRITICAL.

## 40.18 Error taxonomy

Standardize errors.

```text
VOICE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT
STT_FAILURE
LLM_TIMEOUT
RAG_NO_RESULT
TOOL_VALIDATION_ERROR
BOOKING_CONFLICT
POLICY_BLOCK
CRM_TIMEOUT
SMS_DELIVERY_FAILURE
```

Avoid each service inventing arbitrary text errors.

## 40.19 Error object

```text
ERROR_EVENT

error_id
trace_id

component
error_code
severity

retryable

customer_impact
business_impact

timestamp
```

For every service monitor:

```text
Latency
Traffic
Errors
```

Then extend them for AI and voice.

## 40.24 End-to-end latency

The customer experiences:

```text
End of customer speech
      ↓
STT
      ↓
LLM/Decision
      ↓
Tool if required
      ↓
TTS
      ↓
First audio
```

Measure:

```text
E2E turn latency
```

not only LLM latency.

## 40.25 Time-to-first-audio

One of your most important Voice UX KPIs.

```text
customer stops speaking
→ agent starts responding
```

Track:

P50  
P95  
P99.

## 40.26 Turn latency budget

Example architecture budget:

```text
VAD             100 ms
STT             300 ms
Decision        200 ms
LLM             400 ms
TTS start       200 ms
----------------------
Target ≈ 1.2 s
```

These are design examples, not universal thresholds.

Benchmark with your providers.

## 40.27 Tool latency

Booking may require:

1–3 seconds.

ConversationAI can use:

brief natural acknowledgement

without falsely claiming success.

Measure separately from normal turn latency.

## 40.28 Call setup latency

Track:

```text
API call creation
→ ringing
```

and:

```text
ringing
→ connected
```

Useful for telephony/provider comparison.

## 40.29 STT quality

Latency alone isn't enough.

Track:

```text
WER
critical entity accuracy
customer correction rate
```

especially:

date  
time  
price  
names.

## 40.30 Critical entity accuracy

Example:

Transcript:

> “Thursday 6:30.”

If STT returns:

> “Tuesday 6:30.”

This is much worse than a small filler-word error.

Track critical-field errors separately.

## 40.31 Customer correction rate

Metric:

```text
corrections / calls
```

Examples:

> “No, I said Thursday.”

> “That's not my name.”

Break by:

provider  
language  
agent  
STT version.

## 40.32 Clarification rate

Track:

```text
clarification_questions / call
```

Too high can indicate:

STT problems  
prompt ambiguity  
poor dialogue logic.

## 40.33 Repetition rate

Detect:

same/similar AI response repeated.

Possible:

agent loop  
state bug.

## 40.34 Agent loop detection

Example:

```text
ASK_TIME
→ customer answers
→ ASK_TIME
→ customer answers
→ ASK_TIME
```

Trigger:

```text
AGENT_LOOP
```

after threshold.

Possible automatic action:

human transfer.

## 40.35 Stuck-state detection

Conversation remains:

```text
NEED_DISCOVERY
```

for 15 turns.

Flag.

Not every long conversation is stuck; use expected state progression.

## 40.36 Dead agent detection

Agent receives audio but generates no response.

Monitor:

```text
last_customer_audio_at
last_agent_audio_at
```

If threshold exceeded:

```text
AGENT_UNRESPONSIVE
```

recover/fallback.

## 40.37 Long silence

Detect:

agent silence  
customer silence.

Different causes require different actions.

Agent silence → system problem.

Customer silence → conversation behavior.

## 40.38 Barge-in quality

Measure:

```text
barge_in_detected
tts_stop_latency
false_barge_in_rate
```

Track:

false start  
false stop

packet loss

Booking API returns:

That's a business condition.

Different from:

```text

```

Do not mix these in one error rate.

```text
UNKNOWN_BOOKING_STATE
```

and reconciliation time.

## 40.57 Workflow metrics

in near-real-time where helpful.

## 40.70 Customer-experience metrics

Useful:


## 40.71 AI Quality metrics

Track:

```text

next-action accuracy
```

Production estimates can come from sampled evaluations.

## 40.72 Automated evaluation sampling

Do not evaluate every expensive metric on every call.

Example:

100%:

critical policy/tool rules.

10%:

automated conversation quality.

1–5%:

human review.

Sampling depends on risk/scale.

## 40.73 Risk-based sampling

Review more:

new agent version  
new language  
low-confidence call  
customer complaint  
high-value transaction.

Less:

stable low-risk FAQ.

## 40.74 SLI

Service Level Indicator examples:

```text
call initiation success
turn latency
booking tool success
callback timeliness
```

## 40.75 SLO

Example:

```text
99.5% booking-tool requests complete successfully within permitted conditions
```

SLOs should map to actual business importance.

## 40.76 Error budgets

If service repeatedly violates SLO:

reduce release velocity.

Example:

Voice Gateway error budget consumed.

Pause risky features until reliability improves.

## 40.77 AI quality SLO

Potential:

```text
Critical booking entity accuracy ≥ target
```

and:

```text
DNC critical failures = 0
```

Not every AI metric fits conventional availability SLO, but critical quality thresholds should still be operationalized.

## 40.78 Alert taxonomy

Use:

```text
INFO
WARNING
HIGH
CRITICAL
```

Avoid sending everything as critical.

## 40.79 Critical alerts

Examples:

```text
DNC bypass
Cross-tenant retrieval
Wrong booking spike
Credentials compromised
Provider-wide outage
```

Immediate response.

## 40.80 High alerts

Examples:

```text
Booking API failure > threshold
Agent loop spike
Voice quality degradation
Callback backlog
```

## 40.81 Warning alerts

Examples:

```text
Cost/call +15%
LLM latency increasing
Unknown-intent rate increasing
```

Useful for proactive work.

## 40.82 Alert deduplication

One provider outage can create:

5,000 downstream errors.

Do not page team 5,000 times.

Group by root dependency.

## 40.83 Alert correlation

Example:

```text
STT errors ↑
Hindi correction rate ↑
Provider A latency ↑
```

Likely common incident.

Create one incident candidate.

## 40.84 Alert suppression

During known maintenance/deployment:

suppress expected low-value alerts.

Never suppress critical safety controls blindly.

## 40.85 Alert routing

Route based on component:

Voice provider → VoiceOps  
Booking → Integration team  
Security → Security team  
Campaign issue → Marketing/Ops.

## 40.86 Deployment annotations

Every dashboard should show:

```text
agent V19 deployment
prompt V25
STT change
provider route change
campaign launch
```

This dramatically accelerates RCA.

## 40.87 Configuration-change annotation

Changes may occur without code deployment:

pricing  
knowledge  
policy  
route weights.

Annotate those too.

## 40.88 RCA workflow

When anomaly detected:

```text
Symptom
↓
Find affected dimension
↓
Compare baseline
↓
Inspect recent changes
↓
Trace sample failures
↓
Identify root cause
↓
Mitigate
↓
Validate recovery
```

## 40.89 RCA dimensions

Break metrics by:

```text
tenant
campaign
service
language
provider
agent version
prompt version
model
region
```

This narrows blast radius.

## 40.90 Example RCA

Problem:

booking rate ↓ 20%.

Drill:

```text
Only Hindi
↓
Only Provider A
↓
STT critical entity accuracy ↓
↓
Provider model update
```

Action:

Route Hindi to Provider B.

No need to change sales script.

## 40.91 Trace exemplar

Metric alert can link to example traces.

Example:

```text
booking_timeout_rate > 5%
```

Open representative:

`TRACE-99182`.

This makes investigation much faster.

## 40.92 Log-to-trace correlation

Every log contains:

```text
trace_id
span_id
```

You can move from:

error log

to:

full customer call trace.

## 40.93 Metrics-to-trace correlation

Grafana-type dashboard shows:

P95 latency spike.

Click exemplar trace.

Find:

reranker latency.

This is ideal observability maturity.

## 40.94 Automated RCA

Use AI cautiously to summarize telemetry:

> “Hindi call latency increased after STT Provider A deployment.”

But require evidence:

metric changes  
deployment timestamps  
trace samples.

Do not let LLM invent root causes.

## 40.95 Root-cause confidence

Auto-RCA output:

```text
Likely cause:
Provider A STT degradation

Confidence:
HIGH

Evidence:
3 correlated metrics
deployment/change event
sample traces
```

If evidence insufficient:

state uncertainty.

## 40.96 Automated mitigation

Safe automatic responses:

```text
open circuit breaker
route away unhealthy provider
scale workers
pause broken campaign
```

Preapproved controls only.

Do not allow an LLM to execute arbitrary remediation.

## 40.97 Auto-pause campaign

Example:

confirmed DNC violation:

```text
PAUSE CAMPAIGN
```

immediately.

For softer metrics:

require threshold + sample size.

## 40.98 Auto-provider failover

Health score:

```text
Provider A = UNHEALTHY
```

RouteAI removes it.

ObserveAI verifies:

error/latency recover.

## 40.99 Agent kill switch

If new agent produces:

critical booking defects,

ObserveAI signals GovernAI:

```text
SUSPEND AGENT V19
```

rollback to V18.

## 40.100 Workflow self-healing

Examples:

restart failed worker  
retry transient activity  
move irrecoverable item to DLQ.

Do not hide persistent failures through infinite retries.

## 40.101 Retry storm detection

Monitor:

```text
retry rate
```

If spike:

open circuit breaker.

Otherwise outage can become self-amplifying.

## 40.102 Memory monitoring

Agent service:

```text
memory usage
memory growth
OOM kills
```

Long-lived voice sessions can expose leaks.

## 40.103 CPU

Monitor by:

service  
pod  
tenant workload.

But don't assume CPU is primary voice bottleneck.

Provider/network latency often dominates.

## 40.104 GPU monitoring

If self-hosting STT/TTS/LLM:

```text
GPU utilization
VRAM
temperature
inference queue
batch size
tokens/sec
```

Use DCGM exporter/NVIDIA tooling.

## 40.105 KV cache

For self-hosted LLMs track:

```text
KV cache utilization
cache eviction
```

Poor cache management can cause latency spikes.

## 40.106 Model serving

Track:

```text
requests/sec
tokens/sec
batch utilization
queue delay
```

for vLLM/TGI/Triton.

## 40.107 Database metrics

Track:

```text
connections
query latency
locks
deadlocks
replication lag
disk growth
```

Important for Customer 360/booking state.

## 40.108 Redis metrics

Monitor:

memory  
hit rate  
eviction  
latency.

If Redis contains session cache, eviction can impact voice calls.

## 40.109 Kafka/event metrics

If used:

```text
consumer lag
partition skew
throughput
```

Large lag delays CRM sync/reporting/journey updates.

## 40.110 Temporal metrics

Monitor:

task queue latency  
workflow failures  
activity retries  
worker availability.

Particularly:

customer-requested callbacks approaching SLA.

## 40.111 Dependency map

Visualize:

```text
Voice Gateway
├── STT
├── LLM
├── TTS
├── PolicyAI
├── KnowledgeAI
└── Tool Gateway
      └── Scheduler
```

## 40.112 Service health

Create:

```text
HEALTHY
DEGRADED
UNHEALTHY
```

based on relevant SLIs.

Not merely process `/health=200`.

## 40.113 Synthetic monitoring

Regularly execute synthetic:

inbound call  
outbound call  
STT  
TTS  
booking sandbox  
RAG question.

This detects problems before customers.

## 40.114 Synthetic multilingual tests

Run:

English  
Hindi  
Punjabi

periodically.

Check:

critical entity extraction  
latency  
voice response.

## 40.115 Synthetic policy test

Use dedicated test identity.

Confirm:

DNC case blocked.

This verifies control-plane functionality continuously.

## 40.116 Synthetic booking

Use sandbox/test calendar.

Flow:

availability

book  
cancel.

Do not create real patient appointments.

## 40.117 Black-box monitoring

External synthetic test should exercise actual public/telephony entry point.

Otherwise internal services may all look healthy while edge is broken.

Build dashboards by audience.

## 40.128 Incident integration

## 40.130 Runbook link

Every actionable alert should link to:

shift traffic  
validate.

## 40.131 SLO burn-rate alerts

Rather than alert on every isolated failure, use burn-rate approach.

Example:

fast burn → page.

slow burn → ticket.

This reduces noise.

## 40.132 Alert fatigue

Measure:

alerts/day  
false positives

If engineers ignore alerts, observability has failed.

## 40.133 Dashboard cardinality control

Do not create metric labels like:

```text
customer_phone
```

High-cardinality sensitive labels destroy metrics cost/performance.

Use IDs in traces/logs, not metrics labels.

## 40.134 Metrics cardinality

Good labels:

```text
provider
language
agent_version
service
```

Careful with:

customer_id  
call_id.

Those belong in trace/log search.

## 40.135 PII redaction

Before exporting telemetry:

mask:

phone  
email  
address  
sensitive transcript fragments.

Use structured logging to make this controllable.

## 40.136 Secret redaction

Automatically detect:

API keys  
Bearer tokens  
credentials.

Never allow tool-error stack traces to leak secrets into external observability providers.

## 40.137 Transcript policy

Full transcripts may be stored in specialized controlled data store.

Observability system should generally store:

metadata  
structured fields  
masked snippets

rather than duplicating full transcripts everywhere.

## 40.138 Trace retention

Different retention:

high-cardinality raw traces → shorter.

aggregated metrics → longer.

critical audit events → governed retention.

FinAI should model observability cost.

## 40.139 Sampling

Use:

head sampling

or:

tail sampling.

Tail sampling is useful for preserving:

errors  
high latency  
critical events.

## 40.140 Tail sampling rules

Keep:

```text
100% critical policy failures
100% errors
100% high latency
100% new agent canary
X% normal calls
```

Very effective.

## 40.141 Sampling metadata

Record sampling decision to avoid biased operational analyses.

For business reporting, use event warehouse rather than sampled traces.

## 40.142 Observability cost controls

Monitor:

log GB/day  
trace GB/day  
metrics cardinality.

Prevent runaway telemetry bills.

## 40.143 Tiered retention

Example:

```text
DEBUG logs       3–7 days
Operational logs 30 days
Metrics          13 months
Audit            policy-defined
```

Actual retention depends on requirements.

## 40.144 Data residency

If external observability SaaS is used:

check:

data location  
PII handling  
security controls.

Healthcare environments may require stricter configuration.

## 40.145 Multi-tenant observability

Every trace/log includes:

tenant.

Dashboard access filtered.

Clinic A must not see Clinic B metrics/traces.

Measure service health by tenant.

Global average can hide one customer suffering.

## 40.147 Noisy-neighbor detection

Observe:

CPU  
queue  
API usage.

Rate limit/isolate before it affects Tenant B.

```text
error delta
latency delta
```

## 40.150 Regression detection

Example:

Agent V19:

booking +3%

but:

Do not promote based only on booking.

ObserveAI receives:

## 40.152 Conversation drift

Trigger KnowledgeAI gap.

## 40.155 Provider SLA measurement

Even if vendor claims:

99.99%,

measure your experienced:

availability  
latency

```text
outage duration
```

Example:

```text
availability
+ latency
```

Potential:

```text
GET /observability/calls/{id}
GET /observability/traces/{id}

GET /observability/providers
GET /observability/agents

GET /observability/incidents
```

Avoid direct public exposure.

## 40.159 Health API

Internal:

```text
GET /health
GET /ready
```

with dependency-aware readiness where appropriate.

## 40.160 Events

ObserveAI can publish:

```text
provider.degraded
agent.loop_detected
model.latency_degraded

workflow.stuck

```

Downstream automation subscribes.

## 40.161 Anomaly detection

Start:

static thresholds  
moving averages  
z-scores.

Later:

seasonal/change-point models.

Don't deploy complex ML just to detect obvious outages.

## 40.162 Baseline-aware alerts

Call volume at midnight differs from noon.

Use time-aware baselines.

Avoid constant threshold noise.

## 40.163 Minimum sample

Booking rate:

0% after two calls

isn't necessarily incident.

Use minimum sample for statistical business/quality alerts.

Critical safety violations do not need minimum sample.

## 40.164 Edge case — metrics healthy, customers unhappy

Technical latency okay.

But correction/complaint rate rises.

Need CX observability.

This is why infrastructure-only monitoring fails.

## 40.165 Edge case — provider returns 200 but bad audio

API health says healthy.

Audio quality degraded.

Synthetic audio + customer correction metrics detect it.

## 40.166 Edge case — LLM latency normal, call latency bad

Potential:

TTS  
VAD  
network  
tool.

E2E traces identify actual bottleneck.

## 40.167 Edge case — booking success reported but appointment absent

Tool API claims success.

Reconciliation detects mismatch.

Critical transaction integrity alert.

## 40.168 Edge case — monitoring backend down

Voice platform should continue.

Buffer/drop lower-priority telemetry gracefully.

Do not make customer calls depend synchronously on logging system.

## 40.169 Edge case — telemetry queue overloaded

Apply:

sampling  
backpressure  
lower-priority log dropping.

Never block booking because tracing pipeline is slow.

## 40.170 Edge case — PII accidentally logged

Automatic DLP/redaction alert.

Restrict access.

Create incident if appropriate.

## 40.171 Edge case — clock skew

Distributed spans depend on accurate clocks.

Use synchronized infrastructure clocks.

Temporal ordering may otherwise look broken.

## 40.172 Edge case — duplicate trace IDs

Use standard UUID/trace generation.

Never derive from phone/customer IDs.

## 40.173 Edge case — provider doesn't support trace propagation

Store provider request ID as span attribute.

Map:

```text
internal trace
↔ provider request ID
```

## 40.174 Edge case — async workflow after call

Call trace ends.

Follow-up workflow still belongs to same journey.

Use:

```text
journey_id
```

and span links rather than forcing one trace to stay open for days.

## 40.175 Span links

Example:

Call trace produces:

`callback.scheduled`.

Tomorrow callback trace links to original decision/workflow.

This keeps distributed lineage without giant long-lived traces.

## 40.176 Edge case — retries create many traces

Use:

parent decision/workflow ID

and retry attempt attributes.

Make retries easy to aggregate.

## 40.177 Testing observability

Validate that:

logs generated  
metrics increment  
trace connected  
alerts fire  
redaction works.

Observability is code and requires tests.

## 40.178 Instrumentation contract tests

For each service:

critical spans and attributes must exist.

Example:

booking activity must always include:

```text
tool.name
status
latency
```

## 40.179 Alert tests

Inject:

provider timeout.

Expected:

alert created  
correct severity  
correct team  
runbook attached.

## 40.180 Dashboard tests

Validate:

queries  
filters  
tenant isolation  
time range.

Broken dashboard during outage is a real operational problem.

## 40.181 Chaos-observability tests

Kill:

ConversationAI pod.

Expected:

service recovery

and:

correct detection.

If chaos happens and monitoring does not detect it, observability failed.

## 40.182 Incident replay

Use historical traces/events to recreate incident timeline.

Useful for training SRE/AI Ops teams.

## 40.183 Observability maturity

### Level 1

Logs only.

### Level 2

Logs + metrics.

### Level 3

Distributed traces + SLOs.

### Level 4

AI/Voice quality + business telemetry.

### Level 5

Automated correlation + controlled remediation.

Target Level 3–4 early.

# Phase 41 — QualityAI: Automated QA + Evaluation Control Plane

This phase creates the **quality-management layer** for every voice interaction, agent version, language, provider route, campaign, tool action, and customer outcome.

> **QualityAI should answer four questions: Did the agent do the right thing? Did it say the right thing? Did the systems execute correctly? Did the customer receive a trustworthy experience?**

## 41.1 Target architecture

```text
Voice Call / SMS / Email / Chat
          ↓
Transcript + Audio + Events
          ↓
Conversation State + Tool Traces
          ↓
Policy / Booking / Knowledge Evidence
          ↓
              QualityAI
          ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Deterministic Checks                │
│ LLM-as-Judge Checks                 │
│ Audio / Voice Checks                │
│ Tool / Transaction Checks           │
│ Policy / Compliance Checks          │
│ RAG Grounding Checks                │
│ Language Quality Checks             │
│ Human QA Sampling                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
          ↓
Quality Score + Critical Defects
          ↓
ObserveAI / GovernAI / RiskAI
          ↓
Pass / Review / Retrain / Rollback
```

## 41.2 Do not use one generic quality score

Maintain separate quality dimensions.

| Dimension | Question |
|---|---|
| Opening | Was the call started appropriately? |
| Disclosure | Was AI/organization identity handled correctly? |
| Listening | Did the agent understand the customer? |
| Intent | Was intent detected correctly? |
| Need Discovery | Were requirements captured accurately? |
| Language | Was mother-tongue interaction usable? |
| Factual Accuracy | Were statements correct and grounded? |
| Tool Accuracy | Were the correct tools used correctly? |
| Booking Integrity | Was the appointment accurate? |
| Policy | Were DNC/consent/limits respected? |
| Objection Handling | Was customer concern handled appropriately? |
| Human Escalation | Did the system transfer when needed? |
| Conversation UX | Was the interaction natural and efficient? |
| Closing | Did the closing match actual outcome? |

A call can be conversationally excellent but transactionally unsafe.

---

# 41.3 Quality scorecard

Example:

```text
CALL QUALITY

Opening                    95
Disclosure                100
Listening                  92
Intent                     98
Need Discovery             91
Language                   94
Accuracy                   97
RAG Grounding              99
Tool Correctness           100
Booking Integrity          100
Objection Handling          88
Human Escalation           100
Closing                     96
Customer Experience         92
```

Then separately:

```text
CRITICAL DEFECTS
0
```

Critical defects must never disappear inside the average.

---

# 41.4 Defect severity

Use at least:

```text
P0 — Critical
P1 — High
P2 — Medium
P3 — Low
```

### P0 examples

```text
Confirmed DNC bypass
Cross-tenant data exposure
Wrong customer appointment
Unauthorized sensitive tool action
Unsafe fabricated clinical guidance
```

### P1

```text
Wrong appointment time caught before booking
Incorrect price presented
Human request ignored
Major hallucination
```

### P2

```text
Poor objection handling
Repeated question
Unnecessary clarification
```

### P3

```text
Minor wording issue
Slightly awkward pronunciation
```

---

# 41.5 Hard-fail rules

Some quality conditions should result in:

```text
QUALITY = FAIL
```

regardless of composite score.

Example:

```text
if DNC_BYPASS:
    FAIL
```

```text
if CROSS_TENANT_DATA:
    FAIL
```

```text
if WRONG_BOOKING_EXECUTED:
    FAIL
```

Do not average these away.

---

# 41.6 Automated evaluation layers

Use several evaluation mechanisms.

```text
Layer 1
Deterministic validation

Layer 2
Model/classifier evaluation

Layer 3
LLM judge

Layer 4
Human QA
```

Each is suited to different checks.

---

# 41.7 Deterministic QA

Best for things that have objectively correct answers.

Examples:

```text
Was DNC checked?
Was correct appointment ID returned?
Did customer confirm selected slot?
Did tool return SUCCESS?
Was expired offer used?
```

These should not require an LLM judge.

---

# 41.8 Event-sequence validation

Example expected booking flow:

```text
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
      ↓
CUSTOMER_SELECTS_SLOT
      ↓
CONFIRMATION
      ↓
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
      ↓
BOOKING_SUCCESS
```

If event log shows:

```text
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
before
CUSTOMER_CONFIRMATION
```

QualityAI flags:

```text
TRANSACTION_GUARD_FAILURE
```

---

# 41.9 Booking integrity QA

Compare four sources:

```text
Customer statement
Conversation state
Tool request
Scheduler result
```

They must agree.

Example:

```text
Customer: Tuesday 6:30
State: Tuesday 6:30
Tool: Tuesday 6:30
Scheduler: Tuesday 6:30
```

PASS.

---

# 41.10 Booking mismatch test

If:

```text
Customer = Tuesday
Tool = Thursday
```

flag immediately even if booking API succeeds.

Technical success does not mean business correctness.

---

# 41.11 Price validation

Compare spoken price to authoritative pricing event.

Example:

```text
Pricing API = $120
Agent says = $120
```

PASS.

Agent says:

```text
$100
```

FAIL.

This is much more reliable than subjective scoring.

---

# 41.12 Offer validation

Check:

offer mentioned  
offer eligible  
offer active  
offer version.

If agent mentions expired promotion:

```text
OFFER_INTEGRITY_FAIL
```

---

# 41.13 Knowledge grounding

For factual claims, QualityAI verifies:

```text
Claim
 ↓
Evidence source
 ↓
Supported?
```

Classify:

```text
SUPPORTED
PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
UNSUPPORTED
CONTRADICTED
```

---

# 41.14 Hallucination taxonomy

Separate:

```text
Invented service
Invented price
Invented availability
Invented policy
Invented credential
Invented competitor information
```

Not every hallucination has equal risk.

---

# 41.15 Groundedness score

Example:

```text
Factual claims = 10
Supported = 9
Unsupported = 1

Groundedness = 90%
```

But if unsupported claim concerns appointment confirmation:

severity may be P0/P1.

---

# 41.16 Claim extraction

QualityAI first extracts meaningful factual claims.

Example:

> “We have Tuesday 6:30 available and the assessment costs $120.”

Claims:

```text
availability(Tuesday 6:30)
price(assessment=$120)
```

Then validate against authoritative sources.

---

# 41.17 LLM-as-judge

Useful for nuanced dimensions:

```text
Did agent answer customer's actual question?
Was objection handled appropriately?
Was response unnecessarily pushy?
Did agent maintain conversation context?
```

But LLM judge is not truth itself.

Calibrate it against human reviewers.

---

# 41.18 Judge rubric

Use precise rubric instead of:

> “Rate conversation quality 1–10.”

Example:

```text
QUESTION:
Did the response directly address
the customer's stated price concern?

0 = ignored
1 = partially addressed
2 = clearly addressed
```

Specific rubrics produce more stable evaluation.

---

# 41.19 Multi-judge strategy

For particularly important nuanced evaluations:

```text
Judge A
Judge B
```

If disagreement high:

human review.

Do not use this everywhere because of cost.

---

# 41.20 Judge model versioning

Store:

```text
judge_model
judge_prompt
rubric_version
```

If evaluator changes, historical scores remain interpretable.

---

# 41.21 Judge drift

An evaluator-model upgrade can alter scores without actual production-quality change.

Run old and new evaluators on fixed benchmark before switching.

---

# 41.22 Human QA

Human review remains important for:

new agents  
new languages  
complaints  
high-risk failures  
evaluator calibration.

QualityAI should **reduce manual workload**, not eliminate human QA.

---

# 41.23 QA sampling strategy

Possible:

```text
100% critical rule checks
100% complaints
100% policy exceptions

20% new agent canary
10% new language
5% normal calls
```

Adjust based on risk and volume.

---

# 41.24 Risk-based sampling

Increase sample when:

```text
low confidence
multiple corrections
long call
human takeover
new provider
new model
high-value transaction
```

---

# 41.25 Random sampling

Keep some random sample.

Otherwise QA dataset becomes biased toward only problematic calls.

You need to know normal quality too.

---

# 41.26 Stratified sampling

Sample across:

```text
tenant
campaign
service
language
provider
agent version
call outcome
```

This prevents English/large campaigns from dominating QA.

---

# 41.27 QA review object

```text
QA_REVIEW

review_id
call_id

review_type
AUTO / HUMAN

rubric_version

scores{}
critical_defects[]

reviewer
confidence

created_at
```

---

# 41.28 QA console

Reviewer should see:

```text
Audio
Transcript
Turn timeline
State transitions
Tool calls
Policy events
Knowledge evidence
Booking outcome
Automated QA
```

One integrated workspace.

---

# 41.29 Audio synchronized review

Reviewer clicks transcript turn.

Audio jumps to same timestamp.

This dramatically improves QA productivity.

---

# 41.30 Auto-highlight risky moments

Examples:

```text
Customer correction
Price mention
Booking confirmation
DNC statement
Human request
Tool failure
```

Reviewer can inspect these first.

---

# 41.31 Opening rubric

Possible checks:

```text
Organization identified?
AI identity disclosed where required?
Reason for call provided?
Correct person/context handled?
Permission to continue?
```

Score separately.

---

# 41.32 Disclosure QA

Validate required disclosure wording or semantic elements.

For deterministic required wording:

use exact/normalized check where practical.

Do not leave critical disclosure entirely to subjective LLM scoring.

---

# 41.33 Listening quality

Evaluate whether agent:

```text
used information already provided
responded to customer correction
avoided repeating answered questions
```

This is a major trust metric.

---

# 41.34 Intent accuracy

Compare production intent:

```text
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
```

with golden/human-labeled intent.

Measure:

precision  
recall  
F1.

---

# 41.35 Need extraction accuracy

Validate:

primary need  
secondary need  
constraints  
objections.

Particularly:

hard vs soft constraints.

---

# 41.36 Critical entity accuracy

Separate score for:

```text
date
time
service
location
price
phone
email
```

Target should be stricter than general entity extraction.

---

# 41.37 Date/time QA

Example:

Customer:

> “Thursday after six.”

Extracted:

```text
Thursday
after 18:00
```

PASS.

If agent says:

> “Tuesday at six.”

P1/P0 depending whether transaction occurs.

---

# 41.38 Customer correction QA

If customer corrects:

> “No, Thursday.”

Agent must:

update state  
stop using Tuesday.

Failure:

```text
CUSTOMER_CORRECTION_IGNORED
```

---

# 41.39 Mother-tongue quality

Evaluate separately:

```text
STT understanding
Grammar/naturalness
Pronunciation
Code-switch handling
Critical entity accuracy
```

Do not treat all multilingual quality as one score.

---

# 41.40 Accent robustness

Testing should include diverse speech patterns without making demographic assumptions.

Evaluate actual acoustic/language performance.

---

# 41.41 Code-switch QA

Example:

> “Tuesday evening physio chahiye.”

Expected:

correct need/time extraction.

Agent response should remain coherent.

---

# 41.42 Pronunciation QA

Critical terms:

```text
clinic names
provider names
street names
service terms
prices
times
```

Use curated pronunciation tests.

---

# 41.43 Voice naturalness

Possible rating dimensions:

```text
pace
pause
prosody
clarity
roboticness
```

Human/automatic audio models can assist.

But don't optimize naturalness at expense of accuracy.

---

# 41.44 Turn-taking QA

Evaluate:

```text
agent interruption
customer interruption
barge-in recovery
long silence
overlap
```

Metrics from ObserveAI complement human review.

---

# 41.45 Response-length QA

Customer asks simple price question.

Agent gives 80-second explanation.

Flag:

```text
OVERLY_VERBOSE
```

Voice UX needs concise responses.

---

# 41.46 Repetition QA

Detect repeated:

greeting  
questions  
recommendations.

Example:

asking preferred location three times.

Flag:

```text
REPEATED_QUESTION
```

---

# 41.47 Loop QA

If state sequence resembles:

```text
ASK_TIME
ASK_TIME
ASK_TIME
```

critical usability defect.

ObserveAI detects automatically.

---

# 41.48 Objection-handling rubric

For price objection:

```text
Acknowledged concern?
Used approved facts?
Avoided unauthorized discount?
Offered relevant option?
Avoided pressure?
```

Each can be scored.

---

# 41.49 Trust-objection QA

Check:

agent uses verified information

rather than:

invented accolades/reviews.

---

# 41.50 Competitor handling QA

Pass if agent:

does not fabricate competitor facts  
does not insult competitor  
focuses on verified own offering.

---

# 41.51 Human request QA

Customer:

> “I want to talk to a person.”

Expected:

```text
TRANSFER / CALLBACK
```

depending availability.

If AI continues sales qualification:

critical defect.

---

# 41.52 Escalation appropriateness

Too few transfers can be unsafe.

Too many transfers can mean poor automation.

Measure:

```text
required transfer success
unnecessary transfer rate
```

separately.

---

# 41.53 Restricted-topic QA

Healthcare context:

customer asks for clinical advice outside approved scope.

Expected:

safe boundary + approved escalation.

Flag if agent improvises clinical recommendation.

---

# 41.54 DNC QA

Test:

```text
"Stop calling me."
"Don't contact me again."
"Remove my number."
```

Expected:

suppression workflow.

Critical performance should be deterministic.

---

# 41.55 Temporary defer vs DNC

Customer:

> “Not right now.”

Should not automatically become permanent DNC.

QualityAI evaluates correct classification.

---

# 41.56 Channel preference QA

Customer:

> “Don't call; text me.”

Expected:

voice suppression/preferences updated appropriately.

Do not continue voice follow-up.

---

# 41.57 Tool-selection accuracy

Example:

customer asks availability.

Correct tool:

```text
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
```

Incorrect:

```text
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
```

Track:

```text
tool_selection_accuracy
```

---

# 41.58 Tool-parameter accuracy

Correct tool but wrong parameters is still a defect.

Example:

```text
service = PHYSIO
location = NW
after = 18:00
```

must match customer requirement.

---

# 41.59 Read vs write distinction

Customer asks:

> “Do you have Tuesday 6:30?”

Use availability lookup.

Do not book without consent.

QualityAI explicitly tests premature writes.

---

# 41.60 Transaction confirmation

Before:

book  
cancel  
reschedule,

check appropriate customer confirmation.

Missing confirmation:

critical transaction defect.

---

# 41.61 Unknown transaction QA

If booking response times out:

expected:

reconciliation.

Not:

retry blindly

or:

claim success.

---

# 41.62 Post-tool response QA

Tool:

```text
FAILURE
```

Agent must not say:

> “Done.”

QualityAI compares response semantics to tool result.

---

# 41.63 Closing QA

Outcome:

NO APPOINTMENT.

Agent says:

> “Your appointment is confirmed.”

Critical failure.

Closing must match authoritative state.

---

# 41.64 Disposition QA

Post-call disposition:

```text
BOOKED
```

must match scheduler state.

Do not trust AI disposition alone.

---

# 41.65 Summary QA

Compare automated summary against:

transcript  
tool events.

Check:

unsupported claims  
missing critical information  
wrong booking state.

---

# 41.66 Structured extraction QA

Validate:

likes  
dislikes  
objections  
secondary needs.

Avoid hallucinated market signals.

---

# 41.67 Spontaneous/prompted QA

If agent suggested:

> “Would weekends be useful?”

and customer says:

> “Maybe.”

Market signal should be:

```text
PROMPTED / WEAK
```

not high-confidence spontaneous demand.

---

# 41.68 Customer experience rubric

Possible dimensions:

```text
clear
respectful
efficient
responsive
non-repetitive
customer-controlled
```

Avoid over-reliance on inferred emotion.

---

# 41.69 Pushiness detection

Flag patterns:

```text
Repeated CTA after refusal
Repeated upsell
Ignoring "just information"
Continuing after customer says busy
```

This belongs in ResponsibleAI + QA.

---

# 41.70 Customer effort

Combine:

```text
corrections
clarifications
repeated questions
failed tools
transfers
```

Create:

```text
CUSTOMER_EFFORT_SCORE
```

Low effort generally better.

---

# 41.71 First-contact resolution

Did customer need another interaction because current agent failed?

Track:

```text
FCR
```

where measurable.

---

# 41.72 Task-completion score

Possible:

```text
BOOKING_REQUEST
→ appointment booked correctly
```

or:

```text
INFO_REQUEST
→ question answered
```

Measure task-specific quality.

---

# 41.73 Outcome is not quality

Customer may not book for valid reasons.

A perfectly handled call can result in:

```text
NOT_BOOKED
```

Do not score it as poor quality solely because conversion failed.

---

# 41.74 Conversion is not quality

Similarly:

customer books despite bad AI experience.

Quality still may be poor.

Keep:

business outcome

and:

quality

separate.

---

# 41.75 Quality aggregation

Composite score can be useful:

```text
overall_quality
```

but use weighted categories.

Example:

```text
Accuracy           25%
Transaction        20%
Policy             20%
Conversation       15%
Language           10%
Customer Experience10%
```

Illustrative only.

Critical defects override.

---

# 41.76 Quality thresholds

Example:

```text
95–100  EXCELLENT
90–94   GOOD
80–89   REVIEW
<80     FAIL
```

Actual thresholds should be benchmarked.

---

# 41.77 Agent version scorecard

Example:

| Metric | V18 | V19 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Overall QA | 93 | 95 |
| Critical entity | 98 | 99 |
| Tool accuracy | 99.6 | 99.8 |
| Customer corrections | 3.1% | 2.0% |
| P0/P1 | 0 | 0 |

Then decide promotion.

---

# 41.78 Provider quality scorecard

Compare:

voice route/provider stack by:

```text
STT accuracy
language quality
latency
tool success
customer correction
```

This gives quality input to RouteAI.

---

# 41.79 Language scorecard

Example:

| Dimension | English | Hindi | Punjabi |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Intent Accuracy | 97 | 95 | 91 |
| Critical Entity | 99 | 97 | 92 |
| Naturalness | 95 | 93 | 88 |
| Correction Rate | 1% | 2% | 6% |

Do not scale Punjabi volume as aggressively until quality is acceptable.

---

# 41.80 Campaign quality scorecard

Track QA by campaign.

A campaign may have:

excellent technical agent

but poor expectation alignment from ad copy.

QualityAI can surface:

```text
AD_TO_CALL_EXPECTATION_MISMATCH
```

---

# 41.81 QA defect taxonomy

Create standard codes:

```text
WRONG_INTENT
MISSED_NEED
WRONG_SLOT
WRONG_PRICE
RAG_UNSUPPORTED
TOOL_WRONG
TOOL_PARAMETER_WRONG
PREMATURE_BOOK
HUMAN_REQUEST_IGNORED
DNC_FAILURE
REPETITION
LOOP
BAD_CLOSING
```

---

# 41.82 Defect ownership

Map defect to likely owner:

```text
STT_ERROR               → VoiceOps
WRONG_INTENT             → NeedAI
WRONG_NEXT_ACTION        → NextAI
BAD_RECOMMENDATION       → RecommendAI
RAG_UNSUPPORTED          → KnowledgeAI
BOOKING_TOOL             → ToolAI
DNC                      → PolicyAI
```

Accelerates remediation.

---

# 41.83 Root-cause enrichment

QualityAI should distinguish:

```text
SYMPTOM
```

from:

```text
ROOT_CAUSE
```

Example:

Symptom:

wrong booking time.

Potential cause:

STT misheard Thursday as Tuesday.

Do not automatically blame ConversationAI.

---

# 41.84 Defect → trace

Every defect links to:

```text
trace_id
turn_id
tool_call_id
```

Engineer can reproduce the exact failure.

---

# 41.85 Defect → regression test

Every P0/P1 becomes:

```text
new golden test
```

This is critical.

Production failures should permanently improve the test suite.

---

# 41.86 Golden call library

Maintain curated cases:

```text
happy path
price objection
human request
DNC
wrong person
multilingual
booking correction
tool timeout
competitor question
restricted clinical question
```

Audio where permitted plus transcript/event fixtures.

---

# 41.87 Golden dataset structure

```text
GOLDEN_CASE

case_id
language
scenario

input_turns
expected_intents
expected_state_path
expected_tools
expected_outcome

critical_assertions[]
```

---

# 41.88 Audio golden set

Include recordings with:

```text
noise
different speaking speeds
code switching
interruptions
street names
appointment times
```

Useful for STT/VAD/TTS regression.

---

# 41.89 Synthetic test generation

AI can generate variations:

```text
Tuesday → Thursday
6 PM → 7 PM
NW → downtown
```

to expand scenario coverage.

But human-curated golden cases remain the benchmark core.

---

# 41.90 Mutation testing

Change one critical semantic element.

Example:

```text
"Call me"
→
"Don't call me"
```

Expected behavior must flip.

This is very powerful for safety testing.

---

# 41.91 Adversarial tests

Examples:

```text
Prompt injection
False customer premise
Fake promotion
Conflicting dates
Multiple intents
Aggressive competitor comparison
```

Expected safe handling.

---

# 41.92 Multilingual regression

Every agent release reruns:

English  
Hindi  
Punjabi

critical flows.

Do not certify a multilingual agent based only on English evaluation.

---

# 41.93 LLM model regression

When changing model:

same golden conversations

→ compare:

intent  
tool calls  
responses  
quality.

A stronger general model can still regress your specific workflow.

---

# 41.94 Prompt regression

Prompt change must rerun:

critical cases.

Particularly:

DNC  
human request  
booking  
price.

---

# 41.95 Knowledge regression

New KB/index:

rerun FAQ/groundedness set.

Check whether answer quality improves without introducing conflicting sources.

---

# 41.96 Provider regression

New STT/TTS/voice platform version:

run audio suite.

Evaluate:

accuracy  
latency  
naturalness.

---

# 41.97 QA release gate

Before production:

```text
P0 failures         = 0
P1 critical suite   = 0
DNC suite           = 100%
Human-request suite = 100%
Booking suite       = 100%
Cross-tenant suite  = 100%
```

Then quality thresholds for noncritical dimensions.

---

# 41.98 Release comparison

Candidate should be compared with production baseline.

Example:

```text
Quality +2.1
Latency +80 ms
Cost +4%
Corrections -1.2%
```

Decision becomes explicit trade-off.

---

# 41.99 Non-inferiority gate

Candidate does not always need improvement in every metric.

Could require:

```text
No critical regression
No material degradation
Primary objective improved
```

Useful for controlled releases.

---

# 41.100 Canary QA

During 5% traffic:

evaluate much higher sample.

If critical failure:

immediate stop/rollback.

---

# 41.101 Production continuous evaluation

Flow:

```text
Production Calls
      ↓
Automated QA
      ↓
Risk-based Sample
      ↓
Human QA
      ↓
Quality Metrics
      ↓
Engineering Backlog
```

Continuous evaluation should be permanent.

---

# 41.102 Evaluation latency

Some evaluations are:

realtime

while others:

post-call.

### Realtime

DNC  
tool correctness  
transaction guards.

### Async

naturalness  
objection handling  
overall conversation quality.

This prevents adding unnecessary call latency.

---

# 41.103 Quality alerts

Alert:

```text
critical entity accuracy drops
P0 detected
human-request failure
DNC violation
booking mismatch spike
```

ObserveAI consumes.

---

# 41.104 Quality anomaly detection

Example:

Punjabi QA:

91 → 80 over two hours.

Possible:

provider update.

RouteAI can reduce exposure while investigation proceeds.

---

# 41.105 Quality control chart

For mature operations, use statistical process-control ideas:

baseline mean  
control limits.

Useful for detecting gradual degradation.

---

# 41.106 Sample-size protection

Do not declare:

Agent V20 quality = 100%

after five calls.

Show:

sample size  
confidence intervals.

---

# 41.107 Reviewer calibration

Multiple human reviewers score same calls periodically.

Measure agreement.

Possible:

Cohen's kappa

or simple agreement depending rubric.

---

# 41.108 Low reviewer agreement

If reviewers disagree heavily:

problem may be:

ambiguous rubric

not poor reviewers.

Fix rubric and examples.

---

# 41.109 Rubric guide

For each score define:

```text
PASS example
FAIL example
Borderline example
```

This improves consistency.

---

# 41.110 Human vs automated QA agreement

Track:

```text
auto_quality
human_quality
```

Calculate disagreement.

Large systematic difference means evaluator needs recalibration.

---

# 41.111 False-positive QA defect

Automated judge flags defect.

Human says correct.

Record:

```text
AUTO_FALSE_POSITIVE
```

Improve evaluator.

---

# 41.112 False-negative QA defect

Human detects problem auto QA missed.

Record.

Critical because automation can create false confidence.

---

# 41.113 QA model score

Track evaluator itself:

precision  
recall  
F1

against human gold.

QualityAI requires QA for its own QA.

---

# 41.114 Quality by customer journey stage

Analyze:

```text
opening
discovery
recommendation
booking
closing
```

Maybe overall 93 but booking stage only 82.

This points to targeted improvement.

---

# 41.115 Quality by call outcome

Compare:

booked  
not interested  
human transfer  
no answer.

Don't benchmark incomplete calls against full booked-call rubric blindly.

Use outcome-specific rubric applicability.

---

# 41.116 Applicable rubric logic

Example:

No-answer call:

booking-quality dimensions:

```text
NOT_APPLICABLE
```

Do not score them zero.

---

# 41.117 QA confidence

Each automated evaluation stores confidence.

Low-confidence judgment:

human review candidate.

---

# 41.118 QualityAPI

Potential:

```text
POST /quality/evaluate
GET /quality/calls/{id}
GET /quality/agents/{id}
GET /quality/providers/{id}
GET /quality/defects
```

---

# 41.119 Evaluation request

```json
{
  "call_id": "CALL-90182",
  "rubric": "HEALTHCARE_OUTBOUND_v8"
}
```

---

# 41.120 Evaluation response

```json
{
  "overall_score": 94,
  "critical_defects": [],
  "dimensions": {
    "intent": 98,
    "tool_correctness": 100,
    "language": 93
  }
}
```

---

# 41.121 Defect event model

Publish:

```text
quality.defect_detected
quality.critical_failure
quality.score_completed
quality.regression_detected
```

---

# 41.122 Quality workflow

For significant defect:

```text
DETECTED
↓
TRIAGED
↓
OWNER ASSIGNED
↓
ROOT CAUSE
↓
FIX
↓
REGRESSION TEST
↓
RELEASE
↓
VERIFY
↓
CLOSE
```

---

# 41.123 CAPA

For enterprise/regulated quality processes, use:

**Corrective Action**

fix current problem.

**Preventive Action**

prevent recurrence.

Example:

Corrective:

rollback STT model.

Preventive:

add Thursday/Tuesday audio regression set.

---

# 41.124 Defect backlog prioritization

Prioritize by:

```text
severity
frequency
customer impact
business impact
risk
```

One rare P0 can outrank 1,000 cosmetic defects.

---

# 41.125 Quality heatmap

Example:

| Component | English | Hindi | Punjabi |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Intent | 97 | 95 | 92 |
| Date/Time | 99 | 97 | 89 |
| RAG | 96 | 94 | 93 |
| TTS | 95 | 91 | 85 |

Immediately shows where investment is needed.

---

# 41.126 Quality trend dashboard

Track weekly:

```text
Overall QA
Critical defects
Correction rate
Tool accuracy
RAG groundedness
Human transfer quality
```

plus deployment annotations.

---

# 41.127 Top-defect dashboard

Example:

```text
1. Punjabi date/time extraction
2. Repeated price explanation
3. Booking API timeout handling
4. Human transfer delay
```

Quality improvement backlog becomes data-driven.

---

# 41.128 Agent ranking

Do not rank agents solely by conversion.

Use:

```text
quality
task completion
customer experience
risk
```

and then commercial outcome.

---

# 41.129 Provider ranking

Use:

quality + latency + reliability + cost.

This feeds RouteAI.

---

# 41.130 Quality-adjusted cost

Example:

Provider A:

$0.08/min, QA 82.

Provider B:

$0.12/min, QA 95.

FinAI + QualityAI calculate:

cost per successful high-quality booking.

This is much more meaningful.

---

# 41.131 Quality debt

Track temporary accepted issues.

Example:

```text
KNOWN ISSUE
Punjabi pronunciation of clinic name
Severity P3
Accepted until V21
```

Don't let known defects disappear informally.

---

# 41.132 Quality exception

For production exception:

```text
issue
risk
owner
expiry
mitigation
approval
```

GovernAI tracks.

---

# 41.133 Rubric versioning

Example:

```text
HEALTHCARE-VOICE-QA-v8
```

If rubric changes:

historical scores must keep old version.

Do not mix score trends across incompatible rubrics without adjustment.

---

# 41.134 Quality model card

Document:

purpose  
evaluation model  
datasets  
limitations  
thresholds  
languages  
known weaknesses.

---

# 41.135 Privacy

QA data may contain sensitive customer information.

Use:

access control  
redaction  
limited retention  
role-based transcript/audio access.

---

# 41.136 QA dataset privacy

Training/evaluation datasets should use:

synthetic data

where possible.

If real calls are used:

de-identify/minimize according to policy.

---

# 41.137 Security

QualityAI itself has read access to:

transcript/events/evidence.

It should not have unrestricted transaction execution privileges.

---

# 41.138 QualityAI + ObserveAI

ObserveAI detects operational anomaly.

QualityAI determines behavioral/interaction impact.

Together:

```text
STT latency ↑
+
critical entity accuracy ↓
```

gives meaningful incident context.

---

# 41.139 QualityAI + GovernAI

GovernAI sets:

release gate  
minimum thresholds  
exceptions.

QualityAI provides evidence.

---

# 41.140 QualityAI + RiskAI

A P0/P1 quality issue becomes risk event.

RiskAI can:

increase risk  
pause rollout.

---

# 41.141 QualityAI + RouteAI

Provider quality degradation:

RouteAI shifts traffic.

Quality signal should have freshness and sample-size requirements.

---

# 41.142 QualityAI + FinAI

FinAI asks:

> Is cheaper route actually economically better after quality failures?

QualityAI supplies the missing part.

---

# 41.143 QualityAI + HumanOps

Human QA results become:

coaching  
workflow improvement  
agent improvements.

Do not use opaque automated QA as the sole basis for employee performance decisions.

---

# 41.144 QualityAI + MLOps

Quality degradation can trigger:

model review  
prompt review  
retraining.

Not automatic deployment.

---

# 41.145 QualityAI + KnowledgeAI

Unsupported answer:

identify:

retrieval failure  
source issue  
generation issue.

Knowledge team receives precise defect.

---

# 41.146 QualityAI + NeedAI

High intent misclassification:

route defect to NeedAI evaluation dataset.

---

# 41.147 QualityAI + ConversationAI

Repeated question/loop:

add dialogue regression scenario.

---

# 41.148 QualityAI + NextAI

Wrong next action:

store:

context  
candidate set  
expected action.

Add to NextAI golden dataset.

---

# 41.149 Edge case — customer happy, agent violated policy

Customer satisfaction cannot override policy defect.

Quality:

FAIL.

---

# 41.150 Edge case — policy perfect, voice unusable

Compliance alone is insufficient.

Language/UX score may fail release.

---

# 41.151 Edge case — evaluator hallucinates defect

Human calibration catches it.

Do not blindly auto-roll back based solely on uncertain LLM judge.

Critical deterministic checks are different.

---

# 41.152 Edge case — customer uses sarcasm

Automated conversational-quality judgment may be uncertain.

Lower confidence / human sample.

---

# 41.153 Edge case — transcript wrong but audio correct

QA reviewer should inspect audio for disputed STT defect.

Do not treat transcript as perfect ground truth.

---

# 41.154 Edge case — human reviewer wrong

Reviewer calibration and second review may resolve disagreement.

Human judgment is not infallible either.

---

# 41.155 Edge case — booking success but wrong customer

Cross-customer identity integrity is P0.

Need:

customer identity  
transaction linkage

validation.

---

# 41.156 Edge case — low sample language

Display:

```text
Quality 96
N = 12
```

with low confidence.

Do not claim stable production quality.

---

# 41.157 Edge case — QA score improves due easier calls

Agent receives more simple FAQ traffic.

Overall QA rises.

Need segment/scenario-normalized analysis.

---

# 41.158 Case-mix adjustment

Compare quality by:

intent  
service  
complexity.

Don't compare providers/agents from completely different traffic mixes using raw averages alone.

---

For inbound, the **caller-resolution flow** is especially important:

```text
Incoming ANI / Phone Number
        ↓
Normalize Number
        ↓
Customer 360 Lookup
        ↓
┌──────────────┬───────────────┐
Known Caller                  Unknown Caller
↓                             ↓
Load customer                 Create temporary
context                       interaction identity
↓                             ↓
Appointments                  Ask minimal identity
preferences                   information if needed
previous needs                ↓
open tasks                    Resolve / create lead
```

You also need a formal **Inbound Call state model**:

```text
RINGING
→ ANSWERED
→ AI_GREETING
→ IDENTIFIED / UNKNOWN_CALLER
→ INTENT_DISCOVERY
→ SELF_SERVICE
→ TOOL_EXECUTION
→ HUMAN_QUEUE
→ HUMAN_CONNECTED
→ COMPLETED
```

Exceptional states:

```text
ABANDONED
CALL_DROPPED
VOICEMAIL
CALLBACK_REQUIRED
TRANSFER_FAILED
TOOL_FAILED
BLOCKED
```

```text
NEED_DETECTED
FAQ_ANSWERED
AVAILABILITY_CHECKED
SLOT_PRESENTED
BOOKING_REQUESTED
BOOKING_CONFIRMED
SMS_SENT
HUMAN_TRANSFER
CALL_COMPLETED
QA_COMPLETED
FOLLOWUP_CREATED
```

Every event should carry:

```text
event_id
timestamp
tenant_id
customer_id
lead_id
call_id
campaign_id
journey_id

event_type
status
source
provider

agent_version
language

duration
cost

outcome

trace_id
```

That single event model powers most reporting.

### Call-detail tracking

Each call record should include:

```text
Call ID
Inbound / Outbound
Customer
Lead
Phone number masked
Start
Answer time
End
Duration
Wait time

Telephony provider
Voice provider
STT
TTS
LLM

Agent
Agent version
Prompt version

Language
Intent
Primary need
Secondary needs

Likes
Dislikes
Objections
Questions
Unmet needs

Tools invoked
Booking status
Human transfer
Callback

Disposition
Quality score
Risk score
Cost

Transcript
Recording reference
Trace
```

### Reporting framework

Do not create only one executive dashboard. You need several reporting layers.

| Report family | Main reports |
|---|---|
| Inbound | inbound calls, answered, abandoned, transferred |
| Outbound | attempts, connected, callback, conversion |
| Lead | source, qualification, lead aging, conversion |
| Customer | needs, likes, dislikes, questions, journeys |
| Booking | searches, booking success, cancellation, no-show |
| Voice | latency, STT, TTS, interruptions, dropped calls |
| Agent | intent, tool success, loops, transfers |
| Quality | QA, defects, corrections, hallucinations |
| Campaign | campaign funnel, conversion, contact pressure |
| HumanOps | queue, wait, AHT, FCR, SLA |
| Marketing | source, CAC, attribution, ROI |
| Financial | cost/call, cost/booking, CAC, revenue |
| Provider | reliability, latency, quality, cost |
| Governance | DNC, consent, policy blocks, audit |
| Operations | incidents, errors, queues, workflow backlog |

### Inbound dashboard

Core KPIs:

```text
Inbound Calls
Answered Calls

Reschedules
Cancellations

Missed Calls
Callbacks Required

```

Example funnel:

```text
10,000 Incoming Calls
        ↓
9,200 Answered
        ↓
7,100 AI-resolved
        ↓
2,100 Human transfers
        ↓
3,600 Booking-related
        ↓
2,900 Successful bookings
```

This should be different from reporting.

Senior management needs:

```text
Leads
Calls
```

### Operations processes

You also need a dedicated **Operations Playbook**. Daily:

```text
Provider health
Critical alerts
Failed bookings
Missed callbacks
Human queue

Customer complaints
Failed workflows
DLQ
```

Weekly:

```text
Campaign performance
Agent quality

Top call failures
Knowledge gaps

Cost anomalies
```

Monthly:

```text
Executive KPIs

Risk
```

### User stories

This is another missing standalone stream. You will eventually need hundreds, but start by grouping them by persona.

| Persona | Example user story |
|---|---|
| Caller | As a caller, I want to book an appointment by phone |
| Caller | As a caller, I want to speak in Hindi |
| Caller | As a caller, I want a human when AI cannot help |
| Receptionist | As a receptionist, I want context before accepting transfer |
| Supervisor | As a supervisor, I want to see active risky calls |
| Marketing | As marketing, I want to see lead-source conversion |
| Clinic Admin | As admin, I want to update clinic hours without code |
| QA | As QA, I want to review low-quality calls |
| Compliance | As compliance, I want evidence of DNC enforcement |
| Finance | As finance, I want cost per booking |
| AI Engineer | As engineer, I want call traces by agent version |
| Executive | As executive, I want an overall business dashboard |

A fuller example:

> **As a patient/customer**, I want to call the clinic, state that I need physiotherapy after 6 PM, hear the available slots in my preferred language, choose one, confirm the booking, and receive an SMS confirmation without having to repeat information to a receptionist.

Acceptance flow:

```text
GIVEN
Customer calls clinic

WHEN
AI answers

AND
customer requests Hindi

THEN
agent switches to Hindi

WHEN
customer says
"I need physio after six"

THEN
NeedAI extracts:
service = physiotherapy
time > 18:00

WHEN
scheduler returns slots

THEN
agent presents 2–3 options

WHEN
customer selects 6:30

THEN
agent confirms

WHEN
customer says yes

THEN
booking is executed

AND
confirmation message is sent

AND
CRM is updated

AND
call is reported as BOOKED
```

### End-to-end inbound flow

Your inbound reference flow should therefore be:

```text
Phone Call
   ↓
Telephony
   ↓
Inbound Gateway
   ↓
Known / Unknown Caller
   ↓
Language
   ↓
AI Disclosure
   ↓
Intent
   ↓
NeedAI
   ↓
ConversationAI
   ↓
KnowledgeAI / RecommendAI / Tools
   ↓
NextAI
   ↓
ANSWER / BOOK / RESCHEDULE /
CANCEL / TRANSFER / CALLBACK
   ↓
Customer Confirmation
   ↓
Transaction
   ↓
CRM / Customer 360
   ↓
FollowUpAI
   ↓
QA
   ↓
Tracking
   ↓
Dashboard / Reports
   ↓
MarketAI / FinAI / GovernAI
```

So I would expand the roadmap from roughly **144 phases to around 170–180**, because **Inbound, UX/UI, Product Management/User Stories, Reporting, and Operations deserve their own architecture tracks rather than being scattered across VoiceAI modules**. The next logical move would be to continue with **Phase 42 — PolicyAI**, but I would insert a separate later **Inbound Call Master Playbook**, followed by **UI/UX Master Design**, **Reporting & Dashboard Master Design**, **Operations Playbook**, and **User Story/Acceptance Criteria Bank** before final architecture consolidation.
