## 🤖 Assistant — msg #123

# Phase 42 — PolicyAI: Consent, DNC & Contact Governance Control Plane

PolicyAI becomes the **authorization layer in front of every inbound/outbound communication and sensitive voice-agent action**.

The key design principle is:

> **The LLM can propose an action. PolicyAI decides whether that action is permitted.**

For healthcare voice agents, this is especially important because inbound calls, outbound marketing, callbacks, appointment communication, recording, customer preferences, and sensitive-data access can have different rules.

---

## 42.1 PolicyAI responsibilities

PolicyAI controls:

| Area | Examples |
|---|---|
| Contact permission | Can we call this person? |
| DNC | Has the customer requested no calls? |
| Consent | What did the customer agree to? |
| Purpose | Marketing vs appointment reminder |
| Channel | Voice/SMS/email/WhatsApp |
| Calling time | Is contact allowed now? |
| Frequency | Have we contacted too often? |
| Recording | Can this call be recorded under configured policy? |
| Disclosure | What must the agent say? |
| AI actions | Can the agent perform this tool action? |
| Data access | Can this agent retrieve this information? |
| Campaign | Is customer eligible? |
| Tenant | Which clinic's rules apply? |
| Geography | Which configured jurisdiction rules apply? |
| Human escalation | When must AI stop? |
| Overrides | Who may override which policy? |
| Evidence | Why was the action allowed/blocked? |

---

# 42.2 Architecture

```text
               Customer / Lead
                     ↓
             Customer 360 / CRM
                     ↓
               Consent Store
                     ↓
             Preference Store
                     ↓
                 DNC Store
                     ↓
                     │
Campaign ────────────┤
Inbound Call ────────┤
Outbound Call ───────┤
SMS / Email ─────────┤
AI Agent ────────────┤
Tool Request ────────┤
                     ↓
               ┌──────────┐
               │ PolicyAI │
               └──────────┘
                     ↓
       ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
       ↓             ↓             ↓
     ALLOW         BLOCK         REVIEW
       ↓                           ↓
ConversationAI                 HumanOps
       ↓
ToolAI
       ↓
Execution
       ↓
AuditAI
```

---

# 42.3 Never let ConversationAI decide DNC

Bad architecture:

```text
Customer
   ↓
LLM
   ↓
"Should I call?"
   ↓
LLM decides
```

Better:

```text
Agent proposes:

CALL(customer_123)

       ↓

PolicyAI

       ↓

DNC?
Consent?
Purpose?
Channel?
Time?
Frequency?
Tenant?
Campaign?
Jurisdiction configuration?

       ↓

ALLOW / BLOCK / REVIEW
```

The decision is deterministic wherever possible.

---

# 42.4 Central policy decision API

Create one common interface.

```text
POST /policy/evaluate
```

Example request:

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "clinic_101",
  "customer_id": "cust_802",
  "action": "OUTBOUND_CALL",
  "purpose": "MARKETING",
  "channel": "VOICE",
  "campaign_id": "CMP_88"
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "decision": "ALLOW",
  "policy_version": "CONTACT-v17",
  "reason_codes": [
    "CONSENT_VALID",
    "NOT_DNC",
    "WITHIN_CONTACT_WINDOW",
    "FREQUENCY_OK"
  ]
}
```

---

# 42.5 Standard decision model

Use:

```text
ALLOW
BLOCK
REVIEW
```

Optionally:

```text
ALLOW_WITH_CONDITIONS
```

Example:

```text
ALLOW_WITH_CONDITIONS

condition:
appointment_information_only
```

---

# 42.6 Reason codes

Never return only:

```text
BLOCKED
```

Return machine-readable reason.

Examples:

```text
DNC_GLOBAL
DNC_VOICE
CONSENT_MISSING
CONSENT_EXPIRED
PURPOSE_NOT_ALLOWED

CALLING_WINDOW_BLOCK
FREQUENCY_CAP
CAMPAIGN_EXCLUDED

RECORDING_NOT_ALLOWED
IDENTITY_NOT_VERIFIED

HUMAN_REQUIRED
POLICY_CONFIGURATION_ERROR
```

These become valuable for:

operations  
audit  
reporting  
customer support  
ExplainAI.

---

# 42.7 Consent model

Avoid:

```text
consent = true
```

That is too primitive.

Model consent as:

```text
CONSENT

customer
tenant

purpose
channel

source

granted_at
expires_at

policy_version

status

evidence_reference
```

---

# 42.8 Purpose-specific consent

Possible purposes:

```text
MARKETING
APPOINTMENT
REMINDER
FOLLOW_UP
SURVEY
SERVICE
PAYMENT
SUPPORT
```

A customer allowing appointment reminders does not automatically mean every marketing use is permitted.

---

# 42.9 Channel-specific preferences

Store independently:

```text
VOICE
SMS
EMAIL
WHATSAPP
```

Example:

```text
VOICE       BLOCK
SMS         ALLOW
EMAIL       ALLOW
WHATSAPP    UNKNOWN
```

This becomes important in your customer-acquisition architecture.

---

# 42.10 Customer preference center

Customer 360 should contain:

```text
Contact Preferences

Voice       OFF
SMS         ON
Email       ON

Preferred Language
Hindi

Preferred Time
Evening

Marketing
OFF

Appointment Reminders
ON
```

PolicyAI consumes these preferences.

---

# 42.11 Global vs clinic-level suppression

Design:

```text
GLOBAL DNC
TENANT DNC
CHANNEL DNC
CAMPAIGN DNC
```

Example:

Customer tells Clinic A:

> Don't call me about promotions.

Do not automatically interpret that as every conceivable communication restriction without applying the relevant policy semantics.

Store exactly what happened.

---

# 42.12 DNC event

```text
DNC_EVENT

customer_id
phone_hash

scope
channel

reason
source

timestamp

call_id
agent_id
```

Evidence should point back to the interaction.

---

# 42.13 DNC detection

Customer expressions:

```text
"Stop calling me."

"Don't call again."

"Remove me from your call list."
```

ConversationAI may detect the statement.

But enforcement becomes:

```text
ConversationAI
     ↓
DNC Intent
     ↓
Policy Service
     ↓
Suppression Store
     ↓
Immediate Campaign Exclusion
```

---

# 42.14 Immediate suppression

Do not rely on nightly CRM synchronization.

Expected:

```text
Customer: "Stop calling."

        ↓

DNC detected

        ↓

Central suppression

        ↓

All future applicable call jobs blocked
```

near immediately.

---

# 42.15 Execution-time DNC check

This is essential.

Suppose campaign creates:

```text
10,000 calls
```

at 8 AM.

Customer opts out at 10 AM.

Their queued call runs at 3 PM.

If DNC was checked only when the campaign was created, you may still call them.

Therefore:

```text
Campaign selection
       ↓
Policy check #1
       ↓
Queue
       ↓
WAIT
       ↓
Policy check #2
       ↓
IMMEDIATELY BEFORE CALL
       ↓
Telephony
```

---

# 42.16 Defense in depth

For high-risk actions:

```text
Planning
    ↓
Policy Check

Execution
    ↓
Policy Check

Provider Call
```

Policy may change between planning and execution.

---

# 42.17 Contact-frequency engine

Track:

```text
attempts today
attempts 7 days
successful contacts
SMS sent
emails sent
campaign contacts
```

Policy can evaluate:

```text
FREQUENCY_OK
```

or:

```text
FREQUENCY_CAP
```

---

# 42.18 Cross-channel frequency

Don't evaluate voice alone.

Example customer receives:

```text
3 calls
4 SMS
5 emails
```

Technically each channel may be below its own limit while overall contact pressure is excessive.

Create:

```text
CUSTOMER_CONTACT_PRESSURE
```

---

# 42.19 Contact-pressure score

Possible internal metric:

```text
Voice attempts
+
SMS
+
Email
+
WhatsApp
+
recent successful conversations
```

Apply policy weights.

Do not let an LLM invent the threshold dynamically.

---

# 42.20 Calling-window engine

Evaluate:

```text
customer timezone
tenant
campaign
purpose
configured applicable rule
```

Then:

```text
ALLOW
```

or:

```text
CALLING_WINDOW_BLOCK
```

Avoid assuming the clinic's timezone equals the customer's timezone.

---

# 42.21 Timezone resolution

Possible hierarchy:

```text
Verified customer timezone
        ↓
Customer address region
        ↓
Phone metadata
        ↓
Campaign geography
        ↓
Unknown
```

If uncertainty matters:

use conservative policy.

---

# 42.22 Daylight-saving time

Store timestamps in UTC.

Evaluate communication window using resolved local timezone.

This prevents DST errors.

---

# 42.23 Holiday policies

Certain clinics may configure:

```text
No promotional calls:
Christmas
New Year's Day
clinic holidays
```

PolicyAI should support calendar-based restrictions.

---

# 42.24 Inbound vs outbound policy

These are different.

### Inbound

Customer initiated contact.

Primary concerns:

```text
Disclosure
Recording
Authentication
Data access
Sensitive actions
```

### Outbound

Additional concerns:

```text
Contact authorization
DNC
Calling window
Frequency
Campaign eligibility
Purpose
```

---

# 42.25 Inbound PolicyAI flow

```text
Incoming Call
      ↓
Identify Clinic
      ↓
Load Tenant Policy
      ↓
Disclosure Policy
      ↓
Recording Policy
      ↓
Language
      ↓
Intent
      ↓
Authentication requirement?
      ↓
Tool Authorization
      ↓
Action
```

---

# 42.26 Outbound PolicyAI flow

```text
Lead
 ↓
Campaign Eligibility
 ↓
Consent / Permission
 ↓
DNC
 ↓
Purpose
 ↓
Channel
 ↓
Calling Window
 ↓
Frequency
 ↓
Fraud / Risk
 ↓
ALLOW
 ↓
Queue
 ↓
Execution-Time Recheck
 ↓
Call
```

---

# 42.27 Recording policy

Before recording:

PolicyAI determines applicable configuration.

Possible output:

```text
RECORDING_ALLOWED
DISCLOSURE_REQUIRED
```

or:

```text
RECORDING_DISABLED
```

Voice infrastructure obeys it.

---

# 42.28 Recording separation

Support:

```text
Call enabled
Recording disabled
```

Do not design recording as inseparable from calling.

---

# 42.29 Recording consent event

Where applicable:

```text
recording_notice_played
recording_choice
timestamp
policy_version
```

Store evidence without unnecessarily duplicating sensitive content.

---

# 42.30 AI disclosure

Policy configuration may define required introduction.

Example conceptually:

> Virtual assistant for Clinic X.

QualityAI validates required disclosure elements.

PolicyAI decides what disclosure applies.

---

# 42.31 Disclosure versioning

Store:

```text
DISCLOSURE-v7
```

with:

language  
tenant  
purpose.

This makes historical calls auditable.

---

# 42.32 Multilingual disclosure

Don't translate critical disclosure dynamically every time.

Maintain approved:

```text
English
French
Hindi
Punjabi
...
```

versions as needed.

---

# 42.33 Campaign eligibility

Before customer enters campaign:

evaluate:

```text
customer status
service
location
preferences
consent
DNC
previous conversion
existing appointment
frequency
```

---

# 42.34 Existing customer protection

Example:

customer already has appointment tomorrow.

Do not send:

> Would you like to book an appointment?

Policy/campaign eligibility can exclude them.

This is both governance and good CX.

---

# 42.35 Duplicate campaign protection

Customer accidentally enters:

```text
Campaign A
Campaign B
Campaign C
```

PolicyAI can enforce campaign-family exclusion/frequency.

---

# 42.36 Campaign policy object

```text
CAMPAIGN_POLICY

campaign_id
purpose
eligible_segments

channels

contact_limits

allowed_hours

suppression_lists

effective_from
effective_until

approval_status
```

---

# 42.37 Campaign activation gate

Before:

```text
START CAMPAIGN
```

check:

```text
policy configured?
consent strategy?
suppression list?
calling windows?
frequency limits?
approved script?
agent approved?
```

If not:

```text
CAMPAIGN_BLOCKED
```

---

# 42.38 Policy-as-code

Policies should be version controlled.

Possible technology:

OPA/Rego or custom deterministic rules engine.

Concept:

```text
allow_outbound_call
IF
not_dnc
AND
purpose_allowed
AND
within_window
AND
frequency_ok
```

---

# 42.39 Why policy-as-code?

Benefits:

```text
Versioning
Testing
Peer review
Deployment control
Audit
Rollback
```

Avoid burying critical policy rules inside prompts.

---

# 42.40 Policy repository

```text
/policies

/contact
/dnc
/consent
/recording
/disclosure
/tool
/data
/campaign
/tenant
```

Git-controlled.

---

# 42.41 Policy lifecycle

```text
DRAFT
 ↓
REVIEW
 ↓
APPROVED
 ↓
TEST
 ↓
DEPLOY
 ↓
MONITOR
 ↓
RETIRED
```

---

# 42.42 Policy owner

Every policy requires:

```text
business owner
technical owner
risk/compliance owner where appropriate
```

No orphan policies.

---

# 42.43 Policy version

Every decision stores:

```text
policy_version
```

Example:

```text
CONTACT-CA-v17
```

Later you can answer:

> Why was this call allowed six months ago?

---

# 42.44 Effective dates

Policy:

```text
effective_from
effective_to
```

Do not overwrite old policy definitions.

---

# 42.45 Tenant-level configuration

Clinic A and Clinic B may have different:

```text
hours
services
recording preferences
transfer policies
campaign configurations
```

Use:

```text
GLOBAL POLICY
      ↓
REGIONAL POLICY
      ↓
TENANT POLICY
      ↓
CAMPAIGN POLICY
```

with explicit precedence.

---

# 42.46 Policy precedence

Example:

```text
Global hard prohibition
      ↓
Regional requirement
      ↓
Tenant restriction
      ↓
Campaign restriction
```

Lower layer must not weaken mandatory upper-level controls.

---

# 42.47 Policy conflict detection

Suppose:

```text
Regional:
BLOCK

Tenant:
ALLOW
```

System should flag:

```text
POLICY_CONFLICT
```

and apply safe precedence.

---

# 42.48 Tool authorization

PolicyAI should also protect tools.

Example:

ConversationAI proposes:

```text
CANCEL_APPOINTMENT
```

PolicyAI checks:

```text
identity verification?
customer owns appointment?
confirmation obtained?
agent authorized?
```

Then:

```text
ALLOW
```

---

# 42.49 Read vs write policy

Different authorization:

```text
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
```

versus:

```text
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
```

Write actions should generally receive stronger controls.

---

# 42.50 Sensitive information policy

Customer asks:

> Tell me my appointment details.

Policy may require identity checks depending on information/action and configured environment.

ConversationAI should not decide this itself.

---

# 42.51 Identity assurance level

Policy can require:

```text
IAL0
No verification

IAL1
Basic verification

IAL2
Stronger verification
```

depending action.

Exact implementation depends on system requirements.

---

# 42.52 Action risk levels

Classify tools:

```text
LOW
READ_CLINIC_HOURS

MEDIUM
CHECK_CUSTOMER_APPOINTMENT

HIGH
CANCEL_APPOINTMENT

CRITICAL
CHANGE_SENSITIVE_ACCOUNT_INFORMATION
```

Higher risk → stronger authorization.

---

# 42.53 PolicyAI + RiskAI

PolicyAI:

> Is this allowed?

RiskAI:

> How risky is this?

Example:

```text
Policy = ALLOW
Risk = HIGH
```

may produce:

```text
REVIEW
```

depending configured rule.

---

# 42.54 PolicyAI + ResponsibleAI

ResponsibleAI handles principles such as:

non-manipulation  
fairness  
human oversight.

PolicyAI turns approved principles into enforceable rules.

---

# 42.55 PolicyAI + ExplainAI

Customer asks:

> Why can't you call me?

ExplainAI can translate:

```text
DNC_VOICE
```

into appropriate human explanation.

Do not expose internal security rules unnecessarily.

---

# 42.56 PolicyAI + GovernAI

GovernAI controls:

policy owner  
approval  
exceptions  
reviews.

PolicyAI executes the approved policy.

---

# 42.57 PolicyAI + ObserveAI

Observe:

```text
policy requests
allow rate
block rate
review rate
latency
errors
```

A policy engine outage is a serious production event.

---

# 42.58 Fail-safe design

If critical contact policy cannot be evaluated:

For outbound marketing:

```text
FAIL CLOSED
```

rather than:

```text
"Policy service unavailable,
call anyway."
```

Different low-risk actions may have explicitly designed fallback rules.

---

# 42.59 Policy latency

Policy checks should be fast.

Target architecture:

```text
local/cacheable configuration
+
central decision service
```

Do not add seconds to every voice turn.

---

# 42.60 Policy caching

Cache:

```text
static policy definitions
tenant configuration
```

Be careful caching:

DNC/customer preferences.

These can change immediately.

---

# 42.61 Cache invalidation

DNC update should publish:

```text
CUSTOMER_SUPPRESSION_CHANGED
```

Invalidate relevant caches immediately.

---

# 42.62 Policy audit event

Every significant decision:

```text
POLICY_DECISION

decision_id
timestamp

tenant
customer

action
purpose
channel

decision
reason_codes

policy_version

trace_id
```

---

# 42.63 Policy dashboard

Core metrics:

```text
Policy Decisions
Allowed
Blocked
Review

DNC Blocks
Consent Blocks
Frequency Blocks
Calling-Window Blocks

Tool Blocks
Recording Blocks

Policy Errors
Policy Latency
```

---

# 42.64 DNC dashboard

```text
DNC Requests Today
DNC Processing Success

Future Calls Prevented

DNC Violations
0

Average Suppression Latency

Top DNC Campaigns
```

This is useful operationally and strategically.

---

# 42.65 Consent dashboard

Track:

```text
consent by source
consent by purpose
consent by channel
withdrawal
expired consent
unknown status
```

Do not interpret high consent rate as a reason to weaken UX.

---

# 42.66 Contact-pressure dashboard

Show:

```text
Customers contacted 1×
2×
3×
4×+

Cross-channel touches

Complaints vs touch count
DNC vs touch count
Conversion vs touch count
```

This can help find the optimal contact strategy.

---

# 42.67 Policy operations UI

Admin screen:

```text
POLICIES

Contact
DNC
Consent
Recording
Disclosure
Campaign
Tools
Data

Version
Status
Owner
Effective Date
Last Test
```

# 42.68 Customer preference UI

# 42.70 User story — DNC

> As a customer, I want my request to stop marketing calls to take effect promptly so that the system does not continue calling me.

Acceptance flow:

```text
GIVEN
Customer is active in campaign

WHEN
Customer says
"Don't call me again"

THEN
DNC intent is detected

AND
suppression is persisted

AND
future applicable queued calls are blocked

AND
CRM is synchronized

AND
audit evidence is stored.
```

---

# 42.71 User story — channel preference

> As a customer, I want to receive SMS but not promotional phone calls.

Expected:

```text
VOICE MARKETING = BLOCK
SMS = ALLOW
```

Campaigns respect this automatically.

---

# 42.72 User story — clinic administrator

> As a clinic administrator, I want to configure approved contact policies without editing AI prompts.

Policy configuration becomes controlled configuration rather than prompt engineering.

---

# 42.73 User story — compliance/risk reviewer

> As a reviewer, I want to see why a call was allowed or blocked and which policy version made the decision.

UI:

```text
Decision
BLOCK

Reason
DNC_VOICE

Policy
CONTACT-v17

Timestamp
14:31:07

Evidence
DNC event #88219
```

---

# 42.74 User story — AI engineer

> As an AI engineer, I should not be able to bypass mandatory policy controls merely by changing a prompt.

This is a critical architectural acceptance criterion.

```text
C001
No DNC

C002
```

# 42.76 Critical test

Scenario:

```text
08:00
Customer queued

10:00
Customer requests DNC

15:00
Call worker picks job
```

Expected:

```text
EXECUTION-TIME POLICY CHECK

→ BLOCK

→ NO CALL
```

This must be part of every regression suite.

# 42.77 Race-condition test

Customer DNC request and call execution happen almost simultaneously.

Test concurrency.

Central suppression update should have clearly defined consistency guarantees.

---

# 42.78 Duplicate DNC

Customer says stop multiple times.

Operation should be idempotent.

```text
DNC
DNC
DNC
```

must not create broken state.

---

# 42.79 Phone-number normalization

These:

```text
4035551234
+14035551234
1-403-555-1234
```

must resolve consistently where they represent the same number.

Otherwise suppression can fail.

---

# 42.80 Reassigned number edge case

Phone numbers can change owners.

Do not permanently infer identity solely from number.

IdentityAI will address this deeper later.

---

# 42.81 Shared family number

One number may be used by several family members.

Avoid blindly merging all identities.

Policy scope must be carefully modeled.

---

# 42.82 Unknown consent

Do not silently convert:

```text
UNKNOWN
```

to:

```text
YES
```

Define explicit behavior.

---

# 42.83 Consent withdrawal

Withdrawal should:

```text
Update consent
↓
Publish event
↓
Invalidate caches
↓
Remove applicable queued actions
↓
Update campaign eligibility
```

# 42.84 CRM sync failure

Central PolicyAI says:

```text
DNC = TRUE
```

CRM update fails.

The voice system should still honor central DNC.

Retry CRM synchronization asynchronously.

CRM should not be the sole enforcement point.

```text
Policy unavailable
↓
DO NOT CALL
↓
Retry later
```

Raise operational alert.

```text
BLOCK RATE
10% → 100%
```

Trigger:

rollback/review.

# 42.87 Shadow policy

Before deploying new rule:

run:

```text
CURRENT POLICY
vs
CANDIDATE POLICY
```

against production-like events without enforcing candidate.

Compare decision differences.

## 🤖 Assistant — msg #125

# Phase 42A — Inbound Call Master Plan: AI Receptionist + Booking + Support + Human Handoff

Inbound calling needs its own architecture because the customer initiates the conversation. The agent must first determine **who is calling, why they are calling, whether self-service is appropriate, what data/actions require verification, and when a human should take over.**

> **Inbound AI should behave like an intelligent receptionist: answer quickly, understand the reason for the call, resolve simple requests, complete permitted transactions, and route difficult or sensitive cases to the right person without forcing the caller through unnecessary questions.**

## 42A.1 Primary inbound objectives

| Objective | Example |
|---|---|
| Answer calls | 24×7 or configured business hours |
| Understand intent | “I want to book physio” |
| Identify caller | Known vs unknown caller |
| Answer FAQs | hours, location, parking |
| Explain services | dental, physio, massage |
| Check pricing | approved pricing source |
| Check availability | live scheduler |
| Book | new appointment |
| Reschedule | existing appointment |
| Cancel | existing appointment |
| Handle callback | “Have someone call me tomorrow” |
| Route calls | dental/admin/billing/provider |
| Human transfer | receptionist/specialist |
| Capture new leads | unknown prospective callers |
| Recover missed calls | callback journey |
| Collect feedback | post-interaction |
| Track everything | call → intent → action → outcome |

---

```text
   ↓

   ↓

   ↓
             NextAI
                ↓
 ┌──────────────┼─────────────────┐
 ↓              ↓                 ↓

 ↓              ↓                 ↓
FAQ         Scheduler/CRM      Receptionist
Price       Booking            Specialist
Hours       Reschedule         Billing
Location    Cancel             Clinical route
                ↓
        Customer Confirmation
                ↓
          Transaction
                ↓
         Customer 360
                ↓
          FollowUpAI
                ↓
 SMS / Email / Callback / Task
                ↓
 QualityAI + ObserveAI
                ↓
 Reporting / Dashboard
```

# 42A.3 Entry scenarios

An inbound caller may be:

```text
Existing customer
New prospect
Returning lead
Existing appointment holder
Family member / representative
Corporate customer
Provider/vendor
Wrong number
Unknown caller
Spam/fraud caller
```

Do not assume every inbound phone call is a new sales lead.

---

# 42A.4 First-stage call routing

When the call arrives:

```text
Incoming ANI
    ↓
Determine called number/DID
    ↓
Resolve tenant
    ↓
Resolve clinic/location
    ↓
Load clinic configuration
    ↓
Check business hours
    ↓
Start inbound workflow
```

The called number can identify:

clinic  
department  
campaign  
service

before the AI says anything.

---

# 42A.5 DID strategy

You may have:

```text
Main clinic number
Dental number
Physio number
Campaign tracking number
Corporate sales number
After-hours number
```

Store:

```text
PHONE_NUMBER_CONFIG

number_id
tenant_id
clinic_id
department
purpose
business_hours
agent_profile
fallback_route
```

---

# 42A.6 Known caller resolution

Incoming number:

```text
+1 403 xxx xxxx
```

Lookup:

```text
Contact Point
    ↓
Customer 360
```

If unique reliable match:

```text
KNOWN_CALLER
```

Load minimal context:

```text
First name
Current appointment
Open callback
Current lead/service
Language preference
Open human task
```

Do not announce sensitive information before appropriate identity assurance.

---

# 42A.7 Unknown caller

If no customer match:

```text
UNKNOWN_CALLER
```

Create:

```text
TEMPORARY_INTERACTION_ID
```

Then learn only what is required through conversation.

Example:

> “How can I help you today?”

Do not force account creation merely to answer clinic hours.

---

# 42A.8 Multiple customer match

Shared family number:

```text
Phone
 ├── Customer A
 └── Customer B
```

Do not guess.

For account-specific actions, ask for necessary identifying information according to policy.

For general questions:

no identity resolution required.

---

# 42A.9 Greeting flow

Basic structure:

```text
Greeting
↓
Organization identification
↓
AI disclosure where configured/required
↓
Open question
```

Example:

> “Thank you for calling ABC Physiotherapy. I’m the clinic’s virtual assistant. How can I help you today?”

Then listen.

Avoid:

> “Press 1 for booking, press 2 for…”

unless a simple deterministic IVR fallback is intentionally used.

---

# 42A.10 Language selection

Three sources:

```text
Known preference
Customer request
Language detection
```

Priority:

```text
Customer explicit request
>
Confirmed stored preference
>
Detection
```

Example:

> “Hindi mein baat kar sakte ho?”

Immediately switch.

Do not restart the call.

---

# 42A.11 Inbound intent taxonomy

Core intents:

```text
BOOK_APPOINTMENT
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
RESCHEDULE
CANCEL

PRICE
SERVICE_INFORMATION
CLINIC_HOURS
LOCATION
PARKING

PROVIDER_INFORMATION
INSURANCE_ADMIN

EXISTING_APPOINTMENT
PAYMENT_ADMIN

CALLBACK_REQUEST
HUMAN_REQUEST

COMPLAINT
FEEDBACK

CLINICAL_RESTRICTED

SALES / CORPORATE
OTHER
UNKNOWN
```

---

# 42A.12 Intent router

```text
Caller utterance
     ↓
Intent Detection
     ↓
Confidence
     ↓

HIGH
→ route

MEDIUM
→ clarify

LOW
→ general clarification/human
```

Example:

Customer:

> “I need to change my Tuesday appointment.”

Intent:

```text
RESCHEDULE
```

No need to ask:

> “Are you calling to book?”

# 42A.13 Inbound state machine

```text
RINGING
   ↓
CONNECTED
   ↓
GREETING
   ↓
LANGUAGE
   ↓
INTENT_DISCOVERY
   ↓
 ┌───────────────┬────────────────┐
 FAQ          TRANSACTION       HUMAN
 ↓                ↓                ↓
ANSWER       VERIFY IF NEEDED    QUEUE
                  ↓
               TOOL
                  ↓

                  ↓

                  ↓

```

Global exceptional transitions:

```text
ANY → DNC/PREFERENCE
ANY → HUMAN
ANY → CALLBACK
```

Customer:

```text
Inbound call
↓

↓

↓

↓
Answer
↓

↓
```

identity verification

required unless there is another reason.

# 42A.16 Booking flow

```text
BOOK_REQUEST
     ↓

CHECK_AVAILABILITY
```

# 42A.17 Inbound use case 3 — Reschedule

Customer:

> “Move my appointment from Tuesday.”

Flow:

```text
Intent = RESCHEDULE
↓
Identity assurance
↓
Retrieve appointments
↓
Select appointment
↓
Check alternatives
↓
Customer selects
↓
Confirm change
↓
Reschedule tool
↓
Confirmation
```

This is different from creating a new appointment.

# 42A.18 Inbound use case 4 — Cancel

Because cancellation changes an existing transaction:

```text
Caller
↓
Identify appointment
↓
Verify appropriate identity/context
↓
Explain relevant approved cancellation policy if necessary
↓
Explicit confirmation
↓
CANCEL_APPOINTMENT
↓
Authoritative result
↓
Confirmation
```

Never cancel based on ambiguous:

> “I don't think I can make it.”

Clarify intent.

---

# 42A.19 Inbound use case 5 — Pricing

Customer:

> “How much is massage?”

Flow:

```text
PRICE intent
↓
Service resolution
↓
Pricing API
↓
Current price
↓
Concise answer
↓
Optional:
"Would you like me to check availability?"
```

Do not read stale pricing from prompt.

---

# 42A.20 Inbound use case 6 — Insurance

Customer:

> “Does my insurance cover physiotherapy?”

This may require careful administrative boundaries.

Possible:

```text
General approved insurance/admin information
        ↓
If customer-specific verification required
        ↓
Human/Admin route
```

Do not guarantee coverage without authoritative information.

# 42A.21 Inbound use case 7 — Human request

Customer:

> “Can I speak to someone?”

Immediate candidate:

```text
TRANSFER_HUMAN
```

queue  
skills  
language

If unavailable:

Do not force five AI questions before transfer.

# 42A.22 Inbound use case 8 — Complaint

Customer:

> “I've called three times and nobody fixed my appointment.”

Flow:

```text
COMPLAINT
↓
Stop sales behavior
↓
Capture issue
↓
Check current transaction if appropriate
↓
Human escalation
↓
Complaint task
↓
SLA
```

Commercial upselling should be suppressed.

---

# 42A.23 Inbound use case 9 — Existing appointment inquiry

Customer:

> “What time is my appointment?”

General lookup is different from general FAQ.

Flow:

```text
Identity requirements
↓
Appointment lookup
↓
Authoritative scheduler
↓
Provide permitted details
```

Avoid exposing appointment information based solely on caller ID if policy requires stronger verification.

---

# 42A.24 Inbound use case 10 — New unknown prospect

Caller:

> “I'm just trying to understand what services you offer.”

AI answers.

During conversation:

```text
Interest = Physiotherapy
```

If caller voluntarily provides contact information or requests follow-up:

create:

```text
CUSTOMER/LEAD
```

Do not turn every anonymous FAQ caller into a forced CRM lead.

# 42A.28 Missed inbound call

A major business opportunity.

If inbound call is unanswered before AI/platform pickup or fails:

create:

```text
MISSED_CALL
```

Potential workflow:

```text
Missed Call
↓
Known customer?
↓
Policy
↓
Callback task / AI callback
```

Do not lose it.

---

# 42A.29 Abandoned call

Different from missed call.

Customer enters queue and hangs up.

Track:

```text
ABANDONED
wait_duration
queue
```

Potential callback strategy depends on context and policy.

---

# 42A.30 Dropped AI call

Customer was talking to AI and connection dropped.

Store:

```text
CALL_DROPPED
last_state
completed_actions
pending_action
```

FollowUpAI decides appropriate recovery.

Do not necessarily redial automatically.

---

# 42A.31 After-hours inbound

Determine:

```text
clinic_open?
human_queue_open?
AI_self_service_available?
```

Possible flow:

```text
After Hours
    ↓
AI answers
    ↓
FAQ
Booking self-service
Callback scheduling
Message capture
```

```text
NEXT_BUSINESS_DAY_TASK
```

# 42A.32 After-hours greeting

Example:

> “The clinic is currently closed, but I can help with general information, check appointment availability, or arrange a callback.”

AI can reduce voicemail dependence dramatically.

# 42A.52 AI containment

Definition:

```text
calls completely resolved by AI
/
eligible inbound calls
```

But do not chase 100%.

Some calls should go to humans.

---

# 42A.53 Correct transfer rate

More useful than minimizing transfer.

Measure:

```text
Required transfers successfully transferred
```

and:

```text
Unnecessary transfers
```

separately.

---

# 42A.54 First Contact Resolution

Question:

Did this inbound call resolve the reason the customer called?

Examples:

FAQ answered → yes.

Booked → yes.

Human transferred and issue solved → yes.

Callback still required → not yet.

---

# 42A.55 Average Handle Time

Measure:

AI-only  
AI→human  
human-only.

Don't simply minimize AHT.

Fast incorrect call is worse than a slightly longer resolved call.

---

```text
Repeated questions
Corrections
Transfers
Failed tools
Long waits
```

```text
→ Booking
```

```text
call_id
```

```text
UNKNOWN_INTENT_RATE
```

```text

TOOL_FAILURE

```

# 42A.61 Inbound QA

QualityAI evaluates:

```text
Greeting
Disclosure
Intent
Need
Listening
Language
Knowledge accuracy
Tool usage
Booking
Transfer
Closing
```

Inbound-specific rubric differs from outbound sales.

---

# 42A.62 Inbound sales guardrail

Customer called for:

appointment cancellation.

Don't suddenly:

> “Would you like our massage package?”

Cross-sell should be relevant and context-sensitive.

Customer intent comes first.

---

# 42A.63 Lead-capture guardrail

Customer asks:

> “What time do you close?”

Do not immediately ask:

name  
email  
postal code  
marketing permission

unless required for requested service.

Reduce friction.

---

# 42A.64 Authentication by risk

Not every inbound question needs verification.

```text
Clinic hours
→ none

General service info
→ none

My appointment time
→ stronger context as policy dictates

Cancel my appointment
→ higher assurance

Sensitive account changes
→ stronger assurance
```

This keeps the experience usable.

---

# 42A.65 Fraud/abuse controls

Inbound risks:

```text
Robocalls
Call flooding
Harassment
Credential guessing
Appointment enumeration
Booking abuse
Repeated cancellation
Premium transfer abuse
```

FraudAI + SecurityAI inspect signals.

---

# 42A.66 Rate limiting

One caller repeatedly invokes expensive AI interactions.

Use:

```text
caller/session velocity
tenant-level protection
```

without blocking legitimate retry behavior unfairly.

---

# 42A.67 Caller ID spoofing

Caller ID is not strong identity proof.

Do not use ANI alone to authorize high-risk account actions.

---

# 42A.68 Clinical boundary

Caller asks:

> “Should I go to emergency?”

Healthcare-specific routing must follow an approved safety/clinical escalation framework.

Do not let general sales/reception AI improvise medical assessment.

---

# 42A.69 Emergency boundary

Build a dedicated:

```text
URGENT / EMERGENCY CLASSIFIER
```

according to clinic-approved protocols.

When triggered:

commercial flow stops.

Follow approved escalation messaging/process.

This needs dedicated governance/testing before production.

# 42A.70 User story — new customer booking

> **As a new caller, I want to call the clinic, explain what service I need, hear available times, book one, and receive confirmation without waiting for a receptionist.**

Acceptance flow:

```text
GIVEN
Unknown inbound caller

WHEN
Customer says:
"I need physiotherapy Tuesday after six."

THEN
Need = PHYSIO
Time constraint = after 18:00

WHEN
Scheduler returns:
18:30
19:15

THEN
AI presents these options

WHEN
Customer chooses 18:30

THEN
required customer details are collected

AND
critical details confirmed

AND
booking executed

AND
confirmation sent

AND
Customer/Lead/Appointment linked

AND
call disposition = BOOKED
```

---

# 42A.71 User story — existing customer

> **As an existing customer, I want the system to understand that I already have an appointment and help me reschedule it.**

Acceptance:

```text
Existing caller detected
↓
Customer says reschedule
↓
Appropriate verification
↓
Appointment retrieved
↓
Alternative slots
↓
Explicit confirmation
↓
Reschedule
↓
Old reminders cancelled
↓
New reminders generated
```

---

# 42A.72 User story — language

> **As a caller, I want to speak in my preferred supported language without restarting the call or losing information I already provided.**

Acceptance:

```text
English call starts

Customer requests Hindi

→ Language changes
→ Conversation state retained
→ Existing slots retained
→ Booking continues
```

---

# 42A.73 User story — human transfer

> **As a caller, when I request a staff member I want the AI to route me appropriately and give the staff member my existing context.**

Acceptance:

```text
Customer asks for human
↓
No unnecessary qualification
↓
HumanOps determines queue
↓
Context summary prepared
↓
Warm transfer
```

---

# 42A.74 User story — after-hours

> **As a caller after business hours, I want to know what the AI can still help me with and be able to schedule a future callback when staff assistance is required.**

# 42A.84 Edge case — caller says only “appointment”

Don't guess:

new booking

vs:

existing appointment.

Ask:

> “Would you like to book a new appointment or change an existing one?”

---

# 42A.85 Edge case — customer gives everything at once

> “I need physio at NW Thursday after six.”

Extract everything.

Do not ask four redundant questions.

---

# 42A.86 Edge case — language changes halfway

Maintain:

service  
date  
time  
customer state.

Only language changes.

---

# 42A.87 Edge case — caller wants two appointments

Example:

physio for self  
massage for spouse.

Create separate booking contexts.

Do not accidentally use one customer's details for another.

---

# 42A.88 Edge case — customer already booked

Customer:

> “I want physiotherapy Tuesday.”

Customer already has Tuesday appointment.

NextAI should clarify:

new appointment

or existing appointment discussion.

Avoid duplicate booking.

---

# 42A.89 Edge case — two appointments exist

Customer:

> “Cancel my appointment.”

Ask which one if ambiguity remains.

Never arbitrarily cancel.

---

# 42A.90 Edge case — scheduler goes down

Customer can still:

ask general questions.

For booking:

```text
BOOKING_UNAVAILABLE
```

Offer:

callback/human follow-up.

Never fabricate availability.

---

# 42A.91 Edge case — transfer fails

Do not hang up abruptly.

Return:

```text
TRANSFER_FAILED
```

Offer:

callback  
voicemail  
another valid queue.

---

# 42A.92 Edge case — human does not answer

Queue/transfer SLA expires.

Return caller to controlled fallback.

Do not leave indefinite hold.

---

# 42A.93 Edge case — customer hangs up during booking

If booking had not executed:

no booking.

If tool state uncertain:

reconcile.

Follow-up only according to current eligibility/preferences.

---

# 42A.94 Edge case — call reconnects

Attempt to recognize recent dropped-call context where appropriate.

But verify critical transaction state before resuming.

---

# 42A.95 Edge case — background noise

STT confidence low.

Clarify critical values.

Do not repeatedly fail without human fallback.

---

# 42A.96 Edge case — child/representative calling

Do not automatically assume authority to manage another person's appointment.

Identity/authorization policies govern account-specific actions.

---

# 42A.97 Edge case — caller refuses AI

> “I don't want to talk to a bot.”

Set:

```text
HUMAN_PREFERRED_CURRENT_CALL
```

Route human/callback.

Don't argue.

---

# 42A.98 Edge case — unsupported intent

Customer asks something outside system capabilities.

Outcome:

```text
UNSUPPORTED
```

then:

appropriate human route or information.

Do not turn AI into a general-purpose unrestricted assistant.

---

# 42A.99 Edge case — caller uses abusive language

AI can remain neutral.

If no valid business need / repeated abuse:

follow configured termination/escalation policy.

Human safety/operations rules matter too.

---

# Phase 42B — Inbound UI/UX Master Design

This phase designs the actual screens used by **clinic admins, receptionists, supervisors, QA reviewers, support teams, and managers** to operate inbound AI calling.

The principle is:

> The UI should show the right context at the right moment, minimize tab switching, make risky actions explicit, and let humans take control without losing conversation state.

## 42B.1 User roles

| Persona | Primary UI need |
|---|---|
| Receptionist | Handle transferred calls and appointments |
| Supervisor | Monitor live calls and intervene |
| Clinic Admin | Configure services, hours, routing |
| QA Reviewer | Review calls and defects |
| Support Engineer | Diagnose technical issues |
| Compliance | Review policy and consent events |
| Manager | Track call and booking performance |
| Executive | View high-level business outcomes |

Role-based screens matter because not every user should see the same data or controls.

## 42B.2 Main navigation

```text

 ├── Live Calls
```

## 42B.4 Live Calls screen

This is the central operational screen.

Columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Call ID | internal call reference |
| Duration | current call duration |
| Caller | masked/authorized identity |
| Clinic | tenant/location |
| Language | active voice language |
| Intent | current intent |
| State | booking/FAQ/transfer/etc. |
| AI confidence | latest confidence |
| Risk | normal/watch/intervene |
| Agent | active AI version |
| Status | AI / Human / Queue |
| Action | open/watch/take over |

Example:

```text
CALL-8811 | 02:41 | Raj S. | NW | Hindi
Intent: BOOK
State: AVAILABILITY
Confidence: 96%
Risk: NORMAL
AI: PHYSIO-v18
```

## 42B.5 Live call detail screen

When the supervisor opens a call:

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ CALL-8811                         LIVE 03:42         │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Raj Sharma                                         │
│ Known customer | Hindi/English | NW clinic         │
│ Intent: BOOK PHYSIO                                │
│ Risk: NORMAL                                       │
├───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┤
│ LIVE TRANSCRIPT           │ CUSTOMER CONTEXT       │
│                           │                        │
│ Customer: Tuesday after   │ Current appointment   │
│ six works.                │ None                   │
│                           │                        │
│ AI: I have 6:30 and 7:15. │ Preferred location NW │
│                           │ Price concern Medium   │
├───────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┤
│ CURRENT STATE                                      │
│ AVAILABILITY                                       │
│                                                    │
│ NEXTAI                                             │
│ Recommend Tue 6:30 / Tue 7:15                     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ TOOL STATUS                                        │
│ Scheduler        HEALTHY                           │
│ CRM              HEALTHY                           │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [LISTEN] [TAKE OVER] [TRANSFER] [CALLBACK] [END]  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 42B.6 Information hierarchy

The live screen should prioritize:

```text
1. What does the customer want?
2. What is happening now?
3. Is anything risky?
4. What action is recommended?
5. What can the human do?
```

Do not bury these under technical telemetry.

## 42B.7 Live transcript design

Each transcript turn should show:

```text
timestamp
speaker
text
confidence if relevant
intent
important entities
```

Example:

```text
14:31:06 CUSTOMER
"Thursday at six thirty."

Entities:
DAY = Thursday
TIME = 18:30
Confidence = 98%
```

Critical low-confidence entities can be highlighted.

## 42B.8 Tool timeline

Show tool activity separately:

```text
14:31:22 CHECK_AVAILABILITY
SUCCESS
Latency 720 ms

14:32:01 BOOK_APPOINTMENT
WAITING FOR CUSTOMER CONFIRMATION
```

This prevents supervisors from confusing AI statements with actual transactions.

## 42B.9 Customer context panel

Show only immediately relevant information:

```text
Name
Preferred language
Active appointment
Current lead
Current need
Previous call outcome
Open callback
Important communication preference
```

Do not dump the entire CRM profile into the live screen.

## 42B.10 NextAI panel

Example:

```text
NEXT RECOMMENDED ACTION

CHECK AVAILABILITY

Why:
✓ Customer requested appointment
✓ Tuesday evening
✓ NW preferred

Confidence:
97%
```

Also show:

```text
Alternative:
TRANSFER HUMAN
```

when relevant.

## 42B.11 Human takeover

When supervisor clicks:

```text
TAKE OVER
```

UI should require:

```text
Reason
```

Example reasons:

```text
Customer requested human
AI misunderstanding
Tool problem
Complaint
Policy concern
Supervisor intervention
```

Then:

```text
AI speaking → STOP
Human audio → CONNECT
```

Never let both speak simultaneously.

## 42B.91 User story — receptionist

> As a receptionist, I want transferred calls to arrive with a concise summary so I can continue immediately without asking the caller to repeat everything.

Acceptance criteria:

```text
Transfer reason visible
Customer need visible
Current appointment visible
Completed AI actions visible
Pending issue visible
```

## 42B.92 User story — supervisor

> As a supervisor, I want to see live inbound calls that are at risk so I can intervene before the customer experience fails.

Acceptance:

```text
Risk status
Corrections
Loop detection
Tool failure
Takeover
Transfer
```

available in one screen.

## 42B.93 User story — clinic administrator

> As a clinic administrator, I want to update business hours and inbound routing without modifying code.

Acceptance:

```text
Edit hours
Preview
Validate
Publish
Audit
```

## 42B.94 User story — QA reviewer

> As QA, I want to hear audio while viewing synchronized transcript, tool calls, and policy events.

Acceptance:

one synchronized review timeline.

## 42B.95 User story — manager

> As a manager, I want to understand why callers are transferred to humans.

Dashboard must show:

```text
transfer reason
service
language
agent
time
```

## 42B.96 User story — support engineer

> As support, I want to open a failed call and jump from business timeline to technical trace.

Acceptance:

```text
Call ID
→ Trace ID
→ failed span
```

without searching multiple tools manually.

## 42B.97 User story — compliance

> As compliance, I want to inspect disclosure, recording, verification, and policy decisions for a specific call.

## 42B.98 User story — executive

> As an executive, I want a simple view showing whether inbound AI is reducing missed calls, increasing appointments, maintaining quality, and lowering operational cost.

```text
Outcome captured
     ↓
CALL DETAIL CREATED
     ↓
QA
     ↓
REPORTING
     ↓
OPERATIONS DASHBOARD
     ↓
IMPROVEMENT
```

The next inbound-focused phase is **Phase 42C — Inbound Use-Case + User-Story Master Library**, where we can create the complete catalogue of **100+ inbound scenarios** covering new callers, existing patients, booking/reschedule/cancel, pricing, insurance/admin, provider inquiries, human transfer, complaint, missed calls, after-hours, multilingual conversations, payment questions, wrong numbers, spam, tool failures, identity issues, dropped calls, edge cases, and acceptance criteria.

# Phase 42C — Inbound Use-Case + User-Story Master Library

This phase turns the inbound architecture into a **complete production scenario catalogue**. The goal is to ensure product, engineering, QA, operations, security, and clinic teams all agree on what the inbound AI must handle.

> **Every production use case should have: trigger → user story → inputs → flow → systems/tools → success outcome → failure path → tracking → tests → edge cases.**

## 42C.1 Master use-case categories

| Category | Example scenarios |
|---|---|
| New caller | general inquiry, new booking, pricing |
| Existing customer | appointment lookup, reschedule, cancel |
| Scheduling | availability, waitlist, provider preference |
| Administrative | insurance, billing, receipts, forms |
| Clinic information | hours, directions, parking |
| Service information | physio, dental, chiro, ENT, massage |
| Human support | receptionist, billing, specialist |
| Language | Hindi, Punjabi, English, code-switch |
| After-hours | booking, callback, FAQ |
| Missed-call recovery | callback, voicemail |
| Complaint | service issue, booking issue, AI complaint |
| Customer acquisition | lead creation, source attribution |
| Follow-up | SMS/email/callback |
| Security | caller spoofing, account access |
| Fraud/abuse | spam, call flooding, booking abuse |
| Technical failure | scheduler/CRM/provider outages |
| Healthcare boundary | clinical/urgent request |
| Quality | corrections, loops, misunderstood caller |

---

# 42C.2 Use Case UC-IN-001 — General clinic information

**User story**

> As a caller, I want to ask basic clinic questions without having to identify myself or wait for staff.

Examples:

```text
"What time do you close?"
"Are you open Saturday?"
"Where are you located?"
"Do you have parking?"
```

Flow:

```text
Inbound Call
↓
Greeting
↓
Intent = GENERAL_INFORMATION
↓
KnowledgeAI / Clinic Config
↓
Answer
↓
Ask if anything else
↓
Close
```

Input:

```text
clinic/DID
question
language
```

Output:

```text
grounded answer
source
confidence
```

Tracking:

```text
intent
question_type
knowledge_source
resolution_status
call_duration
```

Success:

`FAQ_RESOLVED`

Edge case:

conflicting clinic hours → abstain/escalate rather than guess.

---

# 42C.3 UC-IN-002 — New customer service inquiry

Customer:

> “Do you provide physiotherapy?”

Flow:

```text
Intent = SERVICE_INFORMATION
↓
Resolve service
↓
KnowledgeAI
↓
Explain service
↓
Customer interested?
↓
Optional availability/booking
```

Do not immediately demand:

name  
email  
phone.

Anonymous FAQ should remain possible.

---

# 42C.4 UC-IN-003 — New appointment booking

User story:

> As a new caller, I want to describe the service and timing I need and book an available appointment during the same call.

Flow:

```text
CALL
↓
Need = PHYSIO
↓
Constraints
location
date
time
↓
Scheduler
↓
RecommendAI
↓
Present slots
↓
Customer selects
↓
Capture required identity/contact
↓
Confirm
↓
Policy/Tool authorization
↓
BOOK
↓
Confirmation
↓
CRM/Customer 360
```

Success criteria:

```text
Correct customer
Correct service
Correct date
Correct time
Correct clinic
Appointment exists in scheduler
Confirmation generated
```

Critical failure:

AI says booked but scheduler shows no appointment.

---

# 42C.5 UC-IN-004 — Availability only

Customer:

> “Do you have anything Tuesday evening?”

The customer may not be ready to book.

Flow:

```text
CHECK_AVAILABILITY
↓
Service missing?
    → ask service
↓
Scheduler
↓
Present available times
↓
Customer chooses to book?
```

Do not create a booking until explicit confirmation.

---

# 42C.6 UC-IN-005 — Exact-slot booking

Customer:

> “I want Tuesday at 6:30.”

If service/location already known:

```text
Check exact slot
↓
Available?
 YES → confirm → book
 NO → alternatives
```

Do not force full recommendation flow when unnecessary.

---

# 42C.7 UC-IN-006 — Booking with multiple constraints

Customer:

> “I need physiotherapy after 6 PM, NW only, sometime this week.”

Extract:

```text
service = PHYSIO
time >= 18:00 HARD
location = NW HARD
date range = this week
```

RecommendAI filters accordingly.

# 42C.8 UC-IN-007 — No matching appointment

Customer needs:

```text
Sunday
NW
after 7 PM
```

No match.

Options:

```text
Waitlist
Different day
Different time
Different location
Human help
```

Never silently relax hard constraints.

User story:

> As a caller, if no acceptable appointment is available, I want to join a waitlist rather than repeatedly call back.

Flow:

```text
NO_MATCH
↓
Waitlist permitted?
↓
Capture acceptable conditions
↓
Confirm
↓
CREATE_WAITLIST
↓
FollowUpAI
```

Track:

```text
service
location
date range
time range
priority rules
```

# 42C.10 UC-IN-009 — Existing appointment lookup

Customer:

> “What time is my appointment?”

Flow:

```text
Intent = EXISTING_APPOINTMENT
↓
Identity assurance according to policy
↓
Scheduler lookup
↓
Appointment(s)
↓
If unique → provide permitted details
If multiple → clarify
```

Caller ID alone should not be assumed sufficient for sensitive account access.

```text
↓

↓
Select new slot
↓
Confirm
↓
RESCHEDULE
```

New reminders generated.

book

Inbound number should have resilience strategy:

alternate SIP/carrier/failover number depending architecture.

Monitor missed-call impact.

---

# 42C.111 UC-IN-110 — Database outage

Critical state operations may fail closed.

Keep degraded FAQ functionality only if safely separable.

---

# 42C.112 UC-IN-111 — Redis/session failure

Conversation state should be recoverable or safely degraded.

Do not lose confirmed transaction state silently.

---

# 42C.113 UC-IN-112 — Human transfer provider outage

Offer callback.

Create durable task.

---

# 42C.114 UC-IN-113 — Call ends during tool execution

Booking result may become unknown.

Reconciliation workflow:

```text
tool request ID
↓
scheduler lookup
↓
SUCCESS / NOT_CREATED
↓
follow-up if needed
```

---

# 42C.115 UC-IN-114 — Duplicate tool request

Same booking command retried.

Idempotency prevents duplicate appointment.

---

# 42C.116 UC-IN-115 — Slot lost during booking

Recommended slot becomes unavailable.

Flow:

```text
BOOK
↓
SLOT_UNAVAILABLE
↓
Do not claim booked
↓
Retrieve alternatives
```

---

# 42C.117 UC-IN-116 — Caller cancels while booking is processing

Need clear transaction state.

If request not committed:

cancel.

If unknown:

reconcile.

---

# 42C.118 UC-IN-117 — Customer wants to stop recording

If supported by policy/architecture:

recording state changes independently of call.

Do not automatically terminate service unless required.

---

# 42C.119 UC-IN-118 — Customer asks what data is being used

Use approved privacy explanation.

Avoid revealing internal security implementation.

---

# 42C.120 UC-IN-119 — Customer asks to update communication preference

Examples:

```text
"Text me, don't call."
"Email only."
```

Update Preference/Policy systems.

Confirm scope appropriately.

---

# 42C.121 UC-IN-120 — Customer says “stop calling”

For inbound call, this may refer to future outbound contacts.

Capture applicable suppression intent.

Do not ignore because current call was inbound.

---

# 42C.122 UC-IN-121 — Customer asks to delete information

Create governed privacy request workflow.

Do not let voice agent directly erase production records without approved process.

---

# 42C.123 UC-IN-122 — Customer requests transcript/recording

Route through approved privacy/customer-service process.

Do not expose internal recording directly without authorization.

---

# 42C.124 UC-IN-123 — B2B corporate inquiry

Caller:

> “I'm looking for physiotherapy services for our employees.”

Route into corporate lead model:

```text
Organization
Contact
Company size
Need
Timeline
Decision process
```

Not ordinary patient booking.

---

# 42C.125 UC-IN-124 — Corporate demo request

Create:

```text
B2B_LEAD
intent = DEMO
```

Human sales callback/demo scheduling.

---

# 42C.126 UC-IN-125 — Vendor/supplier call

Not a customer lead.

Route:

administration/vendor queue.

Avoid putting into marketing pipeline.

---

# 42C.127 UC-IN-126 — Employment/job inquiry

Caller asks:

> “Are you hiring?”

Knowledge answer or HR route.

Do not create healthcare-service lead.

---

# 42C.128 UC-IN-127 — Media inquiry

Route to appropriate business contact if configured.

---

# 42C.129 UC-IN-128 — Emergency-services misuse

Caller repeatedly uses clinic line for unrelated emergency/general services.

Handle according to safe routing/termination policy.

---

# 42C.130 UC-IN-129 — Caller reports website/form issue

Create support/website issue.

Potentially help them complete desired service through voice.

---

# 42C.131 UC-IN-130 — Caller cannot use online booking

AI can perform booking via voice.

Track:

```text
DIGITAL_ACCESS_BARRIER
```

This may reveal UX issues with website.

---

# 42C.132 UC-IN-131 — Accessibility accommodation request

Capture relevant service accommodation request appropriately.

Route human where operational confirmation is needed.

---

# 42C.133 UC-IN-132 — Caller requests paper form

Create administrative fulfillment workflow if offered.

---

# 42C.134 UC-IN-133 — New patient form status

Caller:

> “Did you receive my form?”

Requires identity/context lookup and form-system integration.

---

# 42C.135 UC-IN-134 — Incomplete form

AI can explain missing required administrative fields or send secure link.

Do not solicit unnecessary sensitive details over voice.

---

# 42C.136 UC-IN-135 — Referral status

Caller asks:

> “Did you receive my referral?”

Requires verified integration/human route.

---

# 42C.137 UC-IN-136 — Provider referral call

Different caller role.

Route appropriately to clinic administration.

---

# 42C.138 UC-IN-137 — Customer asks for cancellation fee

Use current approved policy/pricing.

Do not state fee unless source supports it.

---

# 42C.139 UC-IN-138 — Late arrival

Customer:

> “I'm going to be 15 minutes late.”

Use clinic policy and optionally notify front desk/provider through approved workflow.

---

# 42C.140 UC-IN-139 — Customer asks to join waitlist after cancellation

Possible flow:

cancel existing appointment

then:

separate waitlist action.

Confirm each transaction.

---

# 42C.141 UC-IN-140 — Caller wants earlier appointment

Existing booking remains until alternative is successfully confirmed.

Do not cancel current appointment before new slot is secured unless workflow explicitly requires and customer agrees.

---

# 42C.142 UC-IN-141 — Multiple locations acceptable

Customer:

> “NW or NE is fine.”

Recommend across both.

Track preference set.

---

# 42C.143 UC-IN-142 — Any provider acceptable

Provider becomes nonconstraint.

Recommend earliest appropriate option.

---

# 42C.144 UC-IN-143 — Specific provider mandatory

Filter only provider.

If no availability:

do not quietly substitute another provider.

Offer alternatives only after explaining.

---

# 42C.145 UC-IN-144 — Earliest appointment priority

Customer:

> “Anywhere, anyone, just earliest.”

Ranking:

earliest valid slot dominates.

---

# 42C.146 UC-IN-145 — Lowest-price priority

Customer asks cheapest valid option.

Use authoritative prices.

Do not infer broader financial status.

---

# 42C.147 UC-IN-146 — Customer compares competitors

> “Another clinic charges less.”

Capture competitor mention as customer-reported.

Explain own verified services without attacking competitor.

---

# 42C.148 UC-IN-147 — Customer requests promotion/discount

OfferAI only.

No invented concession.

---

# 42C.149 UC-IN-148 — Customer asks for manager

Route supervisor/manager queue or callback.

Treat as human request, potentially elevated priority.

---

# 42C.150 UC-IN-149 — Repeated AI failure

If corrections/loops exceed threshold:

```text
AUTO_ESCALATE
```

Don't make caller keep fighting the agent.

---

# 42C.151 UC-IN-150 — Customer disconnects immediately after greeting

Outcome:

```text
EARLY_ABANDON
```

Track separately.

Could indicate wrong number, bot, bad greeting, latency.

---

# 42C.152 Common user-story template

For every remaining inbound scenario, use:

```text
USER STORY

As a <persona>,
I want <goal>,
so that <business/customer value>.

PRECONDITIONS

INPUT

MAIN FLOW

ALTERNATE FLOW

TOOLS / SYSTEMS

POLICY REQUIREMENTS

DATA CREATED / UPDATED

SUCCESS CRITERIA

FAILURE CRITERIA

TRACKING EVENTS

KPIs

TEST CASES

EDGE CASES

OWNER
```

This should become your standard product backlog template.

---

# 42C.153 Master inbound acceptance framework

Every scenario should be scored against these checkpoints:

```text
1. Did we identify the correct intent?
2. Did we understand the correct customer need?
3. Did we avoid unnecessary questions?
4. Did we apply the correct policy?
5. Did we call the correct tool?
6. Were tool parameters correct?
7. Was customer confirmation obtained where needed?
8. Did authoritative system state match what we told the caller?
9. Was customer language handled correctly?
10. Was human escalation available?
11. Was outcome captured?
12. Was follow-up created/cancelled correctly?
13. Did tracking/reporting receive the event?
14. Did QualityAI evaluate it?
15. Is the whole call reproducible through trace/audit?
```

---

# 42C.154 Scenario priority model

Do not implement all 150 simultaneously.

### P0 — Production-critical

```text
Greeting
FAQ
Booking
Availability
Reschedule
Cancel
Human request
Appointment lookup
DNC/preferences
Clinical boundary
Tool failure
Transfer failure
```

### P1 — High-value

```text
Pricing
Insurance/admin
Missed call recovery
After-hours
Waitlist
Multilingual
Complaint
SMS/email follow-up
```

### P2 — Expansion

```text
B2B
Referral
Forms
Payment admin
Provider-specific flows
Advanced customer preferences
```

### P3 — Optimization

```text
Market research signals
Advanced recommendation
Upsell/cross-sell
Advanced experimentation
```

# 42C.155 MVP inbound scope

For the first clinic deployment, I would limit production to approximately **20–25 core use cases**:

```text
1 Greeting
2 Language selection
3 Clinic hours
4 Location
5 Parking
6 Service information
7 Pricing
8 Availability
9 New booking
10 Appointment lookup
11 Reschedule
12 Cancellation
13 Confirmation resend
14 Human request
15 Department transfer
16 Callback
17 After-hours FAQ
18 After-hours callback
19 Complaint
20 Insurance/admin handoff
21 Missed call recovery
22 Wrong number
23 Unsupported request
24 Clinical-boundary escalation
25 Tool/provider failure recovery
```

Everything else can be added after quality stabilizes.

Before calling the inbound system production-ready:

```text
Call Answering                  PASS
Intent Routing                  PASS

Booking                         PASS

Human Transfer                  PASS
Callback                        PASS

English                         PASS

Critical Entity Accuracy        PASS
Booking Integrity               100%
Critical Policy Failures        0

Provider Failures Recover       PASS

Tracking                        PASS
Dashboard                       PASS

```

## Phase 42C final view

Your inbound system is no longer just:

```text
PHONE
→ AI
→ BOOK
```

It becomes:

```text
                          INBOUND CUSTOMER
                                 ↓
                         PHONE / SIP / DID
                                 ↓
                         INBOUND GATEWAY
                                 ↓
                    KNOWN / UNKNOWN / ROLE
                                 ↓
                             LANGUAGE
                                 ↓
                              INTENT
                                 ↓
                               NEED
                                 ↓
              ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
              ↓                  ↓                  ↓
           GENERAL           TRANSACTION         HUMAN
              ↓                  ↓                  ↓
          KNOWLEDGE       IDENTITY/POLICY        QUEUE
              ↓                  ↓                  ↓
          ANSWER           TOOL EXECUTION       TRANSFER
              │                  │                  │
              └──────────────────┼──────────────────┘
                                 ↓
                              OUTCOME
                                 ↓

                                 ↓

                                 ↓
```
